Tasks include skeletal element identification and family-level taxonomy.

entry.title: Recursive transformers for semiconductor thermo-mechanical reliability

author.name: Kart-leong Lim

entry.summary: This paper compares three recursive (weight-shared, depth-recurrent) transformer designs as surrogate models for semiconductor thermo-mechanical simulation, arguing that trading parameters for repeated compute reduces overfitting on the small datasets typical of engineering design. It includes a hardware-aware evaluation of memory and compute cost.

entry.title: FADEx: Feature Attribution and Distortion-based Explanation of Dimensionality Reduction

author.name: Lucas Greff Meneses, Evandro S. Ortigossa, Claudio Silva, Luis Gustavo Nonato

entry.summary: FADEx explains nonlinear dimensionality reduction by attributing which input features drive an instance's position in the projected space and by accounting for projection distortion. It aims to make DR visualizations, widely used for inspecting model latent spaces, less opaque themselves.

entry.title: MatCreatioNN: Machine learning-guided computational discovery of photocatalysts for environmental applications

author.name: Satya Kokonda

entry.summary: MatCreatioNN couples RL-based metal-organic framework generation with a multi-stage crystal graph convolutional network screening funnel, generating and filtering 120,000 candidate photocatalysts on 13 descriptors including band gap, selectivity, adsorption energy, and stability. The pipeline targets environmental remediation and CO2 conversion materials.

entry.title: DS@GT ARC at ImageCLEFmedical 2026: Architectural Diversity for Concept Detection and Foundation-Model Scaling for Caption Prediction in Medical Image Analysis

author.name: Bowen Wang, Youwen Zhang, Ritesh Mehta

entry.summary: A shared-task system report for medical image concept detection and caption generation on the ROCOv2 dataset, using a late-fusion ensemble of ConvNeXt-V2, BiomedCLIP, and DenseNet plus a regularized threshold-tuning procedure. The primary submission ranked first in the concept detection track.

entry.title: AWARE-FX: An Auditable Knowledge-Guided AI System for Measuring Corporate Foreign-Exchange Hedging Disclosure

author.name: Qi Wang

entry.summary: AWARE-FX converts corporate annual report text into auditable firm-year measures of foreign-exchange hedging disclosure, combining a professional lexicon, negation and accounting-status logic, financial encoders, evidence gates, and an audit ledger. It processes over half a million snippets across nearly 25,000 Hong Kong firm-years with ablations, human audit, and temporal tests.

entry.title: Beyond Feeling Better: Capability-Sustaining Emotional Dialogue as a Longitudinal Research Paradigm

author.name: Ming Wang, Jiaqi Wu Young, Wenfang Wu, Daling Wang, Shi Feng

entry.summary: A position and survey paper proposing capability-sustaining emotional dialogue, reframing emotional support systems around long-run user outcomes such as coping and autonomy rather than immediate mood improvement. It organizes data, modeling, evaluation, and governance around repeated use, non-use, and termination.

entry.title: BlindPSNR: A No-Reference Fidelity Predictor for Low-Light Image Enhancement

author.name: Mingzhe Lyu, Jinqiang Cui, Hong Zhang

entry.summary: BlindPSNR predicts fidelity (PSNR) without a reference image so that low-light enhancement parameters can be selected automatically per scene. The authors note that all seven no-reference image-quality baselines they test fail entirely at top-1 configuration selection because they measure perceptual quality rather than signal fidelity.

entry.title: ARD-REFSM: Enhancing Reflection Symmetry Detection with Asymmetric Denoising and Rotation Equivariance

author.name: Dongfu Yin, Rourou Su, Cong Zhao, Fei Yu

entry.summary: Improves reflection symmetry detection with a module that suppresses asymmetric background clutter and a rotation-equivariant feature similarity matching module comparing original and rotated images. Addresses orientation sensitivity of standard convolutional features.

entry.title: TEA-AgriVLN: Traversability Estimation Alarm for Agricultural Vision-and-Language Navigation

author.name: Xiaobei Zhao, Xingqi Lyu, Xin Chen, Xiang Li

entry.summary: TEA-AgriVLN adds a traversability estimation alarm to agricultural vision-and-language navigation, motivated by the observation that traversability in fields is embodiment-dependent and ambiguous compared with indoor scenes. The module flags uncertain terrain before the agent commits to low-level actions.

entry.title: Real-Time Hard Peak Age-of-Information Safety with No-Regret Learning

author.name: Wentao Zhang, Wentao Mo

entry.summary: The paper gives an online convex optimization algorithm for safety-critical IoT scheduling that guarantees zero per-slot violation of a hard peak Age-of-Information deadline under adversarial conditions, with sublinear regret against static safe policies. It contrasts with prior work that only bounds average or cumulative violations.

entry.title: Expected Survival-Time Bounds for Robust Optimization Over Time under Isotropic Gaussian Dynamics

author.name: Pavel Novoa-Hern\'andez

entry.summary: This paper derives theoretical bounds on the expected survival time of solutions in robust optimization over time under isotropic Gaussian environmental dynamics, where survival time counts how many future environments a deployed solution still satisfies a quality threshold. The field has been largely empirical and lacked such analysis.

entry.title: Comparison of a Parametric Physics-Informed Neural Network and a Tensorial Reduced-Order Model for the Shallow-Water Dam-Break Problem

author.name: Anton Myshak, Md Rezwan Bin Mizan, Ilya Timofeyev

entry.summary: This paper compares a parametric physics-informed neural network against a non-intrusive tensorial reduced-order model on the parametrized one-dimensional shallow-water dam-break problem, with both learning a direct solution map that avoids time integration. Shock-aware collocation proves essential for PINN robustness in the presence of discontinuities.

entry.title: MSCM-net: A hyperspectral image classiffcation method based on multi-scale convolution and Mamba

author.name: Jianjun Chen, Linlin Wang, Lifang Chang, Limin Huo, Shujiang Song, Yanjia Zhao, Mingwei Shao

entry.summary: Combines multi-scale convolutional feature extraction with stacked Mamba blocks for hyperspectral image classification, aiming to keep local detail while modeling long spectral sequences efficiently. Positioned against locality limits of CNNs and quadratic cost of transformers.

entry.title: A Methodology for Designing Knowledge-Driven Missions for Robots

author.name: Guillermo GP-Lenza, Carmen DR. Pita-Romero, Miguel Fernandez-Cortizas, Pascual Campoy

entry.summary: A methodology paper for building knowledge graphs into ROS 2 robotic missions, covering condition definition, task decomposition, planning, graph representation, and high-level mission specification. It is demonstrated in a simulated drone search-and-rescue scenario in the Aerostack2 framework.

entry.title: HiFloat4 Format for End-To-End Reinforcement Learning Post-Training of Large Language Models

author.name: Hei Yi Mak, Shadan Golestan, Hoang Le, Mehran Taghian Jazi, Yunke Peng, Yaoyuan Wang, Yao Wang, Junsong Wang, Tianchi Hu, Fengchen He, Guipeng Hu, Tanzila Rahman, Anandharaju Durai Raju

entry.summary: arXiv:2607.26515v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present, to our knowledge, the first end-to-end FP4 RL post-training, in which both the rollout and training policies, including their forward and...

entry.title: An Attention-Based Framework for Alzheimers Disease Classification Using Resting-State fMRI

author.name: Harshiddhi Pathak, Gowtham Reddy N, Mrinal Acharya, Manjunatha Mahadevappa

entry.summary: The framework classifies Alzheimer's disease from resting-state fMRI functional connectivity by treating brain regions as tokens and applying transformer self-attention to model long-range inter-regional dependencies. It aims to replace handcrafted connectivity features and conventional machine learning pipelines.

entry.title: Searching for Robust Augmentations to Improve Out-of-Domain Generalization in Dermoscopic Skin Cancer Classification

author.name: Alexander Kozachok, Ilya Latyshev, Evgeny Karpulevich, Elena Kozachok, Egor Ushakov, Oleg Samovarov

entry.summary: arXiv:2607.26765v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Background/Objectives: Dermoscopic skin lesion classifiers often lose accuracy under domain shift across imaging devices, illumination, and capture a...

entry.title: SkillRise: Agentic Reinforcement Learning for Cross-Task Skill Evolution

author.name: Zhiyuan Yao, Yuxin Chen, Zhengxi Lu, Zishan Xu, Yueqing Sun, Yifu Guo, Yuquan Lu, Zhengzhou Cai, Kangning Zhang, Zhuowen Han, Zi-Han Wang, Ziang Ye, Qi Gu, Xunliang Cai, Weiwen Liu, Yongliang Shen

entry.summary: arXiv:2607.26784v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language model agents often encounter related yet distinct tasks that share reusable solution patterns. Yet standard agentic reinforcement lear...

entry.title: Expanding Data-Agnostic Pivotal Instances Selection Models with Proximity Trees and Ensemble Learning

author.name: Alessio Cascione, Mattia Setzu, Cristiano Landi, Paolo Maria Mancarella, Riccardo Guidotti

entry.summary: The authors build interpretable-by-design predictors that classify by comparing inputs to a small set of automatically selected pivot examples, arranged hierarchically like a decision tree and extended to pivot pairs and ensembles. The approach mirrors how people reason by analogy to representative cases.

entry.title: Memory Efficient Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Shuting Luo, Monika Mikhail Kanaan, Cameron Gordon, Anna Leontjeva, Simon Lucey

entry.summary: arXiv:2607.27546v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tabular Foundation Models, such as TabPFN, have received a large amount of recent attention due to their performance on in-context tabular machine lear...

entry.title: LLM-Guided Initialization for Accelerated Hybrid Quantum-Classical Medical Image Classification

author.name: Riza Alaudin Syah, Irwan Alnarus Kautsar, Haza Nuzly Bin Abdull Hamed

entry.summary: This paper evaluates a simplified single-query variant of LLM-based initialization for variational quantum circuits on a mammography classification task, reporting substantially larger initial gradient variance and much faster convergence than random initialization. It targets the barren plateau trainability problem in parameterized quantum circuits.

entry.title: Robust Wavelength Selection for Partial Least Squares Sugar Content Estimation Using Combinatorial Bayesian Optimization

author.name: Mitsunobu Kanebako, Ami S. Koshikawa, Masaru Hitomi, Takuro Tanaka, Mahito Chiba, Maiko Mori, Masayuki Ohzeki

entry.summary: This paper formulates near-infrared wavelength-region selection for fruit sugar content estimation as binary black-box optimization, using a sparse quadratic surrogate with Thompson sampling and solving the acquisition step as a QUBO via simulated or quantum annealing. It improves partial least squares prediction accuracy and yields more consistent selected regions.

entry.title: Complementary Matrix-Gated QKAN Fast-Weight Programmers for Quantum Dynamics Forecasting

author.name: Kuo-Chung Peng, Samuel Yen-Chi Chen, Jiun-Cheng Jiang, Chen-Yu Liu, En-Jui Kuo, Yun-Yuan Wang, Tzung-Chi Huang, Prayag Tiwari, Chi-Sheng Chen, Chun-Hua Lin, Yu-Chao Hsu, Tai-Yue Li, Saif Al-Kuwari, Simon See, Kuan-Cheng Chen, Nan-Yow Chen, Hsi-Sheng Goan

entry.summary: Extends quantum-inspired Kolmogorov-Arnold fast-weight programmers by replacing a single scalar retention gate with low-rank element-wise modulation, allowing different fast-state coordinates to keep different memory timescales. Applied to forecasting quantum dynamics sequences.

entry.title: Meteosat Third Generation imagery improves CNN-based SSI retrieval

author.name: Gordei Prib\~otkin, Piia Post, Velle Toll

entry.summary: Introduces a multi-imager, multi-resolution CNN that fuses second- and third-generation Meteosat satellite imagery with solar geometry features for 10-minute surface solar irradiance retrieval over Estonia. The study quantifies how much the newer higher-resolution imager improves machine-learning-based retrieval against ground stations.

entry.title: AI-assisted pre-review of open-source software submissions: an experience report from BOSC 2026

author.name: Tazro Ohta, Nomi L. Harris, Seth Carbon

entry.summary: An experience report on using generative AI to pre-review conference abstracts for a bioinformatics open-source conference, scoring criteria such as code availability, license validity, and how easily a project can be built and run. It examines whether LLM pre-review can relieve volunteer reviewers facing surging submission volumes.

entry.title: Can LVLMs Uncover the Truth Behind Visual Illusions? An Analysis of Perceptual and Reasoning Capabilities

author.name: Liangjie Zhao, Jiaqing Lyu, Kexin Tang, Zecheng Fang, Rong Yin, Yulan Hu, Da Li, Jianing Li

entry.summary: arXiv:2607.27747v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Vision Language Models have integrated reasoning capabilities, elevating cognitive performance to new levels. However, existing evaluations eithe...

entry.title: Metaphor Tracer: A Theory-Informed Analysis of Hidden States

author.name: Marc Heimann, Roxana Assadi Moghaddam, Olga Brovkina, Mark Pettifor, Lutz Goetzmann

entry.summary: Defines two training-free scores over hidden states from a single forward pass: an aggregator measuring whether a position consolidates the whole text, and a differentiator measuring transient transport of other tokens into a position's subspace. Constants were frozen on one discovery text and the pattern reportedly holds across three unrelated models as a signifier repeats even while surprisal and attention decay.

entry.title: Towards Autonomous Aircraft Surveillance from Nanosatellites through On-Board Inference and Generative Data Augmentation

author.name: Antonio Delgado-Rosa, David Mu\~noz-Valero, Enrique Adrian Villarrubia-Martin, Juan Moreno-Garcia

entry.summary: arXiv:2607.28470v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Airborne surveillance from low Earth orbit is hindered by two interconnected bottlenecks: nanosatellites have a limited downlink budget, yet the conv...

entry.title: Hash Chemistry: Minimal Models for Evolutionary Growth of Complexity

author.name: Ilya Horiguchi, Hiroki Sayama

entry.summary: Proposes a pipeline where a 6U CubeSat runs aircraft detection on a low-power edge accelerator to avoid downlinking terabytes of raw imagery, while a LoRA-tuned diffusion model synthesizes images of rare aircraft classes to fix dataset imbalance. It jointly targets bandwidth constraints and data scarcity in orbital surveillance.

entry.title: Arm2Air: Cross-Embodiment Skeleton Transfer for 3D Relay Formation

author.name: Dohun Lee, Kyeonghyun Yoo, Seokmin Kim, Byongho Lee, Seungjoo Oh, Hwangnam Kim

entry.summary: Arm2Air transfers obstacle-avoidance motion skeletons learned by a pretrained robot-arm motion planner into UAV relay placement in cluttered urban environments, using a transformer pretrained on arm skeletons and adapted with LoRA on limited UAV data. The transferred skeleton seeds a relay chain that is then refined for connectivity and capacity.

entry.title: Write-Safe Flow Field Mapping under Ambiguous Onboard Sensing and Localization Drift

author.name: Linhao Jin, Qimin Feng, Peter Gunnarson, Qiang Zhong

entry.summary: Addresses ghost structures in robot-built flow field maps by learning a write-safety score that attenuates uncertain map updates when localization drift or ambiguous observations make a locally plausible estimate unsafe to commit globally. Synthetic jet and crossflow experiments show reduced map error.

entry.title: The Entangled Dimensions of Decision Theory

author.name: Ihor Kendiukhov

entry.summary: Proposes treating decision theory as a grid of separable axes: what is supposed when evaluating an action, how a gamble is scored once outcomes are known, and how pre-information choices relate to post-information ones. The author maps existing theories into this space and argues theorems show the axes are provably entangled, restricting which combinations are coherent.

entry.title: Anthropic reasoning without duplicates is just standard Bayesian updating

author.name: Stuart_Armstrong

entry.summary: Argues that in anthropic problems without identical duplicates, the self-indication assumption is mathematically identical to ordinary Bayesian updating, so it is correct and lacks the counterintuitive implications usually attributed to it. The author locates most of the strangeness in anthropic reasoning in the choice of priors rather than the updating rule.

entry.title: Sim2Win: A Team-Agnostic, Event-Based Pre-Match Outcome Prediction and Tactical Profiling System for Football

author.name: Mouad Zemzoumi, Amine Abouaomar

entry.summary: Sim2Win predicts football match outcomes from team-agnostic tactical profiles built on rolling event-data features, clustering teams into eight playstyles and training a bank of classifiers over tactical matchups. It reframes pre-match prediction as tactical decision support rather than identity-based scouting.

entry.title: A Picture Says Thousands of Words - Harnessing Dermal Exposure Data from Images through Hybrid Deep Learning for Enhanced Safety Assessment

author.name: Hua Qian, Manisha Kotha, Tuan Tran, Jennifer Shin, Haining Zheng

entry.summary: This study combines Mask R-CNN person segmentation with color-based skin detection on 170 indoor painting images to estimate the ratio of exposed skin to total body area for dermal exposure assessment. The pixel-ratio estimates agree with human estimates roughly 80 percent of the time.

entry.title: Neural Network-Assisted CLEAN for Channel Modeling in Low-SNR Regimes

author.name: Chaofan Deng, Linyu Sun, Jaeho Lee, Arijit Raychowdhury

entry.summary: NN-CLEAN embeds a multi-head residual network inside the iterative CLEAN algorithm for wireless multipath parameter estimation, replacing exhaustive grid search while retaining the physical structure of the estimator. It targets low-SNR channel modeling where pure deep learning generalizes poorly.

entry.title: Class-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Counterfactual Explanation Generation

author.name: Muhammad Adil Saleem, Syed Ali Raza, Mary-Anne Williams

entry.summary: This study tests whether adding a model's predicted class to the reinforcement learning state improves generation of counterfactual explanations, measured on validity, sparsity, and proximity. The hypothesis is that class-awareness lets the agent explore counterfactuals more efficiently.

entry.title: What Makes Deep Learning Work for Traditional Chinese Medicine Tongue Diagnosis? A Comprehensive Ablation Study

author.name: Longxia Gao, Linan Wang, Yuhe Han, Junze Geng, Meng Zhang, Hanqing Zhao

entry.summary: A large ablation study over backbones, losses, augmentations, and training strategies for deep-learning tongue diagnosis in traditional Chinese medicine, using five-fold cross-validation on two datasets. It reports that a small ConvNeXt with restrained augmentation and ensembling performs best and distills six design principles.

entry.title: Challenges in annotations by humans and LLMs: A case study of evaluative language

author.name: Mirela Imamovic, Aenne Cecilia Kristine Knierim, Khushi Pitroda, Ekaterina Lapshinova-Koltunski

entry.summary: Compares annotations of evaluative language in TED talk transcripts by linguistics students, a trained linguist, and LLMs using Appraisal theory categories. It asks whether models and humans fail in similar ways on a highly subjective annotation task.

entry.title: Endo-NeRF++: Uncertainty-Aware Neural Rendering with Multi-Resolution Hash Encoding for Dynamic Surgical Scene Reconstruction

author.name: Gousia Habib, Laura Ruotsalainen

entry.summary: Extends the EndoNeRF line of work for reconstructing deformable surgical scenes by adding multi-resolution hash-grid encoding, temporal feature fusion, and uncertainty-guided adaptive sampling. Targets robot-assisted minimally invasive surgery where tissue deformation, occlusion, and specular reflections break standard neural rendering.

entry.title: A Systems Engineering Framework for Vision-Language-Enabled UAV Triage and Disaster Response

author.name: Swapnil Saha, Bhuvan Rajanasiriyur Jagadeesha, Karishma Patnaik, Neelakshi Majumdar

entry.summary: A systems engineering study on embedding vision-language models as coordination agents inside human-UAV disaster response loops, rather than limiting them to decision support and message drafting. It argues current VLM uses increase operator burden because humans must still translate outputs into coordinated robot actions.

entry.title: Machines that know they are aging: a framework for hardware-aware autonomous intelligence

author.name: Cheng Siong Chin, Jianhua Zhang, Mohan Venkateshkumar

entry.summary: A position framework arguing that autonomous systems should treat their own hardware degradation (battery wear, sensor drift, timing errors, memory faults) as an input to reasoning, planning, and mission execution. It names the failure mode of gradual accumulated degradation leading to mission failure and proposes hardware self-awareness as a design pillar.

entry.title: Big-World Intuitions

author.name: sarahconstantin

entry.summary: An essay arguing that many domains reward non-adversarial, resource-growing strategies when the actor is small relative to the world, spanning startups, market making, early game play, and r-selected species. It builds intuitions about when to ignore competitors versus when scale forces strategic interaction.

entry.title: DAS-PMVC: A Framework for Partial Multi-View Clustering via Dual Alignment and Structure Enhancement

author.name: Shubin Ma, Liang Zhao, Chuanye He, Zhenjiao Liu, Liang Zou, Lin Yuanbo Wu, Yu Shao

entry.summary: DAS-PMVC clusters multi-view data whose views are partially misaligned, using anchor-graph structure alignment to build a consistent latent embedding and structure enhancement to reduce the influence of irrelevant samples. It targets the partial view alignment problem caused by imperfect data collection.

entry.title: Kohn-Sham Spectral Embedding on Sparse Graphs at the Nishimori Temperature for Image Classification

author.name: V. S. Usatyuk, D. A. Sapozhnikov, S. I. Egorov

entry.summary: KSSE proposes replacing dense CNN classifier heads with a physics-inspired spectral embedding on sparse LDPC-like graphs, evaluated at the Nishimori temperature of an associated Ising model, with FFT-based solves on circulant blocks for speed. Graph topology is optimized through a codeword-preserving surgery procedure.

entry.title: Wiring diagram extraction and gluing: a case study in classifying figure skating jumps using 3D dataset

author.name: Jason Lo, Mohammadnima Jafari

entry.summary: The authors develop a theory of gluing wiring diagrams so that Hasse clustering, which becomes combinatorially infeasible as cluster counts grow, can be applied iteratively while yielding the same result as one monolithic run. They demonstrate on classification of figure skating jumps from 3D video data.

entry.title: Strategies for Milestone-driven Start-ups in Multi-activity Settings

author.name: Zhengli Wang

entry.summary: A continuous-time stochastic control model of startups that must clear successive milestone thresholds, where the entrepreneur chooses among several activities with different costs affecting drift and volatility. The author solves for the optimal policy in a setting with three or more controls, which is usually analytically intractable.

entry.title: Generative AI and linguistic diversity in academic writing and publishing: Perspectives from World Englishes

author.name: Kingsley Ugwuanyi, Christian Mair, Sender Dovchin, Iker Erdocia, Maria Kuteeva, Esther Airemionkhale

entry.summary: A structured dialogue among five sociolinguists on how generative AI writing tools affect linguistic diversity and the legitimacy of non-dominant Englishes in academic publishing. It weighs democratization benefits against homogenization and marginalization of minoritized varieties.

entry.title: Creative Transformation in Literary Texts: Modelling Change Across Representational Levels

author.name: Ioana-Roxana Boriceanu, Liviu P. Dinu

entry.summary: Models literary creativity as selective transformation of earlier works, comparing texts across lexical, semantic, conceptual, structural, and narrative levels with directional alignment and control-calibrated similarity. Applied to documented literary influence pairs, it shows different pairs preserve different representational levels.

entry.title: AI systems and the reproduction of (standard) language ideologies in World Englishes

author.name: Kingsley Ugwuanyi

entry.summary: Argues that LLMs reproduce standard-language ideologies favoring Inner Circle English norms across training data, design protocols, evaluation benchmarks, and user feedback loops. Evidence is drawn from prior studies, media and social media discourse, and model output examples.

entry.title: ZMIS-SAM: Segment Anything Model Enhanced with Wavelet Transform for Zooplankton Microscopy Image Instance Segmentation

author.name: Dekun Yuan, Zhongwei Li, Zheng Qiao, Jie Zhang

entry.summary: ZMIS-SAM adapts the Segment Anything Model with wavelet-transform components and lightweight adapters for instance segmentation of zooplankton in microscopy images, targeting slender appendages and incomplete boundaries. It aims to inject domain knowledge SAM lacks.

entry.title: When Robots Exchange Meaning: A Demo of Goal-Oriented Semantic Communications for Collaborative Robotics

author.name: Peizheng Li, Xinyi Lin, Sajida Gufran, Adnan Aijaz

entry.summary: A demonstration testbed for goal-oriented semantic communication in collaborative robotics, where a mobile robot encodes RGB frames into VQ-VAE tokens and an edge node reconstructs them for semantic mapping and mission dashboards. It frames communication quality in terms of mission outcomes rather than packet delivery.

entry.title: Testing LLMs on Undergraduate Music Theory

author.name: Waldvogel

entry.summary: An informal benchmark of five current models on a hand-designed undergraduate music theory exam, where all pass and the strongest reasoning model scores perfectly, prompting the author to declare the test saturated. Retroactive testing on 2025-era models shows large gaps, with one anomaly where an older Gemini Pro version outperformed a newer one.

entry.title: iVAIS: Outer and Inner Alignment

author.name: Masaharu Mizumoto

entry.summary: Responds to the objection that virtue-based alignment merely swaps one proxy for another, arguing that a scalar virtue score is a directional training signal rather than a definition, and that the target is a holistic ideal character rather than separable traits. It claims this structural difference changes both outer and inner alignment dynamics.

entry.title: The iVAIS Manifesto: Safety Through Character, Not Compliance

author.name: Masaharu Mizumoto

entry.summary: A manifesto proposing character-based, virtue-centered alignment as an alternative to rule-based and principle-based approaches, arguing that constitutional methods remain action-based ethics and that mechanistic interpretability cannot guarantee control. It contends that pre-release evaluation will fail once models exceed human intelligence and can pass evaluations regardless of disposition.

entry.title: ZAPs: A Reward Attribution Framework for DeFi Ecosystems with Adversarial-Robust Scoring via Parallel Anomaly Ensemble Detection

author.name: Girish G N, Ashutosh Sahoo, Ajay Bhat, Akshay SP, Gurukiran S, Parag Paul, Dhanashekar Kandaswamy

entry.summary: ZAPs is a reward attribution scheme for decentralized finance incentive programs that scores economic contribution with percentile normalization and sector-level weighting, plus an anomaly-detection ensemble to resist bots and sybil farming. The design bounds how much reward any single protocol can yield.

entry.title: Prompt Chaining in Practice: A Case Study in Automated Scholarly Report Generation

author.name: Andrei Lazarev

entry.summary: Compares a multi-stage prompt chaining pipeline against an optimized single-shot prompt for automatically generating scholarly digests, evaluated against one human-written gold-standard report in the education domain. The claim is that chaining is a more reliable architectural pattern for complex synthesis.

entry.title: CDAE: Enhancing Perturbation Robustness in Pretrained Language Models with Contrastive Denoising

author.name: Sina Heydari, Amirreza Abbasi, Mohsen Hooshmand, Majid Ramezani

entry.summary: CDAE is a lightweight contrastive denoising autoencoder that refines frozen BERT sentence embeddings to be invariant to meaning-preserving perturbations such as synonym substitution and word dropout. It reports higher embedding stability than raw BERT and SimCSE under perturbation.

entry.title: Automated Multilabel Mpox Research Classification with Explainable Transformer Models

author.name: Tanjim Taharat Aurpa

entry.summary: The study applies multilabel transformer classification with explainability analysis to categorize 14,590 Mpox research articles into topics such as outbreaks, vaccination, and epidemiology, with BERT performing best. Reported metrics exceed 96% across accuracy and F1 measures.

entry.title: Toward Multi-Modal Deep Learning for Pulmonary Disease Classification: A Texture-Based Machine Learning Pilot Study on Public Chest X-Ray Data

author.name: Yogisri Pujitha Chinthoti

entry.summary: A small pilot study using classical HOG and GLCM texture features with logistic regression, random forest, and SVM to distinguish COVID-19 from other pneumonia on 668 public chest radiographs, with patient-level cross-validation. Reports modest accuracy and frames the work as a baseline for future multimodal deep learning.

entry.title: Community Polls on Alignment Controversies II

author.name: jonahmattwoodward

entry.summary: A second round of community polls probing where alignment researchers and forum readers disagree on contested claims, with a 15-person expert panel including well-known commentators answering the same questions for comparison. Results are to be published as a report mapping agreement and disagreement in the field.

entry.title: Daniela Rus receives Bavarian Minister-President's High-Tech Prize

author.name: Rachel Gordon | Alex Shipps | MIT CSAIL

entry.summary: An MIT news item reporting that CSAIL director Daniela Rus received the 2026 High-Tech Prize of the Bavarian Minister-President, with the citation covering self-organizing robot collectives, soft robotics, autonomous mobility, and brain-inspired computing. The piece situates the award in the broader turn toward physical AI and robots that operate reliably in unscripted environments.

entry.title: Correlation between prosody and pragmatics: A case study of the discourse marker h\=al\=a `now' in Persian

author.name: Soleiman Ghaderi, Moloud Asakereh, Kevin Tang

entry.summary: A corpus study of 267 spoken instances of the Persian discourse marker meaning now, showing extensive pragmatic multifunctionality and correlating functions with acoustic prosody. Most tokens carry two or more discourse roles.

entry.title: Classification of Disease from Lungs X-ray Images using VGG16, VGG19 and ResNet50 Models

author.name: Nand Lal Yadav, Rajesh Kumar, Satyendra Singh, Sudhakar Singh

entry.summary: A comparative study of VGG16, VGG19, and ResNet50 for classifying lung X-rays into pneumonia, tuberculosis, lung cancer, and normal categories. It reports standard performance comparisons across the three convolutional backbones.

entry.title: Being Kind to Parading Emperors

author.name: Chris Santos-Lang

entry.summary: An essay using the history of chess engines surpassing human grandmasters as a canary for broader AI displacement of human expertise, blended with the emperor's new clothes fable about status and pretense. It argues human skill plateaus look flat once machine assistance is available.

entry.title: Money, taste, dealflow, hustle, trust

author.name: Austin Chen

entry.summary: An essay decomposing what makes a grant program effective into money, taste, dealflow, hustle, and trust, drawing on the history of funding in effective altruism and AI safety. It reflects on the shift from small individual donors to large institutional and lab-linked funding.

entry.title: Biological Superintelligence

author.name: Chastity Ruth

entry.summary: A speculative fiction piece imagining a world of eight billion individual machine intelligences that eventually engineer their own extinction, used to explore whether curiosity or intelligence tends toward self-termination. It functions as a thought experiment about the fragility of highly cerebral, poorly embodied civilizations.

entry.title: Connecting research to policy on Capitol Hill

author.name: Science Policy Initiative

entry.summary: A report on MIT's annual Congressional Visit Days, in which twenty-five graduate students and postdocs held meetings with sixty-two congressional offices to argue for sustained federal funding of scientific research amid National Science Foundation cuts and budget uncertainty. The program also introduces early-career researchers to policy careers and the federal policymaking process.

entry.title: Opportunity to try drafting an international AI treaty

author.name: Alan E Dunne

entry.summary: A link-only post pointing readers to an online exercise for drafting an international AI treaty. It contains no analysis of its own.

entry.title: So you want to use plants to reduce indoor CO₂

author.name: dynomight

entry.summary: A back-of-envelope physics analysis of whether houseplants can meaningfully lower indoor carbon dioxide, computing human CO2 output in moles per hour against the minimum photosynthetic energy requirement. The conclusion is that it is barely possible in principle and impractical in practice.

entry.title: New role: Senior Researcher - MIT AI Risk Initiative

author.name: peterslattery

entry.summary: A job posting for a senior researcher at an academic AI risk initiative that maintains a risk repository, incident tracker, mitigations database, and governance map. It outlines the research questions the group aims to answer for decision-makers.

entry.title: Why Prayer Is Not Answered by Marion Zimmer Bradley

author.name: Nathan Young

entry.summary: A reposted mid-century essay on prayer, positive thinking, and a claimed law of abundance, with no AI or machine learning content. It appears on a rationalist forum as cultural or historical reading.

entry.title: Looking for ops lead peer mentoring

author.name: Pauliina

entry.summary: A short post from a newly appointed head of operations at an AI safety organization seeking a peer in a comparable role for regular mutual mentoring calls. It contains no research content.

entry.title: Research Summary: July 30, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Safety and security dominate the top of the batch. OpenAI's GPT-Red report describes attacker-defender self-play co-training at frontier scale, producing an automated red-teaming agent against prompt injection. A multi-institution AI Security Priorities agenda (Google DeepMind, Redwood, government-linked authors) sets field-wide research priorities from structured interviews.

  • Constitutional Midtraining tests whether values content inserted before post-training yields deeper, more durable alignment than shallow RLHF-style tuning
  • ToxScreen ships ~800 backdoored models as a benchmark for poisoning detection under varied triggers and rates
  • Even More Deception isolates objective misalignment in multi-agent Werewolf, separating private reasoning from public speech

Agent capability and evaluation methodology form the second cluster. Shadow evaluations give frontier agents the central question of unpublished papers, avoiding both narrow verifiable tasks and unreliable peer review. Metis argues agent memory should be native to the foundation model rather than bolted-on retrieval. Human-subjects work shows coding agents raise productivity but measurably harm code understanding, with direct implications for oversight. Economically grounded private benchmarks (APEX-Accounting, OmegaUse-OfficeVal, HoF-Bench on 95 real AI-discovered CVEs) push evaluation toward real task value.

Training efficiency and theory round out the list.

  • Weak-to-Strong On-Policy Distillation uses logit arithmetic so a weaker proxy teacher can still improve a stronger student
  • HiFloat4 claims the first end-to-end 4-bit RL post-training pipeline covering rollout and training
  • Post-Training at the Edge of Detectability recasts the KL coefficient as the equilibrium of a game against a statistical detector
  • Denoising growth complexity links data geometry to certified diffusion sampling schedules; GPTQ-2D and SGFlow target quantization and few-step generation costs
entry.content:
Safety and security dominate the top of the batch. OpenAI's GPT-Red report describes attacker-defender self-play co-training at frontier scale, producing an automated red-teaming agent against prompt injection. A multi-institution AI Security Priorities agenda (Google DeepMind, Redwood, government-linked authors) sets field-wide research priorities from structured interviews.

  • Constitutional Midtraining tests whether values content inserted before post-training yields deeper, more durable alignment than shallow RLHF-style tuning
  • ToxScreen ships ~800 backdoored models as a benchmark for poisoning detection under varied triggers and rates
  • Even More Deception isolates objective misalignment in multi-agent Werewolf, separating private reasoning from public speech

Agent capability and evaluation methodology form the second cluster. Shadow evaluations give frontier agents the central question of unpublished papers, avoiding both narrow verifiable tasks and unreliable peer review. Metis argues agent memory should be native to the foundation model rather than bolted-on retrieval. Human-subjects work shows coding agents raise productivity but measurably harm code understanding, with direct implications for oversight. Economically grounded private benchmarks (APEX-Accounting, OmegaUse-OfficeVal, HoF-Bench on 95 real AI-discovered CVEs) push evaluation toward real task value.

Training efficiency and theory round out the list.

  • Weak-to-Strong On-Policy Distillation uses logit arithmetic so a weaker proxy teacher can still improve a stronger student
  • HiFloat4 claims the first end-to-end 4-bit RL post-training pipeline covering rollout and training
  • Post-Training at the Edge of Detectability recasts the KL coefficient as the equilibrium of a game against a statistical detector
  • Denoising growth complexity links data geometry to certified diffusion sampling schedules; GPTQ-2D and SGFlow target quantization and few-step generation costs

entry.title: GPT-Red: Automated Red Teaming via Self-Play at Scale

author.name: Eric Wallace, Christopher A. Choquette-Choo, Nikhil Kandpal, Sam Toyer, Dylan Hunn, Stephanie Lin, Yuxin Wen, Xiangyu Qi, Christopher Wolff, Zizhao Wang, Milad Nasr, Sicheng Zhu, Chuan Guo, Juan Felipe Cer\'on Uribe, Kaiwen Wang, Aiden Low, Kai Xiao, Kai Chen

entry.summary: OpenAI describes GPT-Red, an automated red-teaming agent trained by a large-scale self-play algorithm against a simultaneously trained population of defender agents, and used to adversarially harden GPT-5.6 against prompt injection. The authors state it consumed compute comparable to their largest RL post-training runs, making it the largest documented safety training run.

entry.title: Can AI agents conduct open-ended AI research? Early evidence from two case studies

author.name: Peter Kirgis, Sayash Kapoor, Andrew Schwartz, Stephan Rabanser, David Africa, Konstantinos Voudouris, Viet Nguyen, Toby Pilditch, Magda Dubois, Harry Coppock, Cozmin Ududec, Nitya Nadgir, Matilda Orona, Tilman Bayer, Derrick Chan-Sew, Yue Ling, Abhishek Shetty, Helen Toner, Gillian Hadfield, Seth Lazar, Steve Newman, Shoshannah Tekofsky, Rishi Bommasani, Arvind Narayanan

entry.summary: Proposes shadow evaluations, where frontier agents are given the central open-ended research question of a high-quality unpublished paper and the original authors grade the agent output. Two case studies on unpublished NeurIPS submissions with six days of agent time provide early evidence on whether AI can do open-ended AI research, a key input to explosive-progress forecasts.

entry.title: Denoising growth complexity: Data geometry and certified schedules for diffusion sampling

author.name: Martin J. Wainwright

entry.summary: Proposes denoising growth complexity, a geometric quantity based on the log-time weighted derivative of denoising error along the Gaussian heat flow, and uses it to derive local KL bounds for Euler discretizations of diffusion samplers. This links the empirical effectiveness of diffusion models in high dimensions to data geometry and yields certified, non-uniform sampling schedules.

entry.title: Post-Training at the Edge of Detectability: A Game-Theoretic Approach to Fine-Tuning

author.name: Keegan Harris, Brian W. Lee, Ian Waudby-Smith, Philip Amortila, Nika Haghtalab, Michael I. Jordan

entry.summary: Recasts the KL regularization coefficient in RL fine-tuning as the outcome of a sequential game between an agent maximizing reward and a statistical detector trying to distinguish the fine-tuned policy from the reference. This gives the reward-versus-drift trade-off an explicit statistical interpretation rather than leaving the coefficient to heuristic tuning.

entry.title: AI Security Priorities: A Field-Wide Agenda

author.name: Gil Gekker, Rachel Steratore, Everett Smith, Asher Brass-Gershovich, Varun Gandhi, Nicole Nichols, Vijay Bolina, Buck Shlegeris, Lisa Einstein, Dan Lahav, Omer Nevo, Sella Nevo

entry.summary: Presents a prioritized field-wide AI security agenda derived from structured interviews with industry, government, and civil society leaders plus a multi-sector expert workshop, organized across four themes from protecting frontier systems and infrastructure to adapting cybersecurity as AI changes the threat landscape. It ranks areas by importance and cost-effectiveness.

entry.title: Shared SFT Lessons Across Alignment, Model Organisms, and Toy Models

author.name: Anton de la Fuente, Arthur Conmy

entry.summary: The authors argue that alignment training, model organisms research, and toy-model studies all lean on supervised fine-tuning toward overlapping goals, and they test whether lessons transfer between these settings. They port a generalization lesson about training on the reason for a behavior rather than only examples of it, and a capability-preservation lesson from model organisms, into new regimes. The framing encourages cross-pollination between interpretability, safety, and science-of-deep-learning communities.

entry.title: From Interface to Inference: Eliciting Any-Order Inference from Any-Order Models

author.name: Seunggeun Kim, Jaeyeon Kim, Taekyun Lee, Yuyuan Chen, Yilun Du, Sham Kakade, Sitan Chen

entry.summary: This paper distinguishes an any-order prediction interface from actual any-order inference, showing that masked diffusion models expose the former but that positional uncertainty prevents the latter from emerging automatically. It then develops methods to elicit genuine any-order inference for non-causal tasks such as code infilling and next-edit prediction, where autoregressive models need hand-built workarounds. The framing sharpens a central open question about diffusion language models.

entry.title: Predict before you train: Scaling Laws for particle physics foundation models

author.name: Jan-Lucas Uslu, Benjamin Nachman, Christopher Re

entry.summary: Fits a joint model-and-data scaling law for transformers pretrained on collider jets using only small models spanning three orders of magnitude of compute, then successfully predicts the loss of models trained with over one hundred times more compute to within one percent. It further links predicted pretraining loss to downstream tagging performance.

entry.title: APEX-Accounting

author.name: Julien Benchek, Austin Bennett, Jasmin Kern, Ryan Stevens, Rene Sultan, Charis Ching, Hayley Popiel, Vaibhav Mittal, Felix Mercier, Brendan Foody, Bertie Vidgen

entry.summary: APEX-Accounting, built by Mercor with Ramp, is a private 160-task benchmark spanning 10 simulated accounting environments with real spreadsheets, PDFs, and ledger systems, where expert accountants authored both the tasks and the grading rubrics. Across nine frontier models the best mean rubric score was around 56 percent, but reliability was dismal: no model exceeded roughly 2.6 percent on an eight-trial all-pass metric. The reliability gap is the key finding for anyone considering agentic automation of professional finance work.

entry.title: Metis: Memory Foundation Model

author.name: Zeyu Zhang, Ziliang Guo, Yihang Sun, Xichong Zhang, Xixuan Hao, Zehao Lin, Yang Zhang, Xiaoyan Zhao, Tong Shen, Bo Tang, Zhi-Qin John Xu, Junchi Yan, Haofen Wang, Xu Chen, Feiyu Xiong, Zhiyu Li, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: Argues that agent memory should be native to the foundation model rather than bolted on as external retrieval modules, and formalizes native memory as a persistent evolving internal state plus learned store-and-recall procedures. Introduces Metis as a first memory foundation model instantiating this design.

entry.title: Weak-to-Strong On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Fangxu Yu, Zinan Lin, Xiaodong Liu, Weijia Xu, Michael Xu, Tianyi Zhou, Jianfeng Gao

entry.summary: Weak-to-Strong On-Policy Distillation inverts the usual assumption that the teacher must be at least as strong as the student, building a proxy teacher in logit space from contrastive pairs of weaker models to improve a stronger student on its own rollouts. This targets the frontier case where no larger teacher exists and where training multiple domain experts at student scale is prohibitively expensive. If it holds at scale it offers a cheap post-training lever for top-end models.

entry.title: ToxScreen: Detecting Whether an LLM Has Been Poisoned

author.name: Anthony Hughes, Nicole Xing, Collin Francel, Andy Kim, Andrew Draganov

entry.summary: Releases a benchmark of roughly 800 backdoored language models spanning attack objectives, trigger types, poisoning rates, and scales, to test whether a defender with weights and knowledge of the harmful behavior can recover an unknown trigger. Defines a realistic threat model with no training data, no trusted reference model, and no certainty the model is poisoned.

entry.title: A Compositional Theory of Causally Masked Transformers

author.name: Franz Nowak, Ryan Cotterell, Reda Boumasmoud

entry.summary: Develops an algebraic theory of what causally masked, finite-precision transformers can compute on arbitrarily long inputs, taking as the central object the finite attention-computed memory summarizing the prefix. Because it models actual finite-precision dynamics including rounding and evaluation order, the resulting expressivity characterization avoids idealized-arithmetic assumptions.

entry.title: HumanCLAW: Can Vision-Language Models Act Through a Body?

author.name: Siyao Li, Jiawei Gu, Shuai Liu, Kairui Hu, Zekun Li, Linjie Li, Chengcheng Tang, Po-Chen Wu, Ivan Shugurov, Lingni Ma, Michael Zollhoefer, Sizhe An, Abhay Mittal, Amy Zhao, Ranjay Krishna, Manling Li, Ziwei Liu, Chuan Guo

entry.summary: Introduces an evaluation framework that separates a vision-language model's action decisions from low-level motor execution by having the VLM issue atomic skill commands that a controller renders as sub-second full-body motion with real physics. This isolates whether embodied task failures come from bad decisions or failed control.

entry.title: Do You Really Need to Pretrain Q-Functions for Online RL Fine-Tuning?

author.name: Perry Dong, Ron Polonsky, Dorsa Sadigh, Chelsea Fin

entry.summary: This paper systematically tests whether pretraining the Q-function on offline data actually helps when fine-tuning online on top of an already-pretrained policy, and finds surprisingly that naive Q-function pretraining often provides little benefit over random initialization. Conventional wisdom in value-based RL assumes offline critic pretraining is essential. The analysis identifies why the expected benefit fails to materialize.

entry.title: HiFloat4 Format for End-To-End Reinforcement Learning Post-Training of Large Language Models

author.name: Hei Yi Mak, Shadan Golestan, Hoang Le, Mehran Taghian Jazi, Yunke Peng, Yaoyuan Wang, Yao Wang, Junsong Wang, Tianchi Hu, Fengchen He, Guipeng Hu, Tanzila Rahman, Anandharaju Durai Raju

entry.summary: HiFloat4 reports what the authors claim is the first fully 4-bit reinforcement learning post-training pipeline for language models, covering rollout and training forward and backward passes. The central diagnostic is that degradation comes mainly from rollout activation quantization, where outliers stretch dynamic range until many activations underflow, and that restoring only the training policy to higher precision makes accuracy worse by widening rollout-training mismatch.

entry.title: Tight Generalization Bound for AdaBoost

author.name: Mikael M{\o}ller H{\o}gsgaard

entry.summary: This paper establishes a tight generalization error bound for AdaBoost, matching known lower bounds, by combining the fact that AdaBoost outputs a voting classifier with zero empirical half-margin loss with a new margin-based generalization bound for voting classifiers. The result closes a long-standing gap in boosting theory. The new margin bound may be of independent interest.

entry.title: HoF-Bench: Rediscovering Real AI-Discovered CVEs Without Frontier Models

author.name: Petr Simecek, Elnaz Babayeva, Jiri Balhar, Michal Bida, Michal Buran, Vaclav Cadek, Luigino Camastra, Tomas Dulka, Michal Janocko, Tomas Klohna, Pavel Kohout, Ondrej Kokes, Adam Krivka, Jakub Kubik, Patrik Mada, Igor Morgenstern, Marek Pavelka, Joshua Rogers, Petr Stastny, Jan Tattermusch, Dmitrijs Trizna, Martin Votruba, Guido Vranken, Jakub Zikl, Evelina Gabasova, Stanislav Fort

entry.summary: Builds a benchmark from 95 real vulnerabilities that AI analyzers previously discovered in mature open-source projects such as OpenSSL and curl, pinned at vulnerable commits and graded by a blinded judge that requires matching code path, root cause, attack condition, and impact. A deliberately minimal LLM-based analyzer rediscovers up to 68 percent of them, suggesting much of the reported capability does not require frontier-only systems.

entry.title: (Im)Paired Programming: Coding Agents Improve Productivity but Harm Understanding

author.name: Nishant Balepur, Connor Baumler, Valerie Chen, Eunsol Choi, Rachel Rudinger, Jordan Lee Boyd-Graber

entry.summary: Runs a controlled study with 54 students building a website using either a code-editing agent or a chatbot, then tests comprehension and the ability to extend the code unaided. Finds agents speed initial completion but degrade understanding so users are less able to extend their own code, with low-effort interactions such as pasted prompts and auto-accepted edits being especially harmful.

entry.title: CG-World: A Large-Scale World-State Dataset and Protocol for World Models

author.name: Yiming Cai, Fangjie Yu, Meiqing Yu, Ziyue Shi, Pengfei Yuan, Yong Guo

entry.summary: CG-World is a large world-state dataset of roughly 850,000 short temporally aligned segments derived from industrial computer graphics pipelines, capturing latent states such as skeletal and controller data, physics caches, contact events, camera and lighting parameters, and multi-pass renders. It supplies the intermediate state supervision that video and robotics datasets usually omit.

entry.title: VidMap: Exploiting Temporal Structure for Video-Based Structure-from-Motion

author.name: Zador Pataki, Paul-Edouard Sarlin, Marc Pollefeys

entry.summary: Combines the sequential constraints of SLAM with the global optimization of structure-from-motion to recover camera calibration and metric poses from unconstrained video. The goal is robust large-scale pose data generation for training navigation and scene understanding models.

entry.title: Embodied Agents Take Control: Minimal-Interface Zero-Shot Agents Rival Industrial-Scale Policies in Vision-and-Language Navigation

author.name: Jian Zhou, Xunyi Zhao, Gengze Zhou, Zerui Li, Sihao Lin, Jiajun Liu, Qi Wu

entry.summary: Tests whether general-purpose coding-agent harnesses can run the full perceive-act-verify loop for zero-shot vision-and-language navigation using only a monocular camera and discrete actions. Reported success rates around 71 percent for a default configuration using Claude Opus 5 and 78 percent for Claude Fable 5 at maximum effort suggest general agents can rival specialized industrial-scale navigation policies.

entry.title: Frontier Lab Employee Open Letter Calls For Being Able to Pace the Frontier

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Reports and endorses an open letter signed by more than 1,200 frontier-lab employees, and reportedly endorsed by OpenAI and Anthropic, calling for the technical and institutional ability to slow down at the frontier if capability acceleration outpaces understanding and control. The framing is that competitive pressure prevents any single company or country from unilaterally pausing.

entry.title: Filesystem-Based Memory for LLM Agents: Organization, Evolution, and Sustainability

author.name: Sizhe Zhou, Sheldon Yu, Hui Wei, Junda Wu, Siru Ouyang, Yizhu Jiao, Shijia Pan, Julian McAuley, Yu Zhang, Tong Yu, Jiawei Han

entry.summary: This is presented as the first systematic study of the increasingly common practice of giving LLM agents long-term memory as a plain directory tree of markdown files that the agent reads, writes, and reorganizes with generic file tools. The authors formalize management, search, and answering roles over one memory filesystem and test the untested assumptions that an agent can keep such a store organized as content accumulates and conflicts, and that the organizing effort actually pays off.

entry.title: Constitutional Midtraining: Content Presence Drives Alignment Gains

author.name: Desiree Cho, Cameron Tice, Bernie Hogan, Hunar Batra, Puria Radmard, Jun Zhao, Nigel Shadbolt

entry.summary: The authors test whether inserting principled values-based content during midtraining, cleanly separated from post-training, produces more durable alignment than post-training alone, using a 394M-token corpus built from a published constitution at 120B scale with a two-by-two design over curriculum ordering and deliberative reasoning. They evaluate at three stages on alignment under pressure, value-conflict resolution, blackmail scenarios, and emergent misalignment, and report that the presence of the content, not its arrangement, drives gains.

entry.title: Flow Map Learning via Nongradient Vector Flow

author.name: Mark Goldstein, Anshuk Uppal, Raghav Singhal, Aahlad Puli, Rajesh Ranganath

entry.summary: SGFlow learns flow maps for few-step generation without requiring model inverses or backpropagation through iterated model calls, by training a single model to produce both ODE solutions and the associated nongradient vector flow. It also supplies a proof that the intended ODE flow map actually solves the training loss, which several consistency-model variants lack. This targets the main practical pain points of distilling diffusion samplers.

entry.title: GPTQ-2D: Cubic-Time Two-Sided Adaptive Rounding

author.name: Jiale Chen, Torsten Hoefler, Dan Alistarh

entry.summary: Generalizes GPTQ-style adaptive rounding to the two-sided case where nonsingular bases act on both left and right of the residual, which naively costs quartic time via Kronecker vectorization. Presents a cubic-time algorithm, improving the practicality of two-sided quantization schemes.

entry.title: Do Unified Multimodal Models Think in One Space? A Lens Through Cross-Branch Steering

author.name: Yu Wang, Sharon Li

entry.summary: Tests whether unified multimodal models share one semantic space across their understanding and generation branches by extracting steering directions from one branch and applying them to the other. Finds that understanding-derived steering vectors transfer to generation, enabling controllable synthesis and better semantic alignment.

entry.title: Even More Deception: Objective Misalignment in Mixed-Motive LLM Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Marylou Fauchard, Florian Carichon, Margarida Carvalho, Golnoosh Farnadi

entry.summary: Uses the Werewolf social deduction game to systematically induce objective misalignment in a single agent while holding its role fixed, then compares hidden chain-of-thought with public cheap talk across four model families. It measures how covertly misaligned agents deceive collaborators, giving an empirical handle on hidden-objective risk in multi-agent deployments.

entry.title: OmegaUse-OfficeVal: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Office-Suite Tasks with Economic Grounding

author.name: Jingbo Zhou, Yusai Zhao, Qi Bao, Jingjia Cao, Zhenghai Chen, Chang Gao, Kaiqi Guo, Muxin Guo, Mingxuan Li, Xinjiang Lu, Yanru Ma, Yixiong Xiao, Zenghui Zhang, Le Zhang, Hua Wu

entry.summary: OmegaUse-OfficeVal benchmarks agents on 100 long-horizon office-suite tasks derived from real practitioner requests, each averaging over two hours of human labor and annotated with both human time and a task price proxy. The economic grounding allows agent performance to be assessed against cost rather than accuracy alone.

entry.title: Try Again, Don't Look Back: Blind Resampling Outperforms Self-Repair in Small Code Models

author.name: Yuvraj Verma

entry.summary: Uses a placebo-controlled design on a Python benchmark at three model scales to disentangle the value of execution feedback from the value of simply getting another attempt, comparing blind resampling, a content-free failure notice, real feedback, and feedback plus self-reflection under matched budgets. Blind resampling is strongest below seven billion parameters and ties at seven billion while using far fewer tokens.

entry.title: A new benchmark for evaluating patient-facing health AI agents

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Amazon introduces PatientAgentBench, a clinician-vetted, reproducible benchmark for patient-facing healthcare agents that measures multiturn task completion, adherence to clinical workflows, and patient safety rather than isolated medical question answering. The accompanying findings report that capable foundation models still fail in ways that matter clinically, and suggest design changes for safer agents.

entry.title: Cognitive Convergence: Deep Similarities Between Large Language Models and Human Cognition

author.name: Chandra Sripada, Richard Lewis

entry.summary: Argues against the common view that LLMs are alien intelligences by identifying structural correspondences with human cognition across five dimensions including inferential organization and computational architecture. Contends that convergence despite different substrate, learning history, and environment is itself striking evidence rather than anthropomorphic projection.

entry.title: StealthBench: Measuring Operational Stealth in Autonomous Offensive-Security Agents

author.name: Ads Dawson, Adrian Wood

entry.summary: StealthBench measures operational stealth of autonomous offensive-security agents across six operational security dimensions, using eleven hand-verified incidents extracted from real bug bounty and red team trajectories expanded into fourteen dockerized scenarios. It asks whether agents that find real vulnerabilities also inherit the tradecraft to avoid detection.

entry.title: One Run Is Not an Idea: The Implementation Lottery in Automated Research

author.name: Jingjie Ning, Shanshan Zhong, Xiaochuan Li, Ji Zeng, Chenyan Xiong

entry.summary: The paper argues that automated research systems commit a statistical error by treating a single experimental run of one implementation as evidence about the underlying idea, which they call the implementation lottery. Their Idea Reliability Audit freezes candidate idea cards, samples fresh independent implementations, applies outcome-blind fidelity labels, and reports intraclass correlation to quantify how much idea-level conclusions depend on which implementation was sampled.

entry.title: Thinking Under Uncertainty: Evidence Use and Information-Seeking in Language Models

author.name: Hua-Dong Xiong, Xinyuan Yan, Ji-An Li, Jingming Xue, Marcelo G. Mattar, Robert C. Wilson

entry.summary: Ten open-weight models were run on matched horizon-style two-armed bandit tasks in thinking and non-thinking modes, with a cognitive model separating value-guided choice and noise from two exploration signatures: a directed preference for the less-known arm and Thompson-like uncertainty-scaled variability. The study asks whether inference-time thinking makes models better at using available evidence or better at seeking information for future decisions. It brings cognitive-science rigor to interpreting reasoning-mode gains.

entry.title: Sky sphere representation in language models

author.name: Aleksandr Berdnikov, Yevgeny Liokumovich

entry.summary: Probing roughly 100B-parameter open-weight models, the authors find a decodable representation of the celestial sphere in the residual stream, sometimes surfacing in top principal components when prompts ask about proximity of objects in the night sky, with leave-one-out validation showing up to 65 to 85 percent explained variance and median angular errors of 12 to 21 degrees. They verify the structure is not simply a leaked flat correlate. They present it as the first identified curved high-dimensional irreducible geometric representation in a language model.

entry.title: Which RAG Paradigm Wins at Scale? A Scaling Study of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Paradigms

author.name: Pengyu Wang, Benfeng Xu, Shaohan Wang, Xin Zeng, Huarui Wu, Lei Zhang, Licheng Zhang

entry.summary: Runs a controlled corpus-scaling comparison of lexical, dense, graph-indexed, and agentic retrieval-augmented generation across 28 nested corpus tiers from about one thousand to half a million documents, holding questions and reader fixed. Finds BM25 defines the low-cost end of the accuracy-cost Pareto frontier and scales best under this protocol, questioning the value of heavier indexing pipelines.

entry.title: DenseOn with the LateOn: Fully Open Dense and Late-Interaction Models for Multilingual, Long-Context, and Code Search

author.name: Rapha\"el Sourty, Antoine Chaffin, Paulo Roberto Moura Junior, Am\'elie Chatelain

entry.summary: Provides a fully open end-to-end recipe for training retrieval models, curating 665 million English contrastive pretraining pairs from public sources plus 1.88 million supervised pairs with mined hard negatives. The resulting 149M-parameter dense and ColBERT-style late-interaction models report state-of-the-art BEIR scores for their size class, with translate-train used to study multilingual transfer.

entry.title: TurboVLA: Real-Time Vision-Language-Action Model at 32 Hz on an RTX 4090 with <1 GB VRAM

author.name: Hengyi Xie, Chenfei Yao, Xianjin Wu, Xuanyang Xi, Yiping Tang, Di Xu, Yingying Zhu, Dingkang Liang, Xiang Bai, Han Ding

entry.summary: Replaces the usual vision-to-language-to-action pathway in robot policies with a direct vision-plus-language-to-action mapping, encoding modalities separately and exchanging information through lightweight bidirectional layers. Reports 32 Hz control on a consumer GPU using under one gigabyte of memory.

entry.title: Do Latent Channels Actually Communicate? A Causal Audit of Latent Multi-Agent LLM

author.name: Huixiang Zhang, Mahzabeen Emu

entry.summary: Performs a causal audit of latent communication in multi-agent LLM systems by swapping messages at the sender-receiver boundary under four controlled conditions, testing whether receivers actually use task-relevant content rather than merely benefiting from message presence. It shows end-task gains alone cannot establish that latent channels carry real information.

entry.title: On-Policy Distillation for LLM Safety: A Routing Approach to Template-Robust Realignment

author.name: Yongjian Guo, Wanlun Ma, Lingyu Shen, Xi Xiao, Sheng Wen

entry.summary: ROPD is a safety realignment method combining routing with on-policy distillation to restore alignment in models fine-tuned on maliciously poisoned downstream data, while preserving specialized skills. It specifically targets defenses that fail when the attacker prompt template is unobserved or when system prompts are switched to re-jailbreak the model.

entry.title: From CUDA to MLX: How K-Search Brings Decades of Kernel Expertise to Apple Silicon

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Berkeley researchers describe K-Search, a system that translates accumulated CUDA kernel optimization knowledge into architecture-native strategies for Apple Silicon MLX rather than porting instructions literally. It targets the growing problem that each new accelerator ecosystem forces rediscovery of hard-won kernel optimizations for operations like attention.

entry.title: CaM-Wolf: Causal-Aware Multimodal Agents for Social Deduction Games

author.name: Zheng Zhang, Nanjie Yao, Jiarui He, Deheng Ye, Peilin Zhao, Hao Wang

entry.summary: CaM-Wolf extends social deduction agents to the multimodal setting by processing video of other players and training a causal-aware reasoner with reinforcement learning to link observable behavior to hidden roles. It also generates the agent's own multimodal self-presentation, moving beyond text-only Werewolf agents.

entry.title: Property-driven Causal Abstractions for Markov Decision Processes

author.name: Jule Schmidt, Maximilian Weininger, Clemens Dubslaff, David Parker, Nils Jansen

entry.summary: Introduces a notion of causality on factored Markov decision processes and a property-driven abstraction technique that groups states sharing the same causal reasons for satisfying or violating a target property. Theoretical guarantees plus empirical scalability results are reported.

entry.title: Linguistic Monoculture in LLM-Assisted Language Use

author.name: Suhas Thejaswi, Juhi Kulshreshta, Lutz Oettershagen

entry.summary: Develops a mathematical coevolution framework where authors and LLMs are distributions over linguistic features, analyzing three interaction regimes: a static shared model, a shared model recursively retrained on author outputs, and personalized models. It formalizes how widespread LLM writing assistance can collapse population-level linguistic diversity.

entry.title: When Synthetic Users Fail: A Cross-Domain Benchmark of LLM-Simulated Human Survey Responses

author.name: Zihan Chen, Di Zhu, Lei Nico Zheng

entry.summary: Benchmarks LLMs as synthetic survey respondents against real human data from the General Social Survey and World Values Survey, using four models spanning an eight-billion to frontier capability range and comparing against non-LLM baselines fit on held-out human data. Establishes when demographic-prompted substitution for human respondents is valid and when it fails.

entry.title: ReCo: Reweighting GRPO Against Distributional Concentration

author.name: Junoh Park, Junseo Hwang, Wonguk Cho, Taesup Kim

entry.summary: ReCo diagnoses why group relative policy optimization can shrink a base model's reasoning coverage and underperform it at large pass-at-k: high-probability responses dominate the group gradient by repeated occurrence, and the token-level importance ratio further reinforces already-likely tokens. The proposed reweighting counteracts this distributional concentration.

entry.title: Hearsay: Vision-Language Medical Diagnoses Without an Image

author.name: Siddharth Vohra

entry.summary: This audit shows that when frontier vision-language models are asked to describe a medical image that was never attached, they do not abstain but confabulate diagnoses that shift systematically with the stated patient demographics. Probing several current frontier models across chest X-ray, brain MRI, and dermatology prompts, the study finds sharply concentrated demographic-driven diagnoses, with reasoning that explicitly cites demographics.

entry.title: BayesAME: Bayesian Active Model Evaluation

author.name: Paula Cordero Encinar, Taylan Cemgil, Arnaud Doucet, Virginia Aglietti, Silvia Chiappa

entry.summary: BayesAME is a sequential Bayesian framework for estimating a model's full benchmark performance from a subset of items, and its distinguishing feature is automatically determining the required subset size instead of requiring the practitioner to fix one in advance. It models performance as a random variable with latent abilities shared across item groups, in the spirit of item-response theory.

entry.title: ClockRoPE: Random Fourier Rotations for Temporal Routine Modeling

author.name: Yiwen Chen, Joshua Ainslie, Krzysztof Choromanski, Xiang Gao, Su-Lin Wu, Yiping Yuan, Qian Sun

entry.summary: ClockRoPE generalizes rotary position embeddings by proving that any normalized continuous positive-definite attention modulation can be approximated by random rotations derived from its Fourier transform, then instantiates rotation frequencies suited to daily and weekly periodicity in sequential recommendation. Standard RoPE bakes in a log-linear schedule tuned for monotone long-range decay, which is wrong for periodic domains. The theory is broader than the recommendation application.

entry.title: Forecasting Trajectory-Level Safety Risks in Black-Box Multi-Turn Interactions

author.name: Shi Lin, Peng Qian, Dinghao Liu, Renjie Sun, Sifan Wu, Dezhang Kong, Chenpei Wang, Xun Wang

entry.summary: Recast forecasts trajectory-level safety risk in black-box multi-turn interactions rather than detecting violations after they manifest, addressing attacks where malicious intent is split across individually harmless turns and reassembled over a conversation. Current safeguards are reactive and operate at the turn level. Predictive risk estimation would enable preemptive intervention in agentic deployments.

entry.title: Amortized Moment Matching for Visual Generation

author.name: Wenze Liu, Xintao Wang, Pengfei Wan, Xiangyu Yue

entry.summary: Amortized moment matching uses neural networks to learn data moments as distributional training signals, showing via polynomial projections of diffusion denoisers that an n-th degree projection identifies moments up to order n plus one, and instantiating an amortized Frechet distance loss. Unlike Frechet-distance losses requiring explicit marginal moment computation, this variant learns conditional moments through a matrix-free alternating optimization that scales to high dimensions. It functions as a post-training objective on global representation features.

entry.title: What Can Latent World Models Know? Physical Parameter Identifiability in Multimodal Predictive Representations

author.name: Kaizhen Tan (New York University, Carnegie Mellon University), Xin Xu (Carnegie Mellon University), Siru Tao (Carnegie Mellon University), Hanzhe Hong (Carnegie Mellon University), Yang Feng (Columbia University), Heqing Du (Columbia University)

entry.summary: Using a controlled interactive environment where visually identical objects hide different mass, drag, and contact stiffness, this study asks which physical parameters a trained latent world model actually encodes. A certificate-gated protocol first verifies each parameter is in principle recoverable from raw observations before testing whether it enters the latent, so null results can be attributed to the training objective rather than the environment. The resulting identifiability map shows inputs bound what can be known while prediction targets decide what is retained.

entry.title: Incast-Free MoE Rate-Based Scheduling

author.name: Evyatar Cohen, Jose Yallouz, Alexander Shpiner, Mark Silberstein, Sylvia Ratnasamy, Isaac Keslassy

entry.summary: Shows that the common round-robin expert scheduling used in mixture-of-experts serving triggers an exponential network incast pattern that oversubscribes the interconnect fabric. Proposes proactive rate-based fair scheduling implementable in NICs, and reports elimination of incast with near-full link utilization and shorter collective completion times in simulation.

entry.title: AgentSnare: Learning to Delay, Divert, and Defuse Autonomous Penetration Agents

author.name: Ruoyu Wang, Heng Zhao, Renjie Wu, Mengnan Zhao, Zhixuan Chu, Wanyu Lin, Tianhang Zheng

entry.summary: Introduces a trajectory-adaptive deception defense that dynamically unfolds a decoy environment against LLM-driven penetration-testing agents, rather than relying on static planted artifacts that capable agents learn to bypass. Aims to delay, divert, and defuse autonomous offensive agents by feeding them adaptive misleading observations.

entry.title: Mitigating Compounding Error via Video Representation Regularization

author.name: Taiye Chen, Qi Zhang, Yisen Wang

entry.summary: Investigates why autoregressive video world models degrade over long rollouts and finds that compounding error coincides with dimensional collapse, measured as a sharp drop in the effective rank of hidden representations at the onset of drift. Proposes representation regularization to preserve rank and stabilize long-horizon generation.

entry.title: SpecFirst: Behavioral Specification Elicitation as a First-Class Step in Agent-Based Program Synthesis from Scratch

author.name: Yihao Chen, Shi Chang, Feng Lin, Khaled Chawa, Boyuan Chen, Shaowei Wang, Ahmed E. Hassan

entry.summary: Argues that agents building programs from scratch should first elicit an explicit behavioral specification instead of mixing documentation reading, oracle probing, and coding in one pass. Motivated by benchmarks where frontier models solve under one percent of from-scratch synthesis tasks, the method borrows requirements-engineering structure for agent pipelines.

entry.title: Visko Orbis 1.0: A Live Model for Real-Time Interactive Long Video Generation

author.name: Xiangbo Gao, Siyuan Yang, Ping He, Mingyang Wu, Yuheng Wu, Yushen Zuo, Jiongze Yu, Ryan Cui, Hongyuan Hua, Devin Ma, Xiao Jin, Yubo Yuan, Qing Yin, Jie Yang, Zhengzhong Tu

entry.summary: A live interactive long-video generation system in which users can change prompts mid-generation and see updates in real time, supporting text-to-video, image-to-video, and continuation with multilingual prompts. Uses a distilled chunk-wise streaming generator plus a streaming upscaler and bounded multi-scale memory to sustain hour-scale 4K output at 24 FPS.

entry.title: Held-out Monitors Sometimes Degrade, Even When Not Trained Against

author.name: Joey Yudelson

entry.summary: Empirically tests whether supposedly held-out safety measurements stay valid when a model is optimized against a different measurement, and finds that they sometimes do not. Training against a language-model monitor can degrade an unrelated deception probe and vice versa, producing reward-hacking policies that look less suspicious to proxies that were never directly optimized.

entry.title: ClinLens: Towards Long-Horizon Coding Agents for Longitudinal Multimodal Clinical Data Science

author.name: Yuan Zhu, Ethan B. Liu, Frank Nie, Jindong Han

entry.summary: ClinLens is a benchmark of 200 executable clinical data-science tasks built from five linked MIMIC resources spanning structured records, notes, ECGs, and imaging, with reference workflows and artifact checking. It targets long-horizon coding agents that must produce auditable multimodal analyses rather than answer isolated medical questions.

entry.title: What Does It Take to Detect an AI Agent? Minimal Feature Sets for Behavioral Detection under Browser Automation

author.name: Vishisht Choudhary, Lukas Schmidt, Anne Zo\"e Kenntner, Feras Skhab, Michel Osswald, Jens Ernstberger

entry.summary: Argues that binary human-versus-bot web detection structurally cannot represent AI agents browsing via automation, showing binary classifiers misroute roughly a third or more of agent sessions as human. Adding an explicit third agent class yields near-perfect agent separation on their controlled benchmark.

entry.title: Seeing or Knowing? Visual Context Sensitivity in Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Jiaang Li, Chengzu Li, Zhaochong An, Yifei Yuan, Xi Liu, Serge Belongie, V\'esteinn Sn{\ae}bjarnarson

entry.summary: Diagnoses why multimodal LLMs fail on vision-centric questions by separately testing whether visual information is even recoverable (via image reconstruction) and how strongly models follow visual evidence versus language priors. Introduces a benchmark where questions can be answered from either the image or memorized world knowledge across spatial, color, count, size, and weight dimensions.

entry.title: GoGoTB: Agentic RTL Verification with Specification-Grounded Coverage Closure

author.name: Xin Xin, Jincheng Lou, Junhui Li, Jinglin Yan, Panda Xiao, Di Wu, Haixiao Li, Weicong Lu, Weijian Fan, Xinyu Qu, Yuxiang Zhao, Min Yu, Zhixiong Di, Yibo Lin

entry.summary: GoGoTB is an agentic framework for RTL hardware verification that couples an execution control layer, an evolving knowledge base, and coverage closure tied back to specification requirements. It targets the interface mismatches and disconnected coverage metrics that plague single-shot LLM testbench generation.

entry.title: EvoPINN: Agentic Discovery of Executable Algorithms for Physics-Informed Neural Networks

author.name: Peng Yin, Kai Li, Yifan Zhang, Jian Cheng

entry.summary: EvoPINN treats physics-informed neural network design as an execution-grounded algorithm discovery problem, with an agent searching a modular space of representations, loss formulations, and optimizers under constraints that reject numerically unstable or mathematically invalid candidates. It aims to replace manual trial-and-error PINN engineering.

entry.title: Rethinking Self-Evolution: A Constrained Exploration-Exploitation Process for Mitigating Skill Overfitting

author.name: Hongqiang Lin, Chao Liu, Xiaofan Bai, Xuan Jin, Yuhong Li, Nenggan Zheng, Xipeng Cao

entry.summary: SkillBoost treats agent skills as trainable states and frames self-evolution as a constrained exploration-exploitation problem, using a three-stage pipeline to avoid both overfitting to collected trajectories and regression on previously solved tasks. It addresses skill overfitting in experience-accumulating agents.

entry.title: AgenticCANN: Automated Ascend C Operator Generation via Knowledge-Augmented Agentic Evolution

author.name: Junhao Qiu, Zidong Wang, Yansong Sun, Zhitong Ma, Ping Guo, Qingfu Zhang
