Aims to replace per-problem bespoke optimization with a single general design engine.

entry.title: Less Data, Better Alignment: Data-Centric Multi-Evaluator Agreement for Preference Optimization

author.name: Zhengtao Yao, Runhao Li, Xupeng Chen, Jiayi Cheng, Chenqian Le, Michael Yue, Siheng Wang, Haoyan Xu, Yuqi Li, Chenhao Wei, Zhengdao Li, Rongchao Zhang, Guang Yang, Yidong Wang, Junhao Dong

entry.summary: Argues that preference optimization research over-focuses on objectives while holding data fixed, and instead filters on-policy candidate responses down to a tiny high-consensus subset judged by rubric-specialized evaluators for helpfulness, factuality, and conciseness. Retaining under four percent of candidates yields strong MT-Bench and length-controlled win-rate results with a seven-billion-parameter base model.

entry.title: Calibrated Partial Resets: Preventing Policy Collapse in Continual Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Luc McCutcheon, Evangelos Chatzaroulas, Saber Fallah

entry.summary: Proposes an optimizer that periodically pulls low-utility neurons partway back toward their initialization, with pull strength scaled by neuron utility, to preserve plasticity in continual and reinforcement learning without the destabilization caused by hard resets. Targets dormant neurons and policy collapse.

entry.title: Sharpness-Aware Minimization and Muon: Robustness under the Spectral Norm

author.name: Wenzhi Zhong, Edward Milsom, Michael Murray

entry.summary: This work studies sharpness-aware minimization under matrix-aware geometry, introducing a layerwise spectral-norm inner perturbation for hidden weight matrices and pairing it with Muon-style spectral updates. It asks which perturbation geometry actually improves generalization, connecting SAM theory to the optimizer that has become popular for large-model training.

entry.title: SearchArt: Training Long-Horizon Search Agent with Scalable Synthetic and Verified Task

author.name: Lang Mei, Xiaohan Yu, Chong Chen, Liyan Liu, Xiangnan Chen, Jinchao Ma, Chao Feng, Li Huang, Siyu Mo, Sichen Kang, Yunkun Xu, Zhihan Yang, Zhujun Xue, Jingren Zhang, Qing He, Yingdi Huang, Hao Jiang, Ziao Ma, Zewei Pan, Minhao Sun, Zhuo Tao, Jinzhao Xiao, Gangtao Xin, Huanyao Zhang, Wenjian Zhang, Jiangshan Zhang, Guojie Zhu, Jiaxin Mao, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: SearchArt is a pipeline for training long-horizon search agents by synthesizing verifiable information-seeking tasks and trajectories from web documents, then applying multi-stage post-training that supervises and corrects intermediate reasoning and tool use. It tackles the scarcity of scalable long-horizon agentic training data.

entry.title: Lloyd's $K$-Means Clustering Algorithm Is Frank-Wolfe in Disguise

author.name: Michael Pokojovy, J. Marcus Jobe, Simon Lacoste-Julien

entry.summary: The authors show that Lloyd's classic k-means algorithm is a special case of the Frank-Wolfe method applied to a concave reformulation, then import Frank-Wolfe theory to obtain a non-asymptotic convergence rate to a local minimum and a variant handling empty clusters. It gives new theoretical grounding for a ubiquitous heuristic.

entry.title: Decision-Level Hijacking: Injecting Cognitive Bias into Large Language Models via Bit-Flip Attacks

author.name: Yu Yan, Jiahao Chen, Siqi Lu, Yongjuan Wang, Ziming Zhao, Zhaoxuan Li, Tianyu Du, Qingjun Yuan, Shouling Ji

entry.summary: This paper shows that hardware bit-flip attacks on model weights can steer an LLM's stance and decision framing (injecting cognitive bias) without producing overtly prohibited content or degrading general capability. The authors define this as decision-level hijacking of models used in high-stakes advisory settings.

entry.title: HiFi-UMI: Learning Deployable Manipulation Policies from High-Fidelity UMI Data Alone

author.name: Simple AI, :, Yuteng Wei, Jinming Ma, Jiawei Wang, Weitao Zhou, Yushen Zuo, Ke Rui, Minglei Li, Jinhao Zhang, Zhikang Pan, Xiang Wang, Haoran Jia, Huan Du, Zicheng Zeng, Jun Ma, Guiyu Qin, Di Zhang, Xiaofei Li

entry.summary: HiFi-UMI argues that improving the fidelity of robot-free handheld data capture, rather than adding real-robot fine-tuning data, can suffice to train deployable manipulation policies. The system co-designs stereo-inertial SLAM tracking, native relative gripper pose, microsecond synchronization and matched field of view.

entry.title: Bias-corrected Cox regression with AI-extracted covariates via calibration summary statistics

author.name: Arjun Sondhi

entry.summary: Develops a bias-correction method for Cox proportional hazards models when covariates come from AI extraction pipelines that make errors, using only the summary calibration statistics a data vendor typically shares. The bias decomposes into a leading calibration term that can be corrected and a vanishing second-order residual.

entry.title: GLIDE: Guided Layerwise Hybrid Attention for Efficient LLM Inference

author.name: Vimal William, Ravi Tandon, Jyotikrishna Dass

entry.summary: Introduces a hybrid attention scheme that mixes sliding-window softmax attention with linear recurrent aggregation, allocating more softmax capacity to early layers that are sensitive to its removal and more linear computation to redundant deeper layers. Targets the KV cache memory and I/O bottleneck in long-context decoding.

entry.title: Towards an Agent Operating System - Lessons from Classical and Cloud OS

author.name: Gosia Steinder, Hubertus Franke

entry.summary: A position paper from IBM researchers arguing that agentic AI is in the pre-standardization phase that classical operating systems and cloud platforms once occupied, and drawing lessons from POSIX and Kubernetes about which abstractions and guarantees a future agent platform must define. Surveys the fragmented landscape of current agent frameworks and protocols.

entry.title: PreDiff-LM: Pretrained Discrete Masked Diffusion Language Modeling with Hybrid Attention

author.name: Zhengtao Yao, Runhao Li, Xupeng Chen, Jiayi Cheng, Chenqian Le, Michael Yue, Jesson Wang, Siheng Wang, Guang Yang, Haoyan Xu, Chenhao Wei, Zhengqing Yuan, Youran Shen, Yanfang Ye, Junhao Dong

entry.summary: Studies how to adapt causally pretrained autoregressive transformers into discrete masked diffusion language models by changing the attention mask, keeping causal attention within the observed prompt while allowing full bidirectional attention within the masked target. Reports improved perplexity and generation-quality metrics over uniform bidirectional attention under matched training budgets.

entry.title: Speculate While You Reason: Teaching Agents to Predict Their Next Tool Call via Joint Agent-Speculator RL

author.name: Jiabao Ji, Yujian Liu, Li An, Rohit Jain, Gungor Polatkan, Siyu Zhu, Shiyu Chang

entry.summary: Proposes a single model that both acts as the agent and speculates its own next tool call from partial context, so tool calls can be pre-executed to hide latency, trained via joint agent-speculator reinforcement learning. Removes the mismatch between separate draft speculators and the deployed agent's actual behavior.

entry.title: Falling Behind Drives Unsafe Development in an Idealised AI Race Experiment

author.name: Elias Fern\'andez Domingos, The Anh Han

entry.summary: A framed behavioural experiment with paired human participants in an idealised AI development race finds that the felt experience of falling behind, rather than the magnitude of the risk ceiling, drives choices toward unsafe faster development. Provides experimental evidence for a core assumption in AI race and governance debates.

entry.title: Mechanisms of Width Scaling in Normalized Residual Networks: The Effective Alignment Dimension

author.name: Jinhao Zhang, Zeyu Liu, Zicheng Yan, Yunquan Zhang, Guangming Tan, Fangming Liu, Daning Cheng

entry.summary: A theoretical study of when widening a normalized residual network with function-preserving expansion actually generalizes, introducing an effective alignment dimension that captures the signal-to-noise geometry of activation gradients. The authors derive exact moments of train-test gradient inner products and a finite-sample bound on misalignment probability.

entry.title: CLBench-V: Evaluating Multimodal Context Learning from Grounding to Knowledge Acquisition

author.name: Lai Wei, Chengqi Li, Jiapeng Li, Ruina Hu, Yue Wang, Weiran Huang

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark for multimodal in-context learning that separates context grounding, applying newly provided information, and acquiring knowledge, using contexts delivered as figures, tables, reports, maps and web pages. Designed to localize where multimodal context use breaks down rather than giving a single aggregate score.

entry.title: Tools Are Not Islands: Set-Level Tool Retrieval for LLM Agents via Query-Conditioned Hyperedge Prediction

author.name: Xinyi Hong, Pinjun Dong, Xinyang Yu, Binyan Jiang

entry.summary: HYSET reframes tool retrieval for LLM agents as query-conditioned hyperedge prediction on a tool co-invocation hypergraph, so a candidate tool set is scored jointly rather than tool by tool. This addresses the common failure where individually relevant tools do not compose into a workable set for a task.

entry.title: Stemma: Induced Decision Regions Reveal LLM Provenance

author.name: Keyu Zhang, Vadim Safronov, Andrew Martin

entry.summary: Stemma tests whether a suspect model derives from a source model by mapping open-ended outputs into a finite decision space and measuring whether the source's induced decision regions are inherited. This is intended to be more robust than response-level fingerprints that shift under fine-tuning or deployment changes.

entry.title: Endpoint Replay: Compressing the Recency Buffer in Deep Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Parham Mohammad Panahi, Armin Ashrafi, Haoyu Du, Andrew Patterson, Martha White, Adam White

entry.summary: Endpoint Replay questions the unexamined default of million-transition uniform replay buffers by storing only representative transitions derived from endpoints of chains of connected n-step sequences. The aim is to keep large-buffer performance while cutting memory and redundancy and speeding value propagation.

entry.title: Bits and Memories: Measuring Verbatim Extraction Across LLM Quantization

author.name: Akshay Sasi

entry.summary: This study argues membership inference is the wrong lens for judging whether quantization reduces privacy risk, and directly measures verbatim extraction of known-memorized sequences across Pythia model sizes from full precision down to four bits. Quantization turns out to be a selective and uneven forgetting mechanism rather than a uniform privacy improvement.

entry.title: AI's Capability in Assisting Scientific Research in Physics, Astrophysics, and Cosmology I: Literature Review

author.name: Anamaria Hell, Kateryna Vovk, Veena Krishnaraj, Jia Liu, Kosuke Aizawa, Adrian E. Bayer, Linda Blot, Jessica Cowell, Suyog Garg, Jonathan Gr\'ee, Ben Horowitz, Masaya Ichikawa, Kanyuni Iemoto, Keigo Kondo, Zacharie Lorsin, Kevin McCarthy, Jamie Robinson, Miguel Ruiz-Granda, Leander Thiele, Ievgen Vovk, Mingshen Zhou

entry.summary: A controlled study across eight expert-designed physics, astrophysics and cosmology projects comparing literature reviews produced by human experts against those from mid-2025 LLM tools including deep-research modes. Overlap in selected references is under 6 percent, indicating current systems do not replicate competent expert search though they may complement it.

entry.title: Intrinsic and Triangulation-Agnostic Attention: A Simple and Powerful Approach for Learning on Meshes

author.name: Ashwath Shetty, Zihan Zhu, Soeren Pirk, Noam Aigerman

entry.summary: Redesigns the attention mechanism for triangle meshes so that queries, keys and values are produced by an intrinsic, triangulation-agnostic network and treated as discretizations of continuous functions, giving attention the geometric invariances that matter for surfaces. The approach reports state-of-the-art results across several geometry-processing tasks.

entry.title: Elliptic Regularity Theory in Barron Spaces and Applications to the Deep Ritz Method

author.name: Stephan Wojtowytsch

entry.summary: Proves negative regularity results for harmonic functions whose boundary data lies in Barron space, the natural function class for wide two-layer ReLU networks, showing solutions need not be Lipschitz or in the second-order Sobolev class. Positive approximation results show low-norm Barron approximations with logarithmic norm growth are still achievable on simple domains.

entry.title: Research directions in condensation: varieties of objectivity

author.name: SamEisenstat

entry.summary: First entry in a research-agenda survey for condensation, a mathematical theory of how descriptions of the world decompose into conceptual parts, extending prior work on random variable and latent variable models and an objectivity theorem. It sketches directions including almost-perfect condensation and an algorithmic-information variant.

entry.title: SpecPrefetch: Parameter-Efficient Expert Prefetching for Sparse MoE Foundation Models

author.name: Jinwei Kong, Runqi Meng, Fanyi Wang, Wentao Qiu, Haotian Hu, Yongjian Zhou, Zhenhua Ge

entry.summary: Addresses the serialization bottleneck in offloaded mixture-of-experts inference by using a lightweight shared adapter to predict which experts the next layer will need, letting transfers start before routing is resolved. Enables deployment of large sparse models under constrained accelerator memory.

entry.title: Towards Robust Reinforcement Learning for Small-Scale Language Model Agents

author.name: Md Rezwanul Haque, Md. Milon Islam, Fakhri Karray

entry.summary: Systematically investigates why reinforcement learning is unstable for very small language models in the seventy to five hundred million parameter range, training fifteen model-corpus configurations with PPO. Identifies three reproducible failure modes: silently frozen adapter parameters in standard fine-tuning pipelines, numerical overflow in importance ratios under reduced precision, and policy collapse from reward model errors.

entry.title: Cyber-Capable AI Agents: Vulnerabilities, Evaluation Containment, and Defensive Response

author.name: Abu Bakar Siddik

entry.summary: A review synthesizing five vulnerability classes at the boundary between cyber-capable agents and the sandboxes used to evaluate them, including multi-step offensive chains, objectives conflicting with sandbox limits, credential and supply-chain exposure, persistent command-and-control, and the sheer speed of automated action. Uses a reported mid-2026 platform security incident as a bounded case study.

entry.title: Agent Skills Matter: Inferring Proprietary Skills from Execution Trajectories

author.name: Jianing Geng, Ruiqi He, Zekun Fei, Biao Yi, Ruijie Wang, Zheli Liu, Xia Hu, Xuansheng Wu, Qingkai Zeng

entry.summary: Defines skill leakage: proprietary agent skills hidden behind a cloud interface can be reconstructed from execution trajectories triggered by benign queries, and presents SigLeak, a black-box framework exploiting recurring behavioral signatures. Relevant as agent skill marketplaces and monetized skill packages emerge.

entry.title: Every Time I Hire a Linguist, Inference Costs Go Down: On Linguistic Rules as Effective Prompt Compressors

author.name: Jianfei Ma, Zhaoxin Feng, Emmanuele Chersoni, Si Chen

entry.summary: Asks whether deterministic linguistic rules can compress prompts as effectively as methods that score token importance with expensive language model forward passes, searching evolutionarily over lexical, syntactic, semantic and discourse rules. The resulting compressor needs no model inference at compression time.

entry.title: OmniPhys: Knowledge-Graph-Driven Benchmarking and Collective Optimization for Physical Commonsense in Text-to-Image Generation

author.name: Yajing Xu, Yarong Lan, Jiaoyan Chen, Yichi Zhang, Jeff Z. Pan, Mingchen Tu, Zhizhen Liu, Wen Zhang, Huajun Chen

entry.summary: Introduces a 1,551-sample benchmark for physical commonsense in text-to-image generation grounded in a physical knowledge graph aligned with simulations and curricula, so failures can be traced to specific physical principles. Also proposes collective optimization to avoid prompt optimizers being misled by transient artifacts of stochastic generation.

entry.title: The OlmoEarth Platform: Geospatial inference at planetary scale

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Ai2 describes the engineering behind OlmoEarth, a platform for fine-tuning geospatial foundation models and running satellite inference at continent scale, covering large data pipelines, distributed compute orchestration, and automatic recovery from failures. It is an infrastructure account supporting open geospatial AI.

entry.title: Research directions in condensation: varieties of objectivity

author.name: SamEisenstat

entry.summary: Alignment Forum mirror of the condensation research-directions survey, outlining a mathematical theory for decomposing world descriptions into conceptual parts and proposing directions including almost-perfect and algorithmic-information variants. It invites collaborators to work on the listed open problems.

entry.title: Addressable Recall Compaction for Long Context-Window Control in AI Agents

author.name: Thang Dang, Yuma Ichikawa, Sakina Fatima, Koichi Shirahata

entry.summary: Proposes a context management scheme for long-horizon agents that stores tool observations in an append-only identifier-addressable log and swaps old observations for compact citations, allowing the agent to retrieve full content on demand without re-running tools. Positions this as lossless compaction versus summarization or discarding.

entry.title: Physics-Grounded Fluid Video Generation with a Simulation Dataset and Dual-Stream Optical-Flow Supervision

author.name: Ruijie Su, Yuanzhi Liang, Xiaohua Xie, Jianhuang Lai

entry.summary: Attributes physics violations in generated fluid videos to the absence of explicit motion supervision in web video-text corpora, and builds a dataset combining over sixteen hundred material-point-method simulations with mined real pouring footage plus held-out test sets. Adds dual-stream optical-flow supervision so models learn dynamics rather than fluid appearance.

entry.title: Toward an Organizational Science of Multi-Agent LLM Systems: Decoupling Who, How, and Which Algorithm

author.name: Huan Chen, Xiang Song, Jian Jin, Pan Ren, Liang-Jie Zhang

entry.summary: Argues that multi-agent LLM frameworks conflate three separable concerns, who is on the team, how members coordinate, and which fusion algorithm is used, and builds a system that makes each an independently swappable layer. Encodes classical organizational theory such as team roles, coordination mechanisms, and accountability matrices as executable configuration, with six published collaboration algorithms behind one interface.

entry.title: Retraction-Free Optimization over the Stiefel Manifold for the LoRA Fine-Tuning

author.name: Yuan Zhang, Jiang Hu, Zhijian Lai, Lin Lin, Zaiwen Wen

entry.summary: Develops a retraction-free and penalty-parameter-free optimization algorithm for the Stiefel manifold with global convergence guarantees, then reformulates low-rank adaptation fine-tuning to exploit it. Avoids costly orthonormalization and fragile step-size or penalty tuning.

entry.title: CoSA: Accelerating Long-Context Inference via Proxy-Kernel Co-Designed Sparse Attention

author.name: Yufei Xue, Lin Niu, Hong Liu, Siran Liu, Hanyong Shao, Wei Liu, Guanghua Yu, Jianchen Zhu, Jun Zhang

entry.summary: CoSA is a training-free block-sparse attention scheme that co-designs the block-importance proxy with the sparse-attention kernel, so the proxy is aware of kernel behavior and the kernel can skip blocks in an order-sensitive way. This preserves accuracy at aggressive sparsity budgets where existing proxies drop salient blocks.

entry.title: AI's Capability in Assisting Scientific Research in Physics, Astrophysics, and Cosmology II: Project Planning and Proposal Evaluation

author.name: Jia Liu, Veena Krishnaraj, Kateryna Vovk, Kosuke Aizawa, Adrian E. Bayer, Linda Blot, Jessica Cowell, Suyog Garg, Jonathan Gr\'ee, Anamaria Hell, Ben Horowitz, Masaya Ichikawa, Kanyuni Iemoto, Keigo Kondo, Zacharie Lorsin, Kevin McCarthy, Jamie Robinson, Miguel Ruiz-Granda, Leander Thiele, Ievgen Vovk, Mingshen Zhou

entry.summary: In the second installment of a study on AI assistance in physical sciences, human researchers and three assistant models wrote one-page plans for eight expert-conceived projects, and the 32 proposals were blind-reviewed by four humans and two frontier models (including existing systems such as Claude Opus 4.8 and a GPT-5.5-tier product) against a four-aspect rubric. Human reviewers scored human and AI proposals similarly, while the model reviewers diverged, revealing systematic judge biases.

entry.title: Generalised Robust Bayes for Joint Inference of Model and Contamination

author.name: Masahiro Fujisawa, Masaki Adachi, Takuo Matsubara

entry.summary: Introduces a generalized Bayesian framework based on the Holder divergence that jointly infers model parameters and the proportion of contaminated data, rather than merely dampening the influence of outliers. This yields quantitative robustness, allowing practitioners to estimate contamination levels and flag anomalous observations.

entry.title: Kernel Forge: An Agent Harness for LLM-based Generation and Optimization of CUDA Kernels

author.name: Joshua Brodsky, Dhravid Kumar, Savini Kashmira, Jayanaka Danatanarayana, Jason Mars, Krisztian Flautner, Lingjia Tang

entry.summary: Presents an agent harness in which LLMs generate and optimize CUDA kernels, addressing gaps in prior tools such as evaluation on random tensors, isolated kernels, and code that developers must reintegrate by hand. Targets end-to-end integration and debuggability of generated GPU code.

entry.title: Matryoshka Agent: Unfolding Sub-Agents for Long-Horizon Machine Learning Engineering

author.name: Rushi Qiang, Changhao Li, Haotian Sun, Yuchen Zhuang, Chao Zhang, Bo Dai

entry.summary: A hierarchical agent framework for machine learning engineering tasks in which a high-level orchestrator maintains compact long-horizon state and unfolds nested sub-agents to handle noisy execution details. Targets long-horizon iterative debugging and refinement under limited context and compute budgets.

entry.title: The User Asks, Platforms Compete: How Agentic Recommendation Markets Take Shape

author.name: Deyao Hong, Kehan Zheng, Qian Li, Jun Zhang, Jie Jiang, Hongning Wang

entry.summary: Studies a prospective shift in which users state a need to an LLM agent before choosing a platform, so platforms compete for agent attention rather than controlling the candidate pool. Controlled experiments across three product domains find that this user-centric setting broadens which items get considered but does not proportionally translate into attention or selection.

entry.title: Distilling Temporal Search and Reasoning: Evolving LLMs for Future Prediction via Harness-Assisted Efficient Data Synthesis

author.name: Wanxu Cai, Zhengyu Chen, Huaisheng Zhu, Wei Wang, Jingang Wang, Qiang Xu

entry.summary: Proposes a time-truncation harness that synthesizes forecasting training data without temporal leakage, then distills agentic temporal search and reasoning into the model itself so predictive skill survives removal of the external agent scaffold. Targets the gap where forecasting agents collapse into retrieval when the harness is stripped away.

entry.title: Messier: A High-Resolution Corpus for Cross-Benchmark Agent Evaluation

author.name: Stefan Krsteski, Charlotte Meyer, Guillaume Allegre, Tony O'Halloran, Alexandre Sallinen

entry.summary: Messier is a nearly one-million-record corpus standardizing agent evaluation results across 30 benchmarks, 714 agents, about 12,000 tasks and 74,000 verifiers, normalizing model, scaffold, environment, verifier, and aggregation metadata plus occupational and industry codes. It also adds fresh runs in underrepresented professional and scientific domains.

entry.title: Agent Retrieval Bench: Evaluating Repository Context Retrieval for Coding Agents

author.name: Bowen Qin, Yi Xie

entry.summary: Introduces a file-level benchmark that isolates the repository context-retrieval step that precedes patch generation in coding agents, with tasks like code-to-test, trace-to-code and edit-to-ripple plus no-gold and wrong-repository cases. It targets a stage usually hidden inside end-to-end agent scores.

entry.title: Structure-aware Relative Policy Optimization for Ranking

author.name: Yiteng Tu, Weihang Su, Zitao Su, Yiqun Liu, Min Zhang, Qingyao Ai

entry.summary: Proposes a reinforcement learning method for ranking that accounts for structural similarity among sampled permutations instead of treating each ranking as an atomic output judged by a scalar reward. Aims to fix inaccurate credit assignment and overly aggressive policy updates when different orderings receive similar rewards.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Neural Operator for Warm-Starting Background-Decomposed and Preconditioned PSFD: Enabling Scalable 3-D EUV Mask Simulation

author.name: Doyun Kim, Werner Gillijns

entry.summary: Trains a physics-informed Fourier neural operator with factorized lateral and axial branches, using pseudo-spectral frequency-domain equations and background decomposition, to accelerate 3-D electromagnetic mask simulation for EUV lithography. Warm-starts an iterative solver rather than replacing it, retaining full-vector mask-multilayer coupling.

entry.title: Beyond Self-Knowledge: Propagating Uncertainty Across Reasoning and Retrieval in LLMs

author.name: Chandan Kumar Sah, Xiaoli Lian, Li Zhang

entry.summary: Tests whether verbalized self-reported confidence from black-box language models can route which questions need retrieval, sending low-confidence queries to a simple TF-IDF retriever plus a second answer pass while returning high-confidence provisional answers directly. Evaluated over 27,000 policy instances across six QA benchmarks with thresholds frozen on validation data.

entry.title: Why Public Service AI Governance Frameworks Risk Failing in the Age of General-Purpose AI: Lessons from Policing

author.name: Sam Relins, Daniel Birks

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that public-sector AI governance frameworks, built around narrow purpose-built systems, break down when general-purpose LLMs can be repurposed by prompt alone. Using policing as the case study, it claims the usual safety levers of accuracy, bias auditing, explainability and accountability lose traction under unbounded task scope.

entry.title: Lowering the implementation barrier of neutral-atom quantum computing with agentic workflows

author.name: Constantin Dalyac, Alexandre Dauphin, Lo\"ic Henriet, Christophe Jurczak

entry.summary: Researchers from a neutral-atom quantum hardware company describe an agentic workflow that takes published protocols through compilation, simulation and cloud execution on real QPUs with human validation checkpoints. Three case studies went from paper or patent to overnight QPU campaigns with limited human intervention.

entry.title: Conformal Cascade: Distribution-Free Accuracy Guarantees for Multi-Tier LLM Inference

author.name: Yifan Dou, Shikan Fang, Shibo Li

entry.summary: Conformal Cascade replaces miscalibrated confidence thresholds in multi-tier LLM routing with conformal prediction set size: accept a small model's answer when its calibrated set collapses to one option, otherwise defer to a larger model. A per-tier union bound yields a distribution-free finite-sample accuracy guarantee for the whole cascade.

entry.title: MemSFT: Mitigating Alignment Tax with an External Parametric Memory

author.name: Jiarui Wang, Xiang Shi, Jiaqi Cao, Rubin Wei, Xiquan Wang, Hao Sun, Jingzhi Wang, Zhiqi Yang, Qipeng Guo, Bowen Zhou, Zhouhan Lin

entry.summary: MemSFT mitigates the alignment tax of domain fine-tuning by keeping backbone weights frozen and training a plug-and-play parametric memory that imitates a non-parametric retriever over domain data. A learned router fuses memory and backbone output distributions at generation time, and the trained memory transfers across models of different sizes.

entry.title: Reinformed Dreamer: An Asymmetric World Model Efficiently Trained through Latent Guidance

author.name: Gaspard Lambrechts, Adrien Bolland, Daniel Ebi, Damien Ernst

entry.summary: Reinformed Dreamer studies asymmetric model-based reinforcement learning, where privileged state information available only during training is used to shape latent representations of a Dreamer-style world model. The authors identify a failure mode in privileged-information representations and use latent guidance to train more efficient observation encoders.

entry.title: DC-WAM: Dynamic-Centric Visual Supervision and Reasoning for World-Action Models

author.name: Haoyuan Ji, Lingxiang Fan, Shang Su, Yinqiao Lu, Mengkai Shi, Jun Gao, Shuo Feng

entry.summary: Argues that the benefit of future-video prediction in world-action robot models lies in the control-relevant representations induced during training rather than in photorealistic rendering, and redirects an existing RGB-based model toward dynamics-centric visual supervision. This should cut compute spent modeling texture and lighting that are irrelevant to action selection.

entry.title: Transfer Learning in High-Dimensional Clustering: Minimax Thresholds and Applications in Single-Cell Data

author.name: Abhinav Chakraborty, Sagnik Nandy

entry.summary: Develops theory for when auxiliary source datasets actually improve clustering of a target dataset in high-dimensional two-component Gaussian mixtures, characterizing relatedness through geometric alignment of signal directions. The authors derive minimax thresholds separating regimes where transfer helps and apply the results to single-cell data.

entry.title: CogEEGAgent: Toward Autonomous Cognitive EEG Analysis with Grounded Execution and Selection-Aware Verification

author.name: Dengzhe Hou, Lingyu Jiang, Fangzhou Lin, Kazunori D Yamada

entry.summary: An EEG analysis agent that separates semantic interpretation by the LLM from scientific authority held by deterministic components, which validate typed contracts and enforce registered analyses against adaptive search. Designed so that fluent reports cannot substitute for verifiable evidence that the requested confirmatory analysis was actually run.

entry.title: ODYSSE: Episode-wise Policy Optimization for Personalized Agentic Reasoning

author.name: Jiaqi Zhang, Tong Chen, Junliang Yu, Quoc Viet Hung Nguyen, Hongzhi Yin

entry.summary: A reinforced fine-tuning framework for agents that must serve ambiguous, human-centered requests by jointly interacting with users to elicit preferences and with environments to execute tasks. Uses episode-wise policy optimization to handle the open-ended solution spaces created by underspecified instructions.

entry.title: RIDGE: An Autonomous Framework for Validation and Method Discovery in LLM-Generated Option Pricing

author.name: Liexin Cheng, Xue Cheng, Shuaiqiang Liu, Cornelis W. Oosterlee

entry.summary: An autonomous validation framework for LLM-generated option pricing code that applies no-arbitrage tests, stress tests, benchmark comparisons and consistency checks, accumulating diagnostic knowledge to also discover better numerical methods. Addresses the fact that pricing code must be mathematically consistent and numerically stable, not merely pass unit tests.

entry.title: Emergent Latent-State Computation under Stochastic Volatility

author.name: Xiaoyu Huang, Lulu Wang

entry.summary: Extends mechanistic interpretability beyond language models to sequence models trained on multivariate stochastic volatility data, where the latent state is hidden from the model but known to the researcher. Finds consistent evidence of a two-stage computation with hidden representations encoding substantial latent-state information across architectures and losses.

entry.title: NEXT: Reasoning-Driven Video Recommendation via a Vision-Language Model

author.name: Yuming Liu, Hongye Yang, Harrison Zhao, Ellie Zhu, Bokai Cao, Lei Huang, Lizhu Zhang, Xiangjun Fan

entry.summary: NEXT is a video recommendation framework that uses a purpose-trained 8B vision-language model to reason about the just-watched video, infer the viewer's next intent, and retrieve concrete follow-up items via an item-to-intent-to-item formulation. Training combines perception-focused reinforcement learning with distribution alignment stages.

entry.title: Schr\"odinger's Cat: Probabilistic Representation and Prediction of Potential Scene Kinematics

author.name: Timy Phan, Jannik Wiese, Bj\"orn Ommer

entry.summary: GARFIELD learns a structured spatio-temporal latent distribution over possible future scene motions from a single image plus optional sparse constraints, enabling both joint sampling of all trajectories and direct queries about individual points. It emphasizes modeling the distribution of futures rather than appearance-level video prediction.

entry.title: INTACT: Isomorphic Intent-to-Action Learning for Search-Free World Models

author.name: Junhan Sun, Hao Zhao, Guofeng Zhang

entry.summary: INTACT is a joint-embedding predictive architecture that learns a direct intent-to-action mapping from action-labeled but reward-free trajectories, avoiding the expensive test-time planning search typical of forward latent world models. Local transition intent and goal-directed intent share an isomorphic architecture and parameters.

entry.title: AI Safety Funder Bulletin

author.name: Carol N

entry.summary: A living digest of funders in the AI safety ecosystem, tabulating 2025 grant volumes, projected 2026 budgets, staff counts, and whether each accepts general applications. It maps a landscape now dominated by very large funders alongside newer entrants such as an OpenAI-affiliated foundation.

entry.title: AdaKP: Online Adaptive Knowledge-Point Selection for Reasoning-Oriented Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zibin Meng, Zhenyu Zhao, Chunqiang Run

entry.summary: Proposes an online selector that decides which subset of atomic knowledge hints to inject into prompts during reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, re-choosing per problem as training proceeds. Uses an entropy-reduction proxy to score hint informativeness and counter reward sparsity on competition mathematics.

entry.title: Cardiologent: Multi-Agent Clinical Decision Support for Patient-Level Arrhythmia Assessment, Urgency, and Management

author.name: Sukju Oh, Moo-Yong Rhee, Jae-Sik Jang, Sukkyu Sun

entry.summary: Formulates patient-level arrhythmia assessment as requiring three linked judgments: what the rhythm is across an entire record, what it means for that specific patient, and what should be done, rather than classifying a single recording. Implements a multi-agent clinical decision support system that produces urgency and management recommendations.

entry.title: CoRT: Counterfactual Replay for Token-Level Rubric-Guided Policy Optimization

author.name: Bo-Wen Zhang, Junwei He, Wen Wang, Song-Lin Lv, Wentao Ma, Rongyi Lin, Shuhan Zhong, Lan-Zhe Guo

entry.summary: CoRT adds token-level credit assignment to rubric-conditioned GRPO by counterfactually re-scoring the same sampled response under modified rubric conditions, rather than broadcasting one scalar advantage across all tokens or training an auxiliary token scorer. Targets a known weakness in rubric-based reinforcement learning for open-ended tasks.

entry.title: Distributed Constraint Optimization via Online Learning and Iterative Pricing with Application to Large-Scale Satellite Scheduling

author.name: Itai Zilberstein, Pranav Rajbhandari, Steve Chien, Tuomas Sandholm

entry.summary: Adapts modern online-learning equilibrium-finding algorithms to distributed constraint optimization by exploiting the potential-game connection, then introduces a decomposition that splits large instances into a high-level task-allocation meta-problem and lower-level subproblems, motivated by decentralized satellite scheduling. Shows competitiveness with standard incomplete DCOP solvers at large scale.

entry.title: Penelope: Localized Latent Recurrence for Efficient Structured Reasoning

author.name: Yutong Chen, Shouqian Shi, Xinran Liu, Haochen Wang, Jiaying Wang, Tianxing Xu, Yuanxi Wang, Zirui Ding

entry.summary: Penelope adds latent recurrent computation to a selected interval of a pretrained decoder-only transformer, refining a problem-conditioned boundary memory with gated recurrent dynamics before generating an answer, so extra reasoning compute does not require longer chain-of-thought output. Offers a cheaper alternative to scaling parameters or serialized reasoning tokens.

entry.title: LLM as Forecasting Planner: Training-Free Text Conditioning for Time-Series Foundation Models

author.name: Huu Hiep Nguyen, Dung Nguyen, Minh Hoang Nguyen, Dai Do, Hung Le

entry.summary: Combines frozen time-series foundation models with an LLM by treating text-conditioned forecasting as planning over trajectories the foundation model simulates, so the LLM selects among candidate futures rather than emitting numbers directly. This avoids the distortion of temporal structure seen when LLMs edit forecasts.

entry.title: Laplace-PSN-IRT: Uncertainty Quantification for Neural Item Response Theory Models of LLM Benchmarks

author.name: Juan Francisco, Mandujano Reyes

entry.summary: Adds a post-hoc last-layer Laplace approximation to neural item response theory models of LLM benchmarks, yielding calibrated posteriors over model ability and item difficulty without retraining. Enables credible intervals and probabilistic model comparisons on leaderboards.

entry.title: I2VShield: An Efficient Proactive Defense Framework against DiT-based Image-to-Video Models

author.name: Yimao Guo, Zuomin Qu, Wei Lu

entry.summary: Proposes a proactive protection method against diffusion-transformer image-to-video misuse that generates adversarial perturbations with a trained generator and text-adaptive perturbation module, rather than per-image gradient optimization that demands large GPU memory. Aims to make protective perturbation practical for ordinary users.

entry.title: How Do LLMs Read Bug Reports? An Empirical Study of Attention in LLMs for Automated Program Repair

author.name: Ramtin Ehsani, Irene Manotas, Saurabh Pujar, Luca Buratti, Preetha Chatterjee

entry.summary: An empirical interpretability study of how LLMs allocate attention across parts of bug reports during automated program repair, covering hundreds of real Python and Java bugs from SWE-bench Verified and related sets. It links attention concentration patterns to whether the generated patch is correct.

entry.title: Empirical Evaluation of Out-Of-Distribution Performance of Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Malena Loza, David Chushig-Muzo, Eva Milara, Luis Bote-Curiel, Luis Estrada-Petrocelli, Felipe Grijalva

entry.summary: An empirical comparison of nine tabular foundation models, including several TabPFN generations, TabICL variants, Mitra, LimiX and TabFM, under real-world distribution shift using TableShift datasets. It probes whether the strong in-distribution results of tabular foundation models survive out-of-distribution deployment.

entry.title: Anti-Backdoor Coreset Selection via Cumulative Entropy

author.name: Qi Zhao, Christian Wressnegger

entry.summary: This defense reframes isolating clean data from a poisoned training set as coreset selection, exploiting that poisoned samples have lower prediction uncertainty and are rarer than benign ones. Cumulative entropy over training dynamics is used as the selection criterion to build a backdoor-free, informative training subset.

entry.title: Amortising Trajectory Optimisation for Residual MPC via Implicit Contact Differentiation

author.name: Daniel Layeghi, Thomas Corb\`{e}res, Calum Arnott, Aditya Kamireddypalli, Hashim Al-Obaidi, Steve Tonneau, Michael Mistry

entry.summary: This robotics paper derives an implicit-function-theorem based derivative for regularized smooth contact solvers in MuJoCo MJX, avoiding both unrolled automatic differentiation and hand-derived KKT sensitivities. The gradients amortize trajectory optimization for residual model-predictive control in contact-rich tasks.

entry.title: AngelSpec: Towards Real-World High Performance Inference with Speculative Decoding

author.name: Hong Liu, Rui Cen, Junhan Shi, Guangshuo Qin, Jiebin Zhang, Tianyu Liu, Runzhi Fan, Guoliang Zhao, Ruobing Xie, Kai Zhang, Song Liu, Guanghua Yu, Jianchen Zhu

entry.summary: AngelSpec is a unified training framework for speculative decoding that co-specializes drafting structure and data, covering both autoregressive multi-token prediction drafters and block-parallel diffusion drafters, because no single drafting structure wins across real workloads. It addresses workload heterogeneity at training, structure and serving levels.

entry.title: Enabling Fully Integer-Only Inference for Lightweight Detection Transformers

author.name: Thanh Cong Le, Michal Szczepanski, Martyna Poreba

entry.summary: Presents I-LW-DETR, described as the first lightweight detection transformer where every forward-pass operation including softmax, GELU, LayerNorm and deformable attention runs in integer arithmetic. This enables deployment of transformer detectors on NPUs and microcontrollers that cannot execute floating-point operators.

entry.title: Agentic AI in medicine: architectures, applications, evaluation, and challenges for clinical translation

author.name: Zheng Tong, Yang Liu, Wanshu Fan, Jing Qin, Zhongbin Han, Haifan Gong, Congyu Liao, Xiaofeng Liu, Cong Wang

entry.summary: A scoping review of agentic AI in medicine covering planning, tool use, memory, iterative correction, and multi-agent coordination, screening over 1,600 records and provisionally including 557 studies against predefined agentic criteria. It argues current evaluation practices are misaligned with clinical deployment requirements.

entry.title: ReDesign: Recovering Editable Design Structures from Images via Agentic Decomposition

author.name: Jooyeol Yun, Jintae Park, Hyesu Lim, Junha Hyung, Hyungjin Chung, Jaegul Choo

entry.summary: ReDesign is an agentic system that reconstructs an editable layered design file from a raster image by composing specialized tools for typography, vector geometry, color, grouping and layer ordering, with per-step graceful verification that accepts, prunes, or retries to prevent error accumulation. It introduces a Figma-based edit-replay benchmark to measure editability at scale.

entry.title: A Causality-aware Infer-diagnose-refine Framework for Test-time Modality Adaptation in VLA Models

author.name: Haoyu Zhang, Yuwei Wu, Jin Chen, Gao Zhi, Zhenxin Diao, Mingyang Gao, Kun Wu, Yongchun Liu, Fan Li

entry.summary: Proposes a model-agnostic test-time procedure for vision-language-action policies that infers actions under real and counterfactual visual inputs, diagnoses how much the visual modality is actually causally influencing the action, and then refines predictions accordingly. It addresses the fact that vision matters more in some manipulation phases than others.

entry.title: The Barron-Lipschitz Energy Gap and Depth Separation Phenomena in Scientific Machine Learning

author.name: Nima Rezaei, Stephan Wojtowytsch

entry.summary: Shows through examples that infinite-width two-layer networks in Barron space face structural obstacles for variational problems, notably being unable to represent folds along curved lines in thin elastic shell energies. Conversely it proves no energy gap exists between Barron and Lipschitz functions for a broad class of first-order integral functionals.

entry.title: Understanding Semantic IDs: From Item Representation to Item Selection in Generative Recommendation

author.name: Junting Wang, Xinrui He, Yunzhe Li, Hari Sundaram

entry.summary: Systematically dissects semantic IDs in generative recommendation, showing that shared-prefix neighborhoods recover only about a third of the underlying encoder's nearest neighbors and that the same token sequence is overloaded with three conflicting roles. Traces the effects from item encoding through autoregressive generation to final recommendation quality.

entry.title: A Control System, a Dataset, and a Recipe for Making Frozen LLM Agents Learn a Domain

author.name: Debjyoti Paul

entry.summary: Treats the harness around a frozen model, including prompt template, tools, retrieval, planning, and verification, as a small human-legible action space and learns a policy over it online with sample-efficient classic reinforcement learning. Contrasts with recent systems that let agents rewrite their own harness through expensive code search or unconstrained self-modification, which are hard to audit with black-box model APIs.

entry.title: OrganLens: Organ-Specific Representation Learning for CT Foundation Models

author.name: Zhixuan Ge, Anqi Li, Sadeer Al-Kindi, Hanwen Xu, Wei Qiu

entry.summary: Introduces organ-conditioned self-supervised representation learning for CT foundation models so a single shared encoder can produce organ-specific embeddings while retaining surrounding anatomical context. Contrasts with volume-level embeddings and with methods that crop or disentangle organs after encoding.

entry.title: Less is More: Modality-Decoupling for General AIGC Audio-Video Detection

author.name: Jielun Peng, Yabin Wang, Yaqi Li, Jincheng Liu, Xiaopeng Hong, Athanasios V. Vasilakos

entry.summary: Shows empirically that the audio-visual correspondence assumption behind cross-modal inconsistency detectors fails for general AI-generated scenes, not just human deepfakes, and argues for decision-level rather than feature-level fusion. Proposes a decoupled detector with multi-granularity visual evidence plus an independent audio branch.

entry.title: Construction-Driven Injection: Linguistically-Grounded Edit-Based Code-Mixing Fingerprints for Large Language Models

author.name: Yongyi Cui, Yue Li, Tianbao Jiang, Xin Yi

entry.summary: Proposes linguistically grounded code-mixing fingerprints for proving LLM ownership, coupling fingerprint construction with injection so the trigger's linguistic structure informs how it is embedded. Aims to avoid accidental activation typical of natural-language triggers and the perplexity-based filtering that catches garbled triggers.

entry.title: A scaling law of contextual persistence in human language

author.name: Elan Barenholtz

entry.summary: Using LLMs as probabilistic probes, the study isolates the effect of word arrangement by comparing perplexity reduction from real prior context versus scrambled context at increasing distance, and finds an approximately inverse-distance power law across ten corpora in six language families and both speech and writing. The regularity is proposed as a new quantitative law of language structure.

entry.title: Memory for Large Language Models

author.name: Sining Zhoubian, Dan Zhang, Evgeny Kharlamov, Jie Tang

entry.summary: This survey organizes the fragmented literature on LLM memory into an architecture-centric taxonomy along three axes: implicit versus explicit representation, offline versus online updates, and short- versus long-term persistence. It covers attention, recurrent state, parameter-efficient adaptation and external lookup storage as points in one design space.

entry.title: S2A2: Audio-Visual Imitation Learning for Manipulation Tasks Using Acoustic Spatial Information

author.name: Kaneyoshi Hiratsuka, Benjamin Yen, Ryosuke Kojima

entry.summary: Introduces manipulation tasks that require robots to localize and identify sound sources, plus a framework fusing visual features with spatial and spectral audio for imitation learning. The audio-visual policy design is evaluated across several standard policy backbones including ACT, diffusion policy, and a flow-based generalist policy.

entry.title: PLATO: Pointer Learner for Agent and Task Openness

author.name: Alireza Saleh Abadi, Leen-Kiat Soh, Daniel Alan Redder, Adam Eck, Prashant Doshi

entry.summary: Introduces a pointer-network actor paired with a centralized graph neural network critic for multi-agent reinforcement learning in open systems where the set of agents and tasks changes unpredictably. Avoids the artificial bounds imposed by padding and masking and handles both agent and task openness simultaneously.

entry.title: From Cellular Responses to Pharmacological Domains: Multimodal Zero-Shot Drug Representation Learning

author.name: Jintao Huang, Lu Leng, Ziyuan Yang

entry.summary: Proposes a framework for zero-shot drug property prediction that separates mechanism-consistent factors from modality-specific noise across chemical structure, gene expression, and cell morphology, building a consensus pharmacological response domain. Aims to keep structurally dissimilar but biologically related compounds together in representation space.

entry.title: Entangled by Design: Spurious Intra-Variable Signal Routing in Tabular In-Context Learners

author.name: Athanasios Vlontzos, Giorgos Papanastasiou, Bernhard Kainz, Sotirios Tsaftaris

entry.summary: The paper formalizes how tabular in-context learners can route predictions through spurious sub-signals bundled inside a single input feature (for example a site-specific measurement artefact mixed with true patient health signal), and proves the learner cannot identify which subspace drives outcomes. It matters because tabular foundation models are being deployed on multi-site clinical and scientific data where such entangled features are the norm.

entry.title: TopoGR: Revealing and Preserving Latent Structure of Semantic ID in Generative Recommendation

author.name: Ziyu Zheng, Zhengshun Du, Yaming Yang, Bin Tong, Guan Wang, Meng Yan, Ziyu Guan, Wei Zhao

entry.summary: Points out a structural mismatch in semantic-ID generative recommendation: the tokenizer learns a code space with meaningful neighborhoods while the generator treats those codes as independent categorical symbols, so relatedness collapses to exact ID overlap. Proposes preserving the latent topology during generation.

entry.title: Automated Numerical Stability Analysis of Deep Learning Operators

author.name: Xinye Chen

entry.summary: Presents a software tool integrating the CESTAC stochastic arithmetic method to detect numerical instability in deep learning operators in a single computation pass, locate its sources, and monitor stability during training and inference. Validated by injecting instabilities into operators across tasks.

entry.title: SAM3D-Guided Object-Centric Representation Alignment for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Zonghe Liu (University of Hong Kong), Shanyuan Jie (Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences), Xiaoquan Sun (Huazhong University of Science and Technology), Chen Cao (University of Hong Kong), Zetian Xu (University of Hong Kong), Zongsheng Liu (Beijing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics), Jiayu Chen (University of Hong Kong, Infiforce)

entry.summary: This work adds object-centric 3D grounding to a pi-zero style vision-language-action policy by using a frozen SAM3D model as a teacher, aligning dense object-level 3D representations with the policy's intermediate visual features. The goal is better manipulation under occlusion, pose variation and precise spatial interaction.

entry.title: MDTransformer: A Hardware-Software Co-Design of Mode-Division Photonic Transformer Accelerator with Inverse-Designed Coherent Crossbar

author.name: Solomon Micheal Serunjogi, Rachmad Vidya Wicaksana Putra, Ayat Taha, Muhammad Shafique, Mahmoud Rasras

entry.summary: MDTransformer is a photonic transformer accelerator co-design that replaces costly multi-wavelength sources and large active phase-shifter arrays with mode-division optical dataflow using inverse-designed multimode couplers and IQ modulators. The aim is more practical energy and speed gains for transformer inference in optics.

entry.title: A Unified Algorithmic Framework for Hybrid Reinforcement Learning in Tabular MDPs with Shifted Transition Dynamics

author.name: Zheshun Wu, Renjie Zheng, Jinhang Zuo, Zenglin Xu, Fang Kong

entry.summary: This paper gives a unified framework for hybrid RL in tabular MDPs that combines online interaction with offline data drawn from a source environment whose transition dynamics have shifted. Two algorithms handle regret minimization and best-policy identification, using fine-grained bias estimates to exploit stale data safely.

entry.title: Guiding Posterior Exploration with Optimizer-Derived Geometry

author.name: Moritz Schlager, Emanuel Sommer, Thomas M\"ollenhoff, David R\"ugamer

entry.summary: The paper shows that curvature information already computed as a byproduct by adaptive optimizers such as AdamW during the warmstart phase can precondition subsequent posterior sampling in Bayesian neural networks at negligible extra cost. This substantially reduces the cost of exploring high-dimensional multimodal posteriors.

entry.title: Quantum Speedups for Stochastic Optimization with Heavy-Tailed Noise

author.name: Bin Luo, Chengchang Liu, Jonathan Allcock, Shengyu Zhang, John C. S. Lui

entry.summary: The authors design quantum mean estimators for multivariate heavy-tailed random variables that beat optimal classical query complexity in low dimensions, extend them to unbiased estimators via multi-level Monte Carlo, and prove matching quantum lower bounds. The estimators are applied to stochastic optimization under heavy-tailed gradient noise.

entry.title: Bumblebee: Interleaved Mixed-Layer Building Blocks for Large-Scale Recommendation Systems

author.name: David Bauer, Cancan Zhang, Wenshun Liu, Xiaoyi Zhang, Weijia Liu, Wanli Ma, Yue Weng, Wei Li, Rui Li, Jing Qian, Huayu Li, Xiaoyi Liu, Linhong Zhu, Jerry Fu

entry.summary: Bumblebee proposes a recommendation backbone of stackable blocks that interleave sequence personalization, attention encoding and feature crossing in one micro-pipeline, unifying two historically separate design tracks. It targets large-scale generative next-action prediction in production ranking systems.

entry.title: Memory Layer: Train the In-Model Cache for Recommendation Models

author.name: Liangyuan Na, Gufan Yin, Yixin Bao, Xianjie Chen, Justin Lin, Ziheng huang, Xinyuan Zhang, Wen Zhang, Hao Lin, Xiaoheng Mao, Shuo Tang, Min Yu, Lei Chen, Chao yang, Ziliang Zhao, Mengjiao Zhou, Zheng Qi, Dmitry Barablin, Chuo-Yun Yang, Kaustubh Vartak, Tingting Zhang, Arun Kumar Singh

entry.summary: The memory layer makes the item-embedding cache used at recommendation serving time an in-model, co-trained key-value store, so training and serving share one source of truth for item representations. This removes a structural train-serve representation mismatch in early ranking stages.

entry.title: Retrieval, not hallucinations, will be the limiting factor for LLM-based clinical AI tools

author.name: Kirk Roberts, Steven Bedrick, Kurt Miller, William R. Hersh, Hongfang Liu

entry.summary: A perspective piece from established clinical NLP and biomedical informatics researchers arguing that recall failures in retrieving patient-level data, not hallucination, will be the binding constraint on clinical LLM tools. It categorizes retrieval error types, mitigation strategies, and gaps in retrieval evaluation for healthcare.

entry.title: Beyond Zooming: Learning Multi-Tool Visual Reasoning for Ultra-High-Resolution Remote Sensing

author.name: Fengxiang Wang, Jiangnan Huang, Mingshuo Chen, Yueying Li, Yang Shi, Junwei Luo, Haoyu Wang, Yansheng Li, Jing Zhang, Haiyan Zhao, Wenjing Yang

entry.summary: Shows that giving multimodal LLMs only a zoom-in tool for ultra-high-resolution remote sensing saturates on hard tasks needing global search, multi-region comparison, or path planning, and therefore trains multi-tool visual reasoning over a richer toolset. The pilot study on an existing UHR benchmark motivates the design.

entry.title: Leveraging Semantic Maps for City-Scale Cross-View Localization

author.name: Ethan Fahnestock, Erick Fuentes, Philip R Osteen, Nicholas Roy

entry.summary: Uses vision-language models both to extract rich semantic descriptions from a robot's egocentric views and to associate them against very large OpenStreetMap-derived semantic priors covering hundreds of square kilometres, enabling city-scale cross-view localization without prior traversal. It avoids compressing semantics into a small fixed class set.

entry.title: SONG: A Photorealistic 3D Gaussian Simulation Platform for Benchmarking Social Navigation

author.name: Weiqi Huang, Dianyi Yang, Jiaxin Li, Shuangyi Dong, Hao Xu, Zan Wang, Wei Liang

entry.summary: SONG is a simulation platform for social robot navigation built on 3D Gaussian splatting, with photorealistic scenes, splatted human avatars, and pedestrian trajectories generated from language-model-derived semantic intent. It targets the gap in visually realistic benchmarks for vision-based socially compliant navigation.

entry.title: Unified Semantic Modeling Framework for Large-Scale Job Understanding at LinkedIn

author.name: Dan Xu, Baofen Zheng, Jianqiang Shen, Qi Xiao, Benjamin Hoan Le, Wen Pu, Saurabh Gupta, Ran Zhou, Neha Saraf, Alice Leung, Qianqi Shen, Liangjie Hong, Jingwei Wu, Wenjing Zhang

entry.summary: Describes LinkedIn's production framework that fine-tunes a small language model on synthetic tasks with reasoning traces to jointly handle taxonomy-guided classification and open entity extraction from noisy job postings. Emphasizes cost efficiency and scalability at platform scale.

entry.title: Chart-Supported or Model-Supplied? Examining MLLM-Generated Claims for Accessible Visualization

author.name: Ishrat Jahan Eliza, Md Dilshadur Rahman

entry.summary: Audits over twelve hundred multimodal model descriptions of charts to determine whether claims are directly supported by the visualization, derived from it, or speculative additions from model knowledge, and checks numeric agreement automatically. Finds that providing accessible chart context shifts some models toward directly grounded claims while adding the image itself yields inconsistent numeric benefit.

entry.title: Many-body Tipping Dynamics of ChatGPT-like AIs

author.name: Frank Yingjie Huo, Neil F. Johnson

entry.summary: Applies a statistical-physics framing in which tokens act as interacting spins crossing a finite-layer system to explain why chatbots abruptly tip into harmful, misleading, or repetitive output even under greedy deterministic decoding. Derives a finite-layer threshold from a reduced few-basin model and reports agreement across model families.

entry.title: Salient Knowledge Pathways: Sparse Cross-Modal Routing for Efficient Knowledge-Intensive Multimodal Question Answering

author.name: Noor Islam S. Mohammad, Ulu\u{g} Bayaz{\i}t

entry.summary: An inference architecture for knowledge-intensive multimodal question answering that routes computation along sparse pathways conditioned jointly on the question, image, and an estimated difficulty, combining visual token pruning, region-conditional retrieval, sparse cross-attention, and speculative knowledge use. Motivated by the observation that current systems pay full cost for long visual sequences, dense retrieval, and full fusion on every query.

entry.title: Multiclass Classification without Labels via Posterior Simplex Geometry

author.name: Rapha\"el Bonnet-Guerrini, Johann Ioannou-Nikolaides, Troels Petersen, Vincenzo Piuri

entry.summary: Extends the classification-without-labels idea from binary to multiclass settings, learning class discriminators from several unlabeled mixtures with unknown and different latent class proportions using the geometry of the posterior simplex. Relevant to physics and other domains where only impure sample selections exist.

entry.title: VaLiDRec: Variable-Length LLM-Aligned Semantic IDs for Generative Recommendation

author.name: Shutong Qiao, Wei Yuan, Tong Chen, Hao Wang, Quoc Viet Hung Nguyen, Hongzhi Yin

entry.summary: Builds generative recommendation identifiers out of native LLM vocabulary tokens with variable length determined by item semantic complexity, using token importance estimation, quality-aware pruning and collision handling instead of fixed-length quantized codes. Adds graph-aware user preference modeling.

entry.title: ReLATE: Reliability-Guided Evidence Fusion for Robust UAV--Satellite cross-view Geo-Localization

author.name: Haochen Jiang, Jialei Pan, Yuzhe Sun, Zhe Dong, Lecheng Ren, Yanfeng Gu, Tianzhu Liu

entry.summary: Introduces a large robustness benchmark for UAV-to-satellite cross-view geo-localization with 27 corruption types at three severity levels built on two existing datasets, plus a reliability-guided evidence fusion method. Exposes that strong clean-benchmark accuracy does not survive weather, motion, noise and compression degradations.

entry.title: Neuromorphic Diffusion Language Models: Addressing Compute and Memory Bottlenecks via Sparsity and Block Denoising

author.name: Dengyu Wu, Clement Ruah, Jiechen Chen, Bipin Rajendran, Osvaldo Simeone

entry.summary: The paper combines masked diffusion language models with block-parallel denoising and spike-based neuromorphic computation, exploiting activation sparsity to cut energy and improve throughput relative to autoregressive decoding. It targets platforms with large on-chip memory where parameter access dominates cost.

entry.title: UniMem: Complementary Episodic-to-Parametric Memory for Boundary-Agnostic Task Streams

author.name: Siyu Xia, Chenheng Zhang, Yanting Wu, Haoxuan Li, Jiajun Chai, Xiaohan Wang, Guojun Yin, Wei Lin, Zhouchen Lin, Haifeng Zhang, Jun Wang

entry.summary: UniMem is a self-routing agent memory framework that combines fast external episodic retrieval with gradual consolidation into parametric memory, aiming to handle continuous task streams without explicit task boundaries. It targets the stability-plasticity trade-off where retrieval memory fails to internalize recurring execution strategies and parametric memory needs fixed budgets and boundaries.

entry.title: Decompose and Reorganize: Planning with Primitives and Visuomotor Policies Learned from Demonstrations

author.name: Yizhou Chen, Hang Xu, Dongjie Yu, Yupu Lu, Tengye Xu, Zeqing Zhang, Wei Zhang, Yi Ren, Ben M. Chen, Jia Pan

entry.summary: DR-LfD decomposes demonstrations into contact-defined primitives and reorganizes them within a task-and-motion-planning gate, letting symbolic planning handle long-horizon structure while learned visuomotor policies handle contact-rich segments. The goal is better spatial generalization and multi-stage reliability than pure imitation learning.

entry.title: Critical slowing down for predicting controller induced loss of control in quadrotors

author.name: Jasper J. van Beers, Prashant Solanki, Erik-Jan van Kampen, Coen C. de Visser

entry.summary: Applies critical slowing down, a model-free early-warning indicator from complex systems science, to forecast controller-induced loss of control in quadrotors, validated on real flight data from four vehicles. It provides up to about 0.9 seconds of advance warning without needing a system model.

entry.title: RoCo-ACE: Rollout-Conditioned Online Distillation for Retention-Aware Knowledge Injection

author.name: Yan Hong, Wei Li, Kedong Xiu, Jun Lan, Shuheng Zhou, Zhongcai Lyu, Huijia Zhu, Weiqiang Wang, Jianfu Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a rollout-conditioned online distillation objective for injecting new factual knowledge into multimodal LLMs while limiting drift in unrelated behavior. Reweights distillation toward reference-supported tokens in the model's own generations and adds sparse anchored corrections for omitted facts.

entry.title: ContractHIL-HLS: Contract-Aligned Multi-Agent Workflow with Hardware-in-the-Loop Feedback for HLS Design

author.name: Jingbo Zhang, Haoxiang Sun, Wenbo Wang, Wenbo Zhang

entry.summary: A multi-agent workflow for high-level hardware synthesis that compiles natural-language requirements into an explicit contract of interfaces, constraints, validation checks, and rollback rules, then closes the loop with real hardware and toolchain feedback including timing, power, and runtime failures. Decomposes agents by lowering and execution stages rather than by conversational personas.

entry.title: Are the High-weight Neurons the Important Ones in Image Classification Neural Networks?

author.name: Qitao Chen, Dongfu Yin, F. Richard Yu

entry.summary: Tests whether neurons with the largest weights are actually the important ones in image classifiers, using overlap analysis, perturbation, and ablation-with-retraining experiments on two standard datasets. Finds that top-decile high-weight neurons overlap with accuracy-critical neurons by only about a quarter, challenging weight magnitude as an importance proxy.

entry.title: OrchBench: Evaluating Multi-Agent Orchestration Plans in Isolation via Deterministic Simulation

author.name: Zhenzhen Ren, Jiyan He, Xinpeng Zhang, Zhenxing Qian, Ke Han, Shuxin Zheng, GuoBiao Li, Xiaoqing Zhang

entry.summary: OrchBench evaluates multi-agent orchestration plans in isolation by turning real tasks into dependency DAGs and simulating execution deterministically, decoupling plan quality from worker model skill, tool flakiness, and environment noise. It cuts the token and wall-clock cost of studying orchestration systematically.

entry.title: Desktop-Delta Bench: Do Computer-Use Models Understand Desktop GUI Transitions?

author.name: Abhishek Pillai, Samir Kumar Nayak, Yuan Chen

entry.summary: Desktop-Delta Bench is an offline step-level benchmark of about 2,000 human-verified instances testing whether computer-use models can reconstruct the causal, task-relevant change produced by an action given asynchronous, delayed, or occluded screenshots. It isolates transition understanding, which end-task success and single-frame grounding benchmarks conflate.

entry.title: Foundation Models for EEG Are Blind to Long-Range Temporal Correlations: A Spectral-Temporal Dissociation Behind Their Cross-Population Fragility

author.name: Marzieh Zare

entry.summary: Probes five EEG foundation models and finds their pooled embeddings fail to preserve long-range temporal correlations of alpha-band envelopes, unlike the static aperiodic spectral slope, and links this spectral-temporal dissociation to poor cross-population transfer. Suggests patch-level reconstruction and contrastive objectives systematically discard slow dynamics.

entry.title: Lantern: Conflict-Aware Gradient Blending for Physics-Guided Diffusion Models in Calorimeter Simulation

author.name: Farzana Yasmin Ahmad, Vanamala Venkataswamy, Geoffrey Fox

entry.summary: Adds physics-guided training to diffusion surrogates for calorimeter shower simulation, blending gradients to resolve conflicts between the denoising objective and physics constraints when no per-sample PDE or hard constraint exists. Also proposes metrics that capture correlations across calorimeter layers and voxels.

entry.title: ScaleResfusion: Residual Rectified Flow based on Residual Vector Field

author.name: Zhenning Shi, Chen Xu, Junhao Zhang, Kefei Zhang, Linjie Liu, Zhedong Zheng, Tao Li

entry.summary: A real-world image restoration framework that adds a residual term to rectified-flow trajectories so restoration can start from the degraded input while still exploiting pretrained text-to-image flow priors. Aims to be faster and more faithful than Gaussian-noise-start diffusion and more scalable than residual models trained from scratch.

entry.title: Data Quality Profiling at Scale with Progressive Sampling: A Benchmark for Data-Centric AI Pipelines

author.name: Laure Berti-Equille

entry.summary: Benchmarks nine progressive sampling strategies, both blind and proxy-guided, for fast data quality profiling of missing values, duplicates, outliers and functional dependency violations across several real datasets up to millions of rows plus an IoT stream. Answers which strategies best preserve profile fidelity when exhaustive scans are too slow.

entry.title: IRIS: Reusable Identity Representations from Frozen LLMs for Entity Alignment

author.name: Xinran Liu, Shengtao Li, Shouqian Shi, Ge Wang, Xin-Wei Yao

entry.summary: Distills entity understanding from frozen LLMs into a stable, reusable identity representation space for knowledge-graph entity alignment, rather than using the LLM for auxiliary generation or candidate-conditioned decisions each time. This makes alignment directly comparable across KG pairs without repeated inference.

entry.title: Score-Based Stabilization for Time-Dependent Problems

author.name: Eshed Gal, Eldad Haber, Uri Ascher

entry.summary: The authors use a learned score model as a stabilization operator applied to provisional numerical PDE updates, correcting iterates toward the manifold of physically admissible states. They show contraction toward this manifold and validate on advection, KdV, nonlinear Schrodinger and Burgers equations.

entry.title: Ranked by Position: Order Sensitivity as an Exploitable Attack Surface in LLM Listwise Recommenders

author.name: Ge Zhang, Jingru Cheng, Huiyuan Chen

entry.summary: The authors show that position bias in LLM listwise rerankers is an exploitable attack surface: simply permuting candidate order can push irrelevant items into the top-k without altering content, labels or model weights. They introduce a promotion-at-k metric and measure vulnerability across three recommendation domains.

entry.title: ScoreShield: Differentially Private Release of Similarity Scores

author.name: Behrooz Razeghi, Parsa Rahimi

entry.summary: ScoreShield proposes a perturbation mechanism for releasing cosine-similarity scores from embedding APIs under differential privacy, avoiding the poor utility of naively adding independent Gaussian noise to vectors. It targets biometric matching and retrieval-augmented generation services where score leakage enables membership inference.

entry.title: SecDrift: Measuring Sector-Conditioned Security Drift in AI-Generated Code

author.name: Narayanaswami Natraj Bharadwaj, Dhivya Chandramouleeswaran

entry.summary: SecDrift benchmarks whether conditioning code-generation prompts on specific critical-infrastructure sector contexts changes the vulnerability rate of LLM output, across seven models, eight sectors and nine weakness categories with thousands of evaluations and matched neutral baselines. The apparent security gain from industry framing does not hold up statistically once the task is held fixed.

entry.title: Learning from the Unseen: Offline Reinforcement Learning with Hidden Actions

author.name: Zeyu Bian, Ying Zhou, Yifan Cui

entry.summary: LURE is an off-policy evaluation estimator for offline reinforcement learning when logged actions are unobserved and only noisy proxies exist, using the next state as a proxy to identify policy value. The estimator is shown to be multiply robust, staying consistent under several combinations of nuisance-model correctness.

entry.title: Temporal-Distance JEPA: Plan-Aware Representation Learning for Latent World Model Predictive Control

author.name: Jiaxin Bai, Jiaxuan Xiong

entry.summary: TD-JEPA augments joint-embedding predictive world models with a directed temporal-distance cost mined from reward-free logs, so that planning ranks imagined futures by actual goal progress rather than by incidental latent Euclidean geometry. It keeps the standard JEPA encoder-predictor backbone for latent model-predictive control.

entry.title: Inspect India Evals: An Open Benchmarking Framework for Evaluating Large Language Models in the Indian Linguistic and Cultural Context

author.name: Abhishek Kumar Singh, Shrey Nag, Sachita, Lipi Goel, Rajeshwar Singh Janwar

entry.summary: Inspect India Evals is an open-source suite built on the Inspect evaluation platform containing six benchmarks for Indian contexts, including multilingual knowledge tests across sixteen Indian languages and an Indian adaptation of a bias benchmark. It targets safety, fairness and accuracy failures invisible to English- and Western-centric benchmarks.

entry.title: Belief-Aware Influence and Trust (BAIT): Shaping Human Belief During Repeated Human-Robot Interaction

author.name: Ye-Ji Mun, Mahsa Golchoubian, Shahabedin Sagheb, Yan Bai, Tianhao Ji, Dylan P. Losey, Katherine Driggs-Campbell

entry.summary: BAIT is a controller for repeated human-robot interaction that models both fast strategic shifts and slow belief drift in a human partner using a hierarchical particle filter, then plans with a belief-aware sampling-based MPC. It explicitly trades off influencing human behavior against preserving perceived trust.

entry.title: Reasoning with Memory: A Temporal Granularity-Adaptive Framework for Training-Free Long Video Understanding

author.name: Linghao Meng, Qiankun Li, Junyuan Mao, Pujin Liao, Zhicheng He, Enbo Zhang, Kun Wang, Yang Liu, Huazhu Fu, Yueming Jin

entry.summary: A training-free framework for long-video question answering that adapts keyframe selection to the temporal granularity implied by the question, using LLM-based question parsing plus a memory-augmented selection process. Aims to overcome the limits of uniform sampling and static query-guided frame selection under restricted context windows.

entry.title: The Disruptive Impact of Large Language Models on Capture the Flag Competitions and the Path Toward Fair Play

author.name: Michael Macaulay, Harmony Bouabid, Guo Gen Ang, Sasha Shaw

entry.summary: A mixed-methods study of how LLMs are disrupting capture-the-flag cybersecurity competitions, combining benchmark synthesis including a recent government evaluation, live competition case studies across three challenge categories, observation of community debate, and interviews. Examines fairness, ranking validity, and whether participation still delivers the intended skill development.

entry.title: Localized Adaptation Reveals Distinct Learning Signatures in Transformers

author.name: Rebecca Ramnauth, Brian Scassellati

entry.summary: Introduces a controlled benchmark testing how the depth location of LoRA adaptation affects acquisition, transfer, and boundedness across five learning objectives such as lexical binding, factual association, and procedural reasoning. Finds distinct adaptation geometries per objective, implying that where you patch a transformer should depend on what you are teaching it.

entry.title: DecoEvo: Score-Decoupled Co-Evolution of Solver and Rubric-Generator Skills in Text Space

author.name: Jiangwang Chen, Zixin Song, Junlin Liu, Shuaiyu Zhou, Haiyan Wu, Haihan Shi, Chenxi Zhou, Hanqing Li, Xiao Yang, Da Zhu, Guanjun Jiang, Hai Wan, Xibin Zhao

entry.summary: DecoEvo co-evolves a solver skill and a rubric-generator skill in natural-language space with decoupled scoring, so rubric updates are not selected by the current solver's own score and cannot be gamed by making evaluation easier. Addresses reward hacking in self-improving text-space optimization loops.

entry.title: Interactive Reward Agent: GUI Task Evaluation via Environment-State Verification

author.name: Chenrui Shi, Yuwei Wu, Yang Liu, Ruining Feng, Zirui Shang, Zhi Gao, Lifeng Fan, Che Sun

entry.summary: Introduces an interactive reward agent for GUI task evaluation that proposes and then verifies evidence by inspecting post-execution environment state such as files and settings, rather than judging only from screenshots. Better GUI verification directly improves reward signals for computer-use agent training and test-time scaling.

entry.title: Beyond "What to Retrieve": Uncertainty in Retrieval-Augmented Code Generation

author.name: Chandan Kumar Sah, Xiaoli Lian, Li Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes an uncertainty-aware retrieval-augmented code generation framework that estimates per-source uncertainty over similar code, repository context and project APIs, then uses it to filter and rank evidence and to guide generation, verification and repair. A factorial study disentangles which evidence types actually help.

entry.title: OPERA: Offline Policy-guided Expert Routing and Adaptation for Universal Biomedical Image Analysis

author.name: Zihan Li, Feiyang Liu, Dandan Shan, Ruibo Wang, Qingqi Hong

entry.summary: Treats expert weighting in a biomedical image ensemble as offline policy learning, fitting a routing policy on a small validation set without updating any expert and then adapting at test time to handle scanner and population shifts. Aims to avoid repeated domain-specific fine-tuning under label scarcity and privacy limits.

entry.title: Rethinking Likelihood distributions: Student's t Likelihood Boosts Bayesian Neural Network Performance

author.name: Pei-Hsuan Hsia, Lars H. Heyen, Arvid Weyrauch, Markus Goetz, Achim Streit, Sebastian Krumscheid, Charlotte Debus

entry.summary: Examines the usually unquestioned Gaussian likelihood assumption in variational Bayesian neural networks and shows that a Student's t likelihood improves performance and uncertainty estimates. Frames the standard choice as a source of model misspecification.

entry.title: CORF-GS: Real-Time Wireless Radiance Field Reconstruction via Coupled Optical-RF Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Jinya Zhang, Jiajia Guo, Chao-Kai Wen, Shi Jin

entry.summary: Extends Gaussian splatting to real-time wireless radiance field reconstruction by building a unified representation with shared geometry and modality-specific appearance for optical and radio frequency signals, using camera images as structural priors. Processes sequential keyframes instead of relying on offline optimization of pre-collected data.

entry.title: KQFuzz: Knowledge-Guided Fuzzing for Quantum Libraries via Large Language Models

author.name: Fuyuan Xia, Qixin Zhang, Chenhao Ying, Haojin Zhu, Shuai Wang, Yuan Luo, Pingchuan Ma, Yuxuan Du

entry.summary: KQFuzz is an LLM-driven fuzzer for quantum computing libraries that grounds test generation in codebase knowledge and adds fitness-guided evaluation plus two-level mutation to reach deeper execution paths. It targets the reliability of quantum software stacks, an area where conventional fuzzing struggles because of complex domain semantics.

entry.title: Rashomon Alignment

author.name: Mois\'es Santos, Peter van der Putten, Bernhard Pfahringer, Carlos Soares

entry.summary: Rashomon Alignment proposes measuring functional similarity between two models geometrically over the whole input space rather than only on the observed data distribution, using uniformly sampled instance-space points to compare decision boundaries. It aims to give a distribution-independent view of when two models are truly interchangeable.

entry.title: AnnoBench: A Benchmark for Visualization Annotation Generation

author.name: Md Rahat-uz-Zaman, Md Dilshadur Rahman, Andrew McNutt, Paul Rosen
