entry.summary: AnnoBench is a benchmark for automatically generating chart annotations, pairing professional visualizations with tests for visual, semantic and stylistic correctness. It fills a gap where annotation quality has never been systematically measured despite many automation tools.

entry.title: Interpretable GOHR Agents via Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Shiwei Tan, Yusong Zhao, Weiyi Qin, Wentian Wang, Jacob Feldman, Lazaros K. Gallos, Paul B. Kantor, Vladimir Menkov, Hao Wang

entry.summary: The paper applies sparse autoencoders to a tokenized autoregressive Transformer agent playing the Game of Hidden Rules, where the agent must implicitly infer which of two shape-to-bucket permutation rules is active from interaction history alone. It asks whether interpretable rule concepts emerge internally without any explicit rule classifier.

entry.title: Rethinking CD: A Reproducibility Study and Extension on the Ineffectiveness of Contrastive Decoding at Mitigating Object Hallucinations in MLLMs

author.name: Arnav Bendre, Guneesh Gupta, Kavish Grover, Chayan Aggarwal, Shreyansh Modi

entry.summary: A reproducibility study re-testing the claim that contrastive decoding does not genuinely reduce object hallucination in multimodal LLMs, verifying that reported gains stem from a unidirectional output distribution shift on discriminative benchmarks. It also confirms that the adaptive plausibility constraint effectively collapses sampling to greedy decoding.

entry.title: Fast, accurate, and differentiable: a neural-network surrogate for NRSur7dq4 precessing binary black hole waveforms

author.name: Michael P\"urrer, Ashwin Girish, Lucy M. Thomas, Scott E. Field, Vijay Varma

entry.summary: The authors train per-component multilayer perceptron surrogates that emulate a precessing binary black hole waveform model, achieving very low mismatches across the parameter space and roughly tenfold speedups on GPU with a differentiable JAX implementation. Differentiability enables gradient-based gravitational-wave inference.

entry.title: Forensic Reproducibility Audit of a Radiology Vision-Language Model Benchmark: From Intended Protocol to Released Artifact

author.name: Mateusz Koz{\l}owski

entry.summary: A retrospective forensic audit of a chest radiograph vision-language model benchmark, tracing consistency between the intended protocol and every released artifact including prompt bindings, DICOM handling, label extraction, and statistical code. It uncovers concrete discrepancies such as prompt mislabeling across dozens of model calls and inversion-handling issues, without rerunning any model.

entry.title: Instruction-based Image Editing: A Survey on Data, Models, Evaluation, and Applications

author.name: Xianghao Zang, Zijian Jiang, Jiarong Cheng, Qianrui Teng, Ying He, Yuxuan Mu, Chao Ban, Huayu Zhang, Lanxiang Zhou, Zerun Feng, Chi Zhang

entry.summary: A broad survey of instruction-based image editing organized around task taxonomy, training-data construction, architectural evolution from GANs to diffusion and autoregressive models, evaluation metrics, and commercial systems. It maps open problems in one-sentence editing systems.

entry.title: LENS: Adaptive Spatio-Temporal Zooming for Keyframe Sampling in Long-Form Videos

author.name: Ce Zhang, Jinxi He, Katia Sycara, Yaqi Xie

entry.summary: LENS is a training-free keyframe selection framework for long video understanding that adaptively trades spatial zoom-ins against broader temporal coverage depending on the text query, within a fixed frame budget. It addresses the conflict between fine detail and temporal breadth under limited multimodal context windows.

entry.title: Medical world models in healthcare: foundations, applications, and challenges for trustworthy clinical translation

author.name: Zhaoyan Chen, Zhongxiu Cong, Zhuanfeng Jin, Wanshu Fan, Dongsheng Zhou, Qi Ai, Haifan Gong, Congyu Liao, Xiaofeng Liu, Cong Wang

entry.summary: A structured review defining medical world models as systems that represent evolving patient states and simulate responses to interventions, screening nearly 1,500 records and finding only 14 studies meeting a strict empirical definition. It organizes the field into patient-state representation, temporal dynamics, intervention-conditioned simulation, and clinical evaluation requirements.

entry.title: PanoLess: Environment Reconstruction from Partial Reflective Views

author.name: Ahitagni Das, Ashok Veeraraghavan, Vivek Boominathan

entry.summary: PanoLess reconstructs a distant environment illumination map from images captured on only one side of a reflective surface, using surface-aligned 2D Gaussian splats with deferred shading to recover normals and reflection cues fused into a neural cubemap. It also outputs a visibility map indicating which environment regions are actually supported by observations.

entry.title: Noise-Free One-Step LoRA for Task-Driven Image Restoration with Diffusion Priors

author.name: Jaeha Kim, Kyoung Mu Lee

entry.summary: Shows that a deterministic single-step noise-free forward pass through a pretrained diffusion prior improves task-driven image restoration, and that the benefit depends critically on the adaptation module, with LoRA succeeding where ControlNet-style conditioning fails. This removes the stochasticity that undermines downstream task consistency.

entry.title: Explicit Layer Modeling for Video Object Insertion and Layer Decomposition

author.name: Kyujin Han, Seungjoo Shin, Sunghyun Cho

entry.summary: Introduces TriLayer, a large-scale triplet dataset of aligned composite, background, and foreground videos where foreground layers include associated visual effects, providing explicit supervision for layered video representations. This enables learned video object insertion and layer decomposition rather than implicit inference or per-scene optimization.

entry.title: SepPrune:A Separator-based Pruning Framework for Efficient Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Yuchen Wang, Qihui Zhu, Yang Liu, Xiaoyan Sun, Siying Wu

entry.summary: SepPrune observes that attention scores from both vision and text tokens spike at modality separator tokens, and exploits this by using the separator as a unified query to rank and select informative vision tokens. The result is a training-free, plug-and-play pruning method that can operate before the prefill stage.

entry.title: Cooperative Multi-UAV Navigation in Complex Environments via Systematic Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yu Su, Nabil Aouf

entry.summary: TriManPolicy enables one human operator to demonstrate three-arm robot behaviors by scheduling arm motions according to dependency structure, so behavior cloning does not inherit artificial serialization delays imposed by the teleoperation interface. It extends imitation learning past the two-channel limit of human operators.

entry.title: ProcAgent: An Agentic Framework for Procedural Task Guidance on Edge with Human-in-the-Loop

author.name: Azizul Zahid, Subrata Biswas, Bashima Islam, Sai Swaminathan

entry.summary: A fully on-device vision-based agent that guides users through physical procedural tasks like assembly and repair on a single embedded GPU board, using a propose-and-verify architecture with continuous low-latency perception and a symbolic task graph. Motivated by privacy and latency constraints that rule out cloud inference.

entry.title: Aletheia: An Offline-First Clinical Decision Support System for Differential Diagnosis in Low-Resource Healthcare Settings

author.name: Joseph Walusimbi, Ann Move Oguti, Abubakhari Sserwadda, Precious Boss Kasasira, Charles Brian Okoboi

entry.summary: An offline-first clinical decision support system built on a fine-tuned three-billion-parameter model with quantized low-rank adaptation, trained on twenty-seven thousand clinical reasoning samples over fifty conditions relevant to sub-Saharan Africa. Designed for frontline workers without reliable connectivity or high-end hardware.

entry.title: From Training to Deployment: Post-Hoc Causal Feature Identification via Sensitivity Ratios

author.name: Athanasios Vlontzos, Giorgos Papanastasiou, Bernhard Kainz, Sotirios Tsaftaris

entry.summary: Introduces the Normalised Sensitivity Ratio, a post-hoc, model-agnostic diagnostic that separates causal from spurious feature reliance in an already-trained model by comparing per-environment sensitivity variability under structured mean shifts. Useful for auditing deployed clinical or genomics models without retraining access.

entry.title: Tokens are All You Need: Dual-purpose Semantic IDs for Achieving LLM-Level I/O Efficiency in recommendation systems

author.name: Baolei Li, Yiping Yuan, Yilin Zheng, Likang Yin, Ling Liu, Fabio Soldo, Romer Rosales, Xinyang Yi, Lichan Hong

entry.summary: Proposes hierarchically quantized semantic IDs that serve simultaneously as collaborative identifiers with learnable embeddings and as compact codes from which a lightweight decoder reconstructs approximate dense embeddings on the fly, replacing massive embedding tables in large-scale recommenders. Targets the memory-wall and input-output bottleneck in industrial ranking systems.

entry.title: Generative Distributionally Robust Optimization

author.name: Ziwei Zhang, Jonathan Yu-Meng Li, Zhihao Jin

entry.summary: Proposes a distributionally robust optimization framework in which the nominal model can be any sampleable conditional generator and worst-case distributions are restricted to a chosen generator family, using a sampler-Sinkhorn pairing to compare laws without needing likelihoods or scores. Aims to combine model-agnostic access with structured adversaries.

entry.title: Analysis of the Shortcut Learning and Clever Hans Effect in CNN based ECG Image Classification

author.name: Abhay Kumar Pathak, Mrityunjay Chaubey, Manjari Gupta, Deepti Mishra

entry.summary: Systematically probes shortcut learning in CNN classifiers on a public ECG image dataset by constructing six feature sets that isolate waveform pixels, metadata text and annotation artifacts such as red arrows. Shows high accuracy can come from non-physiological cues rather than cardiac morphology.

entry.title: TabRank: Chain-of-Thought Distillation for Table Re-Rankers

author.name: Adarsh Singh, Kushal Raj Bhandari, Jianxi Gao, Soham Dan, Vivek Gupta

entry.summary: Distills chain-of-thought reasoning from large reasoning models into smaller table re-rankers for structured retrieval, aiming to bring reasoning-based ranking gains to the tabular setting at lower cost. Targets the reranking stage of multi-stage table retrieval systems.

entry.title: The LAIA Dataset: Labelled Attention for Intelligent Automobiles

author.name: A. Contreras, D. Porres, R. Abad, P. Cano, G. Villalonga, A. M. L\'opez, A. Hern\'andez-Sabat\'e

entry.summary: Releases a synthetic driving dataset collected in the CARLA simulator with over 15 hours of closed-loop driving from 44 participants, annotated with human attention data to support interpretable end-to-end driving research. Aims to address the explainability limits that hinder adoption of end-to-end paradigms.

entry.title: F(AI)2R: Who Did What, and Who Checked? Verifiable AI Provenance as an Executable Skill

author.name: Florian Krebs

entry.summary: Proposes a machine-readable provenance model extending PROV-O to record which parts of a research artifact were drafted, refactored or verified by AI and who checked them, packaged as an executable agent skill that scaffolds continuous integration gating on graph conformance. Extends FAIR principles to AI-in-the-loop research workflows.

entry.title: From Deterministic to Generative Deep Learning for Urban Air Quality Reconstruction from Sparse Observations

author.name: Abhishek A. Sabnis, Mihai Mitrea, Lya Lugon, Karine Sartelet, Marc Bocquet, Xiaoyuan Cheng, Shupeng Zhu, Sibo Cheng

entry.summary: The authors benchmark deterministic deep learning against a new diffusion-based generative framework for reconstructing full urban air-pollution fields from sparse Paris monitoring stations across four pollutants. Training uses simulated full fields while evaluation uses real station observations, testing the sim-to-real transfer of generative reconstruction.

entry.title: MemLens: A Value-Aware Memory Management System with Interactive Analytics for LLM-based Agents

author.name: Shuyue Wei, Chang Liu, Zimu Zhou, Yongxin Tong, Lizhen Cui

entry.summary: MemLens treats agent memory records as first-class data objects and manages them by estimated value, using Shapley-style attribution to decide what to keep, plus an interactive dashboard exposing the full memory lifecycle. It targets the redundancy and low-value clutter that accumulate in current agent memory stores.

entry.title: P3: Probabilistic Policy Propagation for Stable VAE-Based Robot Learning

author.name: Liyun Yan, Jianming Ma, Yang Zhang, Shengcheng Fu, Zhanxiang Cao, Keqi Zhu, Yizhi Chen, Yue Gao

entry.summary: Identifies that standard PPO implementations over VAE latents use a single latent sample to estimate probability ratios and KL terms, creating variance and bias in the surrogate objective. The proposed method uses moment-based distribution-aware estimates to stabilize policy optimization for latent-space robot learning.

entry.title: Modular Robotic Catheters for Endovascular Aneurysm Repair

author.name: Alex Ranne, Jinshi Zhao, Ali Anil Demircali, Songli Moey, Ayhan Aktas, Burak Temelkuran, Nassir Navab, Ferdinando Rodriguez y Baena

entry.summary: Introduces a custom two-segment steerable robotic catheter with four degrees of freedom plus a modular tendon-driven actuation platform for fenestrated and branched endovascular aneurysm repair. The aim is to improve branch vessel access, which surgeons struggle with using standard commercial instruments.

entry.title: RSMeM: Knowledge-Enhanced Memory Evolution for Remote Sensing Agents with Systematic Evaluation

author.name: Bingxian Wu, Yu Zhang, Zonghao Guo, Tang Liu, Chen Qian, Yuxiang Lu, Xingbo Du, Yanghao Li, Yidan Zhang, Chi Chen, Ling Yao, Maosong Sun

entry.summary: Introduces a memory evolution mechanism for remote sensing agents that seeds them with pre-distilled domain knowledge via taxonomy-aware hierarchical retrieval and then accumulates online experience from tool-use failures. Accompanied by a systematic evaluation of multi-step tool execution in geoscience workflows.

entry.title: Context Assembly as the Controlled Variable: A Control-Theoretic View of Harness Policies for Frozen LLM Agents

author.name: Debjyoti Paul

entry.summary: Argues that in control-theoretic treatments of LLM agents the right controlled variable is context assembly itself, meaning which template, examples, and retrieved material enter the prompt, rather than tool selection or the raw action stream targeted by prior work. Positions the claim explicitly against several other recent control-theoretic agent papers.

entry.title: Grounded in Consensus, In Step With Emerging Science: A Consensus-Anchored Multi-Corpus Clinical Chatbot for Long COVID

author.name: Yining Wu, Philip DiGiacomo, Ying Ding, William Brode

entry.summary: A clinician-facing retrieval-augmented chatbot for Long COVID that always anchors answers in expert consensus guidance while optionally pulling from PubMed, trial registries and living systematic reviews with different update cadences. An exploratory automated evaluation on 50 clinician questions found ratings comparable to a commercial medical answer engine.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Broad Learning System: An Efficient Backpropagation-Free Framework for Solving Partial Differential Equations

author.name: Pinki Khatun, M. Sajid, Abhinav Jha, M. Tanveer

entry.summary: Proposes a physics-informed variant of the broad learning system that embeds differential operators and boundary conditions into a linear output-layer problem, removing backpropagation and gradient-based training for PDE solving. Claims large speedups over conventional physics-informed neural networks.

entry.title: Exploring Line Bundle Standard Models with Transformers

author.name: Jacky H. T. Yip, Alessandro Mininno, Gary Shiu

entry.summary: LB-Explorer is a transformer-based reinforcement learning agent that searches heterotic string compactifications for line-bundle configurations yielding standard-model-like gauge groups on Calabi-Yau threefolds. The architecture is designed to generalize across manifolds with suitable geometric structure.

entry.title: Forgetting Is Not a Fix: Path Dependence in Sequential Engram Editing

author.name: Ferdinand M. Schessl

entry.summary: This short paper stress-tests a recent claim that closed-form concept memory edits in model weights compose commutatively, by applying long sequences of edits instead of single or paired ones. It reports path dependence and fatigue-like accumulation, arguing that the compositional memory hypothesis does not survive sequential load.

entry.title: FORGE: Frame Orthogonality in Relevance Geometry for Long-Form Video Understanding

author.name: Ghazal Kaviani, Ghassan AlRegib

entry.summary: FORGE is a training-free, model-agnostic frame-selection method for long-form video question answering that induces a query-conditioned geometry on a pretrained multimodal embedding space and jointly optimizes relevance and orthogonal coverage. It aims to maximize query-relevant information within a fixed frame budget at inference time.

entry.title: MyoCardBench: A Real-World Data Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models in Clinically Authentic Cardiovascular Care Scenarios

author.name: Xiao Li, Mouxiao Bian, Zhaodi Wu, Sijie Ren, Juechen Chen, Lu Lu, Jingru Ding, Yun Zhong, Jie Xu, Yixiu Liang, Junbo Ge

entry.summary: MyoCardBench is a cardiovascular benchmark of 2,263 items drawn from de-identified real clinical records and exams across thirteen task datasets, annotated by sixteen cardiologists with senior cross-review, used to score seven LLMs on nearly sixteen thousand outputs. It targets the longitudinal, multimodal and safety-critical aspects that exam-style medical benchmarks miss.

entry.title: VisualPatchWorld: Code World Models as Latent Structured Representations for Planning

author.name: Jiaxin Bai, Jiaxuan Xiong

entry.summary: VisualPatchWorld represents world dynamics as executable code: short active probes first select a qualitative dynamical form, then free parameters are fit from recorded state transitions, giving an inspectable and editable world model for planning. It positions code between opaque neural predictors and hand-built physics engines.

entry.title: PILA: Plug-and-Play Insertion for LLM-native Advertising

author.name: Zhaowei Zhang, Yuhan Fu, Yihang Zhang, Xiaohan Liu, Ceyao Zhang, Xiaoyuan Zhang, Yipeng Kang, Tonghan Wang, Yaodong Yang

entry.summary: PILA reframes advertisement insertion in LLM outputs as conditional response rewriting handled by a lightweight sidecar module, so monetization can be added to API-only or workflow-based deployments without retraining the base model or entangling ads with generation. It aims to limit degradation of the original answer quality.

entry.title: Polistemics: Evaluating LLMs as Information Mediators in Politics & Elections

author.name: Baran Peters

entry.summary: Polistemics is a theory-grounded benchmark that evaluates LLMs as mediators rather than reproducers of political information, using a normative standard of epistemic modesty and varying input clarity, noise and consistency. It is applied to three current models in the context of recent German and Dutch elections.

entry.title: Crystalis: Progressive Nucleation and Semantic Annealing for Coordinated Multi-View Visualization Generation

author.name: Dazhen Deng, Zhaoping He, Xin Qian, Xiaotong Wang, Zi Ying, Yingcai Wu

entry.summary: Tackles LLM generation of coordinated multi-view visualizations, where linked charts share data flows and cross-view interactions and a single field-level error can silently break other views. Decomposes the problem into structured queries over a dependency graph to make structurally correct output achievable.

entry.title: How Affect Propagates among LLM Agents: Emergent Emotional Contagion in Crowd Simulation

author.name: Funda Durupinar

entry.summary: Simulates a crowd of LLM-driven agents that perceive neighbors through visual, auditory, and tactile channels and appraise them in light of personality, memory, and context, with no hand-coded rule for transferring emotion between agents. Reports that emotional contagion emerges purely from the perception-appraisal-expression loop.

entry.title: Finding Optimal Cost-Bounded Plan Reductions: Refined Model

author.name: Martha Del Toro, Raquel Fuentetaja, Angel Garc\'ia-Olaya

entry.summary: Studies how to extract from an already computed plan a valid ordered subplan that maximizes utility under a newly imposed cost bound, removing actions supporting low-utility goals while preserving executability and original ordering. Proves the decision problem NP-complete and gives two exact solution methods based on oversubscription planning and integer linear programming.

entry.title: A Density-Matrix Framework for Electronic-Structure Analysis of Functional-Group and Salt Effects in Lithium-Metal Electrolytes

author.name: Mingkang Liu, Huize Yu, Yanbin Gao, Nan Yao, Xiang Chen, Lei Shen

entry.summary: Describes a density-matrix-centered machine learning platform for predicting electronic structure of lithium-metal battery electrolytes, covering functional-group and salt-anion effects across diverse solvation shells. It aims to replace expensive quantum-chemical scans in electrolyte design.

entry.title: OmniDelta: Skill-Driven Budget Allocation for Token Compression in OmniLLMs

author.name: Haoyang Huang, Wenjie Huang, Tianqi Xu, Hongyaoxing Gu, Kang Tan, Yikai Fu, Yuhao Shen, Tianyu Liu, Baolin Zhang, Jun Zhang, Xinyi Hu, Jun Dai, Shuang Ge, Lei Chen, Yue Li, Mingchen Wang, Meng Zhang

entry.summary: OmniDelta is a training-free framework that allocates token compression budgets across audio and video modalities based on inferred task intent, then distributes budget within each modality by content, instead of using uniform budgets or raw query-modality similarity. It reduces memory and inference cost for omni-modal LLMs handling long audio-video inputs.

entry.title: HiSkill: Empowering LLM Agents with Hierarchical Skill Graphs

author.name: Yu Hao, Jinxuan Cai, Qi Zhang, Yawen Li, Zhiqiang Zhang, Chuan Shi, Cheng Yang

entry.summary: HiSkill organizes agent experience into a directed hierarchical graph linking high-level reusable skills to executable atomic operations with typed decomposition, transition, and composition edges, instead of storing flat independent skill texts. Aims to close the gap between abstract skills and grounded actions in long-horizon tasks.

entry.title: CHARM: A Multimodal Graph Foundation Model with Hierarchical Context Modeling for Zero-Shot Transfer

author.name: Ankang Yang, Jitao Zhao, Di Jin, Yuxiao Huang, Dongxiao He

entry.summary: CHARM is a multimodal graph foundation model with hierarchical context modeling designed for zero-shot transfer across graph domains where nodes carry text and images, avoiding per-domain fine-tuning. Targets an underexplored intersection of graph foundation models and multimodal node attributes.

entry.title: Unlocking Spatial Grounding in Large Audio-Visual Retrieval models

author.name: Hugo Malard, Michel Olvera, Sanjeel Parekh, Ga\"el Richard, Slim Essid, St\'ephane Lathuili\`ere

entry.summary: Shows that large audio-visual retrieval models trained only for global alignment still contain fine-grained spatial information in intermediate visual tokens, and exploits this to localize sound sources without pixel-level supervision. Demonstrates that spatial detail is lost by upper-layer pooling rather than never learned.

entry.title: Preliminary Guidelines for Using and Evaluating GenAI Tools to Support Systematic Literature Reviews

author.name: Barbara Kitchenham, Sebasti\'an Pizard, Lech Madeyski, Ronnie de Souza Santos, Martin Shepperd, David Budgen

entry.summary: Provides preliminary guidelines for using and evaluating generative AI tools in systematic literature reviews, derived from a rapid review of existing guidance plus the authors' own extensive SLR experience. Aims to protect the rigour, reliability and transparency that reviews require.

entry.title: CondPSE: A Polynomial-Filtered Structural Encoder with Conditional Modulation for Graphs

author.name: Woohyun Lee, Hogun Park

entry.summary: Presents a learned positional and structural encoder for graphs that applies a learnable polynomial filter bank to Gaussian node probes and modulates the resulting branches with FiLM-style conditioning on local and global signals. Intended as a reusable frozen encoder for downstream graph models limited by message-passing expressivity.

entry.title: MyMentorLLM: A psychotherapy GenAI environment with multimodal voice/text patients, trainees and experts for deliberate practice

author.name: Rodolfo Rizzi, Alessandro Grecucci, Massimo Stella

entry.summary: MyMentorLLM is a multimodal voice and text simulation environment that generated 2,100 synthetic CBT training sessions pairing DSM-5-grounded simulated patients, trainee therapists and expert supervisors. The work analyzes emotional dynamics, therapeutic competence and diagnostic accuracy to explore scalable deliberate practice for psychotherapy training.

entry.title: Evaluating VLMs for Autonomous Agent-Driven Geometry Clipping Detection in Video Game QA

author.name: Carlos Celemin, Benedict Wilkins, Adri\'an Barahona-R\'ios, Saman Zadtootaghaj, Nabajeet Barman

entry.summary: The authors evaluate six recent vision-language models zero-shot on detecting geometry clipping bugs in video games, using an exploration agent plus automatic frame-level labeling to avoid manual annotation. All models pick up some visual cues of clipping but produce substantial false positives, and results are sensitive to prompt phrasing.

entry.title: Face De-Identification: A Domain-Centric Survey from Capture to Processing

author.name: Hui Wei, Hao Yu, Guoying Zhao

entry.summary: A survey of face de-identification organized by where privacy protection is applied, spanning post-capture pixel editing, sensor-level privacy mechanisms during acquisition, and physical-domain protections. It maps how the field is moving from post-processing toward privacy-by-design in the sensing pipeline.

entry.title: Detecting Knowledge Inconsistencies Across Text, Tables, and Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Fanfu Wei, Thibault Ehrhart, Rapha\"el Troncy

entry.summary: Kontrast builds a taxonomy of cross-modal knowledge inconsistencies among Wikipedia text, tables and Wikidata, then uses text-to-SPARQL plus LLM reasoning to detect and categorize conflicts. Because these sources feed pretraining and retrieval pipelines, unresolved conflicts propagate into model behavior.

entry.title: HeAD-CP: Heterophily-Aware Diffused Conformal Prediction Sets for Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Phan Binh Nguyen Lam, Nguyen Thai Anh

entry.summary: HeAD-CP shows that the standard graph conformal prediction method, which diffuses non-conformity scores uniformly along edges, implicitly assumes homophily and actively hurts on heterophilic graphs. It replaces the uniform coefficient with node-wise coefficients from a label-free local homophily estimate.

entry.title: Breaking the Periodicity Assumption: Robust Tensorial Multi-View Clustering via Graph-Spectral Low-Rank Learning

author.name: Jintian Ji, Xingsu Li, Songhe Feng

entry.summary: This paper shows that FFT-based tensorial multi-view clustering methods secretly depend on samples being ordered by class, which creates artificial local continuity along the sample mode and favorable spectral structure. Random permutation of sample order collapses their reported advantage, motivating a graph-spectral low-rank alternative.

entry.title: Influence of Prompt Engineering on Small Language Models for Guarded Query Routing

author.name: Richard \v{S}l\'eher, William Brach, Kristi\'an Ko\v{s}\v{t}\'al, Lukas Galke Poech

entry.summary: Evaluates 22 compact open-weight small language models on guarded query routing, where a router must both direct in-distribution queries and reject unsafe or out-of-scope ones, scored by the harmonic mean of both accuracies on a benchmark called GQR-Bench. Mid-size SLMs approach frontier routing quality at far lower latency, with format-following failures being the main cause of degradation, partially fixable via prompt design.

entry.title: WHTMix: Efficient Stereo Depth Estimation via Walsh-Hadamard Token Mixing

author.name: Prathyush Sajith, Emadeldeen Hamdan, Ahmet Enis Cetin

entry.summary: WHTMix replaces the quadratic joint self-attention stage in stereo transformers with a data-independent Walsh-Hadamard token mixer operating at log-linear cost, while retaining data-dependent cross-attention for left-right correspondence. It matches attention baselines on end-point error with reduced compute.

entry.title: LaP-Forensics: Latent-Pixel Consistency Guided Multimodal Reasoning for Deepfake Detection

author.name: Can Wang, Yuhao Wang, Yushe Cao, Canran Xiao, Fei Shen

entry.summary: LaP-Forensics detects deepfakes by pairing RGB semantics with residual maps from a frozen diffusion inversion-reconstruction reference, then producing structured where-what-why explanations and artifact masks, refined with GRPO reinforcement learning rewarding mask overlap and evidence structure. It targets generators that leave few surface artifacts.

entry.title: AVE-Compass: Towards Holistic Evaluation for Audio-Video Editing Abilities

author.name: Yuqing Wen, Yukai Huang, Qianqian Xie, Jiangtao Wu, Yibin Lin, Yikai Gu, Jialu Chen, Yuanxing Zhang, Jiaheng Liu

entry.summary: AVE-Compass benchmarks joint audio-video editing with 145 source videos, 196 audio-visually coupled instructions, and nearly 2,700 checklist items, evaluating instruction following, fidelity, realism, and editing intent through checklist-based multimodal judging. It targets the gap where existing benchmarks test silent-video edits or isolated audio edits.

entry.title: FIRMGrasp: A Friction-Informed Risk Margin for Robust Grasp Synthesis

author.name: Clinton Enwerem, John S. Baras, Calin Belta

entry.summary: FIRMGrasp introduces grasp quality metrics that account for uncertainty in the friction coefficient by evaluating force-closure margins at the conditional value-at-risk of the adverse friction tail, yielding a risk-adjusted margin with proved monotonicity properties. Classical metrics assume a single known friction value and cannot predict failures across plausible friction ranges.

entry.title: Semiconductor Fabs IV: The Safety

author.name: nomagicpill

entry.summary: Fourth installment of a detailed series on semiconductor fabrication facilities, this one covering physical and process safety philosophy, including why automation reduces human-error hazards and how interlock overrides should be deliberate rather than accidental. The author discloses using an Anthropic model for two text blocks and interactive animations.

entry.title: PATHFinder Agent for Tailored Prenatal Care

author.name: Vaibhav Balloli, Carissa Samuel, Samia Abdelnabi, Alex Peahl, Elizabeth Bondi-Kelly

entry.summary: An end-to-end conversational agent that collects patient health and social context, produces individualized prenatal care plans aligned with recent obstetric guidelines, and surfaces local community resources, with a clinician oversight stage. Evaluates frontier LLMs within the four-stage workflow.

entry.title: Extended Reality as a Mediation Layer for Situated Human Control in Human-Robot Teaming

author.name: Jens Grubert, John Dudley, Eyal Ofek, Per Ola Kristensson

entry.summary: A position paper reframing extended reality in human-robot teaming as a mediation layer for situated human control, meaning the ability to understand, shape, authorize and interrupt robot actions in context. Grounded in bedside nursing, multi-arm supervisory control and collaborative assembly scenarios.

entry.title: Spend Experts Where You Are Unsure: Confidence-Adaptive Routing for Mixture-of-Experts LoRA

author.name: Tom Saliencro, Rohan Desai, Priya Nair, Maya Lindqvist, Daniel Whitmore

entry.summary: CARE replaces fixed top-k routing in mixture-of-experts LoRA with nucleus-style routing: experts are admitted until cumulative router mass crosses a threshold, with extra experts when admitted experts disagree, and a controller keeps the average expert budget fixed. The idea is to spend adaptive compute on tokens the model is uncertain about.

entry.title: Probabilistic Symbolic Regression for Equation Discovery via Operator-induced and Regularized Symbolic Forests

author.name: Somjit Roy, Pritam Dey, Bani K. Mallick, Debdeep Pati

entry.summary: This work casts symbolic regression probabilistically, representing equations as ensembles of symbolic trees with a complexity-regularizing prior over topology and an Occam-window based posterior treatment. It aims to give calibrated uncertainty over discovered equations rather than a single heuristic-search result.

entry.title: WorkSurface-Bench: Benchmarking Enterprise Agents on Multi-Surface Knowledge Routing

author.name: Hao Liang, Meiyi Qiang, Sizhe Qiu, Linzhuang Sun, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: WorkSurface-Bench evaluates whether enterprise agents first choose the right knowledge surface (documents, tables, or dependency graphs) before retrieving or computing, with 1,151 atomic tasks whose answers are auditable via executed queries, verified text spans and graph traversals. It isolates surface routing as a distinct capability from retrieval and tool use.

entry.title: Claude Opus 5 Is Highly Capable, But Is No Mythos

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: A detailed independent evaluation of Anthropic's Claude Opus 5, released a few days before this coverage date, framing it not as a frontier-capability leap but as a cheaper, more permissive model that approaches Fable-level performance for most practical work. The reviewer argues it lacks the autonomous multi-step exploit-chaining ability of the Mythos tier and is best used as a strong subagent at medium effort settings.

entry.title: RRS-10K: A Multitask Vision-Language Model Benchmark for Rare Remote Sensing Image Interpretation

author.name: Yuqiao Lai, Jiancheng Qi, Fei Wang, Yuxin Liu, Kun Li, Ye Chen, Yan Gao, Yanyan Wei

entry.summary: Releases a benchmark of roughly ten thousand rare, military-related remote sensing images with question-answer pairs spanning perception, reasoning, and robustness across twenty leaf tasks. Targets the blind spot in existing benchmarks that are dominated by common urban and rural imagery.

entry.title: Everyone is unique: Towards Behaviorally Heterogeneous Negotiation Dialogue Systems for Debt Collection

author.name: Yuhang Yang, Kai Tang, Chao Ye, Haobo Wang, Qiqi Luo, Jinguang Zheng, Zhixin Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces a persona-enriched benchmark for debt collection negotiation dialogue that models behaviorally heterogeneous debtors instead of assuming static rational users with fixed preferences. Positions the domain as a high-stakes testbed for human-centered dialogue systems.

entry.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation in LLMs for Mental Health: Quantifying the Incremental Contribution of Retrieval Within a Layered Safety Architecture

author.name: Anand Gupta, Akshat Surolia, Shubham Mishra, Shakil Imtiaz, Chaitali Sinha

entry.summary: Quantifies how much retrieval augmentation adds on top of the rule-based filters, symbolic escalation, and neural classifiers already used in commercial digital mental health products, evaluating multiple configurations for intent detection in volatile situations. Isolates the incremental contribution of a single safety layer, which is usually unmeasured.

entry.title: Beyond Predictive Accuracy: A Reliability-Aware Audit of Molecular Representations for Human Olfaction

author.name: Kai Lun Huang (California State University, Fullerton), Wei Chieh Sun (University of Washington)

entry.summary: Audits pretrained molecular encoders for human olfaction along four reliability axes: global perceptual geometry, incremental value beyond classical chemistry descriptors, cross-dataset replication, and transfer to unseen mixture components, comparing transformer encoders against RDKit descriptors and fingerprints. Argues downstream accuracy alone does not demonstrate that a representation captures real scientific structure.

entry.title: Automatic Knowledge Graph Construction and Query for Earthquake Catalogs

author.name: Yuxin Zhou, Huai Zhang, S. Mostafa Mousavi

entry.summary: Applies graph-based retrieval-augmented generation directly to raw earthquake catalog tables to build queryable knowledge graphs for three seismic sequences, enabling open-ended questions about sequence character without manual spatiotemporal windowing. Includes a reservoir swarm, Ridgecrest 2019, and the Maduo aftershock sequence.

entry.title: A Human-in-the-Loop Corpus for LLM-Based Simplification of Scientific Summaries

author.name: Kyuri Im, Michael F\"arber

entry.summary: Builds a human-in-the-loop corpus for simplifying scientific summaries, first generating baselines with a small GPT-4 class model, then having non-specialist STEM readers flag difficult text and computer science experts produce reference simplifications informed by that feedback. Targets cross-disciplinary accessibility of research.

entry.title: A2TTA: Anchored-and-Agile Test-Time Adaptation for Evolving Traffic Sensor Networks

author.name: Du Yin, Xiachong Lin, Yue Tan, Jinliang Deng, Estrid He, Hao Xue, Flora D. Salim

entry.summary: A2TTA is a test-time adaptation method for traffic forecasting that handles evolving sensor graphs, where new sensors and edges appear and temporal shifts occur at multiple time scales. It pairs a stable anchor component with a fast-adapting one to avoid catastrophic drift during deployment.

entry.title: Does Runtime Topology Context Improve LLM-Generated Kubernetes Security Patches?

author.name: Farooq Shaikh

entry.summary: This study asks whether giving an LLM the live Kubernetes service call graph improves the security patches it generates from posture-management findings. The concern is that context-free patches can be technically compliant yet break runtime service dependencies and cascade failures across a cluster.

entry.title: Beyond Single-Episode Optimization: Sliding-Window Aware Generative Auto-Bidding for Long-Term Advertising Effectiveness

author.name: Binglin Wu, Chuan Yue, Yingyi Zhang, Xianneng Li, Ruyue Deng, Weiru Zhang, Xiaoyi Zeng

entry.summary: SWAG-Bid moves auto-bidding beyond per-day episodes by optimizing against sliding seven-day efficiency windows that platforms actually use for evaluation, handling the cross-episode coupling this creates. A hierarchical generative framework sets daily targets while anticipating future market conditions.

entry.title: Learned, Relied Upon, or Necessary? Separating Checkpoint Dependence from Task-Level Value in Sheaf GNNs

author.name: Yi Liu

entry.summary: This work separates two frequently conflated claims about learned restriction maps in sheaf graph neural networks: whether a fixed checkpoint relies on them, versus whether learned transport still helps once the rest of the model is retrained without that capacity. A task-null theorem explains why the two can diverge because labels identify only transported classifier directions.

entry.title: Data-Dependent Regret and Polyak Corrections for Constrained Online Convex Optimization

author.name: Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: The paper sharpens regret analysis for constrained online convex optimization with a Polyak feasibility step by retaining observed gradient accumulation instead of a worst-case envelope and identifying a nonnegative correction term measuring cumulative constraint slack. This yields data-dependent bounds that can be much tighter than the standard square-root-T result.

entry.title: AMPBench-MT: A Homology-Controlled Benchmark for Antimicrobial Peptide Potency, Spectrum, and Safety Prediction

author.name: Ziheng Zhou, Huiyu Luo, Xiaohu Zhu, Nan Wang, Xuebiao Qin, Chaoyan Zhang, Jun Yan

entry.summary: AMPBench-MT is a homology-controlled benchmark that unifies antimicrobial peptide recognition, species-conditioned potency regression, spectrum prediction and safety proxies like hemolysis and toxicity in one provenance-preserving protocol. It targets the gap between binary AMP classification and the assay evidence real discovery decisions require.

entry.title: Unifying Active Learning and Semi-Supervised Learning for Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Bahram Jafrasteh, Cheng Wan, Heejong Kim, Johannes C. Paetzold, Qingyu Zhao

entry.summary: RegAL unifies active learning and semi-supervised learning for medical image segmentation under a shared topology-aware Pareto objective, addressing the mismatch that arises when the two are optimized separately in ultra-low-label cold-start regimes. It jointly decides which volumes to annotate and how to exploit unlabeled data.

entry.title: IMPRINT: Image-Conditioned Query Enrichment for Long-Tail Object Goal Navigation

author.name: Jelin Raphael Akkara, Filippo Ziliotto, Luciano Serafini, Lamberto Ballan, Tommaso Campari

entry.summary: IMPRINT improves zero-shot object goal navigation for long-tail categories by enriching text queries with web-retrieved images, encoding them with a vision-language model and matching against a queryable semantic map to produce context-aware localization. It requires no training or changes to the navigation policy.

entry.title: Beyond Background Bias: Saliency-Driven Prototype Alignment for Dataset Distillation

author.name: Yawen Zou, Wenqi Cai, Guang Li, Ling Xiao, Chunzhi Gu, Chao Zhang

entry.summary: A dataset distillation method that builds class-discriminative latent prototypes guided by saliency, so synthesized compact datasets are not contaminated by background regions weakly aligned with the class signal. It aims to improve generalization of diffusion-based distillation in visually complex domains.

entry.title: Few-Shot Open-Vocabulary Remote Sensing Segmentation via Textual Inversion

author.name: Junhyuk Heo, Junghwan Park

entry.summary: Shows that much of the gap in open-vocabulary segmentation on overhead imagery comes from the text query being a weak address into the vision-language embedding space, not from the segmentation model itself. It recovers a better address via textual inversion on a frozen model using a few examples, keeping inference text-only.

entry.title: TIGA: Trajectory-Injected Generative Attack against Black-box AIGC Detectors

author.name: Xia Du, Zhuosen Bao, Zheng Lin, Jizhe Zhou, Jiawei Lian, Chi-man Pun, Jun Luo, Wei Ni, Symeon Chatzinotas

entry.summary: TIGA evades black-box AI-generated-content detectors by steering the DDIM latent trajectory during a single diffusion sampling pass, requiring no source image, no training, and no modification of the frozen generator. This avoids the visible or statistical artifacts introduced by post-hoc perturbation attacks.

entry.title: Mitigating the Impact of Retention Loss on Inference Accuracy in 65 nm Single-Poly Floating-Gate Analog In-Memory Computing

author.name: Mirko Brazzini, Giulio Filippeschi, Alessandro Catania, Sebastiano Strangio, Giuseppe Iannaccone

entry.summary: Demonstrates experimentally on a 65 nm single-poly floating-gate analog in-memory computing array that circuit-level compensation combined with batch-normalization recalibration can recover baseline inference accuracy on CIFAR-scale networks even 60 days after programming. It tackles retention loss, a key barrier to analog compute deployment.

entry.title: Egocentric Station Holding of Robotic Fish in Unknown Turbulent Background Flow

author.name: Xiaozhu Lin, Xu Huang, Hongru Dai, Xiaopei Liu, Junzhi Yu, Yang Wang

entry.summary: SWiFT is a reinforcement learning framework that lets a body-and-caudal-fin robotic fish approach a target and hold station in unknown turbulent flows using only egocentric sensing, integrating a free-swimming simulation toolbox with policy learning. Station holding under complex fluid-structure interaction has remained largely unsolved.

entry.title: SGTP: Sampling-based Game-Theoretic Planning for Real-Time Multi-Vehicle Autonomous Racing

author.name: Zhouheng Li, Fangguo Zhao, Mattia Piccinini, Baha Zarrouki, Yuan Gao, Zitong Shan, Johannes Betz, Chen Lv, Lei Xie

entry.summary: SGTP is a real-time planner for multi-vehicle autonomous racing that combines game-theoretic cost ranking with GPU-accelerated sampling of control sequences and dynamics rollouts, followed by explicit feasibility filtering for track and collision constraints. It aims to produce diverse competitive behaviors without sacrificing real-time performance.

entry.title: Sequential Preconditioned Conjugate Gradient Method for Linear Statistical Models

author.name: Guan-Yu Chen, Dong-Yue Xie, Xi Yang, Zun-Hao Zheng

entry.summary: Proposes a randomized least-squares solver that builds a sequence of sketched subproblems with growing sketch sizes, warm-starting preconditioned conjugate gradient from the previous solution and finishing with a refinement on the full problem. Convergence theory, iteration bounds, and complexity estimates are provided along with experiments.

entry.title: ARC’s research agenda: solid mathematics, an unclear safety case

author.name: Ondřej_Kubů

entry.summary: A mathematician entering AI safety begins a series critiquing theory-first safety organizations, starting with an assessment that ARC's heuristic-argument agenda is mathematically solid but does not clearly connect to a safety case. It mainly links to a longer external writeup.

entry.title: Localized Anomaly Detection via Differentiable D-vine Copulas

author.name: Nicholas Andrea Pearson, Francesca Zanello, Davide Russo, Luca Bortolussi, Francesca Cairoli

entry.summary: Replaces the greedy sequential family selection used to fit D-vine copulas with a differentiable formulation that considers configurations jointly, avoiding early commitment to locally optimal pair-copula choices. Applied to localized anomaly detection in multivariate data.

entry.title: JKO-RAG: Distributional Retrieval as Wasserstein Free-Energy Gradient Flow

author.name: Levi Segal, Murari Ambati

entry.summary: JKO-RAG reframes retrieval reranking as minimizing a free-energy functional balancing relevance, entropy and redundancy under Wasserstein-2 gradient flow, using an embedding-geometry ground metric. A linear-response analysis argues why optimal-transport geometry beats KL-style selection for choosing passage sets rather than ranked lists.

entry.title: VAD to the Bone: Ultra-Tiny Speech Activity Detection for Edge Deployment

author.name: Stephen Bauer, Sheila Seidel, Shanza Iftikhar, Scott Veidenheimer, Gorkem Ulkar

entry.summary: kiloVAD is an ultra-small voice activity detector using only standard Mel features and causal convolutions so it runs on commodity embedded hardware, trained with structured pruning, self-distillation and angle-based quantization-aware training. It reports competitive causal per-frame accuracy with about two thousand parameters.

entry.title: Can Deep Generative Models Reproduce Non-Stationary Gaussian Random Fields?

author.name: Daniel Kua, Yan Song

entry.summary: This benchmarking study asks whether flow matching, DDPM, score-based SDE and VAE models can recover the true mean and covariance structure of a known non-stationary Gaussian random field, with oracle and stationary controls as references. It provides diagnostic metrics for spatial generative modeling where ground truth is normally unavailable.

entry.title: Quasi-SVD: Learning a Lie-constrained matrix factorisation for real-time imaging

author.name: Christopher Hahne

entry.summary: Quasi-SVD replaces sequential singular value decomposition with a fully parallel, differentiable factorization that enforces exact orthogonality on only one Lie-parameterized factor and uses soft constraints for the rest. The asymmetric design targets real-time GPU matrix factorization in clinical imaging pipelines.

entry.title: TimeCapsule: Generative Hallucination as a Method for Historical Sensemaking

author.name: Hayk Grigorian, Hamed Yaghoobian

entry.summary: TimeCapsule is a 1.2B-parameter language model trained only on Victorian-era texts to serve as an epistemologically isolated generative archive, avoiding the contemporary concept contamination of standard LLMs. It reduces perplexity on held-out Victorian prose relative to a GPT-2 baseline and produces period-plausible analogies for modern concepts.

entry.title: Room-Mediated Co-occurrence for Zero-Shot Object-Centric Semantic Navigation via Frontier Scoring

author.name: Adam Scicluna, Gavin Paul, Alen Alempijevic

entry.summary: A training-free object-goal navigation pipeline that routes object-to-object relationships through a compact set of room categories, converting CLIP similarities into room probability vectors and propagating scores over a map with fast marching to rank exploration frontiers. It gives interpretable semantic priors without any training.

entry.title: GrocLM: Grocery Category Recommendation in E-Commerce with Large Language Models

author.name: Yuan Zhong, Chuanwei Ruan, Moein Hasani, Tejaswi Tenneti, Haixun Wang, Fenglong Ma

entry.summary: A production-deployed fine-tuned language model for grocery category recommendation that uses two-stage LoRA training to encode cyclical repurchase patterns into weights, plus trie-based constrained decoding to keep outputs within a valid taxonomy. Reports real-world e-commerce deployment.

entry.title: MusiChat: Vibe Composing for Music Creation

author.name: Callie C. Liao, Duoduo Liao, Ellie L. Zhang

entry.summary: A conversational music creation system that supports iterative refinement of existing compositions rather than regeneration from scratch, using a hierarchical framework that separates lyric-aligned structure generation from expressive surface realization. Enables structure-preserving stylistic edits through dialogue.

entry.title: Quotient Dynamics, Effective Curvature, and Implicit Bias in Positive Quadratic Networks

author.name: Pengcheng Cheng

entry.summary: Analyzes gradient dynamics of positive quadratic networks by identifying the factorization quotient space with the manifold of low-rank PSD matrices, showing factor gradient flow projects exactly onto Riemannian flow and deriving effective curvature and implicit bias results. Contributes to theory of implicit regularization in overparameterized factorized models.

entry.title: Distributing Security Controls Through Harness Engineering

author.name: William Robert Gore

entry.summary: Tests whether off-the-shelf security controls can be layered onto commercial AI coding agents through a custom harness, comparing four configurations across a 23-test suite and avoiding vendor lock-in. Relevant to enterprises where security concerns block agentic coding rollout.

entry.title: dtControl2+$\varepsilon$: Trading Optimality for Explainability in MDPs via Decision Trees

author.name: Tereza Kinsk\'a, Jan K\v{r}et\'insk\'y, Tobias Meggendorfer, Sabine Rieder, Maximilian Weininger

entry.summary: Extends a state-of-the-art decision-tree controller representation tool so that users can trade a bounded amount of optimality for a much smaller, more human-comprehensible tree, with guarantees on the resulting policy quality in Markov decision processes. Useful for explainable and certifiable controller deployment.

entry.title: CARE-MH: Towards Unified, Reproducible, and Comparable Evaluation of Mental Health LLMs

author.name: Asher Sprigler, Yixue Zhao, Yi Ding

entry.summary: CARE-MH provides a unified framework for reproducing and comparing mental health LLM benchmarks, finding that reproducibility depends heavily on model output stability and that cross-benchmark disagreement mostly traces to inconsistent metric definitions rather than genuine capability differences. Calls for standardized evaluation configurations and shared metric specifications.

entry.title: Reading Without a Reader: Large Language Models Collapse Reading and Writing into a Single Entangled Code

author.name: Diego Salda\~na Ulloa

entry.summary: Compares input embedding and output unembedding matrices across nine model families using similarity measures calibrated against independent-initialization floors and weight-tied ceilings, arguing decoder-only models collapse reading and writing into one entangled code unlike the doubly dissociable human systems. Offers a cognitive-neuroscience framing of a structural property of transformers.

entry.title: HVM-GraphRAG: Holistic-View Multimodal Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Complex Document

author.name: Xin He, Yili Wang, Wenqi Fan, Qing Li, Qinggang Zhang, Yi Chang, Xin Wang

entry.summary: HVM-GraphRAG constructs a multimodal document graph under a holistic view to reduce noisy and conflicting updates, building reliable indices between concept nodes and supporting multimodal chunks, then searching to avoid expensive traversal. Targets question answering requiring evidence scattered across distant regions and modalities of complex documents.

entry.title: GraphRareBench: An Auditable Graph-Evidence Benchmark for Phenotype-Driven Rare-Disease Diagnosis

author.name: Guiling Guo, Jia Yang, Jiahao Xu, Shuyuan Zheng, Zhonghai Sun, Qiyuan Li

entry.summary: GraphRareBench is a provenance-preserving rare-disease diagnosis benchmark with over 2,300 ontology-derived cases and 18,000 target-confounder pairs, exposing graph-defined hard confounders and source-linked evidence rather than only reporting the rank of the correct disease. It compares supervised rankers against tool-using agents on a gene-disjoint test split.

entry.title: Spectral Truncation in Synthetic Control

author.name: Mojtaba Eslami

entry.summary: Analyzes synthetic control estimators that match treated units in coordinates from the leading temporal singular vectors of the donor panel, plus a hybrid weighting retained and discarded directions. Proves the family collapses to standard synthetic control at full rank and characterizes underdetermination and bias mapping.

entry.title: Multi-Scale Structural Features for Continual, Comprehensible Visual Recognition in a Developmental Learning Framework

author.name: Zeki Doruk Erden

entry.summary: Improves a gradient-free developmental learning framework that builds a discrete topological model of inputs through local variation and selection, replacing a low-expressivity visual feature representation with multi-scale structural features. The framework offers continual learning without replay buffers or task boundaries.

entry.title: Contrastive Representation Learning of Longitudinal Disease Trajectories on Temporal Graphs

author.name: Bastian Pfeifer

entry.summary: Models longitudinal patient data as temporal graphs where nodes are observations over time and edges capture temporal continuity and trajectory similarity, then learns embeddings with contrastive graph neural networks guided by structure-aware random walks. The embeddings support clustering of patients with similar disease progression.

entry.title: Shared Voxel-Map-Based Cooperative Indoor UAV Guidance with a Multi-Agent Soft Actor-Critic Controller

author.name: Thomas Hickling, Dylan Wynne, Yu Su, Nabil Aouf

entry.summary: This work combines a shared voxel occupancy map fused from multiple drones with a multi-agent soft actor-critic controller that acts on ego-aligned bird's-eye-view crops. The integrate-in-world, act-in-ego design supports centralized training with decentralized execution for indoor multi-UAV navigation.

entry.title: FinAbstain: Uncertainty-Calibrated Multimodal RAG for Selective Financial Forecasting

author.name: Dorothy Torres, Wei Cheng, Henan Huang

entry.summary: FinAbstain is an uncertainty-calibrated multimodal RAG framework for financial forecasting that enforces point-in-time retrieval and aggregates agent assessments with contradiction and consistency signals to decide when to abstain. It targets confident model outputs generated from sparse, stale or conflicting evidence.

entry.title: Physics-Informed CNN-LSTM for Street-Scale Urban Flood Prediction: Reconciling Aggregate Accuracy and Street-Level Plausibility

author.name: Luc DCosta, Yidi Wang, Jonathan L. Goodall, Rohan Chandra

entry.summary: A CNN-LSTM urban flood surrogate is trained with three differentiable physics penalties, discouraging water flowing uphill, enforcing local mass conservation with rainfall-adaptive thresholds, and penalizing false alarms using topographic wetness. The goal is street-level physical plausibility rather than only good aggregate error metrics.

entry.title: Zhinv: Real-time hub-height wind field reconstruction using only local sparse observations

author.name: Zongwei Zhang, Chin Chun Ooi, Lianlei Lin, Sheng Gao, Tiantian He, Yew Soon Ong, Junkai Wang, Hangyi Yu, Jiaqi Zhang, Hanqing Zhao, Yu Zhang

entry.summary: Zhinv reconstructs continuous hub-height wind fields directly from sparse, irregular local observations, validated in Northeast China, Europe and Southeast Asia. Fine-grained regional wind knowledge supports wind power regulation, resource assessment and low-altitude environmental perception.

entry.title: TWICE: Two-Clock, Two-Window Learning for Long-Horizon Conversion Prediction in Online Advertising

author.name: Kaiyuan Li, Kun Wang, Zhongbo Wang, Teng Sha, Ming Yan, Yanhua Cheng, Xialong Liu

entry.summary: TWICE handles long-horizon conversion prediction in advertising, where clicks are observed on one clock but conversions mature over a much longer window with delay composition biased by historical click cohorts. It factorizes long-horizon CVR into target-window components to reconcile timely partial supervision with delayed labels.

entry.title: PIcsC: Partitioning-Induced Covariate Shift Correction

author.name: Behraj Khan, Behroz Mirza, Syed Ahmad Chan Bukhari, Tahir Qasim Syed

entry.summary: PIcsC uses a Fisher Information Matrix approximation of divergence between data partitions and a reference distribution as a regularizer, correcting covariate shift that biases model selection in cross-validation, lifelong learning and federated settings. One formulation covers both centrally partitioned and inherently distributed data.

entry.title: MorphUNet: Alpha-Controlled Biometric Transport for Diffusion-Based Face Morphing Attacks

author.name: Taimoor Rizwan, Sara Atito, Zhenhua Feng, Muhammad Awais, Josef Kittler

entry.summary: MorphUNet builds diffusion-based face morphs by treating two-parent generation as alpha-controlled biometric transport, keeping each parent's ArcFace identity evidence in separate token banks routed through parent-separated dual cross-attention inside the denoising network. The goal is to produce morphs that verify against multiple identities, exposing weaknesses in border-control face verification.

entry.title: OpenPVMapper: A Multi-source, Nationwide Database of Rooftop Photovoltaic Systems in France

author.name: Gabiel Kasmi

entry.summary: OpenPVMapper assembles a nationwide installation-level database of over a million rooftop photovoltaic systems in France by reconciling deep-learning detections on aerial imagery with OpenStreetMap and probabilistic building-level detections. It fills a gap where public registries only record installations above a capacity threshold.

entry.title: CD-RMOT-Bench: Benchmarking the Cross-Domain Referring Multi-Object Tracking

author.name: Xiangqun Zhang, Likai Wang, Zekun Qian, Ruize Han, Wei Feng

entry.summary: Introduces cross-domain referring multi-object tracking, where a language-conditioned tracker trained on a labeled source domain must follow natural-language expressions under unseen visual conditions, together with the CD-RMOT-Bench benchmark. It probes robustness of language-guided tracking to domain shift.

entry.title: Towards Reliable Stain Transfer: An Iterative Data-Model Co-Optimization Framework Based on Multimodal Expert-Guided Assessment

author.name: Siyuan Xu, Yan Wang, Haofei Song, Lili Gao, Jiansheng Wang, Qing Zhang, Dan Huang, Boxiang Yun, Hongkai Xiong, Qingli Li

entry.summary: DMCoStain iteratively co-refines training data and model capability for virtual immunohistochemistry staining from hematoxylin-and-eosin images, using multimodal expert-guided assessment to handle pixel-unaligned supervision across heterogeneous biomarkers. It targets both staining accuracy and interpretability.

entry.title: Group Equivariant Diffusion for Anomaly Detection in Computational Cytology

author.name: Swarnadip Chatterjee, Ssharvien Kumar Sivakumar, Anirban Mukhopadhyay

entry.summary: Proposes a group-equivariant diffusion model for unsupervised anomaly detection in cytology whole-slide images, exploiting the fact that rotating or flipping a single-cell patch should not change its diagnostic class or its anomaly score. Standard diffusion models produce transformation-dependent reconstructions that destabilize scoring.

entry.title: Beyond Facial Consistency: Personalized Person Image Generation with Holistic Identity Preservation

author.name: Yuxuan Xiao, Shanshan Zhang, Jian Yang, Shengcai Liao

entry.summary: Addresses the trade-off in personalized person image generation between facial fidelity and overall appearance consistency using a dual-branch baseline plus Dynamic Balancing Scaling, a fine-tuning strategy that coordinates the contributions of the global-appearance and local-face branches. It targets holistic rather than face-only identity preservation.

entry.title: Adversarial Deepfake Generation and an Investigation of Purification-Based Adversarial Detection

author.name: Junghyun Kim, Seunghyun Kim, Jiyoung Woo

entry.summary: A shared-task entry that generates identity-preserving deepfakes evading twelve detectors simultaneously via multi-model projected gradient descent with compression and transformation robustness, achieving 90 percent evasion against organizer detectors. It also builds an ensemble detector combining vision foundation model features, reaching high accuracy on baseline sets.

entry.title: On the Use of Synthetic Data for Threshold Calibration in Face Recognition: Performance and Security Implications for Border Control Systems

author.name: Arto Apila

entry.summary: Investigates whether synthetic face data can be used to calibrate verification thresholds for the European Entry/Exit System at the very low false-match rates required by border control, given legal and privacy constraints on real data. It analyzes how well synthetic score distributions align with operational ones and the resulting security implications.

entry.title: Motion Generation With Environmental Constraints

author.name: El\H{o}d P\'all, Oliver Brock

entry.summary: This work argues that robots should deliberately use contact with the environment to simplify motion planning rather than always avoiding collisions, calling the idea Environmental Constraint Exploitation. It integrates the idea into sampling-based planners such as RRT and shows reduced planning complexity and improved execution robustness in a real-world task.

entry.title: Atmospheric Diffusion-Guided Spatio-Temporal Transformer for Nuclear Radiation Forecasting

author.name: Tengfei Lyu, Jindong Han, Hao Liu

entry.summary: A spatio-temporal transformer guided by atmospheric diffusion physics for forecasting environmental radiation levels across thousands of monitoring stations. Addresses non-stationary station time series driven by decay, weather variability, and human interventions.

entry.title: Dual-Domain Manifold Modeling for Hyperspectral Image Fusion

author.name: Chengxin Xie, Qiya Song, Yangbangyan Jiang, Renwei Dian, Xudong Kang

entry.summary: A dual-domain framework for hyperspectral image fusion that adds explicit geometric constraints in the spatial domain to counter low-frequency bias and exploits local manifold structure induced by spectral similarity in the spectral domain. Targets simultaneous spectral richness and spatial fidelity.

entry.title: Loss Invariance Determines What Concept Layers Encode: Volume Grounding in Echocardiography

author.name: Hyunkyung Han, Min Jung Kim

entry.summary: Examines whether concept bottleneck models genuinely ground their intermediate variables, using left-ventricular volumes as concepts for ejection fraction estimation from echocardiography video. Shows that what a concept layer actually encodes depends on which transformations the training loss is invariant to, so accurate downstream prediction does not imply valid concepts.

entry.title: A Cost-Effective Multimodal LLM Reasoning Framework for Question Answering over Irregular Clinical Time Series

author.name: Frank Nie, Ethan B Liu, Yuan Zhu, Wei Fan, Jindong Han

entry.summary: ClinPRISM is a cost-conscious multimodal LLM framework for question answering over irregular clinical time series, using an irregularity-aware multi-scale encoder plus a temporal evidence distiller to compress sparse asynchronous observations before reasoning. Targets the mismatch between general time-series LLMs and real clinical sampling patterns.

entry.title: Large Language Model for Operations Research Formulation Selection in Multi-Warehouse Inventory Allocation

author.name: Jintao Xu, Yingzheng Ma, Jiong Dong, Yongzhi Qi, Jianshen Zhang

entry.summary: Frames multi-warehouse inventory allocation as instance-wise selection among a library of solver-executable mixed-integer formulations, training a language-model selector with solver feedback to match each instance regime to the right formulation. Applies LLMs to formulation choice rather than to generating optimization code from scratch.

entry.title: From Naive RAG to Deep Agentic Retrieval: An Evolving Context Engineering Pipeline for Regulatory Compliance

author.name: Mishca de Costa, Muhammad Saleh Anwar, Dave Mercier, Issam Hammad

entry.summary: Traces the production evolution of a regulatory-compliance retrieval pipeline at a large power utility from naive RAG through hybrid retrieval with reranking to agentic function calling and finally a deep multi-agent architecture with code-based tool synthesis and explicit planning, documenting the failure modes that forced each transition. A rare longitudinal industrial account of context engineering at scale.

entry.title: When Thinking Before Retrieval Hurts: TraceBound Diagnostics for Adaptive Knowledge-Graph Retrieval

author.name: Partha Sarathi Purkayastha (ETH Z\"urich)

entry.summary: Introduces a diagnostic protocol that adds pre-retrieval query profiles and post-failure trace hints to an adaptive knowledge-graph retriever, and reports that this extra conditioning improves inspectability but consistently degrades retrieval quality with open-weight controllers. A useful negative result on when reasoning before retrieval hurts.

entry.title: Dual-Level Atomic and Coordination Geometry Learning for Crystal Property Prediction Using Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Sanjay Chakraborty

entry.summary: Proposes a multi-scale graph network for crystal property prediction that explicitly models coordination polyhedra alongside atoms and bonds through three coupled graphs, arguing that many material properties are governed by these structural units rather than atoms alone. Extends the standard atom-level message-passing paradigm.

entry.title: MedJudgeRAG: Option-Wise Evidence Judgment with Dynamic Knowledge Graphs for Medical MCQA

author.name: Seongwon Seo, Seung Hwan Cho, Young-Min Kim

entry.summary: MedJudgeRAG builds a dynamic knowledge graph from retrieved documents, issues a per-option evidence verdict for medical multiple-choice questions, and selects a knowledge-utilization strategy accordingly, trained by supervised fine-tuning on teacher-generated structured reasoning traces. Addresses the failure of vanilla RAG when retrieved documents are irrelevant or misleading.

entry.title: REPREC: Representation Driven Parameter-Efficient Recommendation System

author.name: Harshini Kavuru, Dwipam Katariya, Giri Iyengar, Pranab Mohanty, Kalanand Mishra, Kalanand Mishra

entry.summary: REPREC makes LLM-based sequential recommendation cheaper by aligning a single fixed-size user embedding from a frozen sequential encoder into the language model's space, avoiding LLM fine-tuning, extra modules, distillation, or long item-level history conditioning. Prioritizes deployment cost in industrial recommendation.

entry.title: MARS: Multi-Agent Re-ranking for Repeat-Order Food Delivery Recommendation

author.name: Jiahao Tian, Zhenkai Wang

entry.summary: A modular multi-agent reranking framework for repeat-order food delivery recommendation that predicts cuisine then ranks vendors, combining graph-based global preference signals, peer evidence and contextual filtering with pretrained LLM reasoning. Serves as a controlled test of how much strong backbones alone contribute inside a structured pipeline.

entry.title: DRIFT: Direct-Recursive Intervention-Conditioned Forecasting of ICU Physiological Trajectories

author.name: Weixin Liu, Juming Xiong, Congning Ni, Yanfan Zhu, Xingtao Lin, Bradley A. Malin, Zhijun Yin

entry.summary: DRIFT is a hybrid forecasting framework for ICU vital signs and labs that combines a direct multi-horizon predictor with a recursive treatment-conditioned corrector, so that planned interventions such as vasopressors actually influence the forecast. It is validated on two large public critical-care cohorts (MIMIC-IV and eICU-CRD) across 8-, 24- and 48-hour horizons.

entry.title: Sharpness-aware Model Merging with Salience Recovery for LLM-based Cross-Domain Sequential Recommendation

author.name: Huwei Ji, Jiajie Su, Yuyuan Li, Xiaohua Feng, Chaochao Chen

entry.summary: SharpRec merges domain-specific LLM adapters for cross-domain sequential recommendation using sharpness-aware objectives plus recovery of salient parameters, diagnosing knowledge conflict and multi-domain saturation as parameter misalignment and statistical homogenization. It targets scalable multi-domain recommendation without overlapping users.

entry.title: A Cross-lingual Comparison of Human and Classification Model Entrainment Behavior in Code-switched Speech Settings

author.name: Debasmita Bhattacharya, Siying Ding, Alayna Nguyen, Julia Hirschberg

entry.summary: This cross-lingual study examines conversational entrainment in Mandarin-, Hindi- and Spanish-English code-switched speech, finding lexical entrainment generalizes while acoustic-prosodic and code-switching style entrainment vary by language pair. It then shows classifiers detect entrainment but rely on features different from those most salient in human behavior.

entry.title: Interpretable Column Annotation with LLM-Symbolized Decision Process Materialization

author.name: Mengqi Wang (UNSW Sydney), Jianwei Wang (UNSW Sydney), Qing Liu (Data61, CSIRO), Xiwei Xu (Data61, CSIRO), Zhenchang Xing (Data61, CSIRO), Michael Bain (UNSW Sydney), Liming Zhu (Data61, CSIRO), Wenjie Zhang (UNSW Sydney)

entry.summary: SymCA makes table column type and property annotation interpretable by having an LLM materialize a global-to-local symbolic decision process over a label-space skeleton rather than mapping learned embeddings straight to categories. The goal is both better accuracy through label semantics and auditable decisions.

entry.title: Instruction-Tuned Models Locally Reuse Human Syntax More Than Humans Do

author.name: Zandi Eberstadt

entry.summary: By substituting model generations for one speaker's turns in existing human dialogues, this study measures turn-adjacent reuse of grammar rules across sixteen open-weight Llama and Gemma models from 1B to 70B at nearly two thousand matched positions. Instruction-tuned models are found to locally mirror human syntax more strongly than humans mirror each other.

entry.title: Decentralized Scalable Exploration via Emergent Adaptive L\'evy Walks on Minimal-Sensing Platforms

author.name: Wai Lun Leong, Teo Swee Huat Rodney

entry.summary: Proposes a lightweight sensor-driven Levy walk controller for sub-50-gram nano-drones with sparse range sensing, where each robot samples its own Levy exponent to diversify search without any inter-robot communication. The approach yields decentralized, scalable exploration on extremely constrained hardware.

entry.title: DynaBridge: Dynamic Summary-Guided Cross-Task Multimodal Fusion for DASS-Structured Mental Health Assessment

author.name: Shiyu Teng, Haichen Yu, Jiaqing Liu, Hao Sun, Yu Song, Shurong Chai, Ruibo Hou, Lanfen Lin, Yen-Wei Chen

entry.summary: DynaBridge fuses acoustic, visual and text cues with frozen-LLM-generated summaries to predict DASS-21 item-level ordinal distributions rather than only coarse depression, anxiety and stress labels. The design respects the psychometric item-to-subscale structure of the questionnaire instead of treating labels as flat targets.

entry.title: Semantic Space Search Trajectory Networks

author.name: Julian Agudelo, Alberto Tonda, Gabriela Ochoa, Vincent Guigue, Cristina Manfredotti, Evelyne Lutton

entry.summary: This work extends Search Trajectory Networks, a graph tool for visualizing optimizer behavior, from raw parameter space to semantic space defined by a model's predictions on a fixed sample set. Because any predictor reduces to a semantic vector, learning dynamics of otherwise incomparable algorithm families become directly comparable.

entry.title: When Does Deep Representation Learning Help Single-Cell Clustering? A Sensitivity-Aware Diagnostic Benchmark for Biomedical AI Pipelines

author.name: Nguyen Thanh Phong, Truong Viet Vu, Nguyen Ha Thu, Tran An Ky, Tran Hoang Thong, Le Pham Thuy Hien, Nguyen Thai Anh

entry.summary: A diagnostic benchmark of nine single-cell clustering pipelines across ten real datasets asks when an extra deep representation learning stage actually beats classical PCA pipelines. The framing is a practical engineering decision about whether the compute and tuning cost is justified.

entry.title: Mind the Missing Split: Resolving Feature Heterogeneity in Swarm Learning with Random Forests

author.name: Mohammad Tajabadi, Dominik Heider

entry.summary: In decentralized swarm learning, sites often have only partially overlapping feature sets, which makes pooled random forest inference ill-defined when a tree traversal hits a split on a locally missing feature. This paper diagnoses that failure mode and proposes resolutions for feature-heterogeneous collaborative tree ensembles.

entry.title: Optimization with Dynamic Constraint Learning (DCL)

author.name: Ezgi Oztekin, Figen Oztoprak, S. Ilker Birbil

entry.summary: Dynamic Constraint Learning handles constrained optimization when constraint functions are unknown and cannot be queried during solving, by fitting local surrogates from nearby data at each iteration and solving subproblems inside a data-supported trust region. It matches global constraint-learning quality with simpler models and smaller subproblems.

entry.title: A Generalized Tangent Approximation based Variational Inference Framework for Strongly Super-Gaussian Likelihoods

author.name: Somjit Roy, Pritam Dey, Debdeep Pati, Bani K. Mallick

entry.summary: The paper generalizes tangent-transformation variational inference beyond logistic regression to the broad class of strongly super-Gaussian likelihoods, giving structured, geometry-exploiting variational updates instead of black-box stochastic optimization. It targets scalable Bayesian computation with theoretical guarantees.

entry.title: Language as a Material Interface for Creative LLM Interaction

author.name: Jon McCormack, Tace McNamara, Chen Wang, Maria Teresa Llano

entry.summary: An HCI study exploring how creative practitioners engage with an LLM when language is treated as a malleable material rather than a directive prompt, using a tangible device called the Memetic Mixer over a two-week ecological deployment with four practitioners. It identifies distinct modes of associative, symbolic and temporally extended language use that current chat interfaces do not support.

entry.title: Diff-ID: Identity Consistent Facial Image Generation and Morphing via Diffusion Models

author.name: Taimoor Rizwan, Sara Atito, Muhammad Awais, Zhenhua Feng, Josef Kittler

entry.summary: Diff-ID is a diffusion framework for identity-consistent face generation and morphing, combining ArcFace identity and CLIP appearance embeddings through dual cross-attention and trained on a purpose-built 210K synthetic caption-augmented face dataset. It targets biometric and security-relevant applications where identity drift is unacceptable.

entry.title: MEDit-Bench: A Dataset for Evaluating Message-Driven Narrative Video Editing

author.name: Katsuya Ogata, Zongshang Pang, Mayu Otani, Yuta Nakashima

entry.summary: MEDit-Bench pairs long-form videos with multiple editing messages and multiple professionally produced edits per message, showing that editorial intent substantially changes which shots are selected from identical footage. It proposes temporal alignment metrics and shows existing summarization-style saliency assumptions fail to capture this diversity.

entry.title: Hyperspectral Intrinsic Decomposition: Joint Recovery of Reflectance and Photometric Components for Non-Lambertian Scenes

author.name: Hao Ye, Zhan Shi, Chenglong Huang, Tao Lv, Mingjie Ji, Qiu Shen, Xun Cao

entry.summary: Revisits the dichromatic reflection model to develop a unified hyperspectral intrinsic decomposition method that jointly recovers reflectance and photometric components for non-Lambertian scenes without auxiliary inputs. It moves beyond the Lambertian and simplified-specularity assumptions of prior work.

entry.title: Gaussian Volumetric Representation for Efficient Shear-Warp Visualization

author.name: Mayuri Mathur (Indraprastha Institute of Information Technology Delhi), Ojaswa Sharma (Indraprastha Institute of Information Technology Delhi)

entry.summary: Proposes a Gaussian-based volumetric representation for medical volume rendering, optimized with Monte Carlo volumetric estimation so training can use a sparse voxel subset while remaining consistent with the dense objective, plus curriculum-based slice sampling. It targets fast, faithful visualization of large medical volumes.

entry.title: HOME: Robust Hough-space Matching Method for Structured and Textureless Videos

author.name: Masaki Satoh

entry.summary: HOME is a training-free feature matching front-end that maps images into Hough space so global linear structures become stable local extrema used for matching, targeting structured or textureless environments where point features like ORB fail. It is designed to be ultra-lightweight for real-time edge robotics.

entry.title: RDVSv2: A Large-scale Benchmark for RGB-D Video Salient Object Detection

author.name: Tianyu Li, Jiahao He, Keren Fu, Qijun Zhao
