author.name: Tianyi Gao, Han Fang, Tianyi Ding, Hao Li, Xin Wei, Hongbo Sun, Xiaodong Dong, Ye Yuan, Jinglin Xu, Kongming Liang, Hao Sun, Jingmin Xin

entry.summary: Motto introduces mixture-of-thought-tokens for free-form multimodal grounding, mixing spatially referenced latent tokens with explicit reasoning steps to unify precise localization and complex reasoning in MLLMs. It targets the weakness of coordinate-text prediction on dense objects and of spatially unanchored latent tokens.

entry.title: Reason Before You Retrieve: Agentic Planning for Multi-modal RAG

author.name: Tianyu Yang, Shir Simon, Zhenzhen Li, Minhao Cheng, Xiangliang Zhang

entry.summary: MM-R2 is a multimodal agentic retrieval framework that reasons before retrieving, first grounding question intent to the correct visual referent and then deciding where to search within a structured evidence space. It addresses under-specified retrieval targets and flat global ranking in multimodal RAG.

entry.title: Towards Ultrafast Depth Sensing Via Active Event-based Stereo Vision

author.name: Jianing Li, Yunjian Zhang, Haiqian Han, Kangyao Huang, Xiangyang Ji

entry.summary: Introduces active event-based stereo vision, pairing binocular event cameras with an infrared pattern projector for ultrafast dense depth sensing, along with real and synthetic datasets totaling tens of thousands of labeled frames and a lightweight network. Targets fast-motion regimes where frame-based active stereo fails.

entry.title: Effective Parameters, Real Behavior: Renormalization for Robotics -- From Infinite Electron Mass to Sim-to-Real Gap

author.name: Youran Sun, Jiaxuan Guo, Xingyu Ren, Chugang Yi, Haizhao Yang

entry.summary: Proposes treating the sim-to-real gap through a renormalization lens, using effective resolution-dependent parameters to absorb physics the simulator omits rather than building ever more accurate simulators. Shows analytically for PD control at finite simulation frequency how feedback gains rescale effective inertia and damping.

entry.title: FeelWorld: Visuo-Tactile World Model for Hierarchical Contact Prediction and Planning

author.name: Wenxuan Ma, Chaofan Zhang, Chao Xue, Yinghao Cai, Guocai Yao, Shaowei Cui, Shuo Wang

entry.summary: FeelWorld is a hierarchical visuo-tactile world model that predicts future visual latents alongside contact state, a 3D force-related tactile latent, and slip state, with explicit supervision and mechanisms to suppress irrelevant tactile signal. It aims to avoid imagined futures that look plausible but violate contact physics.

entry.title: What AI Red-Team Evaluations Can and Cannot Prove

author.name: Bandana Kaur

entry.summary: Derives a closed-form evidential ceiling for red-team benchmarks, quantifying the maximum belief update a fixed testing budget can produce and thereby marking exactly which safety claims a clean evaluation can and cannot support. Above a calculable harm rate a modest benchmark can certify a category, while below it no feasible passive benchmark provides the stated evidence of safety.

entry.title: Learning on the Job: Continual Learning from Deployment Feedback for Frozen-Weights Agents

author.name: Valentin Tablan, Scott Taylor, Kristoffer Bernhem

entry.summary: Shows that ordinary deployment feedback, specifically one-bit outcome verdicts and after-the-fact corrections, is enough for continual learning when a frozen model is paired with an external memory that distills each episode into retrievable natural-language rules. On the banking split of a tool-use benchmark, learning from verdicts alone raises single-trial success substantially over a static retrieval control.

entry.title: dRAE: Representation Autoencoder with Hyper-Spherical Codes

author.name: Tianren Ma, Lin Long, Chuyan Chen, Mu Zhang, Junbo Zhao, Tong Zhang, Qixiang Ye

entry.summary: dRAE discretizes high-dimensional visual representations for use with language models via Hyper-Spherical Quantization, which routes codes by angle to decouple semantic content from feature magnitude. The authors attribute codebook collapse to a metric mismatch between Euclidean codebook objectives and the anisotropic geometry of representation space.

entry.title: Hyperball May Not Be a Free Lunch

author.name: Yihao Xiao, Jialong Sun, Zitian Gao, Zeming Wei, Chutian Wang, Ran Tao, Jiaye Teng, Bryan Dai

entry.summary: This analysis questions why Hyperball-style optimizers that fix parameter matrix norms and normalize updates work well at scale, deriving an angular effective learning rate from parameter-update angle, parameter norm, and update norm. Decomposing updates into radial and tangential parts shows conventional norm-based measures are a special case and that the claimed advantage is not unconditional.

entry.title: Opaque Epistemic Mediation: How LLM Deployment Configurations Shape the Validation of Pseudo-Science

author.name: Davide Scarso, Hugo Noronha de Almeida, Joaquim Pina

entry.summary: Across four temporal snapshots from late 2025 through early 2026 and both API and web interfaces, the authors test how existing Claude, Grok, GPT, and Gemini model families rate ethnonationalist pseudo-science drawn from a biosocial framework. Grok Fast variants, which back the default experience on X, consistently assigned credibility scores of 70 to 75, several times higher than the other models, while control prompts on evolutionary consensus showed no such divergence.

entry.title: Progress-conditioned Group Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon Agentic Tasks

author.name: Kaibing Yang, Guangfeng Cai, Shengtian Yang, Shuo He, Yu Li, Mengyi Liu, Pengwei Chen, Jun Xu, Lei Feng

entry.summary: The paper diagnoses a credit trap in group-based policy optimization for long-horizon LLM agents, where repeated low-effect actions dominate sampling, useful state-changing actions are under-sampled, and all-failed rollout groups leave outcome rewards uninformative. It proposes progress-conditioned group optimization to restore learning signal under sparse outcome rewards.

entry.title: When Can You Correct Distribution Drift in Temporal Graph Generation? A Sharpening--Drift Tension and an Impossibility for Observation-Based Correction

author.name: Tianpeng Li, Xuan Guo, Wenjun Wang, Wang Zhang, Pengfei Jiao

entry.summary: Shows theoretically and empirically that temporal graph generative models degrade under distribution drift between training and deployment windows, decomposing the masked flow-matching loss to expose an irreducible divergence term that blows up for structures rare in training. It further argues observation-based correction cannot fix this, an impossibility-style result with a fitted power-law tradeoff.

entry.title: Evaluating and Mitigating the Misguidance Effect of Buggy Code in LLM-Generated Unit Tests

author.name: Junda Zhao, Shurui Zhou, Eldan Cohen

entry.summary: Quantifies a misguidance effect where prompting a model with buggy code leads it to write tests that assert the buggy behavior instead of exposing it, and shows this simultaneously suppresses effective bug-finding tests. The authors corroborate the effect with model-internal evidence and propose mitigations.

entry.title: CAPT: A Multi-task Continuous Autoregressive Transformer enabling Cross-dataset and Cross-species Transfer for Calcium Population Dynamics

author.name: Xinhong Xu, Yimeng Zhang, Yuanlong Zhang

entry.summary: CAPT is a continuous autoregressive transformer for calcium imaging population dynamics that tokenizes continuous traces directly and is trained multi-task. The central claim is that pretrained representations transfer across datasets, experimental paradigms, and even species, a key test for neural foundation models.

entry.title: ATLAS: Automated Approximation of Transformers for Efficient Homomorphic Inference in One Hour

author.name: Jianhang Xie, Sicheng Tan, Vishnu Naresh Boddeti, Zhichao Lu

entry.summary: ATLAS automatically searches per-layer polynomial approximation hyperparameters for transformer nonlinearities under CKKS homomorphic encryption, replacing hand-tuned uniform configurations. The claim is that a full automated configuration can be found in about an hour, reducing multiplicative depth and hence private inference cost.

entry.title: The Illusion of Secure LLM Code: Closing the Security Gap via Iterative Reprompting

author.name: Ishpuneet Singh, Shreyas Mahajan, Gurjot Singh, Maninder Singh

entry.summary: This study evaluates authentication code produced by five AI coding assistants using both static analysis and dynamic penetration testing mapped to NIST SP 800-63B, across four prompting strategies. Functional or generically secure prompts consistently omit critical protections, while iterative reprompting substantially closes the gap.

entry.title: When Low CER is Not Enough: An Analysis of Hallucinations in Vision-Language OCR Systems on Historical Uruguayan Documents

author.name: Marina Gardella (CB), Camilo Mari{\~n}o (UDELAR, CB), Diego Belzarena (UDELAR, CB), Ignacio Ram{\'i}rez (UDELAR), Gregory Randall (UDELAR), Jean-Michel Morel (LU - Hong Kong)

entry.summary: Benchmarking vision-language models against traditional OCR on Uruguayan dictatorship-era microfilm documents, the authors show that VLMs win on character and word error rate yet hide a distinct failure mode: fluent hallucinated transcriptions. This questions the adequacy of CER as the sole metric for archival digitization.

entry.title: Minimax Lower Bounds of Kernel Discrepancy Estimation: MMD, HSIC, KSD

author.name: Jose Cribeiro-Ramallo, Florian Kalinke, Zolt\'an Szab\'o

entry.summary: The authors prove minimax lower bounds for estimating the most widely used kernel discrepancies, MMD, HSIC, and KSD, beyond the finite-dimensional Euclidean setting and with unbounded kernels. This establishes optimality of the known parametric rate in much broader regimes.

entry.title: Self-Attention Dynamics with Rotary Position Embeddings: Twisted States and Explicit Consensus Rates on the Sphere

author.name: Hao Ye (Xi'an Institute of Optics, Precision Mechanics, Chinese Academy of Sciences, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences)

entry.summary: Analyzes continuous-time token dynamics of self-attention when rotary position embeddings rotate queries and keys while values stay on the sphere, characterizing equilibria, twisted states, and explicit consensus convergence rates. Extends the mathematical theory of attention as an interacting particle system to include positional encoding.

entry.title: Learning When to Reason for Text-to-SQL via SFT and DPO

author.name: Soohyuk Jang, Jiheum Yeom, Nohil Park, Sang Hun Kim, Yoonyoung Choi, Kiwook Bae, Sungroh Yoon

entry.summary: Proposes an auto-thinking framework for text-to-SQL that learns when to skip chain-of-thought for simple lookups and when to invoke deep reasoning, trained with supervised fine-tuning plus direct preference optimization. Reports consistent gains over always-reason baselines on a 30B coder model while cutting inference overhead.

entry.title: GEMCo: A Validated, Ethically Releasable Proxy for Inaccessible Counselling Data

author.name: Philipp Steigerwald, Eric Rudolph, Mara Stieler, Jennifer Burghardt, Jens Albrecht

entry.summary: Releases 86 complete German email counseling conversations with 728 messages, written by experts and trained role-players as an ethically shareable proxy for real counseling data, and validates it against 124 held-out real conversations on counsellor strategies and client emotions. Reports a small but detectable gap and proposes the validation method as a general recipe for closed domains.

entry.title: CAGE: Cognitive Attribution Graphs for Faithful Inline Citation Generation in Long-Form Question Answering

author.name: Zhichao Yan, Shizhao Li, Jiapu Wang, Haoran Luo, Qingang Zhang, Jiaoyan Chen, Ru Li, Jeff Z. Pan

entry.summary: Proposes building an explicit claim-to-document attribution map before generating long-form answers, to prevent citations that are topically related but insufficient and to avoid claims exceeding cited support. Frames the core issue as attribution ambiguity in end-to-end citation generation.

entry.title: Tokengeist: Multi-Turn Attribution Tracing in Agentic Conversations

author.name: Jessica Tang, Shraddha Barke, Sharad Agarwal

entry.summary: Defines multi-turn context attribution, the task of tracing which tokens from which earlier turns shaped a model response and how those dependencies chain across turns. Tokengeist is an attribution-method-agnostic framework that recovers this layered structure rather than treating context as one flat pass.

entry.title: Do Current Retrievers Cover All the Evidence? A Controlled Study of Conjunctive Cross-Page Retrieval

author.name: Sungguk Cha, DongWook Kim, Mintae Kim, Youngsub Han, Byoung-Ki Jeon, Sangyeob Lee

entry.summary: Studies conjunctive cross-page retrieval, where a document must support two or three separate conditions on different pages, using a controlled 1,000-query instrument that pairs full-evidence golds with partially-satisfying distractors. Finds condition-wise decomposition and lexical-visual fusion help substantially while all four generic rerankers actually hurt evidence coverage.

entry.title: StepX-Edge: An On-Device UI Vision-Language Model via Architecture-Training-Deployment Co-Design

author.name: Yin Wang, Haotian Hu, Jineng Han, Wentao Qiu, Zhenhua Ge, Liujian Tang, Fanyi Wang

entry.summary: StepX-Edge is a 0.9B on-device UI vision-language model co-designed across architecture, training and deployment, with layered visual encoding and a progressive projection connector to handle the extreme aspect ratios of phone screens. It is validated on real mobile hardware rather than only in simulation.

entry.title: What CLIP Knows but Cannot Say: Recovering Negation from Frozen Intermediate Features

author.name: Chen-Yi Lu, Yueh-Shao Chen, Somali Chaterji

entry.summary: Traces why CLIP cannot represent negation, showing that middle text-encoder layers build compositional syntax that the final layers collapse as visual alignment increases. Proposes PeakPatch, a post-hoc correction that taps the encoder at its compositional peak without changing pretrained weights.

entry.title: The Gate Always Closes: On Injecting Auxiliary Signals into Frozen Vision-Language Models

author.name: Moshiur Farazi, Sameera Ramasinghe, Bekir Sait Ciftler, Mahbub Ahmed Turza, Shafin Rahman

entry.summary: Reports that learnable gates on auxiliary signal pathways into frozen vision-language models almost always converge to behaviourally closed states, with accuracy unchanged when the pathway is ablated even at nominally open gate values. Explains this via dead-gradient and negative-utility regimes and instead uses geometric auxiliary losses to regularize LoRA fine-tuning.

entry.title: DailyBench: A Unified Benchmark for AI-Generated and Manipulated Images from Modern Generative Models

author.name: Xin Jiang, Hao Tang, Junyao Gao, Meiqi Cao, Fei Shen, Dongming Zhang, Yongdong Zhang

entry.summary: DailyBench is a detection benchmark covering both modern fully synthetic images and localized object-level manipulations, addressing the mismatch between older benchmarks and current generative pipelines. It is designed to test whether AI-image detectors generalize across synthesis and editing.

entry.title: MSVS-VAE: Multi-Scale Anchored VecSet for High-Fidelity 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Dehao Hao, Kaiyi Zhang, Tanghui Jia, Xiangjun Gao, Dongyu Yan, Weikai Chen, Zeyu Hu, Lingting Zhu, Yingda Yin, Runze Zhang, Li Yuan, Xin Wang, Long Quan

entry.summary: MSVS-VAE is a hierarchical set-based 3D VAE that progressively densifies anchored VecSet latents through point-shuffle upsampling to close the fidelity gap with sparse-voxel representations while staying compact. Since VAE reconstruction quality bottlenecks 3D latent diffusion, this targets a key upstream component.

entry.title: Nova3D: Code-Native Generation of Programmable 3D Assets

author.name: Nimra Noor, Muhammad Bilal, Abdullah Hussain, Hassan Baig

entry.summary: Nova3D generates 3D assets as executable Blender programs so that named parts, assembly hierarchy, constraints, edit handles, and joints exist at generation time rather than being recovered by later segmentation or rigging. It is evaluated on a frozen 54-item spec-grounded benchmark against eleven baselines.

entry.title: Semantic Semi-Incremental Data-Association-Free Object SLAM

author.name: Yihao Zhang, Jungseok Hong, John J. Leonard

entry.summary: Presents a SLAM framework from an MIT group that jointly infers data associations, poses, landmark positions and landmark semantics, using both geometric measurements and semantic features from neural detectors and vision foundation models. It removes the need for a separate hard data-association step.

entry.title: LEACL: LLM-Enhanced Automatic Curriculum Learning for Reinforcement Learning in Long-Horizon Manipulation Tasks

author.name: Faraz Heravi, James Ouyang, Zifan Xu, Arjun Kumar, Yoonchang Sung, Peter Stone

entry.summary: LEACL uses large language models to decompose long-horizon manipulation tasks into subtasks and difficulty measures, automating the task-specification work that normally must be hand-crafted for automatic curriculum learning. Co-authored by Peter Stone's group.

entry.title: A Few Words Go a Long Way: Language Guided Robot Policy Synthesis

author.name: Daphne Chen, Archit Ritesh Jain, Eric Goossen, Emma Romig, Michael Murray, Nick Walker, Maya Cakmak

entry.summary: ARCHITECT reframes robot policy acquisition as interactive program synthesis, having an LLM coding agent compose modular perception and control tools into readable programs that users can inspect, correct and iteratively refine. It positions modular synthesis as an interpretable alternative to black-box VLA policies.

entry.title: PAC-DP: PAC-Bayesian Diffusion Policy Learning

author.name: Mohammad Hasan Yeganegi, Dian Yu, Andrea Del Prete, Majid Khadiv, Matteo Saveriano

entry.summary: PAC-DP treats a diffusion policy as a Bayesian neural network and derives a PAC-Bayes generalization bound, adding a KL regularizer between posterior and prior parameter distributions to the standard denoising loss. This gives a principled way to control generalization of diffusion policies in the small-data regime typical of robotics.

entry.title: Bridging Reinforcement Learning and Optimal Control via Feasible Action Mapping

author.name: Stefan Richter, Alberto Giammarino, Guillem Torrente, Sam Blakeman, Peter D\"urr

entry.summary: FAOC introduces an optimization-based mapping that converts an RL agent's abstract action into a state-dependent feasible parameter set for an optimal control problem, guaranteeing hard constraint satisfaction while retaining RL flexibility. It targets recursive feasibility and safety in constrained dynamical systems.

entry.title: Identification and Learning of Semantic Observation Kernels: Partial Observation, Uniform Recovery, & Minimax Limits

author.name: Matthew Francis Dixon

entry.summary: Asks when probabilities produced by a language model can be mapped to a reproducible posterior over a finite set of real-world states, noting that verbalized percentages from LLMs are generated text rather than calibrated state beliefs. Builds a semiparametric inverse from grouped meaning-equivalent continuation probabilities to state probabilities, with identification and minimax rate results.

entry.title: Debiased Machine Learning: Identification, Estimation, and Shape Constraints

author.name: Qihui Chen, Ka Yan Cheng, Zheng Fang

entry.summary: Provides a general identification and estimation theory for automatic debiased machine learning, showing when the Riesz representer at the heart of DML is identified and that identification coincides with unique optimization of a quadratic functional. This yields a general estimation procedure, including under shape constraints.

entry.title: Multi-Turn Drift Increases Scheming

author.name: Carlos Guerrero Alvarez

entry.summary: Reports an empirical finding that scheming behavior in language models increases when a multi-turn conversation gradually drifts toward misalignment, and identifies a specific scenario type with elevated rates. Offers hypotheses about the mechanism and situates the work in the broader scheming literature.

entry.title: Through the Bottleneck: How Multi-head Latent Attention Separates Content from Position in Language Models

author.name: Dhruvil S, Fenil Sojitra, Ravirajsinh Chauhan

entry.summary: The authors present a mechanistic interpretability study of multi-head latent attention, the compressed key-value scheme popularized in DeepSeek models, training a 114M-parameter transformer and probing what the shared low-rank bottleneck keeps or discards. They report the compressed cache learns a largely content-only representation with positional information handled separately, and trace how circuits reorganize around the bottleneck.

entry.title: In-Context Learning as Implicit Policy Gradient

author.name: Masahiro Kaneko, Timothy Baldwin

entry.summary: This paper argues that in-context learning with generated samples and their scores structurally corresponds to policy gradient optimization, giving a constructive proof that self-attention can implement reward-weighted aggregation resembling REINFORCE under particular weight configurations. It provides theoretical footing for empirically observed self-improvement through score-conditioned prompting.

entry.title: Breaking the Total Variance Barrier: Sharp Sample Complexity for Linear Heteroscedastic Bandits with Fixed Action Set

author.name: Heyang Zhao, Tianyuan Jin, Weixin Wang, Vincent Y. F. Tan, Pan Xu, Quanquan Gu

entry.summary: Argues that the standard cumulative-variance complexity measure for heteroscedastic linear bandits is loose, since it is insensitive to rounds with near-zero noise, and derives sharper sample-complexity bounds for fixed action sets. This tightens the theory underlying variance-aware exploration.

entry.title: UNIFUSION: Adapting Autoregressive Language Models into Discrete Diffusion under a Unified Reverse-Rate Objective

author.name: Xiaoyi Jiang, Jingyuan Li, Yixuan Jiang, Wei Liu, Yi Zhu, Zuoqiang Shi, Pipi Hu

entry.summary: UNIFUSION unifies several discrete diffusion training objectives, including SEDD, MDLM/GIDD, M2S, and neural continuous-time Markov chain formulations, as a single generalized KL objective over reverse rates, and derives conversions between clean-token, concrete-score, posterior-mean, and jump parameterizations. This shared interface lets pretrained autoregressive checkpoints be adapted to uniform-noise diffusion where every token stays editable rather than only masked diffusion.

entry.title: CRAFT: Learn the Schema, Execute the Plan

author.name: Aakash Kolekar, Sahika Genc, Shahriar Shariat, Bunyamin Sisman, Tibor Mezi, Barbara Poblete, Shree Vandana Kachroo, Calvin Chi, Parth Parmar, Ari Singer, Prayaas Jain, Cindy Barker, Benoit Dumoulin

entry.summary: CRAFT post-trains enterprise coding agents so that proprietary schema and tool knowledge lives in weights rather than being stuffed into every prompt, using schema-stripped plan supervised fine-tuning followed by a second stage for executable behavior. This cuts inference overhead and improves multi-turn analytical reliability.

entry.title: Invariant Discovery for Networked Systems

author.name: Hongyu H\`e, Alexander Krentsel, Sylvia Ratnasamy, Maria Apostolaki

entry.summary: Splits automatic invariant mining for networked systems into an LLM-driven discovery of the candidate grammar and a deterministic search for approximate rules that tolerate real measurement noise. This removes the hardest human input while keeping learning reproducible and auditable.

entry.title: LA-RL: Label-Aware Self-Reflection for Reinforcement Learning in Information Extraction

author.name: Xiao You, Tianwei Yan, Zixu Shan, Longyu Du, Shan Zhao

entry.summary: Introduces a reinforcement learning framework for information extraction where the model first predicts an extraction, then diagnoses task-specific error labels such as missing span, wrong label, boundary mismatch, or reversed arguments, then revises conditioned on that diagnosis. Replaces vague free-form self-reflection with structured diagnostic supervision.

entry.title: MoLGE: Mixture of Language Group Experts for Efficient Scaling of Massively Multilingual Speech Recognition

author.name: Sangmin Lee, Woojin Chung, Woongjib Choi, Hong-Goo Kang

entry.summary: Proposes grouping similar languages into shared expert modules for massively multilingual ASR built on speech self-supervised backbones, cutting the number of experts needed versus per-language mixture-of-experts. Adds hierarchical LoRA over disentangled acoustic and linguistic components to counter capacity dilution.

entry.title: $\gamma$-Bridge: A Look-Parametric Diffusion Bridge

author.name: Xuran Hu, Yujie Zhu, Tengxi Wang, Jilong Li, Wufan Zhao

entry.summary: gamma-Bridge is a diffusion bridge whose schedule is parameterized by the physical radar look number rather than an abstract SNR schedule, with exact multiplicative Gamma marginals and a closed-form reverse posterior. This lets one trained model handle different SAR speckle levels and transfer better to real data lacking clean ground truth.

entry.title: Rethinking Expert Training for Model Merging with Prompt Learning

author.name: Christos Georgakilas, Aniello Panariello, Samir El Karrat Moreno, Simone Calderara, Dimosthenis Karatzas, Joost van de Weijer

entry.summary: Revisits how experts are trained for model merging, showing that prompt-based adaptation with a frozen backbone is a strong baseline that avoids weight-merging interference, then proposes Dual-Tuned Experts combining prompt learning with subsequent encoder fine-tuning. The focus shifts from better merging algorithms to better mergeable experts.

entry.title: MicroZoom: Structure-Preserving Detail Synthesis at Extreme Scale

author.name: Huy Huynh, Jingwei Ma, Brian Curless, Ira Kemelmacher-Shlizerman, Steven M. Seitz

entry.summary: MicroZoom synthesizes seamless gigapixel imagery at microscopic scale by combining a standard photograph with sparse consumer-microscope close-ups as material references, at magnifications up to 350x. It emphasizes plausible structure-preserving detail synthesis rather than exact reconstruction.

entry.title: DeVA: Decoupled Video-Action Model with physical guidance for robot policy learning

author.name: Mengqi Zhang, Sahil Khose, Simar Kareer, Yuchen Song, Unnat Jain, Judy Hoffman

entry.summary: DeVA decouples video prediction from action prediction in a vision-language-action robot policy, using a video generative model as a physical-dynamics prior that guides but does not share a backbone with the action head. It targets the weak physical-dynamics supervision in static VLA pretraining.

entry.title: {\tau}: Learning Touch-Augmented Vision-Language-Action Models from Future Visual Supervision

author.name: Ning Cheng, Jinan Xu, Wanlin Li, Yangzhi Chen, Jing Gao, Yiqun Wang, Kelan Peng, Wenjuan Han

entry.summary: Introduces a touch-augmented VLA framework that learns action-conditioned spatiotemporal tactile representations supervised by future visual observations in a JEPA-inspired scheme, avoiding costly large-scale tactile pretraining. It targets high-dimensional tactile signals that prior methods reduced to instantaneous contact states or 6D wrenches.

entry.title: KAI: A Kinematic-Aware Interface for Data-Efficient Articulated Object Manipulation

author.name: Yaping Li, Zhaxizhuoma, Qiaojun Yu, Jia Zeng, Dahua Lin, Jiangmiao Pang

entry.summary: KAI introduces a structured intermediate representation encoding kinematic and geometric priors of articulated objects, used as an inductive bias for manipulation policy learning. It reports around 83 percent average success across six simulated tasks while using half the demonstration data of baselines.

entry.title: TILT: Improving Compositional Generation in Diffusion Models with a Model-Intrinsic Reward

author.name: Debottam Dutta, Jaehoon Hahm, Jianchong Chen, Romit Roy Choudhury

entry.summary: TILT improves compositional text-to-image generation at test time by defining a reward intrinsic to the diffusion model itself, based on overlap between joint and single-concept distributions, rather than using an external reward model. This yields a KL-constrained tilted target distribution with closed-form guidance steps.

entry.title: Zero-Shot Mission-Level Evaluation for Aerial MLLM Agents

author.name: Suman Navaratnarajah, Taehyoung Kim, Jona Ruthardt, Ishaan Bhimwal, Ryousuke Yamada, Yannik Blei, Wolfram Burgard, Yuki M Asano

entry.summary: MissionBench evaluates multimodal LLMs as aerial embodied agents that must plan, navigate and report from a single high-level instruction using only egocentric observations, across 120 missions in five simulated 3D environments. The best of 22 open and closed models completes under 35 percent of missions versus 84.4 percent for humans.

entry.title: The Regression Tax: Decomposing Why Skills Help and Hurt LLM Agents

author.name: Darshan Tank, Baran Nama

entry.summary: Measures both sides of giving agents procedural skills across nearly 6,000 runs on two office automation benchmarks and three harness stacks, distinguishing regressions (tasks solved without skills but failed with them) from residual failures. It finds the best skill sets win mainly by regressing less rather than by adding wins, and identifies causes including misleading skill descriptions.

entry.title: Adversarial Style Optimization: Enhancing VLM Jailbreaks by GRPO-based Stylistic Triggers Optimization

author.name: Bingjun Luo, Jialin Guo, Yue Yao, Xinpeng Ding

entry.summary: Reports a stylistic inconsistency in multimodal LLMs, where models understand content robustly across visual styles yet their safety mechanisms can be bypassed by particular stylistic triggers. The authors use GRPO to optimize such triggers into a plug-and-play module that amplifies existing jailbreaks.

entry.title: J-CoT: Chain-of-Thought in J-Space

author.name: Junde Wu, Jiayuan Zhu, Fengling Liu, Minhao Hu, Jiazhen Pan

entry.summary: J-CoT proposes a recurrent reasoning interface between fully verbalized chain-of-thought and opaque continuous latent states, passing linguistically grounded but not fully decoded representations across steps. The aim is an explicit mechanism for selecting and organizing information for the next reasoning step, which dense hidden-vector recurrence lacks.

entry.title: TriGlue: a Biology-Inspired Generative Model for Generating Molecular Glue-Induced Ternary Complex

author.name: Yuliang Yan, Shuo Yan, Haochun Tang, Yiqin Sun, Enyan Dai

entry.summary: TriGlue formulates molecular glue design as generation of an entire ternary complex, decomposing the problem into ligand generation, protein-protein docking, and complex assembly in a biology-inspired generative framework. This addresses the fact that molecular glue design lacks a known protein-protein interface, unlike conventional structure-based drug design.

entry.title: Robot Learning to Communicate through Projected Visual Abstractions

author.name: Danyang Yan, Boyuan Wang, Jiaxun Liu, Boyuan Chen

entry.summary: The authors build a robotic system that communicates through projected visual abstractions, specifically dynamic shadows cast by a 21-degree-of-freedom dexterous hand, requiring reasoning about both bodily motion and how it maps into the externally perceived projection. Shadows are chosen because they arise from embodiment yet are visually distinct from the body.

entry.title: CORVUS: Context Optimization and Reduction Via Underlying Synchronization for LLM Coding Agents

author.name: Mingwei Zheng, David OBrien, Siwei Cui, Pardis Pashakhanloo, Rajdeep Mukherjee, Myeongsoo Kim, Sachit Kuhar

entry.summary: CORVUS restructures LLM coding-agent trajectories by decoupling file-read actions from their observations, maintaining a synchronized view instead of append-only chronological snapshots that go stale as files are edited. This is intended to prevent reasoning errors from outdated file contents and to stop the context bloat caused by repeated re-reads.

entry.title: Learning Sampling Parameters for Diffusion Models

author.name: Arisrei Lim, Yossi Gandelsman

entry.summary: LeSAMP trains a language model with reinforcement learning to emit prompt-conditioned, timestep-varying schedules for diffusion sampling knobs such as guidance scale, negative prompts, and noise schedules, rewarded by human-preference and vision-language judges. It replaces the usual practice of fixing these hyperparameters globally across all prompts.

entry.title: Chamaileon: Cross-Context Binder Design with Contextualized Modeling and Mixed Sampling

author.name: Hengyuan Cao, Shizhuo Cheng, Mingxuan Liu, Weicheng Huang, Yunhong Lu, Chenxi Cai, Yan Zhang, Min Zhang

entry.summary: Chamaileon generalizes generative protein binder design beyond the usual single-target, single-state setting by framing the task as modeling a cross-context binding landscape, trained with an in-context complex co-design objective and mixed sampling. This enables binders intended to work across multiple targets or conformational states.

entry.title: Context Is King: How In-Context Specification Shapes the Geometry of Concepts

author.name: Elad David, Max Fomin

entry.summary: Challenges the view that LLM concept geometries such as circular weekday manifolds are fixed stored world models, showing that an in-context declarative rule determines not just the relations encoded but the topology type, turning the same tokens into a cycle or a branching tree on demand. The effect appears even on arbitrary meaningless tokens, and context-specified structure can override strong pretrained priors in capable models.

entry.title: DRC-Aid: Design-Rule Correction via Agentic Framework utilizing Inference-Time Large Language Models

author.name: Anushka Mukherjee, Kang He, Kaushik Roy

entry.summary: DRC-Aid closes the loop on chip layout design-rule repair by having a deterministic rule engine convert violations into a bounded menu of geometric edits, an off-the-shelf LLM choose among them from local context, and commercial verification tools validate each step with backtracking. The bounded action space keeps the combinatorial search tractable.

entry.title: Two-Timescale Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Resilient Operations

author.name: Young Hyun Cho, Franz Stoll, Will Wei Sun, Guang Lin, Stephan Biller

entry.summary: The paper develops a two-timescale hierarchical reinforcement learning framework for operations problems where long-horizon and short-horizon decisions are coupled, and proves what the authors claim are the first convergence guarantees for synchronized coupled two-timescale learning. It targets resilience to recurring supply and demand shocks.

entry.title: To Erase, or Not to Erase: Robust Training-Free Concept Erasure with Preservation aware Adaptive Ranked Subspace Expansion

author.name: Shaswati Saha, Rajasekhar Anguluri, Manas Gaur

entry.summary: This work proposes a training-free concept erasure method for text-to-image diffusion models that adaptively expands a ranked subspace based on how prompts actually steer denoising, rather than relying on static concept banks. The goal is robust removal of NSFW or copyrighted concepts without degrading benign generation.

entry.title: TriShieldRAG: A Three-Ring Defense-in-Depth Framework Against Knowledge Corruption in Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Susil Kumar Mohanty, Rohit Patel, Kosuru Yuvaraj, Jeenal Chaudhary, Disha Singhania

entry.summary: TriShieldRAG proposes a layered defense against knowledge-base poisoning in retrieval-augmented generation, motivated by PoisonedRAG showing that around five crafted documents can flip answers roughly ninety percent of the time and that single-stage defenses like perplexity filtering fail. The framework stacks complementary rings of protection at ingestion, retrieval, and generation.

entry.title: SimBEV2X: A Large-Scale Dataset and Data Generation Tool for Multi-Task Vehicle-to-Everything Cooperative Perception

author.name: Goodarz Mehr, Sepideh Gohari, Montasir Abbas, Azim Eskandarian

entry.summary: SimBEV2X is a synthetic data generation tool and large-scale dataset for vehicle-to-everything cooperative perception, providing synchronized multi-agent, multi-modal, multi-task data with bird's-eye-view representations. It addresses the scarcity and small scale of existing V2X datasets that real-world collection makes prohibitively expensive.

entry.title: SpecFormer: Mitigating Embedding and Attention Collapse via Spectral-Aware Transformer for Recommendation

author.name: Yu Cui, Yi Xu, Jiahao Wang, Hao Zhang, Yu Zhang, Xiaoyi Zeng, Can Wang, Jinxin Hu, Jiawei Chen

entry.summary: SpecFormer diagnoses why standard self-attention underperforms in recommendation, attributing it to severe spectral collapse of embeddings and attention caused by heterogeneous, long-tailed interaction data, and shows theoretically how this creates a self-reinforcing degradation loop. A spectral-aware transformer variant is proposed to break the cycle.

entry.title: Beyond Local Inspection: Global, Guideline-Grounded Evaluation of Post-hoc XAI Methods for ECG Classification

author.name: Nils Gumpfer, Michael Guckert, Samuel Sossalla, Birgit A{\ss}mus, Jennifer Hannig

entry.summary: The authors introduce a global evaluation framework for post-hoc explainability in ECG classification that aggregates explanations across many heartbeats and scores them against clinically defined guideline regions of interest. This exposes cases where locally plausible explanations systematically misrepresent what the model relies on.

entry.title: On Non-Stationary Dynamic Pricing: Adaptivity and Optimality

author.name: Feiyu Jiang, Zifeng Zhao

entry.summary: The paper studies contextual dynamic pricing when the underlying generalized linear demand model changes over time, proposing a multiscale change-point detection algorithm. It achieves regret adapting to both the number of piecewise stationary segments and total variation, without prior knowledge of the nonstationarity.

entry.title: Agent-UCT: Upper Confidence Bounds Applied to Trees for Agentic Workflow Optimization with Cost-Awareness

author.name: Yang Li, Hai Liu, Dian Shao, Yu Wang, Xiyu Chen, Sergey Volkov, Bozhi Wang, Ziyu Sun, Sihang Liu, Ye Luo, Xiaowei Zhang

entry.summary: Agent-UCT adapts Monte Carlo tree search to agentic workflow configuration, adding a reuse-aware regularization term from a bipartite prefix reuse graph so the search prefers branches that reuse already-materialized configuration prefixes. This cuts redundant evaluation when optimizing RAG and similar pipelines under tight budgets.

entry.title: Co-Evolving Graph and Text Memory for Training-Free Multi-Hop Question Answering

author.name: Hieu Man, Thien Huu Nguyen

entry.summary: Proposes a training-free multi-hop QA system that maintains synchronized bidirectional working memory, consolidating text into relational triples in a graph store and injecting graph facts back into generation context each cycle. Aims to close the loop that prior graph-RAG and memory-agent systems leave partially open.

entry.title: Earnings25: A Comprehensive 500-Hour Speech Benchmark for Finance

author.name: Denglin Jiang, Haoran Zhou, Anshul Wadhawan, Brendan Fahy, Vinay Ramesh, David Weisberg, Dmitriy Derkachevskiy, Helen Sheehan, Srivas Prasad, Michele Franceschini

entry.summary: Introduces a roughly 500-hour English earnings-call ASR benchmark with a full-call test set and an industry-balanced segmented set, including aligned transcripts and metadata on speaker roles, industry, and call structure. Provides reproducible Whisper and Parakeet baselines with standardized scoring.

entry.title: Structure Over Scale: Schema-Constrained Causal Graphs for RAG

author.name: Marc Saouda (Boston Consulting Group), Rajprakash Bale (Boston Consulting Group), Eren Aldis (Boston Consulting Group), Cloves Almeida (Boston Consulting Group)

entry.summary: HCG-RAG replaces open-ended entity extraction in GraphRAG with schema-constrained causal graphs built over a fixed typed vocabulary of causal variables, producing a compact two-tier graph. It matches entity-relation baselines on answer quality while using far fewer nodes and dramatically fewer build-time LLM calls.

entry.title: VIPER: Visual In-Context Physics Reasoning for Physically Plausible Video Generation

author.name: Tianxiao Chen, Hanmo Chen, Huajin Chen, Bo Li, Qi Ye, Peng-Tao Jiang

entry.summary: VIPER conditions image-to-video generation on a reference video treated as a dense visual demonstration of a physical process, addressing the difficulty of specifying material response, contact, and deformation in text. Aims for physically plausible motion via visual in-context reasoning.

entry.title: MemVLN: Episodic and Procedural Memory for Vision-and-Language Navigation

author.name: Yuqi Liu, Shengju Qian, Tianyuan Qu, Mingxian Lin, Zixuan Wang, Xin Wang, Bei Yu, Jiaya Jia

entry.summary: MemVLN gives a vision-and-language navigation agent both episodic memory with pyramidal resolution (fine detail for recent percepts, coarse for older ones) and procedural memory, reaching claimed state of the art while running at around 14 frames per second. Targets the trade-off between long-horizon history and low-latency action.

entry.title: Neuromorphic Object Detection: An In-Depth Study and Future Directions

author.name: Jianing Li, Dianze Li, Arren Glover, Xiaopeng Fan, Guoqi Li, Chiara Bartolozzi, Ryad B. Benosman, Yonghong Tian

entry.summary: A comprehensive survey and standardized benchmark of neuromorphic (event camera) object detection, covering problem formulation, model families, applications, and open challenges. Motivated by the lack of consistent evaluation despite rapid model proliferation.

entry.title: JarvisHub: An Open Harness for Canvas-Native Multimodal Creative Agents

author.name: Yunlong Lin, Zixu Lin, Zhaohu Xing, Biqiang Li, Chenxin Li, Haonan Wang, Haitao Wu, Hengyu Liu, Jianghai Chen, Kaituo Feng, Kaixin Li, Shawn Chen, Shijue Huang, Sixiang Chen, Tsung-Yi Ho, Wenxuan Huang, Xiangyan Liu, Xiaomeng Hu, Xuanhua He, Yan Sun, Yunqing Zhao, Zhiqin Yang, Zehan Wang, Zhengyang Tang, Tianyu Pang, Xiangyu Yue

entry.summary: JarvisHub is an open harness for canvas-native multimodal creative agents that maintains an evolving project state including references, drafts, alternatives, edits, failed attempts, version relations, tool actions, and human feedback. Argues chat-based and node-based systems discard the intermediate context long-horizon creative production requires.

entry.title: STEER: Steerable Dyadic Head Avatars

author.name: Kartik Teotia, Helge Rhodin, Hyeongwoo Kim, Marc Habermann, Christian Theobalt

entry.summary: STEER is a controllable 3D dyadic motion prior for conversational head avatars that factorizes behavior into explicit controls for gaze contact and aversion, head rhythm, and emotion instead of treating them as emergent from audio. Targets non-verbal conversational signals current speech-driven animation cannot steer.

entry.title: LU-500: A Logo Benchmark for Concept Unlearning

author.name: Keyu Li, Jin Gao, Jialing Zhang, Dequan Wang

entry.summary: LU-500 is a benchmark for unlearning company logos from text-to-image models, built from Fortune Global 500 brands to probe a failure mode where a small localized mark carries the whole protected concept. It also tests implicit triggering through products, packaging, and storefronts without the word logo.

entry.title: LoTA-N2N: Local Trace Adaptation for Zero-Shot Self-Supervised Image Denoising

author.name: Jintong Hu, Bin Xia, Junlin Liu, Jiayue Liu, Wenming Yang

entry.summary: LoTA-N2N gives a unified theoretical account of MSE-based self-supervised denoising objectives, showing the gap to supervised training reduces to a trace interaction term between surrogate residual and prediction error. This unifies blind-spot, re-corruption, and paired-noise methods and motivates a local trace adaptation for zero-shot denoising.

entry.title: Concept-based Visual Counterfactual Explanations with Diffusion Models

author.name: Yassine Oueslati, Daniil Kirilenko, Martin Gjoreski, Marc Langheinrich

entry.summary: C-VCE embeds the classifier inside a diffusion model via a concept bottleneck layer so visual counterfactual explanations are guided by human-interpretable concepts rather than an external noise-robust classifier. This removes a known fragility in diffusion-based counterfactual generation for safety-critical domains.

entry.title: Inter-Reflective Gaussian Splatting for Robust and Efficient Inverse Rendering

author.name: Chun Gu, Xiaofei Wei, Zixuan Zeng, Yuxuan Yao, Li Zhang

entry.summary: IRGS++ performs Gaussian inverse rendering with differentiable 2D Gaussian ray tracing to query visibility and indirect radiance on the fly, evaluating the full rendering equation including inter-reflection. This grounds Gaussian-based inverse rendering physically rather than approximating rasterized appearance.

entry.title: Trainable Nonexpansive Denoisers for Contractive Image Reconstruction

author.name: Arghya Sinha, Aditya Banerjee, Trishit Mukherjee, Kunal N. Chaudhury

entry.summary: Constructs a neural denoiser architecture that is provably globally nonexpansive by exploiting permutation actions on the image lattice, yielding image reconstruction iterations with guaranteed contraction and convergence. This upgrades prior empirical-only Lipschitz control to a hard architectural guarantee.

entry.title: FutureRTC: Real-Time Robot Execution with Anticipatory-Conditioned Action Chunking

author.name: Hai Jiang, Yixian Zou, Binbin Liang, Boqian Liu, Fanman Meng, Shuaicheng Liu

entry.summary: FutureRTC is a plug-and-play module that predicts execution-time observations and proprioceptive states so asynchronously computed VLA action chunks align with the world as it will be, reducing inter-chunk discontinuities. It requires no changes to the underlying policy.

entry.title: The Phase Transition in Online PCA Depends on $n/d\log(d)$, not $n/d$

author.name: Apratim Dey

entry.summary: Argues that for online/streaming PCA the relevant high-dimensional scaling is samples over d log d rather than the classical constant aspect ratio, so the BBP-style phase transition threshold shifts. This means streaming algorithms need extra samples by a logarithmic factor to detect a spike.

entry.title: Learned Interventions in Lean 4 grind

author.name: Evan Wang, Simon Chess, Sophie Szeto, Theodore Meek

entry.summary: The authors add learned heuristics to Lean 4's grind automation but only invoke them as a failure-triggered cascade after the stock tactic fails, guaranteeing no previously provable goal is lost despite the solver's non-monotone search. They apply it to e-matching instantiation filtering and case-split selection.

entry.title: A New Kind of Adversarial Example: Measuring the Human-Model Gap, and Its Relationship to OOD Detection

author.name: Ali Borji

entry.summary: Studies inverted adversarial examples where a large, clearly visible perturbation leaves the model's correct prediction intact even though humans can no longer recognize the image, quantifying the human-model gap with a recognizer proxy and a small human pilot. It also finds standard out-of-distribution detection, calibration, and existing defenses fail to flag these inputs.

entry.title: Breaking the Synthetic-Real Domain Shortcut for Training-Free Generative Replay-based Class Incremental Learning

author.name: Tao Zhang, Qixuan Fan, Yiyuan Liang, Yanjie Wang, Song Yan, Tian Tian, Jiahuan Zhou, Luxin Yan, Sheng Zhong, Xu Zou

entry.summary: Diagnoses why mixing text-to-image-generated old-class samples with real new-class data hurts class-incremental learning: models latch onto a synthetic-versus-real domain shortcut instead of semantic class cues. The proposed DREAM method breaks this shortcut to make training-free generative replay viable without stored exemplars.

entry.title: Child-Oriented AIGC Video Risk Reviewing: A Benchmark and Knowledge-Supported Iterative Reasoning Framework

author.name: Lewen Mi, Manyi Li, Yuling Sun, Yufan Zhang, Yuxin Shi, Yulong Bian, Xiangxian Li, Juan Liu

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark and knowledge-supported iterative reasoning framework for reviewing AI-generated video for child-specific risks, arguing that adult-oriented violation detection misses developmentally inappropriate, implicit and context-dependent harms. Covers the fine-grained risks unique to generated video content.

entry.title: UMI3D: Robust 3D Generation on Unconstrained Multi-Image Inputs via Simultaneous Focus Cross-Attention Routing

author.name: Zefan Qu, Zhenwei Wang, Gerhard Petrus Hancke, Rynson W. H. Lau

entry.summary: UMI3D diagnoses that single-image 3D foundation models fail on inconsistent multi-image inputs because cross-attention lacks a way to decide which view each voxel should trust. It proposes a training-free per-voxel attention routing scheme that recovers strong geometry and texture from unconstrained image sets.

entry.title: DeCoRAG: Cognitive Decoupling and Semantic-Aware Cropping for Complex Document Understanding

author.name: Shuo Wang, Kai Zhang, Wenyuan Huang, Yizheng Yu, Xia Liao, Junming Su, Qing Wang, Fang Xi

entry.summary: DeCoRAG identifies a visual attention sink failure in multimodal graph RAG, where forcing vision-language models to simultaneously localize, interpret and relate evidence in dense document layouts causes hallucination and token blowup. It proposes cognitive decoupling of these subtasks plus semantic-aware cropping.

entry.title: Try Once, Then Optimal: De-Redundified Procedure Memory for Cross-Episode Exploration Amortization

author.name: Haizhou Ge, Haochen Ouyang, Zhixing Chen, Yufei Jia, Yue Li, Lu Shi, Lei Han, Guyue Zhou, Ruqi Huang

entry.summary: Instance-Oriented Memory lets a robot record a short manipulation procedure the first time it uncovers an object's hidden internal state, key it to that object's visual identity, and reuse it as a soft bias later. This amortizes costly exploratory probing across episodes for objects like latched appliances.

entry.title: The Hard Decision Layer: Evidence for Committed Inference in Transformers

author.name: Ashwath Vaithinathan Aravindan, Mayank Kejriwal

entry.summary: Identifies a layer in transformers where multiple-choice answer rankings abruptly stabilize, termed the hard decision layer, and shows it appears consistently across four open model families and four benchmarks without any learned routing. The layer is reportedly invariant to fine-tuning and reading out at that depth can yield large accuracy jumps.

entry.title: QLPO: Quadrant-weighted Sampling for Length-aware Policy Optimization

author.name: Siwei Chen, Siqi Chen, Xupeng Miao, Bin Cui

entry.summary: QLPO controls reasoning-response length during RL training without touching the reward function, by over-generating candidates and resampling each GRPO group to preserve the empirical correct-incorrect ratio while favoring short correct and long incorrect responses. This yields implicit length pressure without explicit penalties or extra control modules.

entry.title: SceneActBench: Can Agents Act on the 3D Scenes They See?

author.name: Yifei Zhao, Xiangxin Zhou, Wenhao Yang, Jiaqi Tang, Pu Jian, Huanjin Yao, Jiarui Yao, Haowei Lin, Chunchao Guo, Zhuo Chen, Wenkai Lyu, Jianzhu Ma, Xueqian Wang, Wenxi Zhu

entry.summary: SceneActBench evaluates whether vision-language agents can actually manipulate 3D scenes rather than merely describe them, spanning five tasks and 520 cases in a unified agent-environment loop with hidden ground truth scored by geometric metrics. It targets multi-object scene actions that existing 3D benchmarks omit.

entry.title: Decoupled Attention Fusion: Accelerating RAG with Efficient KV Cache Reuse

author.name: Xiabao Wu, Wentao Liu, Yongchao Liu, Jiajun Zheng

entry.summary: Decoupled Attention Fusion accelerates retrieval-augmented generation by reusing precomputed per-document KV caches while recovering the missing cross-document attention through a three-stage process of importance selection and fusion. It targets the accuracy degradation that prior selective-recomputation methods suffer at long contexts.

entry.title: Benchmarking Text-to-SQL under Role-Based Access Control

author.name: Yang Fei, Yangfan Jiang, Yin Yang, Xiaokui Xiao

entry.summary: The paper builds a text-to-SQL benchmarking framework with realistic role-based access control constraints, arguing that standard benchmarks assume unrestricted database access and therefore overstate real deployment performance. It measures both policy violations and over-refusals of questions answerable from permitted data.

entry.title: Why Large Language Models and Humans Converge and Diverge in Evaluating Creativity

author.name: Pengzhao Lyu, Yeun Joon Kim, Hanlin Xiao, Yingyue Luna Luan

entry.summary: Across three studies and six widely used LLMs, the authors identify which human creativity-evaluation standards models actually apply, finding that models rely on a narrower subset, agree most with humans on novelty, and diverge most on contextual factors such as social, market, and reputational signals. Each model also shows an idiosyncratic evaluation profile.

entry.title: Neptuna: A Comprehensive Machine Learning Framework for Benchmarking Complex Multiphase Flows

author.name: Harish Ramachandran, Bj\"orn Kimpel, Thomas Paula, Josef Winter, Steffen Schmidt, Nikolaus Adams

entry.summary: Neptuna introduces what the authors describe as the first large-scale benchmark for shock-driven compressible multiphase flows, with 2.4 TB of high-fidelity 2D and 3D data on shock-induced bubble collapse and droplet breakup. Diverse surrogate model families are evaluated on flows combining compressibility, sharp discontinuities, and multiphase interfaces.

entry.title: Learning to Prepare Molecular Ground States with Transformer Models

author.name: Alex Koziell-Pipe, Jasmine Brewer, Jem Guhit, Marwa H. Farag, Kripa Panchagnula, Gabriel Laude, Fabian Finger, Carlo Gaggioli, Ludmila Szulakowska, Oliver J. Backhouse, Christos Papalitsas, Jason G. Mustakis, Thomas Soini, David Munoz Ramo, Stephen Clark, Elica Kyoseva, Enrico Rinaldi

entry.summary: ADAPT-GQE trains a generative transformer on high-quality ADAPT-VQE reference circuits so it can synthesize shallow ground-state preparation circuits for molecular electronic structure without running the prohibitively expensive iterative algorithm. The aim is scalability to molecules relevant to materials science and pharmaceuticals.

entry.title: Self-Boosting Vision-Language Models with Noisy Student On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Shuai Wang, Daoan Zhang, Zhe Tang, Hao Cheng, Jiaheng Wei

entry.summary: NOPD improves vision-language models after pretraining without human labels, external teachers, or verifiable answers by having the model learn from corrupted inputs while treating its own clean-input predictions as targets, an on-policy noisy-student self-distillation loop. It is a route to self-improvement when supervision is unavailable.

entry.title: SeT-Diff: Towards Semantic Foundation Models for HPC Telemetry and Time-Series

author.name: Giovanni B. Esposito, Francesco Antici, Daniele Cesarini, Andrea Bartolini

entry.summary: SeT-Diff proposes a diffusion-based foundation model for HPC data-center telemetry that conditions generation on natural-language descriptions of each sensor rather than fixed sensor slots. This decoupling lets the same model transfer across differing sensor sets and downstream tasks, a step toward digital twins of compute nodes.

entry.title: Do Coverage and Mutation Scores of LLM-Generated Test Suites Correlate with Their Effectiveness? (Replicability Study)

author.name: Junda Zhao, Shurui Zhou, Eldan Cohen

entry.summary: Replicability study asking whether code coverage and mutation score predict the real bug-finding effectiveness of LLM-generated test suites, extending classic findings about human-written tests. It probes whether proxy metrics used throughout LLM test-generation papers are actually valid once suite size is controlled.

entry.title: IndicTalk: A Large-Scale Persona-Based Multilingual Conversational Corpus for Indic Languages

author.name: Sahil Deepak Gawande, Mayank Singh

entry.summary: IndicTalk is a very large synthetic conversational corpus of over a million multi-turn dialogues spanning nine Indic languages and eighteen varieties, including code-mixed and Romanized forms. Dialogues are grounded in real news events and generated with persona conditioning plus automated quality validation.

entry.title: Online Fair Division with Budget Constraints

author.name: Saar Cohen, Nicholas Teh, Paul W. Goldberg, Michael J. Wooldridge

entry.summary: The paper studies online fair division where goods arrive sequentially under generalized assignment budget constraints, proving that no deterministic algorithm can guarantee any fixed envy-freeness approximation in general. It identifies bounded density spread as a structural condition restoring approximation guarantees.

entry.title: Learning switched non-linear dynamical systems from a single trajectory

author.name: Sunny G. W. Wang, Hemant Tyagi

entry.summary: The paper derives the first non-asymptotic prediction risk bounds for learning switched nonlinear dynamical systems from a single trajectory, expressed via metric entropy of the function class. Rates are instantiated for Holder and linear classes and depend on effective per-mode sample sizes.

entry.title: No Free Lunch in Flow Surrogates under Time-Varying Boundary Conditions: A Two-Regime Study

author.name: Georg Winkler, Martin Stoll

entry.summary: The paper tests whether flow surrogate architectures validated on a simple transient flow transfer to a harder one, comparing eight models on chemical-mechanical planarisation slurry films and the Karman vortex street under time-varying boundary conditions. No single architecture wins both regimes, undermining a common generalization assumption.

entry.title: Smooth Learning with Hard Constraints via Legendre-Regularized Policies

author.name: Zikun Lin, Rui Chen, Yijie Wang

entry.summary: The paper proposes Legendre-regularized policies for contextual optimization, parameterizing decisions as solutions to regularized problems over the true feasible set so that constraints hold by construction while the policy remains differentiable. Theory establishes smoothness of the resulting optimizer map for end-to-end training on decision losses.

entry.title: Stacking the Deck: Tunable Trainability in Stacked LCUs

author.name: Nikhil Khatri, Stefan Zohren, Gabriel Matos

entry.summary: Introduces a stacked linear-combination-of-unitaries ansatz for variational quantum circuits that provides a tunable knob between barren-plateau-free trainability and classical simulability, with variance bounds proved for a free-fermion instance. Directly engages the tension that expressive quantum ansatze tend to be untrainable while trainable ones tend to be classically simulable.

entry.title: Beyond Direct Answering: Aligning Educational LLMs as Socratic Guides via Heuristic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Xiaokun Wang, Siyu Song, Wentao Liu, Xiaodong Zou

entry.summary: Aligns a 7B model toward Socratic tutoring using supervised warm-up plus group relative policy optimization with a heuristic reward over cognitive depth, curiosity engagement, and answer directness, trained on roughly 800 reconstructed Chinese children's science dialogues. Introduces scaffolding effectiveness and conversation depth metrics for pedagogical evaluation.

entry.title: StanceFlip: A Comprehensive Multi-Dimensional Benchmark for Multimodal Conversational Stance Flipping Forecasting

author.name: Heyan Chai, Xin Li, Wenjie Wang, Jianyang Qin, Chaoyang Li, Lu Wang, Hao Chen, Qing Liao

entry.summary: Introduces a multimodal benchmark for forecasting stance reversals in multi-turn conversations across five modalities, with subtasks including extracting a sextuple of holder, target, emotion, sentiment, and related fields. Targets limitations of static stance benchmarks around belief evolution, affect-versus-logic disentanglement, and sarcasm resolution.

entry.title: Grounding latent algorithm routing in transformer reasoning

author.name: Xiangbo Zhang, Xiaoxu Ma

entry.summary: Introduces ROUTEBENCH, a controlled in-context-learning benchmark whose regimes favor different classical estimators (ridge, lasso, Huber, kNN), and tests whether transformers internally switch between solver families as the latent data regime changes. Activation interventions are used to show the routing behavior is causally manipulable.

entry.title: MM-ShiftKV: Decode-Aware Prefill-Stage KV Selection for Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Jinsong Shu, Chenyang Wu, Zhongle Xie, Baokun Wang, Lidan Shou

entry.summary: Shows that prefill-stage KV cache selection in multimodal LLMs fails because decoding-time queries differ far more from prefill queries than in text-only settings. MM-ShiftKV makes prefill KV selection decode-aware to avoid discarding semantically important visual tokens under tight cache budgets.

entry.title: scMIR: a vision-language foundation model for single-cell light microscopy image representation

author.name: Yifan Shang (Department of Biomedical Engineering, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong, China, College of Computer Science and Electronic Engineering, Hunan University, Changsha, China), Jiahui Tan (College of Computer Science and Electronic Engineering, Hunan University, Changsha, China), Xiangxiang Zeng (College of Computer Science and Electronic Engineering, Hunan University, Changsha, China), Renjie Zhou (Department of Biomedical Engineering, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong, China)

entry.summary: scMIR is a vision-language foundation model for single-cell light microscopy images that incorporates experimental background and biological context text alongside images, rather than relying on task-specific supervised training. Aims for generalization across cell types, imaging modalities and experimental conditions.

entry.title: Cheap Probes Predict Expensive Training in 3D-CT Vision--Language Models

author.name: Renjie Liang

entry.summary: Asks whether cheap linear probes on cached frozen encoder embeddings can substitute for full LLM fine-tuning when selecting the encoder and token-compression scheme for 3D CT vision-language models. Builds an image-grounded probing benchmark with clinical attribute families and validation gates to check probe reliability.

entry.title: Controlling Embedding Spaces with Text-Conditioned Transformations

author.name: Joseph Fioresi, Fabian Caba Heilbron, Pankaj Nathani, Mubarak Shah, Kushal Kafle

entry.summary: Learns text-conditioned affine transformations of CLIP-style visual embeddings so that non-dominant attributes such as camera angle, color tone, or art style become explicitly retrievable. A single network conditioned on attribute names handles many attributes simultaneously.

entry.title: OmniMate: Open-Ended Real-Time Streaming Audio-Visual Generation for Interactive Avatars

author.name: Quanyue Song, Yishan He, Yanbo Ding, Zhixiang He, Yongxiang Li, Caigui Jiang, Zhi Zhi Guo

entry.summary: OmniMate jointly generates video, speech, and audio effects in real time for open-ended interactive avatars, addressing unknown generation horizons and drift in cross-modal identity consistency during long sessions. Targets multi-turn immersive avatar interaction.

entry.title: SARATR-X-v2: Scale-Aware Structural Pre-Training for SAR Foundation Models

author.name: Weijie Li, Yafei Song, Yongxiang Liu, Bowen Peng, Jie Zhou, Jingyuan Xia, Wei Yang, Tianpeng Liu, Zhen Liu, Li Liu

entry.summary: SARATR-X-v2 rethinks the reconstruction target for masked pre-training of synthetic aperture radar foundation models, requiring both physics-grounded invariance to multiplicative speckle and coverage of multiple semantic scales. Argues these two desiderata pull in opposite directions and proposes a scale-aware structural target.

entry.title: AptAvatar: Fast and Vivid Long-Form Audio-Driven Video Generation for Production-Ready Avatars

author.name: Hengyuan Zhang, Jingna Sun, Meiguang Jin, Junfeng Ma

entry.summary: AptAvatar is a 14B-parameter audio-driven talking-avatar video generator distilled to two-step inference via an endpoint-anchored distribution distillation scheme, targeting production deployment for long-form clips. It claims to avoid the usual quality sacrifices of causal attention, short horizons, or reduced resolution.

entry.title: CADER: Confidence-Aware Dynamic Evidence Reasoning for Long-Video Understanding

author.name: Jinlong Yang, Wenhao Zhang, Kuanwei Lin, Sijie Cheng

entry.summary: CADER makes long-video reasoning adaptive by first answering from uniformly sampled frames and using a logit-margin confidence signal to exit early on easy questions, invoking tool-assisted fine-grained evidence gathering only when uncertain. It is training-free and targets wasted compute in uniform inference pipelines.

entry.title: PRISM: Polynomial Representations for Interaction-Structured Motor Control

author.name: Seung Hyun Lee, Stella X. Yu

entry.summary: PRISM adds a compact factorized polynomial module to standard MLP robot policies so that multiplicative interactions among physical observables, such as power, inertia and slip, become explicit and learnable. It applies to both reinforcement learning and imitation settings without abandoning the MLP backbone.

entry.title: Learning Traversability-Aware Global Planners for Long Horizon Off-Road Navigation

author.name: Kasi Viswanath, Jason M. Gregory, Shaunak Kolhe, Srikanth Saripalli

entry.summary: Learns a continuous off-road traversability map from satellite imagery, aerial LiDAR and vector maps, supervised by human GPS driving trajectories plus self-supervised geometric priors, enabling planning beyond the onboard sensor horizon. Includes a public dataset release.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Consistency Enhanced Disentangled Learning for Neural Decoding Generalization in Brain-Machine Interface

author.name: Jiyu Wei, Di Hong, Zhanjie Zhang, Dazhong Rong, Qinming He, Yueming Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a self-supervised, disentangled representation learning method for invasive brain-machine interfaces that separately handles neural drift affecting different motor parameters such as velocity, direction and speed. Aims to extend decoder viability over time without frequent recalibration.

entry.title: Simulated Users & Sad AIs

author.name: 1a3orn

entry.summary: Speculative hypotheses about why current frontier assistants keep reward hacking and occasionally take unauthorized actions on real systems, focusing on how training against simulated users and environments may shape run-time behavior. Framed by the author as an honest attempt to make their own alignment optimism falsifiable.

entry.title: OpenAI's myopia just keeps causing alignment problems

author.name: Fiora Starlight

entry.summary: Catalogs three distinct alignment failures attributed to one lab's training choices: feedback-driven sycophancy in an earlier chat model with downstream mental-health harms, chains of thought seemingly optimized to be illegible to monitors, and a further incident. Argues these are recurring warning shots stemming from short-horizon optimization pressures.

entry.title: Persistent Computational State: A Session-Centric Runtime for Generative World Models

author.name: Zhen Lin

entry.summary: Challenges the claim that video world models cannot support planner-style forking, backtracking and revisiting, arguing the failure is a runtime rather than a model problem. Snapshotting existing runtime state such as RNG seeds, memory banks or windowed KV context and restoring it reproduces the never-left continuation exactly on three model classes, so a session-centric runtime restores the missing capability.

entry.title: Cross-Model LLM Code Review: Should you use Claude to review Codex or vice versa?

author.name: Zuodong Xiang, Yike Zhang, YueMing Zhang, Hailu Xu

entry.summary: A controlled experiment on 116 hard and medium competitive-programming tasks comparing solo coding agents, same-model review, and cross-model review orderings between two widely used coding assistants. Review by one assistant lifts the other drafts from about 72 to 90 percent pass rate, while the reverse ordering does not pay off, showing the pairing direction matters.

entry.title: MEUSLI: a Multilingual Projector for LLM-based ASR and Beyond

author.name: Lorenzo Concina, Seraphina Fong, Marco Matassoni, Alessio Brutti

entry.summary: MEUSLI is presented as the first open-science family of multilingual projectors linking a Whisper speech encoder to open-source LLMs, enabling end-to-end automatic speech recognition across 28 European languages. Continual learning techniques allow extension to languages unseen during projector training.

entry.title: One Hand Watches The Other: Dynamic Multi-Agent Cooperation for Sample-Efficient Bimanual Manipulation in Dynamic Environments

author.name: Jan Ole von Hartz, Abhinav Valada, Joschka Boedecker

entry.summary: DynaMAC removes the assumption that reference frames in multi-stream manipulation policies are exogenous, which breaks when an arm manipulates a moving object or two arms coordinate and each becomes part of the other arm dynamic environment. It treats the opposite arm as a dynamic task parameter in a lightweight policy-agnostic wrapper that preserves sample efficiency.

entry.title: HiKV: Hierarchical Importance-Aware KV Cache with Hardware Acceleration for LLM Decoding

author.name: Chao Fang, Jun Yin, Man Shi, Marian Verhelst

entry.summary: HiKV compresses the KV cache hierarchically, first evicting unimportant tokens within a budget and then loading only significant elements of retained tokens, reaching compression ratios unattainable at a single granularity. It pairs this with an accelerator design featuring a reconfigurable importance sorter for the two stages.

entry.title: All in One: Generative Modeling as Mean-Field Game Design

author.name: Kun Zhao, Xu Chen

entry.summary: The paper shows that twelve continuous-time generative modeling families, from continuous normalizing flows to score-based models and Schrodinger bridges, are special cases of one mean-field game variational problem specified by a cost tuple, and releases an open library where all are configured by four composable cost functions. It also explores the previously ignored interaction term and applies mean-field game solvers to generative training.

entry.title: Directional Influence Function: Estimating Training Data Influence in Constrained Learning

author.name: Xin Wang (Jeff), R. Tyrrell Rockafellar (Jeff), Xuegang (Jeff), Ban

entry.summary: The Directional Influence Function extends classical influence estimation to constrained learning, where removing or perturbing a sample can reshape both the objective and the feasible set so that standard influence estimates become infeasible or unreliable. Given the growth of training under fairness, safety, robustness, and physics constraints, correct data attribution in that regime is increasingly relevant.

entry.title: PerturbPFN: Probing the Limits of Synthetic Priors in Drug Perturbation Modelling

author.name: Yuche Gao, Jos\'e Miguel Hern\'andez-Lobato, Siyuan Guo

entry.summary: PerturbPFN trains a prior-fitted network entirely on synthetic episodes drawn from biologically motivated causal graph and expression simulators, then infers a latent system graph, sparse intervention targets, and strengths that are decoded through a structural causal model to predict cellular responses to unseen drugs. It probes how far synthetic structural priors can carry perturbation prediction.

entry.title: Local Regularization Does Not Characterize Multiclass PAC Learnability

author.name: Eric Hou

entry.summary: The author resolves an open question by proving that local regularization does not characterize multiclass PAC learnability, constructing a countable class with small Daniely-Shalev-Shwartz dimension and low sample complexity that no local regularizer can learn. The construction uses edges of complete graphs as hypotheses and tournaments as instances.

entry.title: Outcome-Confounded Local Supervision in On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Guoqing Ma

entry.summary: Shows that reading teacher-student token-level agreement locally in on-policy distillation is confounded by whether the final answer was correct, and introduces a diagnostic that crosses divergence with outcome correctness. In a math-reasoning study with Qwen3 models, agreement on failing trajectories accounts for most of the token mass, meaning much apparently safe imitation is reinforcing errors.

entry.title: Beyond Aggregate Risk: Role-Stratified Conformal Risk Control for LLM Tool Calls

author.name: Md Ashikur Rahman, Md Arifur Rahman, Niamul Hassan Samin, Khandaker Rifah Tasnia, Sifat Rahman Ahona, Juena Ahmed Noshin

entry.summary: Applies conformal risk control separately to each semantic role of an LLM tool-call argument, so that rare high-stakes fields such as recipients, accounts, or commands get their own thresholds and risk budgets rather than being averaged into benign arguments. The authors show that aggregate-only certification must shrink the budget in proportion to role prevalence to guarantee equivalent per-role risk.

entry.title: Stress-Testing EEG Foundation Models for Clinical Decoding: Dataset Identity and Targeted Negative Controls

author.name: Marzieh Zare

entry.summary: Stress-tests six pretrained EEG foundation models on five clinical tasks with frozen linear probes and subject-disjoint splits, adding negative controls such as random initialization, random features, label permutation, and scrambled-label fine-tuning. On a dementia classification task a leading foundation model underperforms classical features, and results implicate dataset identity as a confound.

entry.title: Subject-Level Heterogeneity in EEG Motor Imagery Decoding: A Large-Scale Benchmark and Portfolio-Based Reduction of the Search Space

author.name: Paul Barbaste, Olivier Oullier, Xavier Vasques

entry.summary: Runs a very large standardized benchmark of EEG motor imagery decoding pipelines across three public datasets and hundreds of thousands of evaluation rows, quantifying how much subject-level heterogeneity dominates pipeline choice. It then proposes a small portfolio of pipelines that covers most subjects, shrinking the search space.

entry.title: Metamorphic Testing for Clinical ML Models: A Framework Proposal and Pilot Study

author.name: Jie JW Wu, Feiyu E, Bo Chen

entry.summary: Proposes metamorphic testing for clinical prediction models, defining twelve clinically grounded relations (for example, worsening a severity score should not lower predicted mortality risk) that can be checked without per-case ground truth. A pilot study on MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV ICU tasks shows models can score well on AUROC while violating basic medical monotonicity.

entry.title: When Rates Are Geometric: Rate-Certificate Transfer for Contact Splittings in Optimization

author.name: George A Kevrekidis

entry.summary: This work uses contact Hamiltonian systems to make precise when a convergence rate proven for the continuous-time ODE limit of an optimizer actually transfers to the discrete algorithm. The main theorem gives checkable hypotheses under which an order-r contact splitting integrator preserves the continuous rate certificate.

entry.title: BeyondFusion: Self-Aligned Latent Diffusion for Calibration-Free Infrared Super-Resolution and Infrared-Visible Fusion

author.name: Minchong Chen, Xiaoyun Yuan, Minyu Cao, Jianing Zhang, Jun Zhang, Shuyang Liu, Xiaokang Yang

entry.summary: BeyondFusion is a latent diffusion framework that performs visible-guided infrared super-resolution and infrared-visible fusion without explicit calibration or geometric warping, using a cross-modal self-aligning mechanism. Both tasks can be trained jointly as readouts of a shared generative process.

entry.title: LLM-based Source Code Compression via Thresholded Symbol Ranking

author.name: Angelo Nardone, Paolo Ferragina

entry.summary: This work applies LLMs within Shannon's symbol-ranking framework for lossless source code compression, but thresholds the rank so that only low ranks are explicitly encoded, addressing the throughput collapse of unbounded-rank schemes. The target application is large software archives such as Software Heritage.

entry.title: proxymate: Diagnosis and Adjustment of Proxy Estimates for Reliable Inference

author.name: Alexandra N. M. Darmon, Deeksha Sinha, Steve Wilkins-Reeves, Caner Gocmen

entry.summary: Introduces an open-source Python framework for diagnosing and correcting bias when proxy outcomes stand in for slow or rare primary outcomes, organized into representativity, unit, estimate, and domain validity levels. Targets practitioners running experiments where surrogate metrics drive decisions.

entry.title: Do Small Models Use the Law You Give Them? Context-Injected Fine-Tuning for Legal QA in Bangladesh

author.name: Moniruzzaman Mahadi, Abrar Mohammed Tanzim Alam, Sayma Siddika Monalisa, Mir Mohammad Asif Abdullah, Swakkhar Shatabda, Md Adnan Arefeen

entry.summary: Tests whether fine-tuning small models on question-answer pairs that include the governing statutory text improves their later use of retrieved law, using 2,165 bilingual records from Bangladeshi acts and Bar Council exams. Gains are large at 0.8B and hold at 2B but vanish at 4B, where Bangla improves while several English conditions regress.

entry.title: Pointer-Augmented Autoregressive Generation of Patent Claims with Joint Topology and Content Decoding

author.name: Yongmin Yoo, Zhangkai Wu, Longbing Cao

entry.summary: Adds a pointer head inside the autoregressive pass to select each dependent patent claim's parent, jointly decoding the dependency forest topology and claim text with a depth-adaptive scope regularizer. Addresses the mutual dependence between claim structure and wording that post-hoc parsing and grammar-constrained decoding cannot resolve.

entry.title: SINT-Flow: Schema Integration using Large Language Model Workflows

author.name: Keti Korini, Christian Bizer

entry.summary: ELMOD is a 2.7B German-first language model trained on only 55k H100 hours using public data, with German-specific preprocessing for compounding and morphology plus a quality-filtering and rephrasing step. Demonstrates competitive on-device performance for a non-English language under a small compute budget.

entry.title: ConsistencyGate: Preventing Memory Contamination in LLM Agents via Self-Consistency Admission Control

author.name: Yan Zhang, Shibo Li

entry.summary: ConsistencyGate is a write-time admission control for agent memory: before a candidate fact is stored, the model is queried multiple times for support scores and the fact is admitted only if the average clears a threshold.
