Targets memory contamination, where one hallucinated fact becomes a persistent false premise for all later reasoning.

entry.title: Omni-Prune: Query-Aware Unified Token Pruning for Efficient Omnimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Yiming Zhong, Chang Nie, Caifeng Shan

entry.summary: Omni-Prune is a training-free token pruning method for omnimodal LLMs that jointly prunes audio and video tokens using adaptive time windows and query awareness, preserving cross-modal evidence relevant to the user question. Targets prefill latency and memory in synchronized audio-video models.

entry.title: Layering Virtual Try-On

author.name: Chun Feng, Bowei Chen, Mengyi Shan, Ira Kemelmacher-Shlizerman

entry.summary: Defines Layering Virtual Try-On, where garments are added or removed on top of an existing outfit in sequence instead of a single-item swap, and provides both a benchmark and a method. Argues that cloth-agnostic representations in existing try-on pipelines discard the layering context needed for the task.

entry.title: OmniCache: Multidimensional Hierarchical Feature Caching For Diffusion Models

author.name: Zhaoyuan He, Muhammad Muaz, Lili Qiu

entry.summary: OmniCache identifies four complementary redundancy sources in image and video diffusion inference (intra-frame, inter-frame, motion, and denoising-step) and unifies them in a hierarchical caching framework with token, frame, block, and step caches. Requires no retraining or weight changes.

entry.title: TaoMate: Anchor-Guided Memory Bridging Evolving and Reference States for Real-Time Audio-Video Digital Human Generation

author.name: Qijun Gan, Chenwei Zhang, Meiguang Jin, Junfeng Ma, Qiu Shen

entry.summary: TaoMate enables real-time long-form audio-video digital human generation by keeping an immutable visual anchor, compressing finished blocks into fixed-capacity memory states, and retrieving them via modality-specific residual attention. This avoids both the forgetting of bounded caches and the cost and error accumulation of full-history attention.

entry.title: SADe: Sparse-Atom Support Decontamination for Few-Shot Segmentation with Weak Support Annotations

author.name: Hang Xing, Guangjun Liu, Yan Xia, Xueming Ding

entry.summary: SADe is a predictor-agnostic layer that decontaminates weak support annotations in few-shot segmentation by using sparse autoencoder atom activations inside versus outside the weak region to estimate patch reliability. It addresses distractors and background leaking into prototypes from boxes, scribbles, or pseudo-masks.

entry.title: A Replay-Constrained Simulation Framework for Personalization of Powered Knee--Ankle Prosthesis Controllers

author.name: Duong Le, Ryan Posh, Shihao Cheng, Maani Ghaffari, Robert D. Gregg

entry.summary: Presents a MuJoCo simulation framework for personalizing powered knee-ankle prosthesis impedance controllers by replaying recorded human hip kinematics and ground reaction forces instead of modeling the human neuromuscular system. This enables high-dimensional sim-to-real controller tuning without lengthy human-in-the-loop search.

entry.title: Embodied GPT-5.1: Evidence of a World Model?

author.name: Roberto Spinelli, Thiago C. Martins

entry.summary: An exploratory study using GPT-5.1, an existing OpenAI model released in late 2025, as the high-level controller of a physical mobile robot with only low-resolution first-person images and a discrete action set. The authors report emergent short-term object memory, inference about consequences of its own motion, and other behaviors they interpret as partial evidence of an implicit world model.

entry.title: WARL: Wrench-Augmented Reinforcement Learning for Task-Agnostic Learning in Legged Robots

author.name: Keita Yoneda, Kento Kawaharazuka, Kei Okada

entry.summary: WARL augments the RL action space of legged robots with virtual wrenches (forces and torques) to broaden early exploration, combined with a success-rate curriculum that eventually weans the policy back to pure joint control. Demonstrated on a quadruped across diverse terrains without terrain-specific tuning.

entry.title: NEO: NeRF It Once, Edit It Many Times for Continuous Object Manipulation

author.name: Miko{\l}aj Zieli\'nski, David Hall, Dominik Belter, Peyman Moghadam

entry.summary: NEO provides language-guided NeRF editing for robotics, including multiview-consistent object removal via progressive inpainting and direct NeRF weight editing through teacher-student distillation, plus a new benchmark for evaluating scene edits for manipulation. It lets a robot model future scene states before acting.

entry.title: Physical AI Governance: From Theory to Practice Across Life Cycle

author.name: Wang Yang, Shaobo Wang, Hongxuan Liu, Xiaoran Cai, Yunyu He, Jingzong Zhou, Mengzhong Ma, Yi Yu, Rohit Sharma, Jingjing Fu, Peng Qi

entry.summary: Surveys governance of Physical AI, arguing that embodied systems operating under real-time safety constraints alongside humans raise challenges that existing screen-based AI governance frameworks do not cover, and proposes a unified five-stage life-cycle framework. Bridges principles and operational practice.

entry.title: Cost-Aware Recovery-Pathway Identification and Bayesian Optimization for Autonomous Materials Discovery

author.name: Debajyoti Ray, Niranjan Srinivas

entry.summary: Formulates autonomous materials discovery as a two-stage sequential decision problem, first identifying which recovery pathway to pursue using cost-sensitive Bayesian hypothesis discrimination and then optimizing within it via Gaussian process Bayesian optimization. Provides a bound on expected campaign spend under stated assumptions.

entry.title: DBA-Bench: A Production-Fidelity Benchmark for LLM-Based Database Operations Agents

author.name: Junming Chen, Junyang Jiang, Xu Chen, Zibo Liang, Kai Zheng

entry.summary: DBA-Bench evaluates LLM database-operations agents in live multi-turn read-write environments with production-scale observation spaces of time series, logs, and concurrent activity, open-ended remediation choices, and cascading fault scenarios. It emphasizes outcome-first grading and reproducible scenario control.

entry.title: SM4RT: Learning Structured Motion Geometry for 4D Reconstruction

author.name: Shing Ho J. Lin, Wenzhao Zheng, Dong Zhuo, Yuqi Wu, Jie Zhou, Jiwen Lu

entry.summary: SM4RT extends geometry foundation models to 4D dynamic reconstruction by modeling motion as a structured set of rigid-body SE(3) transformations rather than independent point-wise displacements. The premise is that real objects move collectively under rigid-body kinematics, so structured motion geometry should be learned directly.

entry.title: What Softmax Throws Away: Mass-Aware Attention for Evidence Accumulation

author.name: Minwoo Yu, Young-guk Ha

entry.summary: The authors argue that softmax attention discards evidence magnitude because repeated identical evidence scales numerator and denominator equally, so different amounts of accumulated evidence can yield identical outputs. They propose Mass-Aware Attention, generalizing the L1 normalization to an Lp family so aggregation retains information about how much evidence was seen, demonstrated on temporal graph tasks.

entry.title: Mini-batch Noise Lowers Sharpness via Dominant-Subspace Fluctuations

author.name: Junho So, Dongwook Shin

entry.summary: This analysis reinterprets the Hessian's dominant eigen-subspace not as where SGD reduces loss but as the subspace that explains sharpness dynamics, deriving a sharpness-correction term from averaged gradient fluctuations along dominant directions. It offers a mechanism for why mini-batch noise implicitly reduces sharpness.

entry.title: MixQuant: Adaptive Mixed-Precision Quantization for Large Language Models

author.name: Ashitabh Misra, Madhav Agrawal, Arham Jain, Tarek Abdelzaher

entry.summary: MixQuant makes mixed-precision post-training quantization budget-adaptive with a single offline calibration, and shows that a layer's quantization sensitivity depends strongly on the bitwidths chosen for upstream layers, which existing independent scoring methods ignore. Accounting for this dependence changes the preferred bit allocation.

entry.title: Training with (Swap) Regret Loss in a Single-Layer Self-Attention Model: A Case Study on the Probability Simplex

author.name: Chanwoo Park, Asuman Ozdaglar

entry.summary: The paper analyzes training a single-layer self-attention model with decision-theoretic regret as the loss, showing a stationary point whose forward pass reproduces smoothed fictitious play with a no-regret stepsize, and introduces a swap-regret loss to target the stronger correlated-equilibrium notion. It connects transformer training objectives to classic no-regret learning guarantees.

entry.title: ACRL: Adaptive Control of Training-Inference Discrepancy for Stable Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Wenwu Fan, Qihong Lin, Zhijie Xia, Zhuo Zheng, Sihao Wang, Qiang Chen, Liangsheng Zhu

entry.summary: ACRL diagnoses instability in reinforcement learning for LLMs as stemming from mismatch between training and inference engines plus low-precision inference quantization, and adaptively keeps that discrepancy inside a controlled band. Beyond stabilizing training, the authors report that controlled discrepancy can also be exploited beneficially.

entry.title: MXAttention: Data-Free Optimal Scaling and Pre-Normalization Quantization for MXFP4 Attention

author.name: Jianlin Yu, Jing Lin, Linghui Kong, Aiyue Chen, Weiyi Sun, Chenyu Zeng, Wangli Lan, Jinxi Li, Zhuo Zheng, Ziyang Yue, Danning Ke, Fei Yi, Tianchi Hu, Yuan Ding, Yiwu Yao, Junsong Wang

entry.summary: MXAttention is a data-free post-training quantization scheme for MXFP4 attention in diffusion video generation, deriving a calibration-free optimal power-of-two scaling boundary and quantizing before softmax row normalization to avoid normalization error. It targets the quadratic attention cost that dominates video diffusion inference.

entry.title: FlowCTS: On-policy Continuous Trajectory Supervision of Flow Models

author.name: Kaiyang Ye, Yuan Ge, Junxiang Zhang, Bei Li, Ziming Zhu, Haishu Zhao, Xiaoqian Liu, Chenglong Wang, Jingbo Zhu, Zhengtao Yu, Tong Xiao

entry.summary: FlowCTS extends on-policy distillation from language models to flow-matching generative models by matching student and reference trajectories from the same student-visited state, deriving a temporally weighted velocity-matching bound. It reports better convergence than KL-based on-policy distillation and improvements on image generation benchmarks such as GenEval.

entry.title: Benchmarking LLMs for Verilog Design Flows

author.name: Angshuman Chakravertty, Rahul Koshti, Buddhi Prakash Sharma, Vinay Chamola

entry.summary: Benchmarks open-source language models on fifty Verilog RTL generation tasks with genuine end-to-end toolchain validation including synthesis, waveform analysis, formal equivalence checking, and abstract syntax tree repair, rather than pass@k alone. It shows iterative semantic-aware refinement materially changes measured capability.

entry.title: Traceable LLM Reasoning for Fake-Order Fraud Detection

author.name: Siqi You, Bingsong Xu, Zhixian Zheng, Xinjian Peng, Yang Xie, Ying Wang, Jiarong Xu

entry.summary: DeepScrub applies reinforcement learning on top of a language model to detect fake-order fraud on an online-to-offline platform, converting heterogeneous risk signals into text, continuing pretraining on risk-control corpora, and rewarding both correct predictions and sound reasoning traces. The aim is auditable fraud decisions rather than black-box scores.

entry.title: SMART: LLM-Augmented Hybrid Retrieval for Dynamic Product Ads

author.name: Congfei Zhang, Jingxiao Ma, Xiaodong Liu, Hsiang-wei Chao, Siman Wang, Ge Liu, Shantanu Aggarwal, Vincent Zhang, Meghana Missula, Rachel Liao, Zichu Li, Xiao Bai, Yunzhi Zhou, Yajun Wang, Zhe Liu, Jinchao Li, Yu Zhang

entry.summary: SMART studies dynamic product ad retrieval and finds a clean decomposition: rule-based queries plus BM25 work best for retargeting, while LLM-generated queries plus dense retrieval work best for prospecting into new categories. The hybrid system manages LLM inference cost while serving multi-million-item catalogs at industrial scale.

entry.title: Logit-Coordinate Generative Models for Mixed Continuous-Categorical Tabular Data

author.name: Yuefei Shen, Xiaotong Shen

entry.summary: The paper develops a logit-coordinate framework letting flow matching and diffusion models handle mixed continuous-categorical tabular data by encoding categories as smoothed natural parameters. It introduces a discrepancy separating categorical marginal error from continuous Wasserstein error and derives imbalance-aware convergence rates.

entry.title: HydroAgent: Formalizing Forecaster Expertise into Skill-Orchestrated Flood Forecasting Workflows

author.name: Qingyi Yang, Siqian Qiu, Bing Li, Xu Shan, Jia Feng, Shunan Zhou, Xudong Zhou, Tiantian Xing, Jiale Guo, Xiaoyi Dong, Gaoyu Liu, Xiaohuan Liu, Haiqing Pu, Qingwen Deng, Xun Zhang, Zhongrun Xiang, Haiyang Qian, Ying Yan, Yongkang Xu, Nuo Lei, Tianlong Jia, Baoying Shan, Carlo De Michele

entry.summary: HydroAgent embeds LLMs into an operational flood forecasting workflow through discrete skills that encode explicit expert rules and review checkpoints, bounding model reasoning. It is validated with five recent LLMs on a real river basin, aiming to make tacit forecaster expertise auditable and transferable.

entry.title: Attention-Guided Layer Selection for Contrastive Decoding in Large Language Models

author.name: Yusuke Sakai, Natthawut Kertkeidkachorn, Kiyoaki Shirai

entry.summary: Extends contrastive decoding beyond DoLa by using internal self-attention statistics, via Jensen-Shannon divergence and entropy criteria, to choose the premature layer for contrast. Reports consistent factuality gains on TruthfulQA, especially on multi-answer metrics.

entry.title: AssumptionMiner: Extracting, Tracing, and Revising Implicit Assumptions in LLM Code Generation

author.name: Jie "JW" Wu

entry.summary: AssumptionMiner makes the implicit assumptions LLMs invent when prompts underspecify input formats, error handling or design choices into an explicit, inspectable artifact alongside generated code. Developers can confirm or revise assumptions, which then propagate back into the code.

entry.title: Evidence Attribution in Visual Document Understanding without Coordinates or Region Labels

author.name: Zhuchenyang Liu, Yao Zhang, Yu Xiao

entry.summary: Investigates whether attribution hallucination in visual document QA is partly an artifact of forcing models to output bounding-box coordinates, comparing that interface against a language interface where the model simply quotes supporting text. Uses a verified bilingual subset of CiteVQA for the comparison.

entry.title: Benchmarking the Domain Gap: Model Selection Instability Under Domain Shift in Video Capsule Endoscopy

author.name: Dan Hanson, Debesh Jha

entry.summary: Fine-tunes a suite of pretrained backbones on video capsule endoscopy classification and evaluates the same checkpoints on two out-of-source datasets under a shared label space. Shows that in-domain model ranking is an unreliable predictor of out-of-domain performance, and that the two external targets barely agree with each other.

entry.title: ViDS: Video Diffusion Shader using 3D Face Tracking

author.name: Wenbo Ji, Davide Davoli, Zhe Chen, Liam Schoneveld, Matthias Nie{\ss}ner, Jiapeng Tang

entry.summary: ViDS uses 3DMM face tracking normal maps to condition a video diffusion model acting as a neural shader for identity-preserving portrait animation, with autoregressive sampling to extend beyond the native window. It shows that more accurate 3D tracking yields finer expression control.

entry.title: Learning Dense 2D-3D Correspondence for X-ray-to-CT Registration of Knee Bones

author.name: Rembert Daems, Jonas Grammens, Caro Roten, Andrew Meyer, Thomas Luyckx, Matthias Verstraete

entry.summary: Learns an amortized subject-agnostic dense 2D-3D correspondence to register knee bones from a single plain radiograph to a pre-operative CT, replacing per-patient silhouette alignment or differentiable-rendering optimization. This turns a routine low-dose image into a quantitative joint geometry measurement without extra radiation.

entry.title: Hiding in Plain Sight: An Effective Physical Adversarial Patch Attack against Visual-Infrared Fused Face Detection

author.name: Qiucheng Yu, Tao Ni, Yihe Zhou, Jiayimei Wang, Qingchuan Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes VIPatch, a physically realizable adversarial patch that simultaneously fools visual and infrared fused face detection systems while looking like an ordinary accessory. It targets a gap in prior work that attacked only one modality digitally and produced conspicuous patterns.

entry.title: Benchmarking Zero-Shot LLM-Generated Parent Selection in Genetic Programming for Symbolic Regression

author.name: Hengzhe Zhang, Qi Chen, Bing Xue, Wolfgang Banzhaf, Mengjie Zhang

entry.summary: Benchmarks eight large language models on zero-shot synthesis of parent-selection operators for genetic programming symbolic regression, with no reference operators or iterative feedback. Tests whether LLMs can invent useful evolutionary operators from a task description alone.

entry.title: Memory for Attention: Language-Conditioned Re-Perception with a Vision--Language--Motion Map

author.name: Dibyendu Ghosh

entry.summary: Reports a largely negative result: behavior-annotated persistent maps improve a planning-time objective by about 35 percent but yield only about 4 percent benefit under closed-loop execution, matching an on-demand VLM. The paper instead argues persistent map memory is genuinely useful for deciding what to re-observe under a limited perception budget.

entry.title: FloAff-Kitchen: Bridging Navigation and Manipulation via Canonical and Progressive Floor Affordance Learning

author.name: Ping Zhong, Manling Teng, Tao Wu, Bolei Chen, Jiazhi Xia, Jianxin Wang

entry.summary: FloAff-Kitchen predicts where on the floor a mobile robot should stand to maximize downstream manipulation success, not merely navigation feasibility, using a canonical target-conditioned representation and progressive affordance priors. It targets the interface between navigation and manipulation in mobile manipulation.

entry.title: FlowEvo: Self-Evolving Agents through the Co-Evolution of Workflows and Executable Skills

author.name: Zeyu Ren, Ling Yue, Ran Li, Yishu Wang, Shengxiang Xu, Hanmo Liu, Shaowu Pan, Shimin Di

entry.summary: FlowEvo is a training-free framework that turns successful agent execution traces into reusable skill records (callable code plus structured guidance) stored in a persistent skill bank, with interface, replay and safety admission checks. The aim is to stop useful procedures discovered at inference time from being discarded after each task.

entry.title: Coupled Hierarchical Search over Topology and Execution for Agentic Workflow Synthesis

author.name: Dong Li, Yanchi Liu, Xujiang Zhao, Wei Cheng, Zhengzhang Chen, Xintao Wu, Zhong Chen, Chen Zhao, Haifeng Chen

entry.summary: HierFlow casts agentic workflow generation as a coupled search over workflow topology and execution, where high-level structure sets subtask boundaries and execution feedback reshapes that structure. It is training-free and uses a hierarchical, MCTS-inspired test-time tree search instead of offline workflow training.

entry.title: From Profiles to Steering Vectors: Global Sparse Priors and Local Semantic Calibration for Personalized Text Generation

author.name: Liuji Chen, Zeyu Zhang, Xinyuan Zhang, Shuai Nie, Qiang Liu, Shu Wu, Liang Wang

entry.summary: GLASS personalizes text generation without training by extracting a global user-style prior with sparse autoencoders and building local contrastive style vectors for clustered interaction contexts, then injecting both into different layers at inference. The goal is to separate stylistic signal from semantic content while avoiding storage and fine-tuning overhead.

entry.title: Reasoning Denoiser: Denoising Reasoning Traces for Hallucination Detection in Large Reasoning Models

author.name: Junlin Fang, Do Nguyen-Thanh, Xiaogang Xu, Zhen Fang, Sean Du

entry.summary: REDE improves hallucination detection in large reasoning models by first denoising their long reasoning traces, identifying irrelevant and repetitive steps as two noise types that measurably degrade detection. Confidence scores and naive embedding filtering fail to separate noisy from informative steps, motivating a learned denoiser.

entry.title: IDEAgent: Agentic Quality-Diversity Search for Research Idea Generation

author.name: Varun Gumma, Navonil Majumder, Soumitra Sinhahajari, Soujanya Poria

entry.summary: IDEAgent treats automated research ideation as a quality-diversity search rather than optimizing quality or diversity alone, managing idea lineages in a multi-agent framework with multi-objective feedback driving targeted repair. The aim is to avoid both clustered near-duplicate ideas and large numbers of trivial or unsound ones.

entry.title: TRACE-ROUTER: Task-Consistent and Adaptive Online Routing for Agentic AI

author.name: Ritik Raj, Souvik Kundu, Sarbartha Banerjee, Dheemanth Joshi, Ishita Vohra, Tushar Krishna

entry.summary: TRACE-Router routes at the task level instead of per LLM call, arguing that agentic workflows only produce quality signals at the delayed task outcome so per-call routers cannot attribute credit. It assigns a model at admission with a contextual bandit, pins all subsequent calls to that backend, and updates from task-level feedback.

entry.title: Local Synaptic Rules Can Implement a SIGReg Gradient Without Backpropagation

author.name: Martin Andrews

entry.summary: Proves that two biologically canonical local learning rules, the potentiation arm of spike-timing-dependent plasticity plus homeostatic plasticity, can jointly implement the exact gradient of a self-supervised objective in the SIGReg family, with no backpropagation, weight transport, global error signals or labels. A synthetic clustering task tests whether class structure can be recovered from temporal ordering of inputs alone.

entry.title: On the Depth Scalability of Logic Gate Networks

author.name: Taegun An, Dohun kim, Haebeom Lee, Changhee Joo

entry.summary: Diagnoses why logic gate networks fail to benefit from added depth, separating optimization collapse in deep relaxed networks from a topology-induced limitation that persists even after stabilizing training. The proposed input-anchored variant gives each gate a direct input connection alongside evolving hidden features, preserving a computational spine through depth.

entry.title: Self-Poisoning in Adaptive Out-of-Distribution Detection: A Sharp-Threshold Theory and Certified Label-Free Calibration

author.name: Vishnu Bindu Balachandran

entry.summary: Models the memory bank of a test-time adaptive out-of-distribution detector as a generalized Polya urn and proves a sharp threshold: below a critical admission slope impurity stays bounded, above it the bank is fully poisoned and detection collapses. Measurements across encoder families show the admission kernel sits just under the critical slope, meaning this detector class is near-critical by design, and the paper offers a certified label-free calibration gate.

entry.title: Graph-Theoretic Neural Network Fragmentation with Covariant Direct Molecular Force Learning: Enabling Coupled-Cluster Accuracy AIMD for Fluxional Systems

author.name: Xiao Zhu, Srinivasan S. Iyengar

entry.summary: The paper couples graph-theoretic molecular fragmentation with machine-learned direct prediction of nuclear force vectors, projected onto fragment-fixed inertial axes to guarantee rotational and translational covariance. This enables ab initio molecular dynamics at approximately coupled-cluster accuracy for flexible, fluxional chemical systems that were previously computationally out of reach.

entry.title: Probing Speaker Identity Sensitivity in Audio Deepfake Detectors

author.name: Daniyal Kabir Dar, Arun Ross

entry.summary: The authors argue that audio deepfake detectors generalize poorly partly because training corpora correlate speaker identity with the genuine-versus-synthetic label, letting detectors lean on speaker cues instead of synthesis artifacts. They propose an Identity Sensitivity Score, a label-free per-utterance diagnostic measuring how much detector output shifts across speaker identity contexts.

entry.title: ISPCloak: Weaponizing ISP for Optimization-Free Physical Camouflage against Deepfake Detectors

author.name: Jiale Zhao, Jiajun Wan, Lei Tang, Ye Qin, Kebing Jin, Jinghui Qin

entry.summary: ISPCloak argues that real photographs carry hardware-intrinsic statistical signatures from optical sensors and image signal processing pipelines that generative models lack, and exploits this to camouflage AI-generated content without optimization. The resulting physical-style cloaking sharply degrades deepfake detectors that rely on digital synthesis artifacts.

entry.title: Generalized Neural Operator for Parametric and Boundary-Value Problems

author.name: Ruoyan Li, Yizhou Sun, Wei Wang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a neural operator that generalizes across PDE parameters and boundary conditions, aiming to avoid the trade-off between purely data-driven operators that lack physical constraints and physics-informed networks that require costly per-instance optimization. It targets condition-agnostic deployment with explicit physical fidelity for foundation-scale PDE simulators.

entry.title: Time-Reversed Imaging: A Multimodal Benchmark and Framework for Reconstructing Past Human-Environment Interactions

author.name: Jorge Bacca, Kebin Contreras, Luis Toscano-Palomino, Mauro Dalla Mura

entry.summary: The paper defines time-reversed imaging, inferring recent human-environment interactions from fading physical traces in thermal, ultraviolet, and visible spectra rather than by interpolating video. It releases TRACE-HEI, a tri-modal synchronized dataset of actions such as sitting, touching, and spills recorded up to three minutes after contact, plus a baseline multimodal inference pipeline.

entry.title: MEMENTO: Memory-Guided Memetic Code-as-Policy Evolution

author.name: Alkis Sygkounas, Victor Aregbede, Amy Loutfi, Andreas Persson

entry.summary: MEMENTO evolves executable control programs for long-horizon embodied tasks using an LLM to generate variants, adding a memory-guided sequential local refinement phase that prior code-as-policy evolution methods lack. Combining global variant selection with memetic local search improves rollout-driven program search.

entry.title: From Score Learning to Discretized Sampling: An End-to-End Generalization Analysis of Diffusion Models

author.name: Jinshu Huang, Yiming Jiang, Chunlin Wu

entry.summary: The paper builds an end-to-end generalization and convergence theory for score-based diffusion models with ResNet-type score networks, connecting finite-sample score learning, network parameterization, and discretized sampling instead of assuming an oracle score. It aims to explain jointly what determines generative quality in practice.

entry.title: A Statistical Difference between Single-Layer Learning and Hierarchical Learning in Wide Neural Networks

author.name: Sumio Watanabe

entry.summary: Working with a three-layer network at large but finite width, the author shows that training input-to-hidden weights yields lower generalization error than freezing them, and that the frozen-kernel setting exhibits singular statistical behavior. This gives a concrete statistical separation between fixed-kernel and feature-learning accounts of wide networks.

entry.title: Evaluating Fuzz Testing for Reinforcement Learning Agents

author.name: Zhibin Kang, Hanmo You, Dong Wang, Haiming Zheng, Junjie Chen

entry.summary: First systematic empirical comparison of fuzz-testing methods for reinforcement learning agents, unifying baselines, metrics, and settings across four evaluation dimensions. It aims to resolve conflicting claims in the RL fuzzing literature and identify which methods actually find meaningful failures.

entry.title: Modeling Memory-Dependent Reliability of LLMs: A Hidden Markov Model

author.name: Robab Aghazadeh Chakherlou, Siddartha Khastgir, Peter Popov, Xingyu Zhao

entry.summary: Models language model reliability with a hidden Markov model that captures memory dependence across a session, rejecting the usual assumption that test outcomes are independent trials. This yields uncertainty-aware reliability estimates for sequential interactions where context and error propagation matter.

entry.title: Music-Source-Separation-Training (MSST): A Unified Framework for Training and Evaluating Music Demixing Models

author.name: Roman Solovyev, Ilya Kiselev, Alexander Stempkovskiy, Tatiana Gabruseva

entry.summary: MSST is an open-source, configuration-driven framework unifying training, validation, and inference across many music source separation model families. It standardizes data augmentation, loss and metric choices, and post-processing decisions that heavily affect demixing quality.

entry.title: Anticipatory Risk-Guided Reinforcement Learning for Safe Flight Through Dynamic Clutter

author.name: Yuchao Mei, Guohao Zhang, Luxia Ai, Haopeng Chen, Wenbing Tao

entry.summary: The paper trains quadrotor flight policies using a physics-grounded future collision risk map derived from closest-point-of-approach geometry as privileged supervision in an asymmetric actor-critic setup. This shifts the policy from reacting to current geometry toward anticipating risk from relative motion.

entry.title: AI Strategy: How to Choose What AI Product to Implement

author.name: Foster Provost, Panos Ipeirotis

entry.summary: Provost and Ipeirotis present an expected-ROI framework that decomposes AI project selection into value if successful, likelihood of success, and required investment, illustrated with contrasting real products at a real-estate brokerage. It gives executives a structured way to distinguish superficially similar AI bets.

entry.title: TEmBed-T: A Multi-Dimensional Benchmark for Table-Level Embeddings

author.name: Ayeen Poostforoushan, Liane Vogel, Carsten Binnig

entry.summary: TEmBed-T extends an existing tabular embedding testbed to systematically evaluate table-level embeddings across complementary properties relevant to retrieval, data lake discovery, and table classification. It provides much-needed comparative understanding of how different table embedding approaches behave.

entry.title: Bigger or Cheaper? Scale and Quantization Effects on Uncertainty Signals in Vision-Language Models Under Image Degradation

author.name: M M Asif Ferdous

entry.summary: Empirically studies how model scale and 4-bit quantization affect the reliability of two confidence signals in Qwen2-VL models under realistic image degradation, comparing small-full-precision versus larger-quantized configurations at a fixed memory budget. Finds that verbalized confidence and mean token probability move in opposing directions, complicating deferral decisions on consumer hardware.

entry.title: Certified Parallel-in-Time Sinkhorn for Dynamic Entropic Optimal Transport

author.name: Xinyang Wen

entry.summary: Presents a parallel-in-time Sinkhorn solver for sequences of related entropic optimal transport problems, as arise in optimal-transport flow matching, using certificates that accept only provably safe prefixes of speculative work. Speculation can reorder computation but cannot produce an inaccurate output.

entry.title: The Cross-Domain Generalization Cost of Offensive Language Detection

author.name: Ruixing Ren, Junhui Zhao, Xiaoke Sun, Qiuping Li

entry.summary: Proposes a framework that decomposes cross-domain and cross-lingual degradation in offensive language detection into separable dataset and language effects, then quantifies adaptation efficiency and hidden damage from fine-tuning. Moves beyond simply reporting transfer drops toward attributing and pricing remediation.

entry.title: Guiding Language Models to Be More Empathetic: Culturally Sensitive Mental Health Advice Generation Through Human-LLM Collaboration

author.name: Fatema Tuj Johora Faria, Mukaffi Bin Moin, Md. Mahfuzur Rahman, Khan Md Hasib, Jubayer Al Mahmud, M. F. Mridha

entry.summary: Curates 625 authentic Bangladeshi mental health cases from social posts, a television program, and student questionnaires, then compares licensed psychologist advice against outputs from three proprietary LLMs and explores human-LLM collaboration to improve cultural sensitivity and empathy. Targets a gap in low-resource-language counseling evaluation.

entry.title: EmoTrace: An Emotion Trajectory-Centered Framework for Psychological Support Dialogue Generation

author.name: Kaitong Weng, Lixin Liu, Zihao Liu, Bo Wang, Shiguang Ni

entry.summary: Proposes generating psychological support dialogue corpora around explicit emotion trajectories, addressing prior synthetic data where simulated seekers stay emotionally stable and overly compliant with the counsellor. Aims to train models that handle emotionally volatile scenarios rather than only problem-solving turns.

entry.title: D-Score: A Spectral Hidden-State Signal for Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models

author.name: Bianca Raimondi, Davide Evangelista, Maurizio Gabbrielli, Elena Loli Piccolomini

entry.summary: D-Score is a hallucination detector computed in one forward pass from the spectrum of hidden-state activations, counting how many singular directions stay near the leading singular value. The intuition is that internally inconsistent or unsupported text produces a distinctive activation geometry.

entry.title: STAIF: A Stage-wise Optimization for Complex Instruction Following

author.name: Jian Hong, Chen Cheng, Quan Liu, Yuhao Chen, Enhong Chen

entry.summary: STAIF splits complex instruction-following alignment into two stages: preference optimization with multiple negatives for subjective soft constraints, then RL with verifiable rewards for objectively checkable hard constraints. The decoupling avoids holistic rewards that wash out individual constraint violations.

entry.title: DAMamba-UNet3D: A Parameter-Efficient Mamba State Space U-Net with Dynamic Adaptive Scan for 3D Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Mohammad Arafat Hussain, Ellen Grant, Yangming Ou

entry.summary: DAMamba-UNet3D brings dynamic adaptive scanning, which learns data-dependent token reordering before the selective scan, into 3D medical image segmentation using tri-plane state-space blocks in a hybrid convolutional encoder-decoder. Aims for linear-cost global context with fewer parameters than existing medical SSM segmenters.

entry.title: PCA: Persistence-Aware Compression and Aggregation for Fast Video Large Language Models

author.name: Zihan Song, Shuo Ye, Bo Zhao, Ruixin Zhang, Jiayu Zhang, Shouhong Ding, Zitong Yu

entry.summary: PCA is a training-free preprocessing method for video LLMs that adaptively drops redundant frames by similarity and then enriches each retained keyframe by aggregating motion context from its neighbors. It compresses before encoding, preserving high-fidelity raw visual information rather than pruning tokens afterward.

entry.title: Structured Redundancy Modeling for Efficient Visual Token Pruning in High-Resolution MLLMs

author.name: Jouwon Song, Woohyeong Kim, Kyeongbo Kong

entry.summary: SFPruner restructures visual token pruning for high-resolution multimodal LLMs so redundancy control happens in a single forward pass instead of iterative subset construction. The goal is to convert theoretical FLOPs savings into actual wall-clock speedups.

entry.title: OmniScope: Modality-Decoupled Token Compression for Omnimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Jinsen Su, Yongdong Luo, Yuexiao Ma, Yibo Hu, Meiguang Jin, Xiaowu Zheng

entry.summary: OmniScope is a training-free token compression method for omnimodal LLMs that uses the text query as a shared anchor while estimating audio and video relevance separately, allocating modality-specific budgets. Motivated by the finding that audio and visual salience peak at different moments.

entry.title: A Reconstruction-Based Framework for Caption Evaluation Beyond Reference Captions

author.name: Zhijiang Tang, Jiaxin Qi, Kaihua Tang, Yuhua Zheng, Jianqiang Huang

entry.summary: Proposes evaluating image captions by how well they enable reconstruction of the original image, avoiding dependence on human reference captions, while acknowledging pixel-level comparison is meaningless due to inherent compression. Develops a semantically oriented reconstruction criterion instead.

entry.title: WaveZip: Wavelet-Driven Space-Time Decoupling for Video Token Condensation

author.name: Yuhui Zeng, Wang Chen, Jinfa Huang, Tianyu Xie, Yongdong Luo, Jiayi Ji, Xiawu Zheng, jiebo Luo

entry.summary: WaveZip compresses video tokens for large vision-language models using discrete wavelet transforms to separate temporal redundancy in low-frequency approximations from spatial saliency in high-frequency components. Provides a signal-frequency-domain alternative to purely spatial pruning or merging.

entry.title: Robust 6-DoF Object Pose Tracking with Built-In Recovery under Occlusions and Rapid Object Motions

author.name: Bal\'azs Opra, L\'eo Ghafari, Thomas Stewart, Cyrill Stachniss

entry.summary: A model-based 6-DoF tracker for unseen objects from RGB-D that combines learned keypoint matching with optimization-based alignment and, crucially, adds explicit failure detection and automatic recovery after full occlusions or fast motion. Removes the need for manual re-initialization.

entry.title: MOJITO: Modal Joint Learning for Unified End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Zhijing Cheng, Xuancheng Zhang, Donglin Di, Lei Fan, Baorui Ma, Hao Li, Xun Yang

entry.summary: MOJITO removes the cascaded perception-to-planning interface in end-to-end autonomous driving, jointly learning across modalities from sensors directly to actions so fine-grained detail is not lost in a compressed context. Also aims to better exploit vision foundation model representations.

entry.title: Real-Time Human-Centric World Modeling for Upper-Body Human-Object Interaction

author.name: Chaonan Ji, Jinwei Qi, Peng Zhang, Bang Zhang

entry.summary: A real-time human-centric world model for upper-body interactive generation that jointly evolves body, hand, and facial motion with controllable discrete human-object interaction states. Uses a shared multi-scale latent space for continuous human state plus a discrete interaction channel.

entry.title: PathScale-R1: Cross-scale Reasoning for Pathological Image Analysis

author.name: Chi Phan, Tianyi Zhang, Yufeng Wu, Qiaochu Xue, Jiajie Zhang, Linghan Cai, Zeyu Liu, Sudong Wang, Yueming Jin, Dan Hu

entry.summary: PathScale-R1 builds a cross-scale pathology reasoning benchmark and training framework requiring integration of low-magnification architecture with high-magnification cellular detail, and explicitly filters items solvable by text-only or superficial visual shortcuts. Targets the single-scale limitation of current pathology vision-language models.

entry.title: Gaze-to-text Generation: Beyond Categorical Decoding of Human Attention

author.name: Sounak Mondal, Dimitris Samaras, Gregory Zelinsky, Minh Hoai

entry.summary: Introduces gaze-to-text decoding, generating free-form natural language descriptions of a person's goal from their eye-movement scanpath rather than classifying among predefined categories. Gazette builds on multimodal LLMs and filters idiosyncratic individual variation.

entry.title: Manifold-Constrained Noise Optimization for Diverse Diffusion Sampling

author.name: Qitan Shi, Cheng Jin, Ziyuan Liu, Yuantao Gu

entry.summary: MoNO restores per-prompt sample diversity in few-step distilled diffusion models by optimizing the initial noise on the Gaussian prior manifold with frequency-aware constraints, instead of unconstrained Euclidean updates. Being geometry-respecting removes the need for auxiliary quality-control objectives and their hyperparameters.

entry.title: TimePLE: Rethinking Temporal Representation for Video Temporal Grounding

author.name: Yuhui Zeng, Xinyu Mao, Xiaokun Liu, Xin Tao, Jinfa Huang, Jiayi Ji, Xiawu Zheng

entry.summary: TimePLE reformulates video temporal grounding from predicting two endpoints to predicting a single joint distribution over valid intervals, so validity, duration, and interval-level similarity are modeled explicitly. Maps intervals to points in a canonical space for interval-native grounding.

entry.title: Reasoning to Regulate: Chain-of-Thought for Traffic Rule Understanding

author.name: Yueru Luo, Xu Yan, Changqing Zhou, Yiming Yang, Chao Zhan, Shuqi Mei, Chao Zheng, Zhen Li

entry.summary: Reframes traffic-sign rule compliance as a reasoning problem rather than sequence prediction, adding chain-of-thought that links sign semantics to lane-level map structure using MapDR annotations. It targets safety-critical regulation understanding for autonomous driving.

entry.title: GenSplatCodec: Feed-Forward Gaussian Splatting Compression via One-Step Diffusion

author.name: Qiang Hu, Zhenlong Wu, Lei Huang, Zihan Zheng, Xiaoyun Zhang, Wenjun Zhang

entry.summary: GenSplatCodec reframes low-bitrate compression of feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes as a one-step diffusion generative decoding problem instead of deterministic recovery. Coupling generation with transmitted scene structure is meant to preserve cross-view consistency at low bitrates.

entry.title: URHead: A Unified UV-Space Representation for Joint Mesh-3DGS Optimization in Head Avatars

author.name: Seonghak Lee, Junhee Cho, Jisoo Park, Min-Gyu Park, Jongmin Lee, Ju Hong Yoon, Junseok Kwon

entry.summary: URHead unifies mesh and 3D Gaussian representations for animatable head avatars by making both share a common UV parameterization and jointly optimizing them with adaptive Gaussian sampling. This lets the model automatically allocate geometric control to the mesh and photorealistic detail to Gaussians.

entry.title: JPEG AIC2026: A large-scale dataset for fine-grained assessment of image coding

author.name: Mohsen Jenadeleh, Jon Sneyers, Jo\~ao Ascenso, Thomas Richter, Alexander Karabutov, Panqi Jia, Elena Alshina, Osamu Watanabe, Ant\'onio Pinheiro, Touradj Ebrahimi, Dietmar Saupe

entry.summary: AIC2026 is a large-scale image-coding quality dataset with 70 carefully selected source images encoded by eight conventional and four learning-based codecs across 17 configurations, aimed at fine-grained high-fidelity quality assessment. Source selection used semantic clustering and disagreement among objective quality metrics.

entry.title: ERUnderstand: Evaluating Vision-Language Models on Structured ER Diagrams

author.name: Ali Ansari, Yasmin Mohammadi, Farnoush Nili, Parsa Esmaeilkhani, Longin Jan Latecki, Eduard Dragut

entry.summary: ERUnderstand is a benchmark of nearly 3,000 entity-relationship diagrams paired with machine-readable schema representations, used to test whether vision-language models can recover database structure from diagram images. Results indicate current VLMs fall well short on structured diagram parsing.

entry.title: Sling2Sim2Real: One-Shot Elastic System Identification for Non-Destructive Slingshot Policy Learning

author.name: Wonjae Kang, Geonwoo Kim, Minseok Song, Daehyung Park

entry.summary: Sling2Sim2Real performs one-shot system identification of elastic material properties from a single real trial, then trains slingshot manipulation policies in simulation without destructive repeated real-world launches. Targets the difficulty of inferring elasticity from vision alone.

entry.title: Learning Adaptive Multi-Task Guidance, Navigation, and Control via Hypernetworks

author.name: Ricard Marsal I Castan, Aman Arora, Antoine Richard, Andrej Orsula, C\'edric Pradalier, Miguel A. Olivares-M\'endez

entry.summary: HYPER-GNC uses a hypernetwork that maps physics-informed task embeddings to the weights of a shared actor-critic policy, letting one compact controller handle velocity tracking, docking, inspection and obstacle-avoiding navigation for orbital free-flyers. The continuous embedding space allows zero-shot generalization to new mission configurations.

entry.title: Actuator-Aware Spatiotemporal Tube Synthesis for Temporal Reach-Avoid-Stay Tasks

author.name: Keshab Patra, K Madhava Krishna

entry.summary: Synthesizes spatiotemporal tubes for temporal reach-avoid-stay tasks on unknown nonlinear MIMO systems while embedding actuator saturation limits directly into tube generation, using Bernstein polynomial parameterization whose convex hull property allows sample-free constraint enforcement. Avoids the online re-optimization or controller redesign used by prior methods.

entry.title: Mirror Langevin diffusions: Convergence rates and Markov chain approximations

author.name: Benjamin Capdeville, Young-Heon Kim, Soumik Pal

entry.summary: Analyzes Mirror Langevin diffusions on Hessian manifolds, giving Lyapunov-based sufficient conditions for Poincare and log-Sobolev inequalities and hence exponential convergence, including for targets that are not strongly log-concave. It also studies Markov chain approximations of these diffusions.

entry.title: You (Yes, You) Need A February 2020 Checklist for AI Policy

author.name: davekasten

entry.summary: Urges AI policy practitioners to pre-write a concrete personal action checklist for a sudden crisis moment when AI becomes the dominant political issue, arguing that crisis responses draw on pre-existing prepared plans rather than fresh thinking. Cites historical precedents where prepared reports were rapidly institutionalized.

entry.title: Does ChatGPT really have a strong left-wing bias?

author.name: John-Clark Levin

entry.summary: A methodological critique of a widely shared media study claiming large left-wing bias in chatbots, arguing that forcing very short simplified answers is unrealistic, that some questions mislabel the conservative position, and that models usually present multiple sides under normal use. Includes the author's own replication attempts.

entry.title: ToolGuardian: Declarative Security for AI Agent-Tool Interactions

author.name: Arun Ravindran, Saurabh Deochake

entry.summary: ToolGuardian is a declarative policy framework for securing LLM agent tool use, combining pre-admission vetting of third-party tools with task-aware runtime authorization. It converts tool descriptions, code evidence, and observed behavior into structured facts so that policy decisions are deterministic and auditable rather than delegated to heuristic or LLM judgment.

entry.title: Unified Static-Dynamic Pruning for Efficient LLM Inference

author.name: Jinhyeok Kim, Yejoon Lee, Jaeyoung Do

entry.summary: SPDP unifies unstructured static weight pruning with input-adaptive dynamic pruning for LLM decoding on GPUs, co-designing a tiled column-wise bitmap compressed sparse format with matching kernels. It targets the bandwidth-bound, low-compute-intensity regime that dominates autoregressive inference cost.

entry.title: TRaM-VSR: Importance-Aware Token Routing and Merging for One-Step Diffusion Video Super-Resolution

author.name: Sicheng Gao, Zhuyun Zhou, Yixuan Liu, Tong Shen, Zongwei Wu, Radu Timofte

entry.summary: TRaM-VSR reduces the quadratic cost of diffusion-transformer video super-resolution by estimating token importance from motion cues fused with semantic text similarity, then routing and merging tokens adaptively. It specifically guards against irreversible detail loss and temporal flicker in one-step diffusion models.

entry.title: Interior interpretability with attention rollout: contraction and propagation profiles in Transformers

author.name: Umberto Biccari, Qian Huang, Enrique Zuazua

entry.summary: The paper proposes interior interpretability, studying how explicitly defined interaction operators compose across layers rather than only attributing outputs to inputs, and instantiates it for tabular transformers via attention rollout. Using Doeblin-Dobrushin contraction theory, it shows rollout operators with small Dobrushin coefficients are close to rank-one stochastic matrices, giving quantitative propagation and information-collapse profiles.

entry.title: \k{appa}-LoRA: Condition Numbers Reveal Which LoRA Matrices Worth Updating

author.name: Jianghui Wang, Silong Yong, Francesco Orabona, Marco Canini, Katia P. Sycara, Yaqi Xie

entry.summary: kappa-LoRA shows that LoRA matrices differ in how much they benefit from updating, with matrices having small condition numbers already well-balanced across directions and contributing little to adaptation. Selecting which matrices to update by condition number reduces fine-tuning cost, which matters for very large models and on-device settings.

entry.title: DomainPilot: Domain-Level Loss-Guided Two-Stage Data Mixture Optimization for Efficient Language Model Fine-Tuning

author.name: He Zhang

entry.summary: DomainPilot optimizes pretraining and fine-tuning data mixtures at the domain level by monitoring token-level per-domain loss dynamics in two stages, sidestepping the cost of per-sample selection and auxiliary proxy models. If the reported efficiency holds, it offers a cheap knob for industrial-scale corpus composition.

entry.title: Diffusion-Guided Search via Exponential Tilting (DiffTilt): An Application to Falsification of Safety-Critical Systems

author.name: Tanmay Khandait, Preetom Biswas, Hideki Okamoto, Bardh Hoxha, Georgios Fainekos, Giulia Pedrielli

entry.summary: DiffTilt exponentially tilts a diffusion model's joint distribution over environments and system executions to find rare safety-critical failures, showing that diffusion-guided sampling is exactly importance sampling in the joint space. This attacks the multiplicative rarity problem that makes falsification of autonomous and cyber-physical systems prohibitively expensive.

entry.title: Wrong Design Intent Is Worse Than None: A Derangement-Control Diagnosis of Header Conditioning in CAD Program Completion

author.name: Yang Xiao

entry.summary: Using a design-intent header prepended to CAD programs during LoRA fine-tuning of a small code model, the study runs a pre-registered matrix of correct, wrong, and masked headers and scores outputs with executable geometric assertions independent of the header extractor. It finds a semantically wrong header is worse than no header at all in conditional completion, a clean causal demonstration of conditioning sensitivity.

entry.title: Neural operator discovery from heterogeneous trajectories

author.name: Zituo Chen, Qiaofeng Li, Jiaxin Hu, Sili Deng

entry.summary: This work formulates neural operator discovery as learning a shared solution operator plus low-dimensional latent variables that capture system-to-system variation, without observing physical parameters, geometries, or boundary conditions. Factorized prediction and trajectory-decoupled sampling let it handle heterogeneous trajectory collections from families of dynamical systems.

entry.title: When Can Depth Replace Precision? A Resource Theory of Quantized Neural Computation

author.name: Mojtaba Soltanalian

entry.summary: This paper asks when extra depth of low-bit residual computation can substitute for missing numerical precision, modeling a quantized residual network as a schedule over a low-bit operation library and using relaxed control theory to characterize the infinite-depth limit. It identifies an exact structural floor no amount of depth can remove and gives convergence rates plus an arithmetic penalty that can reverse the conclusion.

entry.title: From Machine Learning to Large-Scale EO Products: Best Practices for Making Maps

author.name: Ghjulia Sialelli, Robin Young, Yuchang Jiang, Cesar Aybar, Linus Scheibenreif, Damien Robert, Clemens Mosig, Adam J. Stewart, Jan D. Wegner, Aleksis Pirinen, Olof Mogren, Konrad Schindler

entry.summary: A best-practices paper for turning machine learning models into credible large-scale Earth observation map products, arguing that preprocessing, dataset design, and global inference choices are tightly coupled and that early errors propagate silently into final maps. It consolidates guidance from a large group of remote sensing and ML researchers.

entry.title: Learning to Optimize at Scale: A Benders Decomposition-TransfORmers Framework for Stochastic Combinatorial Optimization

author.name: Seung Jin Choi, Kimiya Jozani, Josh Cooper, Esra Buyuktahtakin Toy

entry.summary: Embeds a pretrained transformer into Benders decomposition for two-stage stochastic mixed-integer programs, using learned subproblem solution predictions to generate stronger optimality and feasibility cuts. An expandable generation mechanism lets a model trained on a fixed horizon solve arbitrarily long instances.

entry.title: Real2Sim2Real for Vision-Language-Action Manipulation: An AMD ROCm-Based Pipeline

author.name: Qing Yang, Xun Wang, Ziguan Wang, Zhenjiang Li, Hongqiang Wang, Dongdong Weng

entry.summary: Presents a complete real-to-sim-to-real vision-language-action manipulation pipeline running entirely on AMD hardware and the ROCm software stack, spanning datacenter training, rendering GPUs, and edge inference. The point is to demonstrate that embodied VLA training and deployment is not locked to one vendor's ecosystem.

entry.title: TopoFE: topology-aware LLM-guided Automated Feature Engineering

author.name: Sha Li, Naren Ramakrishnan

entry.summary: TopoFE frames automated feature engineering for tabular data as LLM-guided program synthesis, adding memory of prior search experience and heterogeneous multi-population exploration to escape the convergence of static-prompt approaches. The topology-aware element steers search toward complementary feature compositions.

entry.title: Rendering on Real Silicon: GPU Render-Timing as a Passive, AI-Resistant CAPTCHA Signal

author.name: David Noever, Forrest McKee

entry.summary: This work proposes using GPU render-timing dynamics under a controlled WebGL workload as a privacy-preserving CAPTCHA signal that classifies human hardware versus automation without producing a persistent fingerprint. It includes a 12-hour in-the-wild deployment characterizing bot traffic and labeled timing data.

entry.title: Neural Representation of Minimal Surfaces

author.name: Jiayin Sun, Albert Chern

entry.summary: This short paper introduces an exact neural parameterization of minimal surfaces based on the Weierstrass-Enneper representation, avoiding the approximation error inherent in mesh discretization or PINN-style residual minimization. A training objective for the Plateau problem is formulated over this representation.

entry.title: Distributional Split Criteria for Random Forests: Extensions, Shrinkage, and the Robustness of Mean Splitting

author.name: Silas Koemen

entry.summary: The paper systematically compares distributional splitting criteria for random forests, including random-Fourier-feature MMD variants and a sliced-Wasserstein criterion, plus post-hoc kernel-mean shrinkage, inside one honest-forest implementation. A recurring finding is the surprising robustness of plain mean-based splitting.

entry.title: Disentangling Acoustic Cues in Alzheimer's Pathology and Perception: The Roles of Language and Gender

author.name: Liu He, Yuanchao Li, Yin-Long Liu, Rui Feng, Yiming Wang, Jiaxin Chen, Yizhe Wang, Jiahong Yuan

entry.summary: The study compares which acoustic features drive AI models predicting clinical Alzheimer's status versus human perceptual ratings, across Mandarin and Greek and across genders, using SHAP for interpretability. Alignment between pathology and perception holds for Mandarin and female speakers but breaks down for Greek and male speakers where pathology models did not beat chance.

entry.title: The Tokenizer Tax: Quantifying and Explaining the Cross-Lingual Cost of Subword Tokenization for Indian Languages

author.name: Priyansh Srivastava

entry.summary: This paper quantifies the tokenization penalty Indian languages pay under English-centric subword tokenizers, measuring fertility across six tokenizers and fourteen languages on FLORES-200. It reports an average eightfold token inflation relative to English and up to thirteenfold for Malayalam, shrinking effective context windows and raising API costs.

entry.title: Explaining GAND: A Resource on Gender-Ambiguous Natural Data & Contrastive Attribution

author.name: Jani\c{c}a Hackenbuchner, Jasper Degraeuwe, Arda Tezcan, Joke Daems

entry.summary: Releases GAND, a benchmark of naturally gender-ambiguous English source sentences for probing how machine translation systems assign gender when cues are absent, plus a contrastive attribution analysis into two gendered target languages. Aims to reveal which contextual tokens drive stereotyped gender choices.

entry.title: Do LLM Debates Repeat Arguments Differently Across Languages?

author.name: Huiqian Lai

entry.summary: Analyzes eight-turn LLM debates across 71 motions, six languages, and four model agents to measure whether later turns introduce new arguments or restate earlier ones, using a prior-argument similarity diagnostic. Chinese consistently shows more argument repetition than English, robust across embedding models and many controls.

entry.title: CONSISTRE: A Unified Consistency-Aware Framework for Document-Level Relation Extraction with Large Language Models

author.name: Mingxuan Sun

entry.summary: Proposes a consistency-aware framework for document-level relation extraction that enforces logical constraints like transitivity, symmetry, and functional uniqueness which independently generated LLM triple predictions routinely violate. Offers both an inference-time track for black-box models and a training-side track.

entry.title: Low-Latency Turn-Taking via Context-Aware Preface Generation in a Real-World Dialogue Robot

author.name: Yuki Okafuji, Koji Inoue, Yoshiki Ohira

entry.summary: Reduces perceived latency in LLM dialogue robots by generating a short context-aware prefatory utterance as soon as user intent becomes predictable, with a voice-activity-projection model deciding when to speak it. Field-tested with a route-guidance robot in a shopping mall against no-filler and fixed-filler baselines.

entry.title: Gubernaut: A Deterministic Homeostatic Controller for Affect-Regulated LLM Agents, Validated Across Independent Model Families

author.name: Dushyant Sharma

entry.summary: Gubernaut adds a deterministic runtime control layer above an LLM agent that reads only numeric telemetry (intensity, valence, repetition) and returns a regulating posture, aiming to damp escalation, sycophantic drift and perseveration. Because the meta-level ingests no tokens, it is claimed to be immune to prompt injection through that channel.

entry.title: TOM-GS: Editable Video Representation via Temporal Opacity Modulation of Static 3D Gaussians

author.name: Marek Lisowski, {\L}ukasz Smoli\'nski, Kornel Howil, Piotr Bili\'nski, Marcin Mazur, Przemys{\l}aw Spurek

entry.summary: TOM-GS represents video with ordinary static 3D Gaussians whose opacity is modulated over time by a learnable temporal mean and scale, so components fade in and out instead of requiring complex deformation fields. The simpler formulation is aimed at making the representation easier to edit downstream.

entry.title: Fast Fourier Convolutional GAN for 30 m Clear-Sky Land Surface Temperature Gap-Free Reconstruction

author.name: Marwa Alfouly, Smajil Halilovic, Nils Bochow, Thomas Hamacher, Niklas Boers, Konrad Schindler

entry.summary: Uses a multimodal fast Fourier convolutional GAN to reconstruct cloud-obscured pixels in 30 m clear-sky land surface temperature imagery, targeting large contiguous gaps at fine spatial resolution. Provides a scalable pipeline for producing gap-free LST datasets for climate and land-atmosphere studies.

entry.title: ReflexTrack: A Feedback-Driven Agent for Training-Free Referring Video Object Segmentation

author.name: Yuanjia Li, Tianyang Xu, Tao Zhou, Zhangyong Tang, Xiao-Jun Wu, Josef Kittler

entry.summary: ReflexTrack is a training-free agent for referring video object segmentation that adds spatial and temporal feedback loops, iteratively refining boxes and point prompts based on the induced mask instead of trusting one-shot grounding. It closes the verification gap in MLLM-plus-SAM pipelines.

entry.title: NSL-SLAM: High-Fidelity Neural Structured-Light Depth for Practical SLAM and Reconstruction

author.name: Jiaheng Li, Binsheng Zhang, Xinhai Chang, Wenzheng Chen

entry.summary: NSL-SLAM builds a depth-centric SLAM system around improved neural structured-light decoding that incorporates monocular depth priors, cutting depth RMSE by about 35 percent versus prior neural structured-light methods on a simulated benchmark. Stronger geometry then enables more stable tracking and faithful reconstruction.

entry.title: QueenVIS: Rethinking Image-Only Training for Video Instance Segmentation via Query Enrichment

author.name: Arian Kheirandish, Fardin Ayar, Ehsan Javanmardi, Manabu Tsukada, Mahdi Javanmardi

entry.summary: QueenVIS revisits image-only training for video instance segmentation, diagnosing object query quality as the bottleneck that causes identity drift, and enriches queries so inference-time association suffices. This challenges the field's drift toward costly identity-consistent video annotation.

entry.title: DreamStyle3D: Efficient 3D Stylized Asset Generation via Dual-Attention Disentanglement

author.name: Kai Wang, Ziheng Ouyang, Xuying Zhang, Ming-Ming Cheng, Qibin Hou

entry.summary: DreamStyle3D performs native 3D stylized asset generation using a decoupled dual cross-attention mechanism that separates geometric from stylistic features, avoiding indirect 2D-to-3D stylization pipelines. It targets simultaneous style fidelity, geometric consistency, and efficiency for games and VR.

entry.title: Stabilizing Deep Reconstruction Operators with Contractive Anchoring

author.name: Arghya Sinha, Trishit Mukherjee, Kunal N. Chaudhury

entry.summary: Diagnoses the peak-and-collapse instability that plagues Plug-and-Play and Regularization-by-Denoising reconstruction loops and proposes a data-driven contractive anchoring scheme to prevent divergence. The method formalizes instability as a local quantity and regularizes it adaptively.

entry.title: Segmentation Robustness and Predictive Utility in Glioblastoma Radiomics: Evidence for a Trade-off in Survival Modelling

author.name: Mariya Miteva, Maria Nisheva-Pavlova

entry.summary: Systematically tests whether radiomic features that are robust to tumor segmentation variability are also the most predictive of glioblastoma survival, using thousands of features across three tumor subregions. Finds evidence of a trade-off, implying robustness filtering can discard predictive signal.

entry.title: Provable Speedups From Dynamic Population Sizes in Evolutionary Algorithms for Multiobjective Optimization

author.name: Andre Opris

entry.summary: Provides rigorous runtime analysis showing that dynamic population sizing yields provable speedups for evolutionary multi-objective optimizers on a newly introduced bi-objective problem class, including a variant of NSGA-II. Gives theory for a heuristic widely used without justification.

entry.title: Pose-Aware Modeling to Mitigate Pose-Related Artifacts in Tactile Gloves

author.name: Tianhong Catherine Yu, Ziyi Kou, Mia Huang, Taylor Niehues, Yiyue Luo, Li Guan, Dingtian Zhang

entry.summary: Characterizes pose-related artifacts in soft tactile gloves, where sensors respond to hand posture as well as contact force, raising the minimum detectable force. Proposes pose-aware modeling to correct these artifacts and improve low-force contact detection.

entry.title: Continual-RL for Generalization in Autonomous Racing on the RoboRacer Platform

author.name: Joel Siegert, Edoardo Ghignone, Michele Magno

entry.summary: Applies continual reinforcement learning with continual backpropagation to autonomous racing on the RoboRacer platform, framing adaptation to new track and floor combinations as a continual learning problem with minimal new experience. Addresses plasticity loss during real-world adaptation.

entry.title: Recovery of latent inner products from an anisotropic Gaussian random geometric graph

author.name: Cheng Mao, Vidya Muthukumar

entry.summary: Studies recovery of latent inner products from random geometric graphs where latent points are anisotropic Gaussians, using a rank-d spectral approximation of the doubly centered adjacency matrix to handle degree fluctuations. Provides estimation guarantees in a constant-edge-density regime.

entry.title: PIRAMID: Progress and Plans

author.name: Lauren Greenspan

entry.summary: A research-agenda progress update from the PIRAMID effort, sketching team-level results and 6-12 month targets across pillars including statistical-physics-based theories of feature learning and generalization at a mesoscopic level between parameter dynamics and performance metrics. Also a recruiting and funding call.

entry.title: Efficient Learning of Truncated Boolean Product Distributions: Influence to the Rescue

author.name: Rohan Chauhan, Ioannis Panageas

entry.summary: This theory paper gives efficient algorithms for learning truncated Boolean product distributions using influence-based arguments, removing prior requirements such as local connectivity of the truncation set or constant survival mass and improving exponential sample complexities. It strengthens foundational results in high-dimensional statistical estimation under truncation.

entry.title: Verbalized Particle Posterior: Bayesian Inference over Natural Language Hypotheses

author.name: Yan Zhang, Shikan Lian, Shibo Li

entry.summary: Verbalized Particle Posterior treats natural-language hypotheses as Bayesian particles, updating a population of prompts via Metropolis-Hastings or sequential Monte Carlo and predicting by model averaging, all using the LLM as a black box. It supplies the uncertainty quantification and run-to-run stability that single-hypothesis verbalized learning lacks.

entry.title: Transfer Learning Architectures for Scalable Multi-Fidelity Bayesian Optimization

author.name: Jaewook Lee, Ethan Errington, Christian D. Lorenz, Miao Guo

entry.summary: The authors benchmark eleven transfer-learning surrogates against four Gaussian process methods inside closed-loop multi-fidelity Bayesian optimization for molecular and materials search, where GPs scale poorly and smoothness assumptions are violated. It is apparently the first test of transfer learning as the optimization engine rather than just a property predictor.

entry.title: WorldDiT: A Unified Diffusion Architecture for World and Action Modeling

author.name: Sen Wang, R. Gnana Praveen, Bidhan Roy, Marcos Villagra

entry.summary: WorldDiT is a single diffusion transformer that jointly generates robot action chunks and predicts future RGB patches, achieving competitive LIBERO success rates without relying on a large pretrained vision-language backbone. The authors position it as a strong sub-billion-parameter baseline for scaling studies.

entry.title: Physics Transformer: Tailoring Transformer for General PDE Prediction

author.name: Guoze Sun, Rui Zhang, Jiankai Tang, Mengtao Yan, Runze Mao, Zhi X. Chen, Hao Sun

entry.summary: Physics Transformer introduces a function-projection-based tokenizer that treats observed physical fields as finite samples of underlying infinite-dimensional functions, producing physically expressive tokens from arbitrary discretizations. This tailors transformer architectures to general PDE prediction rather than borrowing language or image tokenization.

entry.title: EditCLEVR: A Paired-Scene Intervention Benchmark for Compositional Faithfulness of Object-Centric Representations

author.name: Anuraag Gadehothur Karnam, Tarunesh Sathish

entry.summary: EditCLEVR is a benchmark of paired before/after synthetic scenes differing by exactly one known attribute edit on one known object, plus no-edit pairs to measure representational drift. It tests whether object-centric models change only the right slot in the right way under a controlled semantic intervention.

entry.title: Neural Network-Driven Volatility Drag Mitigation under Aggressive Leverage

author.name: Christian Bongiorno, Efstratios Manolakis, Rosario Nunzio Mantegna

entry.summary: Compresses an end-to-end neural minimum-variance portfolio model from roughly forty thousand parameters to about two thousand by replacing a large lag-transformation layer with a five-parameter weighted moving average and streamlining the eigencleaning and volatility modules. The compact model attains lower realized variance than nonlinear-shrinkage and risk-parity benchmarks under aggressive leverage.

entry.title: Evaluating the Impact of Reviewer Guideline Design on LLM-Based Automated Peer Review

author.name: Haowen Li, Yoichi Ishibashi, Masafumi Oyamada

entry.summary: Compares official conference reviewer guidelines against LLM-generated guidelines imitating strong human reviews for automated peer review, finding official criteria produce reviews most consistent with human judgments. Also finds strict rubric enforcement can be counterproductive.

entry.title: PlanCraft: Sketch, Refine, and Furnish for Architect-Inspired Progressive 3D Residential Scene Generation

author.name: Pengyu Zeng, Yuqin Dai, Jun Yin, Ziyang Han, Ng Cheuk Hei, Jing Zhong, Chaoyang Shi, ZhanXiang Jin, Maowei Jiang, Yuxing Han, Shuai Lu

entry.summary: PlanCraft generates 3D residential scenes progressively, mirroring how architects sketch, refine and then furnish, and treats the 2D floor plan as a hard spatial contract rather than an optional intermediate. This avoids the overlapping rooms and implausible proportions produced by systems that delegate layout directly to language models.

entry.title: Calibration-Free 3D Multi-Camera People Tracking for Indoor Environment

author.name: Ponleur Veng (CADT, M-PSI), Dominique Vaufreydaz (LIG, M-PSI), Phutphalla Kong (CADT)

entry.summary: A multi-camera 3D people tracking pipeline that removes the manual calibration bottleneck by inferring geometry directly from video with a geometry-grounded transformer, combined with detection, re-identification, pose estimation and pose-guided 3D lifting. Enables 3D tracking datasets from unconstrained archives.

entry.title: SILICA: Repurposing Diffusion Priors for Joint Glass Segmentation and Depth Estimation

author.name: Tarun R, Anuj Verma, Laksh Nanwani, Sourav Garg, K. Madhava Krishna

entry.summary: SILICA repurposes text-to-image diffusion priors for joint glass segmentation and monocular depth estimation, targeting the systematic failure of depth sensors and domain-specific models on transparent surfaces. It aims for zero-shot generalization to unseen indoor layouts where glass depth annotations are scarce.

entry.title: KANEx: Translating Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks' Interpretability to Medical Explainability

author.name: Krithi Shailya, Ananya Lakshmi Ravi, Venkatanathan K. V., Sowmya S. Sundaram, Gokul S. Krishnan, Aditi Anand, Balaraman Ravindran

entry.summary: KANEx leverages the spline-based symbolic transparency of Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks to generate more faithful textual explanations for chest X-ray classification, rather than layering a vision-language model over an opaque visual backbone. It argues linguistic fluency alone does not resolve model opacity.

entry.title: Moving-Horizon Estimation and Nonlinear Model Predictive Control of Cable-Driven Soft Manipulators

author.name: Lingxiao Xun, Haihong Li, Gang Zheng

entry.summary: Develops moving-horizon estimation and nonlinear MPC for cable-driven soft manipulators using reduced Cosserat rod dynamics, with a smooth approximation of the cable tension-slackness complementarity condition. Provides a physics-based, control-oriented alternative to purely data-driven soft robot models.

entry.title: SCOPE and SCION: A Benchmark and an Auditable Reference Pipeline for Schema Induction and Fusion from Text

author.name: Miaobo Hu, Xiaobo Guo, Shuhao Hu, Bokun Wang, Rui Chen, Xin Wang, Daren Zha, Jun Xiao

entry.summary: SCOPE is a benchmark for inducing schema graphs directly from raw text corpora, normalized from 24 public information-extraction datasets into evaluation-only gold schemas, and SCION is an auditable reference pipeline for schema construction with ontology normalization. The work targets the usually assumed-away upstream step of knowledge graph construction.

entry.title: Tool-Guided Retrieval-Augmented Repair for Securing LLM-Generated C Code

author.name: Vidyut Sriram, Saatvik Pradhan, Suman Saha

entry.summary: Builds an analysis-and-repair loop for LLM-generated C code that combines compiler diagnostics, static analysis and symbolic execution with retrieval of past repair patterns, evaluated on 5,000 embedded-relevant programming tasks. Baselines show compilation failure rates up to 46 percent and security defect rates up to 49 percent, which the pipeline substantially reduces.

entry.title: MosaicJoin: Compact Semantic Sketches for Value-Level Join Discovery

author.name: Grace Fan, Eden Wu, Majid Daliri, Juliana Freire

entry.summary: MosaicJoin introduces compact semantic sketches that approximate value-level comparison for discovering joinable columns in data lakes, aiming to keep fine-grained value alignment accuracy while avoiding the poor scaling of full pairwise value matching. It targets the accuracy-versus-efficiency trade-off between value-level and column-embedding methods.

entry.title: Sparse by Command: Task-Conditional Compute Skipping for Multi-Task Inference Accelerators

author.name: Afzal Ahmad, Gaoyu Mao, Shoubo Hu, Hui-Ling Zhen, Mingxuan Yuan, Xinyu Chen, Wei Zhang

entry.summary: The paper exploits the observation that a multi-task model knows its task command before inference begins, using a jointly trained lightweight gating network to predict per-tile binary execution masks so task-irrelevant output-channel tiles are skipped on an accelerator. Tile granularity matches the accelerator scheduling unit, giving skipping with essentially no overhead.

entry.title: From Isolated Tasks to Structured Capabilities: A Multilayer Taxonomy for Large Language Models

author.name: Shixin Fang (Fudan University), Jiachen Wo (Fudan University), Wenjuan Qin (Fudan University), Sihang Jiang (Fudan University), Yanghua Xiao (Fudan University)

entry.summary: The authors propose a multilayer capability taxonomy for LLM evaluation with 14 domains and 91 subskills organized into primitive, constructed, and integrative layers, grounded in human cognitive science rather than model architecture. They demonstrate utility by screening over 31,000 papers to map benchmark coverage and identify gaps.

entry.title: SiPhy: Single-Image Physical Property Reasoning

author.name: Hoang Le, Joonwoo Kwon, Elkhan Ismayilzada, Yufei Zhang, Zijun Cui

entry.summary: SiPhy infers physical properties such as mass, stiffness, and elasticity from a single RGB image by sampling pseudo-voxel points, extracting CLIP features, and grounding them to material candidates proposed by a vision-language model. A part-based contrastive aggregator enforces region consistency and a heaviness-aware refinement improves volume and thickness estimation.

entry.title: Phylogenetic signal in marine mammal and bird vocalizations captured by audio foundation models: the limited benefit of domain-specific pretraining

author.name: V\'ictor Rinc\'on Yepes

entry.summary: The study probes four pretrained audio models on a task none was trained for, recovering phylogenetic distance between species from vocalizations, and finds strong correlations for cetaceans with general-purpose models such as CLAP and AST. Notably, domain-specific bioacoustic pretraining provides little advantage over general audio foundation models.

entry.title: CausalGate: Causal Importance Distillation for Transformer Module Pruning

author.name: Kiran Nair, Smriti Regmi, Rodrigue Rizk

entry.summary: CausalGate selects transformer modules to skip by intervention rather than correlation, ablating individual attention and MLP sub-layers during calibration and measuring semantic damage as KL divergence of the final logit distribution. The resulting importance hierarchy is distilled into a static gating policy to avoid runtime routing overhead.

entry.title: The Entropic Bound for Transformers: Why Static Rank Fails and Attention-Native Rank Recovers

author.name: Byeong Hoon Yoon

entry.summary: This paper defines an entropic bound as a task-intrinsic spectral capacity for transformers, proving in a linear attention surrogate that the intrinsic rank of the token-mixing operator is a tight lower bound on required capacity and that gradient descent recovers it under low-rank implicit bias. It argues static rank measures fail and an attention-native rank is needed, potentially predicting minimum model size before training.

entry.title: ParasGB: A Graph Benchmark Suite for Parasitic Estimation on AMS Circuits

author.name: Jiajun Zou, Jiawei Liu, Ao Liu, Junnong Tian, Yibin Zhang, Chengjie Liu, Yuxi Wang, Shan Shen, Wenhua Gu, Jun Yang, Wenjian Yu

entry.summary: ParasGB is an open benchmark suite of large heterogeneous RC networks for graph-neural prediction of parasitic capacitance and resistance in analog and mixed-signal circuits before physical layout. Public high-fidelity data has been the bottleneck for reproducible progress in this EDA subfield.

entry.title: Extending Fourier Neural Operators for Modeling Parameterized and Coupled PDEs

author.name: Cheng Jing, Uvini Balasuriya Mudiyanselage, Abhishek Verma, Kallol Bera, Shahid Rauf, Kookjin Lee

entry.summary: The authors extend Fourier neural operators with hypernetwork-based conditioning on physical parameters and systematically explore component designs for coupled multi-variable systems, evaluating on benchmarks including a one-dimensional capacitively coupled plasma problem. The aim is handling parameterized and coupled PDEs with minimal architectural change and preserved FNO efficiency.

entry.title: Latent-LoRA: Compact Latent-Space Adapters with Gradient-Free Routing for Continual Learning

author.name: Reza Rahimi Azghan, Gautham Krishna Gudur, Giulia Pedrielli, Pavan Turaga, Hassan Ghasemzadeh

entry.summary: Latent-LoRA observes that pooled token embeddings from a frozen LLM embedding layer already separate tasks, so it fits a Gaussian mixture in that space to route inputs to per-task low-rank adapters without any trainable gate. This gives task-identity-free continual learning while avoiding the need to protect a router from forgetting.

entry.title: Why does Greedy Search produce Optimal Clustering Outcomes? A Fixed-Core Assignment Theory

author.name: Kai Ming Ting, Kaifeng Zhang, Sanjay Chawla

entry.summary: Provides a fixed-core assignment theory explaining why greedy search in cluster-as-distribution clustering attains optimal-looking outcomes and matches the spectral clustering objective without eigendecomposition.
