entry.summary: Argues that the classic shutdown problem desiderata are inadequate because an indifferent agent is vulnerable to trade with external agents who have preferences over its shutdown. This suggests indifference-based solutions are fragile and a stronger criterion is needed for corrigibility.

entry.title: Can we teach a model to encode a semantic feature on a chosen manifold in just three channels?

author.name: Phu Hoang

entry.summary: A safety-puzzle submission that trains a small MLP so a semantic feature about countries is encoded along a chosen nonlinear manifold within three reserved channels, probing whether representation geometry can be deliberately controlled. Includes code and interactive write-up.

entry.title: Discrepancy-Rounded Fair Bandits with Static and Time-Varying Exposure Floors

author.name: Ibne Farabi Shihab, Joyanta Jyoti Mondal, Anuj Sharma

entry.summary: This work casts stochastic bandits with hard minimum-exposure floors as a rounding and discrepancy problem, and gives a blockwise algorithm that deterministically satisfies time-varying per-block floors while achieving regret bounds scaling with the discretionary budget rather than the horizon. It matters for recommendation and regulated allocation settings requiring guaranteed provider exposure.

entry.title: Variance-Preserving Orthogonal Selection (VPOS): Greedy Feature Selection via Orthogonal Deflation in PCA Loading Space

author.name: Baran Koseoglu, Berrin Yanikoglu

entry.summary: VPOS greedily selects features in weighted PCA loading space, deflating the chosen direction's variance after each pick so subsequent selections cover orthogonal parts of the covariance structure, with a connection to submodular maximization and a reproducible rule for its single hyperparameter. It reports best reconstruction error on eight benchmarks while running far faster than graph-based selectors.

entry.title: SPRKD: Effective Knowledge Distillation for Deep Neural Networks via Saddle Region Approximation

author.name: Aditya Dewan, Arjun Yogeswaran, Benjamin Fedoruk

entry.summary: SPRKD reframes knowledge distillation away from logit mimicry, instead using the teacher to identify saddle regions with strong further-descent potential and guide the student's optimization curvature. The motivation is that standard distillation often acts as mere regularization rather than substantive knowledge transfer for small students.

entry.title: DP-IVON-Gradsq: Differentially Private Squared-Gradient Improved Variational Online Newton

author.name: Nour Jamoussi, Ikram Dridi, Giuseppe Serra, Marios Kountouris

entry.summary: Introduces a differentially private variant of the Improved Variational Online Newton optimizer that builds its curvature estimate from privatized gradients using a noise-corrected squared-gradient estimator. This reduces harmful interaction between DP noise and Bayesian posterior-sampling noise.

entry.title: DriveDNA: A Large-Scale Multimodal Naturalistic Driving Dataset and Benchmark for Driving Style Identification

author.name: Yuhang Wang, Lingyao Li, Hao Zhou

entry.summary: DriveDNA is a large naturalistic driving dataset of 4,121 drives from 465 drivers across 115 vehicle models with 975 hours of synchronized telemetry and forward video, designed so that driver-specific style can be separated from vehicle and situation confounds. It comes with a benchmark for personalized driving-style identification.

entry.title: Adaptive Data Admission and Retention for Streaming Federated Learning

author.name: Zhuoyi Zhao, Ben Liang

entry.summary: Studies federated learning over streaming data with limited client memory and time-varying data-acquisition costs, deriving an error bound that accounts for effective sample size, distinct-sample growth, and reuse imbalance. From it, a drift-plus-penalty policy jointly decides which new samples to admit and what to retain.

entry.title: MEGA-CL: A Molecular Foundation Model for Generalizable ADMET Prediction through Graph External Attention and Contrastive Learning

author.name: Tinghui Jin, Kedu Jin, Ying Li, Guanghui Ren, Jingzhi Xue, Shiyu Zhou, Xiaoli Dai, Li-bin Wei, Xijing Chen, Di Zhao, Jinfeng Liu

entry.summary: MEGA-CL is a graph neural network foundation model for predicting absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity properties, combining self-supervised contrastive pretraining with multi-head external attention and enhanced message passing to reduce over-smoothing. It reports gains over state-of-the-art baselines across 13 datasets and 21 tasks.

entry.title: AI-Assisted Causal Inference and Mediation Analyses of Environmental and Psychosocial Determinants of Subjective Cognitive Difficulties in the All of Us Research Program

author.name: Cong Cao, Shuangge Ma

entry.summary: Uses All of Us longitudinal data to link daily weather and air-pollution exposures to attention and subjective cognitive outcomes, applying fixed-effects, lagged, and event-study designs plus ML heterogeneity exploration, with BRFSS replication. Reported associations are small and largely attenuate under stricter designs, cautioning against causal overreach.

entry.title: Agent Team Work Zone: An Automated, Persistent Workspace for Long-Lived Coding Agent Teams

author.name: Shouren Wang

entry.summary: Describes a persistent workspace system for long-lived teams of coding agents that survives terminal closure, preserves working detail against context compaction, and tracks accumulated agentic technical debt. It targets concrete operational failures observed with Claude Code agent teams.

entry.title: Visual Information Extraction from Documents via Classification-Guided Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Huafu Li, Guo Chen, Jia Xia, Lei Wang, Wei Du, Yun Yao, Weijun Peng, Liming Li

entry.summary: Proposes decoupling document-type classification from content extraction in visual information extraction, using the predicted type to drive in-context-learning prompts for a large vision-language model. Aims for robust zero-shot extraction across highly variable layouts without layout-specific training.

entry.title: Test-Time Adaptation via Dual Distillation for Videos Under Severe Distribution Shifts

author.name: Andr\'e Sacilotti, Samuel Felipe dos Santos, Jurandy Almeida

entry.summary: Proposes a dual-distillation test-time adaptation method for video models facing continuous, temporally correlated data under severe distribution shifts. It targets a setting most TTA work avoids because of temporal correlation and extreme domain gaps.

entry.title: Denoising 3D images: robustness of persistent homology measures

author.name: Ebru Dagdelen, Aakash Karlekar, Manav Arora, Matthew Illingsworth, Jonathan Jaquette, Linda J. Cummings, Lou Kondic

entry.summary: Empirically studies how spatially uncorrelated noise and various denoising choices distort persistent homology summaries of 3D porous-media images, comparing bottleneck and Wasserstein distances, persistence statistics and persistence images. Provides guidance on which topological measures survive the denoising pipeline.

entry.title: Benchmarking Fine-tuning and Retrieval Strategies for a Multimodal Language Model on the NRC Reactor Operator Licensing Examination

author.name: Isak Hwang, Yoon Pyo Lee

entry.summary: The study benchmarks eight configurations of an existing 31B open-weight multimodal Gemma 4 model, including supervised fine-tuning on Gemini-distilled chain-of-thought and various retrieval setups, against 14 US Nuclear Regulatory Commission reactor operator fundamentals exams from 2015 to 2021. Performance is judged against the standard 80 percent human passing threshold.

entry.title: Explicit Iteration Complexity of Exact Data-Driven Inverse Optimization for Integer Linear Programs

author.name: Akira Kitaoka

entry.summary: This theory paper supplies the missing lower bound on the geometric constant that governs iteration complexity of exact gradient-based data-driven inverse optimization for integer linear programs. Bounding that constant as a function of problem size makes the previously abstract finite-termination guarantee explicitly size-dependent.

entry.title: From Hybrid Mechanistic--Data-Driven Modeling Toward Neuro-Symbolic AI: What, Why, and How

author.name: Moein E. Samadi, Andreas Schuppert

entry.summary: This position and framework paper recasts hybrid mechanistic plus data-driven models as instances of a neuro-symbolic interface, putting first-principles knowledge on the symbolic side, learned modules on the belief side, and explicitly representing validity domains and epistemic uncertainty of the mechanistic component. It offers shared vocabulary for comparing and verifying hybrid designs across domains.

entry.title: Same Predictions, Different Reasons: The Effect of Quantization on Model Explanations

author.name: Kazi Kamruzzaman Rabbi, Md. Zami Al Zunaed Farabe, M. Sohel Rahman

entry.summary: This study asks whether post-training quantization preserves not just accuracy but the reasons behind predictions, comparing Grad-CAM and complementary attributions across five CNNs at 8-bit and 4-bit precision. It finds that predictions can match while internal attribution patterns diverge, which has implications for auditing compressed models.

entry.title: Does Graph Compression Preserve Signal Propagation?

author.name: Kawshik Banerjee, Khaled Mohammed Saifuddin

entry.summary: The authors ask whether graph coarsening and sparsification preserve signal propagation dynamics, measuring diversity and mixing behavior directly rather than judging compression by downstream accuracy alone. Across five datasets they find a consistent tension in which sparsification retains signal diversity while coarsening behaves differently, giving practitioners guidance on which compression to choose.

entry.title: On the post-hoc Evaluation of PDE Discovery: A Multifaceted Challenge of Scientific Advancement

author.name: Baptiste Mathevon, Farah Cherfaoui, Amaury Habrard, Marc Sebban

entry.summary: A position and analysis paper arguing that evaluating discovered partial differential equations requires jointly weighing predictive accuracy, physical consistency, interpretability, and out-of-distribution generalization, which existing metrics cover only partially and sometimes conflict. It surveys and critiques current post-hoc evaluation practice in PDE discovery.

entry.title: Flash-CNNCap: Capacitance Extraction via Image Mapping

author.name: Hector R. Rodriguez, Jiechen Huang, Wenjian Yu

entry.summary: Flash-CNNCap recasts parasitic capacitance extraction in chip layout as image-to-image regression over spatial contribution maps, cutting the number of network passes needed for a full capacitance matrix from quadratic to linear in conductor count. Outputs are aggregated by masks into a physically consistent Maxwell capacitance matrix.

entry.title: DynaCalKV: Key-Value Cache Compression via Head Grouping and Adaptive Rank Allocation

author.name: Tan T. Nguyen, Quan V. Dang

entry.summary: DynaCalKV compresses the transformer key-value cache with low-rank factorization that treats keys and values differently and groups attention heads dynamically according to structural similarity rather than a fixed partition. This targets the long-context memory bottleneck during LLM inference.

entry.title: A Vocabulary for Multi-Agent Automated Research Systems

author.name: Bardiya Akhbari

entry.summary: Proposes a standardized vocabulary describing multi-agent automated research systems along eight axes covering agent roles, available operations, permissions, communication, information visibility, action selection, initialization, and evaluation. It frames each run as a trajectory drawn from a distribution, making design choices comparable across systems.

entry.title: Variable Importance Identification Through Lazy Training for Binary Classification

author.name: Anand Singh, Luke Pennella, Eshan Kabir, Xiaoxi Shen

entry.summary: Extends variable-importance testing based on lazy training from regression to binary classification, offering an efficient feature-selection algorithm with controlled error rates under weak assumptions. Theory is complemented by empirical validation.

entry.title: IKS-Instruct: A 24,000-Example Multilingual Dataset for Teaching Language Models Indian Knowledge Systems

author.name: Shwetha Singaravelu, Gayathri Muruganantham, Lakshmi Rajendran, Santhosh Sivasubramani

entry.summary: IKS-Instruct is a roughly 24,800-example instruction-tuning dataset teaching models to deliver educational content grounded in Indian Knowledge Systems across seven languages and 41 Vedic pedagogical techniques, aligned to the CBSE school curriculum. It targets a domain absent from English-dominated instruction datasets.

entry.title: Mwando: Leveraging AI to Preserve and Teach shiKomori

author.name: Naira Abdou Mohamed, Haidar Nassur Said Ali, Mohamed Hazra, Naoufal Mohamed Soibira, Roushnaty Ali Yamani

entry.summary: Describes a multi-agent educational assistant for shiKomori and its four dialects, combining a curated knowledge base of phrases, proverbs, dictionaries, and grammar with vector search, a knowledge graph, and web-search fallback. Evaluated on 500 queries with strong results on vocabulary and grammar lookups.

entry.title: DINOv3-MIL: Per-Kidney Multi-Label Tumour and Cyst Detection from Foundation-Model Patch Tokens on KiTS23

author.name: Vishalakshi M, Sahil Sharma, Pramod Kumar P

entry.summary: Compares three aggregators over frozen DINOv3 patch tokens for per-kidney tumour and cyst detection on KiTS23: a CLS linear probe, gated attention multiple-instance learning, and a prototype head. Attention MIL performs best and concentrates attention within annotated lesions well above chance.

entry.title: CrossSpine: Multi-scale Cross-sequence Attention with Anatomical Priors for Automated Pfirrmann Grading

author.name: Hai Son Nguyen, Duong Ngoc Vu, Trong-Nghia Nguyen, Bien Tran Van, Van-Dem Pham, Trang Mai Xuan, Huan Vu, Thien Van Luong

entry.summary: CrossSpine fuses features from multiple MRI sequences at several spatial scales via cross-sequence attention for automated Pfirrmann grading of lumbar disc degeneration, and adds disc-level anatomical priors so the model learns level-specific patterns. Contributes a curated grading dataset as well.

entry.title: IJCB-AFMFR 2026: Competition on Adapting Foundation Models for Face Recognition Using Synthetic Training Data

author.name: Tahar Chettaoui, Guray Ozgur, Eduarda Caldeira, Arturas Nakvosas, Hatef Otroshi Shahreza, S\'ebastien Marcel, Rishabh Shukla, Aditya Takkar, Rushil Khullar, Lalak Yadav, Gourav Gupta, Anant Gupta, Shiqi Yu, Vitomir Struc, Naser Damer, Fadi Boutros

entry.summary: Summarizes an IJCB 2026 competition on adapting the CLIP ViT-L/14 foundation model for face recognition using only synthetic identity training data, across full-data and limited-data tracks. Eight submissions from four teams were ranked on standard verification and identification benchmarks.

entry.title: Surgical Re-enactment for Operating Room Workflow Datasets

author.name: Jana Nina Friedrich, Andrea Karin Maria Ross, Angelo Henriques, Mario Peter Martin Weisser, Ling Zhang, Mohammad Ali Nasseri

entry.summary: Describes a methodology for re-enacting full surgical procedures in a reconstructed operating room to generate repeatable, annotatable multi-view workflow datasets. It circumvents ethics, sterility and camera-placement barriers that block data collection in real ORs.

entry.title: Co-planning of Flight Corridors and Communication Infrastructure for Urban Drone Logistics Networks

author.name: Yingjie He, Yikang Wang, Zhenyu Gao

entry.summary: Jointly optimizes base station placement and UAV flight corridor design for urban drone logistics using a channel-reciprocity-guided combinatorial multi-armed bandit, rather than planning connectivity and routes separately. Aims to cut both infrastructure cost and flight detours under connectivity constraints.

entry.title: Multi-Domain Physics-Based MDO of Multirotor UAVs: A Deterministic Framework for Discrete COTS Sizing

author.name: Akshay Gupta Burela, P. B. Sujit

entry.summary: AeroEval is a multidisciplinary design optimization engine for multirotor UAVs that resolves structural, electrochemical, aerodynamic and kinematic couplings simultaneously and maps continuous optima to purchasable off-the-shelf components. It uses a calibrate-then-test protocol on held-out designs to avoid circular validation.

entry.title: Trajectory-Aware Retrieval Agents for Temporal Decision- Making

author.name: Jing Wang, Jie Shen, Xing Niu

entry.summary: TLM is a closed-loop retrieval agent for decisions over long, chronologically structured documents, addressing how standard RAG shatters temporal ordering into isolated snippets. It fits a latent growth curve model over retrieved chunk embeddings to detect trends, turning points and evidence gaps, and refines the evidence set using SHAP-guided feedback.

entry.title: Dynamic Capability Scoping for Enterprise AI Agents: A Synthetic Dataset and Three-Source Permission Architecture

author.name: Halil Burak Noyan

entry.summary: Argues enterprise AI agents should receive dynamically scoped least-privilege credentials rather than static role-wide tool access, on the principle that a credential absent from context cannot be misused regardless of the agent reasoning. It sketches a three-source permission architecture with role ceilings, a task-context classifier, and policy-derived prohibitions, plus a synthetic dataset.

entry.title: MotifRole-Diff: Risk-Optimal Role-Aware Corruption for Masked Molecular Graph Diffusion

author.name: Tasfia Nuzhat Ornee, Elias Hossain, Ivan Garibay, Niloofar Yousef

entry.summary: MotifRole-Diff replaces the uniform masking schedule in discrete diffusion for molecular graphs with role-aware corruption rates set by empirically measured denoising difficulty and each token role influence on the decoded molecule. It keeps the architecture, clean sequence space and lossless representation unchanged.

entry.title: Multi-Horizon Consistency as Geometry: When Latent Dynamics Contract, and When They Do Not

author.name: Kavya Bhand, Aadi Joshi

entry.summary: Treats the weight on multi-step latent consistency in video predictors and world models as a diagnostic knob and measures its effect on transition geometry, finding that strong weighting contracts latent dynamics and halves long-horizon error on Moving-MNIST. The same loss does not produce contraction on action-conditioned control environments or real video, even when error improves.

entry.title: Enhancing SLMs for Sustainable Code Optimization in Radio-Astronomy

author.name: Elisa Chiarotto, Jingbo Li, P. Chris Broekema, Rob V. van Nieuwpoort

entry.summary: Investigates whether small language models can help optimize the large radio-astronomy codebase facing a 40-fold compute increase after a telescope upgrade, with sustainability as an explicit objective. The approach assists developers in evaluating and accelerating existing software and adopting hardware accelerators.

entry.title: Co-design of LLM-based preference agents: participation may drive overtrust

author.name: Michael J. Fell

entry.summary: A qualitative study where twelve participants co-designed personal LLM preference agents for household energy decisions, then validated them. Participants engaged willingly and largely believed their agents represented them well, yet independent validation showed mixed human-agent alignment, suggesting participation can create overtrust rather than fix misrepresentation.

entry.title: From Perturbation Correction to Geometry-Aware Sampling: Sharpness-Guided Equilibrium Sampling for Balanced Flat Minima in Long-Tailed Learning

author.name: Jiaxin Deng, Junbiao Pang

entry.summary: Sharpness-Guided Equilibrium Sampling treats the mini-batch sampling distribution itself as a control variable for optimization geometry in long-tailed learning, upweighting rarely sampled classes while suppressing classes with large sharpness-aware-minimization losses. This intervenes before biased batches are drawn, unlike loss or perturbation reweighting methods.

entry.title: Practical Graph Optimisation and AI-Driven Models for Active Directory Security Hardening

author.name: Huy Q. Ngo

entry.summary: This work extends attack-graph hardening for Microsoft Active Directory to more realistic settings, addressing graph dynamism, active defenses beyond simply revoking vulnerable edges, and uncertain or partially feasible remediations. It combines graph optimization with learned models to produce practical hardening recommendations.

entry.title: Towards Trustworthy and Cost-Efficient Data Integration: From Na\"ive RAG to Agentic RAG

author.name: Chuangtao Ma, Arijit Khan

entry.summary: A vision and survey paper tracing data integration from naive retrieval-augmented generation through GraphRAG and knowledge-graph RAG toward agentic RAG, with trustworthiness defined as evidence-grounded, verifiable, hallucination-resistant reasoning. It outlines cost and accuracy challenges for enterprise deployment.

entry.title: Unboxing Diffusion Models for the Arts: Interactive Model Bending and Practice-Based Explainability

author.name: Ahmed M. Abuzuraiq, Philippe Pasquier

entry.summary: This work reframes explainability for artists as material engagement, providing interactive model bending and inspection controls for text-to-image diffusion models integrated into a ComfyUI node workflow with layer selection and intervention. It argues large models can act as creative materials when internal structure is visible and manipulable.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Privacy Game in Federated Learning: A Unified Mean-Field View

author.name: Kun Zhao, Xu Chen

entry.summary: Federated learning privacy choices are modeled as a mean-field game in which each client picks its own privacy budget and interacts with the population only through a single aggregate statistic, making equilibrium computation tractable as client count grows. This bridges noise-injection mechanisms and game-theoretic accounts of client incentives.

entry.title: XMix: Combating Extremely Noisy Labels via Local Smoothness in Self-Supervised Feature Space

author.name: Chengqi Li, Yangdi Lu, Zhihao Shi, Wenbo He, Chamseddine Talhi, Nadjia Kara

entry.summary: XMix uses local smoothness in a self-supervised feature space, rather than potentially corrupted labels, to drive every stage of clean-sample selection for learning under extremely noisy annotations. It aims to avoid the tuning and prior noise-rate knowledge that current selection methods require.

entry.title: ADVERSARIAL: And-Inverter Graph-Assisted Hardware Trojan Detection At Scale

author.name: Yaroslav Popryho, Debjit Pal, Inna Partin-Vaisband

entry.summary: Detects hardware trojans in billion-gate netlists by converting flattened designs into and-inverter graphs and embedding each edge triple with knowledge-graph embedding techniques, giving constant-size node representations with multi-hop context and linear scaling. Scalability is the central claim.

entry.title: MIME: Multimodal Interactive Motion Encoder

author.name: Addison Zucek, Prerit Gupta, Kamila Kuatova, Aniket Bera

entry.summary: MIME is a text-motion encoder built specifically for two-person interactive motion, using stream-based co-attention with explicit interaction features and curriculum contrastive training. It outperforms early and late fusion baselines on Inter-X retrieval across gallery sizes.

entry.title: Frequency-Based Reservoir computing

author.name: Arthur S Powanwe

entry.summary: Proposes a reservoir computing design built from frequency-tuned oscillatory units inspired by brain rhythms, replacing randomly connected reservoirs to make behavior interpretable and hyperparameter tuning more principled. Aims to explain how reservoirs encode dynamics rather than just tuning them empirically.

entry.title: DishSeg24k: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Food Segmentation with Stochastic Expert Decoding

author.name: Yilin Wang, Haochen Shi, Guanyu Chen, Weiqing Min, Jinkai Zheng, Chenggang Yan, Shuqiang Jiang

entry.summary: Releases DishSeg24k, a dish-level food segmentation benchmark with about 24k images, 112k instances, and 278 fine-grained categories in real dining scenes, plus FEAST, a transformer that treats query decoding as a Markov decision process with expert routing. Targets dense overlap, fine-grained similarity, and long-tail distributions.

entry.title: Multi-Modal Object Re-Identification with Prompt-S6 and Semantic-Aware Knowledge Guidance

author.name: Weixiang Zhou, Jiabei Zuo, Yuhao Wang, Cong Wang, Huchuan Lu, Zhixun Su

entry.summary: PRISM performs multi-modal object re-identification using a prompt-conditioned state-space (Mamba-style) backbone for linear-complexity cross-modal interaction, plus semantic knowledge guidance to suppress background interference and align three modalities. Targets the cost and pairwise-fusion limits of prior work.

entry.title: Geometry Meets Semantics: Fractional Gradient Stabilization for Semantic-Driven Bounding Box Optimization in Visual Detection Tasks

author.name: Qi Ming, Haitian Yang, Xudong Zhao, Mingjing Zhao, Liuqian Wang, Nanqing Liu

entry.summary: Introduces a fractional-gradient semantic IoU loss for oriented bounding box regression, injecting semantic similarity into an otherwise purely geometric objective and stabilizing the unstable orientation gradients that cause convergence oscillation. Applies to oriented object detection.

entry.title: XMatchAD: A Cross-Modal Matching Perspective on Reconstruction-based Anomaly Detection

author.name: Mingxiu Cai, Zhe Zhang, Gaochang Wu, Tianyou Chai

entry.summary: XMatchAD recasts reconstruction-based unsupervised anomaly detection as cross-modal matching, treating the input and its reconstruction as two complementary modalities whose correspondence structure reveals anomalies. Targets subtle defects and blurred anomaly boundaries in multi-class settings.

entry.title: Contrastive Parameter Disentanglement for Multi-modal Remote Sensing Image Generation

author.name: Yu Zhang, Wenda Zhao, Haojun Tang, Haipeng Wang

entry.summary: Generates semantically consistent optical, infrared, and SAR remote sensing images from a single text prompt by disentangling shared semantics from modality-specific attributes at the parameter level within an orthogonal subspace. Extends remote sensing generation beyond single-modality synthesis.

entry.title: Effective Receptive Field Ordering Matters for Infrared Small Target Detection

author.name: Guoyi Zhang, Yanjin Du, Zhengyao Zhao, Tongsu Zhang, Guangsheng Xu, Siyang Chen, Xiangpeng Xu, Han Wang, Xiaohu Zhang

entry.summary: Studies the ordering of effective receptive fields during feature refinement as an architectural dimension for infrared small target detection, distinct from receptive field size design, and casts deep feature transformation as progressive residual correction. Derives scheduling principles from scale-frequency correspondence and related properties.

entry.title: MarineEVT: Advancing Event-Centric Marine Video Understanding via Visual Tool Reasoning

author.name: Tuan-An To, Yuk-Kwan Wong, Tuan-Anh Vu, Ziqiang Zheng, Sai-Kit Yeung

entry.summary: MarineEVT introduces an event-centric marine video understanding dataset and a visual tool-reasoning approach for vision-language models, targeting sparse and unpredictable underwater events. It addresses domain expertise requirements and weak temporal localization in video VLMs.

entry.title: DY-LUT: Depth-Aware YCbCr Lookup Tables for Real-Time Underwater Image Enhancement

author.name: Cunhao Zhu, Xiangtao Kong, Dongliang Xu, Zhiheng Zhang, Tianyu Wang, Yue Yao

entry.summary: DY-LUT conditions learnable 4D lookup tables on depth and per-pixel degradation indices in YCbCr space for real-time underwater image enhancement, with lightweight local refinement. It retains LUT efficiency while allowing spatially adaptive, wavelength-aware correction with a 3.56M-parameter network.

entry.title: Direction-adaptive Mamba: Spatial-Frequency Dual-Domain Collaborative Learning for PolSAR Image Classification

author.name: Junfei Shi, Yu Cheng, Haojia Zhang, Wenqiang Hua, Junhuai Li, Maoguo Gong

entry.summary: Proposes DA-Mamba, a state-space backbone for polarimetric SAR classification that adds edge-aligned direction-adaptive scanning and joint spatial-frequency processing. It targets anisotropic scattering patterns that fixed-order Mamba scans handle poorly.

entry.title: Efficient multidisciplinary design via Bayesian optimization

author.name: Nathalie Bartoli, Thierry Lefebvre, R\'emi Lafage, Paul Saves, Youssef Diouane, Joseph Morlier

entry.summary: Describes SEGOMOE, a Bayesian optimization toolkit built on Gaussian process mixtures that handles mixed continuous, discrete, categorical, and hierarchical design variables plus multi-fidelity data and hidden constraints. It is validated on benchmarks and aeronautical multidisciplinary design problems.

entry.title: Filling Before Advancing: Capability-Gap-Driven Post-Training for Scenario-Specialized Remote Sensing MLLMs

author.name: Yuheng Zong, Minghua Wang, Xin Zhao, Zhi-Hui Zhan, Antonio Plaza, Jon Atli Benediktsson

entry.summary: Filling Before Advancing frames adaptation of remote-sensing multimodal LLMs as a capability-gap problem, first closing prerequisite skill gaps before specializing to a target scenario instead of single-stage supervised fine-tuning. It is instantiated for coastal harbor understanding with a new three-layer multi-source dataset.

entry.title: Quantum Spectral Model: Data Reuploading with Input-Conditioned Frequency Support

author.name: Peiyong Wang, Udaya Parampalli, Casey R. Myers

entry.summary: Quantum Spectral Models construct the generator of the data-encoding unitary directly from each input matrix so that spectral values and subspaces are represented explicitly, unlike common coordinate-wise rotation-gate encodings. Three variants based on symmetric, global block, and patch-local block Hamiltonians are analyzed with input-conditioned frequency support.

entry.title: Semalith v1.4: A Calibrated 184M Safety Classifier Achieving State-of-the-Art Prompt-Injection Detection at 44x Fewer Parameters than Llama-Guard-3-8B

author.name: Tejasvi C. Addagada

entry.summary: Semalith v1.4 is a 184M-parameter DeBERTa-based guardrail that classifies prompt injection, general harm, and financial-services regulatory compliance in a single forward pass using a 22-class head with an auxiliary super-category head, trained on a deduplicated 76,000-row corpus mined from 49 public sources. The claim is state-of-the-art prompt-injection detection at 44 times fewer parameters than Llama-Guard-3-8B.

entry.title: Physically Verifiable Evidence and LLM-Based Reporting for Bearing Fault Diagnosis

author.name: Yuntong Chen, Jianyu Liu, Guobin Zhao, Ziang Wang, Chao Chen, Ju Huang, Xitian Tian, Lijiang Huang

entry.summary: DENet outputs physically checkable evidence for bearing fault diagnosis instead of just a class label with a softmax score, and constrains an LLM report generator to that evidence to limit hallucination in maintenance documentation. The framing that predictions must be verifiable against independent physical knowledge before action is the interesting part.

entry.title: Online Policy Evaluation for MDPs with Dynamic UBSR Measures

author.name: Weikai Wang, Erick Delage

entry.summary: The authors develop online, simulator-free algorithms with linear function approximation for evaluating policies under dynamic utility-based shortfall risk measures, prove almost-sure convergence for the base temporal-difference method, and propose accelerated variants. It broadens risk-aware RL beyond restrictive risk classes.

entry.title: Covariance Last-Layer Ensembles: Function-Space Diversity for Efficient Uncertainty Quantification

author.name: H. Martin Gillis, Isaac Xu, Gabriel Spadon, Thomas Trappenberg

entry.summary: Attacks diversity collapse in last-layer ensembles for out-of-distribution detection by enforcing diversity directly in function space through a covariance-based objective, rather than the indirect weight-orthonormality used by orthonormal certificates. The result is cheap single-pass epistemic uncertainty that retains member disagreement.

entry.title: Controllable Diversity in Normalization-Based Implicit Ensembles via Softmax-Temperature Modulation

author.name: Mihai Suteu, Ovidiu Serban

entry.summary: Introduces a normalization-based implicit ensemble in which each member is treated as a task modulated by sigmoid-bounded scalers on a shared backbone, plus a softmax-temperature regularizer that tunes how much members share during training. This lets practitioners trace the accuracy-versus-diversity tradeoff rather than fixing diversity at initialization.

entry.title: Forecasting the Emergence and Evolution of Crash Hotspots: A Unified Deep Learning Framework for Proactive Traffic Safety

author.name: Jingwen Zhu, Keshu Wu, Pei Li, Steven T. Parker, Bin Ran, David A. Noyce

entry.summary: HERALD is a deep learning framework that treats crash hotspots as episodes with a life cycle, jointly detecting emerging hotspots, forecasting next-week locations, and tracking individual hotspots over time. The aim is to let enforcement anticipate rather than trail risk concentrations.

entry.title: EchoBridge: Long-Tail-Aware ECG-Echocardiography Text Alignment for Echocardiography-Derived Cardiac Findings

author.name: Xiaocheng Fang, Jieyi Cai, Guangkun Nie, Haoyu Wang, Jiarui Jin, Yujie Xiao, Bo Liu, Chenyang He, Qinghao Zhao, Gaofeng Cheng, Hongyan Li, Shenda Hong

entry.summary: EchoBridge aligns ECG signals with text from echocardiography reports using shared-plus-private projections and prototype boundary calibration tuned to class frequency, targeting rare cardiac findings. It aims to let cheap ECG recordings predict echo-derived diagnoses.

entry.title: AI-interpreted Optical Scattering for Robust and Focal Depth-Aware Imaging

author.name: Eunji Ko, Patrick Ross, Corey Hart, Wolfgang Losert

entry.summary: Argues optical scattering can be helpful rather than purely harmful in imaging, comparing scattered and unscattered MNIST speckle datasets with an interpretable variational autoencoder latent space. Scattering appears to spread information spatially, improving robustness to pixel dropout and encoding focal-depth cues.

entry.title: GNN-based Multi-Agent Control of Traffic Shockwaves in Sparse Vehicular Ad-hoc Networks

author.name: Prachi Nandi, Madhuri Malakar, Sonakshi Satpathy, Pabitra Mohan Khilar

entry.summary: The paper proposes decentralized multi-agent RL with a graph neural network for connected autonomous vehicles to damp stop-and-go traffic shockwaves without global traffic state information. The design targets early-stage sparse VANET deployments.

entry.title: Closed-Loop Validation-Repair for Healthcare Interoperability: A Multi-Model Study of Schema Compliance in Clinical LLMs

author.name: Jianru Shen

entry.summary: Evaluates whether small open-weight models can emit clinically valid structured outputs (ICD-10, CPT, FHIR) and tests a closed-loop validate-then-repair wrapper across 320 scenarios and three model families. Finds schema noncompliance is a consistent failure mode independent of model family, and that automated repair loops recover much of it.

entry.title: Structural Loss Metrics for Tensor Approximation via Matrix Low-Rank Approximation

author.name: Hiroki Hasegawa

entry.summary: Provides a theoretical analysis of when matricized SVD truncation is a good surrogate for tensor decomposition, introducing cross-mode Direction Loss and Interaction Loss metrics under an orthogonal Tucker model. It proves an orthogonal decomposition of squared relative reconstruction error and a Wedin-type stability bound, validated on synthetic and hyperspectral data.

entry.title: Learning-based Hierarchical Tracheal Anatomy Understanding from Sparse Surgical Demonstration Annotations for Ultrasound Robots

author.name: Hiu Ching Cheung, Wenchao Yue, Zhengran Han, Mingcong Chen, Guanglin Cao, Hongbin Liu, Hongliang Ren

entry.summary: Combines a YOLOv8n localizer with a prompt-optimized SAM2 decoder to build hierarchical tracheal anatomy understanding from sparse surgical annotations for ultrasound-guided robotic tracheostomy. A hybrid training strategy bridges curated lab data and unconstrained clinical sequences.

entry.title: A Modern ConvNet for Solar Filament Detection

author.name: J. R. Hu, Q. Hao, Z. Zheng, P. F. Chen, C. Li, Y. Meng

entry.summary: Develops a manually annotated H-alpha solar filament dataset and a multiscale dendritic segmentation ConvNet for automated filament detection. Addresses long-tail, thin-structure segmentation challenges in solar physics imagery.

entry.title: A note on the motion representation and configuration update in time stepping schemes for the constrained rigid body

author.name: A. M\"uller

entry.summary: A geometric note arguing that time-stepping integrators for constrained rigid bodies behave differently depending on whether motion is represented on the direct product group SO(3) times R3 or the semidirect product SE(3), and analyzes the consequent constraint-satisfaction behavior. Relevant to multibody dynamics simulator design.

entry.title: Model Predictive Planner for UAV Navigation in Non-Convex Air Corridors

author.name: Henrique Silva Jr., Marcelo A. Santos, Guilherme V. Raffo

entry.summary: Presents a mixed-integer tracking MPC formulation for UAV navigation in non-convex urban air corridors, embedding a shortest-path-based offset cost to avoid local minima and guarantee target convergence without a separate global planner. Validated in numerical simulation.

entry.title: Bayesian Feature Extraction using Gaussian and Diffused-gamma Priors for High Dimensional Spatio-Temporal Data

author.name: Garrett Frady, Dipak K. Dey, Shariq Mohammed

entry.summary: Develops a Bayesian feature-extraction framework for high-dimensional spatio-temporal data using Gaussian and diffused-gamma priors to induce structured sparsity, with a Bregman-divergence likelihood for flexibility across loss types. Includes a two-stage selection procedure and a multi-subject EEG application.

entry.title: FrED: External Data Influence Estimation via Domain Knowledge Graph Grounding

author.name: Theodoros Aivalis, Iraklis A. Klampanos, Antonis Troumpoukis, Joemon M. Jose

entry.summary: FrED estimates the influence of external data on generative model outputs in a fully black-box setting by fusing continuous feature similarity with discrete domain knowledge graphs. The knowledge-graph grounding is meant to reward specific historical sources and prevent generic background data from dominating attribution.

entry.title: MA-DAR: Manifold-Aligned Dynamic Adaptive Routing for Continual Temporal Knowledge Graph Reasoning

author.name: Xiangjun Shi, Chong Mu, Jinchuan Zhang, Lizong Zhang, Yuefeng He, Shang Liu

entry.summary: MA-DAR is a plug-and-play module for continual temporal knowledge graph reasoning that focuses on how replayed historical representations are merged with current ones, rather than what to replay. It diagnoses two conflict modes, norm domination and semantic blurring, and mitigates them with manifold alignment and dynamic adaptive routing.

entry.title: Visual Saliency Steering Distillation for Multimodal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning

author.name: Hao Yang, Jin Wang, Xuejie Zhang

entry.summary: Visual Saliency Steering Distillation improves multimodal chain-of-thought in small models by perturbing images along task-sensitive directions derived from attention maps, then extracting dominant steering vectors via singular value decomposition to guide layer-wise distillation. It targets cases where fusion makes different images with identical text nearly indistinguishable.

entry.title: EVL-MCoT: Enhanced Vision-Language Multi-CoT for Harmful Meme Detection

author.name: Hao Yang, Jin Wang, Xuejie Zhang

entry.summary: EVL-MCoT applies multiple parallel chains of thought with fine-grained visual-prompt alignment to detect harmful memes, arguing single-chain reasoning lacks multi-perspective thinking and that dual-stream models lack background knowledge. It combines local detail fusion with multi-perspective reasoning aggregation.

entry.title: Label-free Industrial Fault Detection via Adversarial Inverse Reinforcement Learning: A System for Run-to-Failure Prognostics

author.name: Dhiraj Neupane, Mohamed Reda Bouadjenek, Richard Dazeley, Sunil Aryal

entry.summary: This work argues that most RL-based machinery fault detection collapses to supervised classification because it discards state transitions and discounting, and instead applies adversarial inverse reinforcement learning offline to recover an intrinsic health reward from run-to-failure trajectories without fault labels. The recovered reward supports label-free detection and prognostics.

entry.title: Foundation Models and Fine-Tuning: Toward a New Generation of Models for Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Morad Laglil, Bertrand Pracca, Emilie Devijver, Eric Gaussier

entry.summary: A review of time-series foundation models covering architectures, pretraining strategies, and optimization, with attention to when fine-tuning a pretrained forecaster beats zero-shot use or dataset-specific models. Useful orientation for a fast-moving area where zero-shot claims are frequently contested.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Discovering Periodic Orbits in the Gravitational Three-Body Problem

author.name: Nikolaos Kollias, Nikolaos Matzakos

entry.summary: Shows that physics-informed neural networks trained on sparse noisy trajectory data, without initial-condition guesses, can recover periodic orbits of the gravitational three-body problem, including orbit families never seen in training. Roughly a quarter of random seeds discover out-of-training families.

entry.title: CALMRec: Causally Aligned Language Memory for Long-Horizon Recommendation

author.name: Gengyu Zhan

entry.summary: CALMRec uses a frozen multimodal language model to convert item content and feedback into semantic evidence units, then maintains separate short-term, long-term, and exposure memories with propensity-weighted updates. The goal is to stop LLM recommenders from confusing repeated exposure with genuine long-run preference.

entry.title: Source-Free Controlled Adaptation of Teachers for Continual Test-Time Adaptation

author.name: Anurag Roy, Riddhiman Moulick, Vinay Kumar Verma, Saptarshi Ghosh, Abir Das

entry.summary: For continual test-time adaptation, replaces the usual fixed exponential-moving-average momentum of the mean teacher with a dynamically controlled momentum that responds to encountered distribution shifts. This is meant to limit teacher drift and error accumulation during long deployment.

entry.title: MAPLE: Efficient and Diverse Multi-Alpha Generation for Portfolio Construction

author.name: Yu-Chen Den, Kuan-Yu Chen, Kendro Vincent, Tien-Hao Chang

entry.summary: MAPLE produces many low-correlation predictive signals per stock from a single model by combining a capacity-scaled multi-head prediction layer, an extreme-rank weighted listwise loss, and an explicit penalty on pairwise correlation between the generated alphas. It recovers the classical diversification principle of alpha mining inside one training pass.

entry.title: Monitoring Post-Disaster Urban Recovery Using High-Resolution SAR Time Series and Unsupervised Learning: Evidence from the 2023 T\"urkiye-Syria Earthquake

author.name: Luigi Russo, Deodato Tapete, Silvia Liberata Ullo, Paolo Gamba

entry.summary: Uses unsupervised deep anomaly detection on high-resolution COSMO-SkyMed SAR time series to identify persistent temporal changes associated with reconstruction, producing recovery maps for four cities hit by the 2023 Turkiye-Syria earthquakes. It works without ground-truth recovery labels.

entry.title: MobiWave: Dispatch-Oriented Graph Wavelets and Drift-Guided Selective Optimization for Autonomous Fleet Rebalancing

author.name: Xiao Han, Pinbo Wang, Yuanshao Zhu, Guojiang Shen, Xiangjie Kong

entry.summary: MobiWave combines dispatch-oriented multi-scale graph wavelets, which separate overlapping regional and local traffic frequency patterns, with a drift-guided scheme that updates only selected network layers as mobility patterns shift. It targets reliable rebalancing of autonomous vehicle fleets under nonstationarity.

entry.title: Attribution and Uncertainty Behavior of Learned Residual Gyro Correction for Gyro-Stellar Estimation

author.name: Mariela De Lucas \'Alvarez, Melvin Laux, Arthur de Freitas Precht, Maurice Martin, Edoardo Caroselli, Frank Kirchner, Alexander Fabisch

entry.summary: Applies heteroscedastic aleatoric plus ensemble epistemic uncertainty estimation and attribution analysis to a CNN that corrects gyroscope bias in a spacecraft attitude estimation loop. Tests whether uncertainty grows appropriately under correlated noise perturbations outside training conditions.

entry.title: Generative Augmentation for EEG Motor Imagery Classification: A Class-Conditional VAE with Cycle-Consistent Decoder Refinement

author.name: Matei Moldoveanu, Alain Sirois, Claire Ben Ali, Fabien Lotte, Florian Yger

entry.summary: Trains a class-conditional VAE with a latent classifier and covariance-preserving constraint to generate synthetic motor-imagery EEG trials, then tests whether independent downstream classifiers actually improve. The decoder-focused alternating training schedule sharpens the generative path used for augmentation.

entry.title: Who Gets Named: Citation Type Predicts Individual Naming by Grounded Language Models, and a Roster Instrument Captures 0.5% of It

author.name: Dmitrij \.Zatuchin (Department of Information Technologies, EUAS, Tallinn, Rankfor.AI, Tallinn)

entry.summary: Measures whether grounded search-connected models name individual professionals (rather than firms) in buyer-intent queries, using 2,400 API calls across four models, four European markets and five languages in a two-hour window. Finds citation type predicts individual naming and that a roster-based instrument captures only a tiny fraction of it.

entry.title: Hybrid Semantic and Spectral Ensemble for Robust Synthetic Image Source Attribution

author.name: Md. Ajwad Hossain

entry.summary: A dual-branch ensemble for attributing synthetic images to their generating text-to-image model, combining a semantic EfficientNet branch with a forensic branch of 126 handcrafted features including SVD spectral profiles and local binary patterns. Designed to survive unknown post-processing such as JPEG compression and blurring.

entry.title: Inverse Bayesian Inference for Extracting Lesion Dynamics from Longitudinal Spectral CT

author.name: Lukas F\"orner, Melina W\"ordehoff, Julian Steffens, Maximilian Schmutz, Rainer Claus, Josua Decker, Thomas Kr\"oncke, Kartikay Tehlan, Thomas Wendler

entry.summary: Proposes an inverse Bayesian framework that infers lesion dynamical parameters from longitudinal spectral CT by decomposing spectral feature evolution into intrinsic dynamics, tumour-burden coupling, and satellite-state change terms. Aims to extract interpretable temporal dynamics rather than static classifications.

entry.title: D3O: Dynamic Distribution Distillation for Ordinal Regression

author.name: Chunlai Dong, Yaojun Hu, Yuyang Xu, Haochao Ying, Jian Wu

entry.summary: D3O replaces fixed supervision targets in ordinal regression with label distributions that evolve during training via self-distillation, plus a contrastive ordinal-aware label enhancement module. Motivated by ambiguous boundaries and subjective annotation noise in ordinal labels.

entry.title: Weakly Supervised Instance-Level Gleason Pattern Estimation Using Primary and Secondary Labels

author.name: Nao Sugeta, Kaito Shiku, Shinnosuke Matsuo, Ryoma Bise

entry.summary: A multiple instance learning framework that recovers instance-level Gleason patterns in prostate histopathology using only routinely available slide-level primary and secondary pattern labels. Aggregates instance predictions into class counts and explicitly models pattern dominance per the clinical scoring definition.

entry.title: DAP-Pose: Deep Temporal Alignment and Physics-aware Cross-modal Sensor Fusion for Robust Pose Estimation

author.name: Jianhan Lin, Yuchu Qin, Jiateng Yuan, Wenbo Zhang, Shuai Gao

entry.summary: DAP-Pose fuses visual, inertial, and GNSS measurements for robot and vehicle pose estimation, with a module that explicitly aligns asynchronous streams in latent space so strict hardware synchronization is unnecessary, plus manifold and GNSS-based physical constraints. Targets robustness in complex environments.

entry.title: RODR: Riemannian Orthogonally Decoupled Regularization for Disentangled Manifold Representation

author.name: Jiayu Zhu, Wenlai Zhao

entry.summary: RODR identifies a geometric gradient interference problem in point cloud denoising, where fitting and projection objectives conflict and cause structural degradation and point clustering, and decouples normal and tangential components via Riemannian orthogonal regularization. Frames denoising as recovery of a smooth embedded 2D manifold.

entry.title: PointCHR: Point Cloud Analysis via Curvature-Aware Hyperbolic Rectification

author.name: Xinxing Yu, Liying Yang, Hao Mo, Hui Ma, Fang Kai, Ajian Liu, Yanyan Liang

entry.summary: PointCHR applies curvature-aware hyperbolic rectification to point cloud analysis, exploiting exponential volume growth in hyperbolic space to better represent sparse high-curvature geometric detail. It seeks to prevent fine geometry from being dominated by smooth low-curvature regions.

entry.title: Effect of User-Prompted Priors on Semi-Automated Cancer Lesion Segmentation in Whole-Body Computed Tomography

author.name: Isac Stark, Johan \"Ofverstedt, Elin Lundstr\"om, Simon Ekstr\"om, H{\aa}kan Ahlstr\"om, Joel Kullberg

entry.summary: Investigates how different user-provided prompts, such as bounding boxes versus single-slice contours, affect semi-automated whole-body CT lesion segmentation for total tumour volume estimation. The motivation is that total tumour volume predicts survival better than RECIST but requires costly expert annotation.

entry.title: Energy Constrained Hierarchical Underwater Monitoring via Local Multi-Agent RAG

author.name: Mohamed Amine Janati, Laurent Gautier, St\'ephane Barbot

entry.summary: Proposes a hierarchical underwater monitoring architecture pairing always-on ultra-low-power microcontrollers with an edge GPU that wakes only for scheduled or event-driven multimodal retrieval-augmented reasoning. It targets energy and bandwidth limits of remote marine deployments.

entry.title: A Case Study on the Acceptance of a Humanoid Robotic Head Employed in Three Public Spaces

author.name: Marcel Heisler, Luca Randecker, Christian Becker-Asano

entry.summary: Reports a field study deploying a conversational humanoid robot head with emotion simulation in three public venues over several days, measuring acceptance with the TAM2 questionnaire. Users generally found it useful and easy to use, though location context shaped the experience.

entry.title: Defining AI-Native Systems: Autonomy as Revision Authority

author.name: Cheng Tan

entry.summary: A conceptual paper defining AI-native systems not by model capability but by revision authority, meaning who is permitted to change a system decision, arranged in a ladder from self-tuning to self-rewriting to self-architecting. A system counts as AI-native when an AI autonomously rewrites its own implementations, and the definition demands an escalation detector.

entry.title: When Is a Learned Command Adapter Worth It? Closed-Loop Identification and Counterfactual Auditing of Frozen Locomotion Policies

author.name: Zongtan Li

entry.summary: Proposes an audit procedure to decide whether adding a learned adapter to a frozen locomotion policy is actually worthwhile, decomposing apparent gains into operating-point improvement, same-state counterfactual headroom, deployment gain over a fixed action, and state-allocation gain. Applied to a quadruped, it shows most apparent headroom is not recoverable at deployment, yielding go, no-go or abstain verdicts.

entry.title: From Obligation to Specification: A Survey on Validating EU AI Act Requirements in RE

author.name: T. Y. Emmy Lai, Sven Giesselbach, Matthias Koch, H\'ector Allende-Cid

entry.summary: A mixed-method study with ten expert interviews and a fifteen-person survey assessing whether organizations are prepared to translate EU AI Act obligations into testable, auditable requirements, and how practitioners perceive LLM-based agentic validation tools for closing that gap. It finds systematic processes are largely missing today.

entry.title: TextSLIP: Text Self-Supervised CLIP for Medical Report Generation

author.name: Haoyu Jiang, Ziping Cong

entry.summary: TextSLIP augments CLIP-style medical vision-language pretraining with intra-modal text contrastive learning so the textual embedding space is more discriminative before it guides visual representation learning. The goal is finer-grained semantic supervision for automated radiology report generation.

entry.title: Learning Spatiotemporal Decision Priors for Efficient Path Planning under Partial Observability

author.name: Yi Liu, Hongda Zhang, Leyao Zou, Chunlei Meng, Ziqing Zhou, Yuning Chen, Zhuo Zou, Lida Xu, Zhongxue Gan, Chun Ouyang

entry.summary: ImiPath distills reusable spatiotemporal decision priors from demonstration trajectories and uses them as directional guidance to bias classical search-based planners under partial observability. The goal is to reduce redundant node expansions and myopic behavior compared with solving every instance from scratch.

entry.title: A Self-Calibrating Agentic AI Framework for Autonomous Edge Resource Allocation

author.name: Fin Gentzen, Marla Grunewald, Iulisloi Zacarias, Mounir Bensalem, Admela Jukan

entry.summary: The authors present an agentic framework for autonomous edge resource allocation that self-calibrates against operational drift in the absence of reliable ground truth, using an ARIMA forecaster to approximate expected behavior. They evaluate whether this preserves integrity of LLM-driven decisions over time.

entry.title: Learning from the Descent Direction: Adaptive Gradient Descent under One-Sided H\"older Regularity

author.name: Arzu Ahmadova, Ismail Huseynov

entry.summary: The authors propose an adaptive gradient descent method under a one-sided Holder condition that bounds only the directional curvature term appearing in the descent inequality, permitting larger steps when gradient variation is orthogonal to the update direction. They prove best-iterate stationarity rates for nonconvex objectives with a sufficient-decrease safeguard.

entry.title: Blood Pressure Estimation from PPG: A Comparative Study of Direct and ECG-Mediated Deep Learning Pipelines

author.name: Bo Wu, Haoling Wang, Zhuodiao Kuang, Kateryna Shapovalenko

entry.summary: This study compares estimating blood pressure directly from photoplethysmography against pipelines that first reconstruct ECG, using correlation analysis on a large clinical waveform database to show PPG couples more strongly with arterial pressure than the indirect route assumes. The practical implication is that added ECG reconstruction stages may be unnecessary complexity for wearables.

entry.title: Optimal Reward Shaping: Autonomous Car Parking Case Study

author.name: Emre \"Ozkaya, Nicolas R. Gauger

entry.summary: Presents a parameterized reward-shaping scheme for autonomous parallel parking under non-holonomic constraints, with alignment gating, direction-switch penalties, and aligned termination. The central claim is that reward parameters and RL hyperparameters are strongly coupled and must be co-optimized, here via Bayesian optimization.

entry.title: Greedy dynamical meta-learning

author.name: Aria Yom

entry.summary: Proposes a meta-learning scheme in which an agent modifies its own weights in a high-dimensional inner loop while a low-dimensional outer loop, optimized with zeroth-order methods, shapes that self-modification process. The motivation is that neither gradient descent nor gradient-free search alone works well over long training horizons.

entry.title: Capacity-Aware Deep Learning for Generalizable Traffic Volume Estimation Across Links and Cities

author.name: L\'eo Hein, Giovanni De Nunzio, Aur\'elie Pirayre, Laurent Najman

entry.summary: Estimates hourly link-level traffic volumes from widely available territorial data such as probe speed profiles, road topology, and weather, avoiding dependence on dense fixed sensors. It is evaluated as a spatial out-of-distribution problem across unseen links and unseen cities.

entry.title: Physics-Guided Generative AI for Property-Targeted 3D Porous Media Design

author.name: Peng Wang

entry.summary: Combines a property-aware variational autoencoder, a conditional latent diffusion model, and a differentiable structure-to-property surrogate to generate three-dimensional porous microstructures hitting target permeability and porosity. The surrogate guides generation toward physically meaningful designs in a compact latent space.

entry.title: Unsupervised Graph Representation Learning with Complementary View Alignment

author.name: Zengyi Wo, Shiyu Zhang, Qiyao Peng, Tianpeng Li, Xuan Guo

entry.summary: AlignGAE extends masked graph autoencoders to preserve the full frequency spectrum through alignment of complementary views, addressing the homophily bias that causes message passing to discard high-frequency signals needed on heterophilous graphs. The goal is unsupervised node embeddings that work on both homophilous and heterophilous data.

entry.title: Trustworthy Medical Segmentation: Uncertainty-Aware U-Net Evaluation Under Clinical Image Degradation

author.name: Pranav Kaliaperumal, Manisha Kaliaperumal

entry.summary: Builds a reproducible framework for evaluating uncertainty-aware medical segmentation under controlled clinical image degradations such as noise, motion, low resolution, and contrast change, using a biophysical phantom brain tumor cohort. U-Net and Attention U-Net with Monte Carlo dropout are assessed on whether uncertainty actually rises when accuracy silently drops.

entry.title: Learning Asymptotics with Convergence-Rate Guarantees using Linear Least Squares

author.name: Christos N. Efrem

entry.summary: The paper proposes Asymptotics Learning Theory, using sliding linear least squares and Tikhonov-regularized variants to numerically recover unknown constants in proven asymptotic expansions, with proofs of convergence and rates. It positions asymptotic constant fitting as an optimization problem.

entry.title: Hierarchical Soft Actor-Critic for Sparse-Reward Long-Horizon Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zahra Abdalla Elashaal, Afef Hfaiedh, Nahla Khraief, Issmail Ellabib, Giansalvo Cirrincione

entry.summary: The authors combine a high-level strategic planner with a low-level Soft Actor-Critic controller for sparse-reward, long-horizon search-and-rescue tasks, reporting improved success rate and coverage efficiency over flat SAC. Both levels use entropy-regularized policy optimization.

entry.title: An Interactive Vision Language Platform for Cognitive Remediation in Schizophrenia

author.name: Nassira Ait Mehdi, Milissa Temmam, Slimane Larabi

entry.summary: An automated vision-language system that verifies whether schizophrenia patients correctly perform structured object-manipulation tasks in a camera-monitored tabletop cognitive remediation setup. Replaces subjective manual clinician observation to make therapy more scalable.

entry.title: AdaKAN: A dual-branch adaptive Kolmogorov-Arnold network for medical image segmentation

author.name: Dalia Alzu'bi, Deep Bhattacharyya, Ali Ayub, A. Ben Hamza

entry.summary: AdaKAN combines convolutions with an efficient Kolmogorov-Arnold Network block using Bernstein polynomial activations plus channel-wise adaptive scaling for medical image segmentation. Targets anatomical complexity and cross-modality variability.

entry.title: Counterfactual Motion Reliability Learning for Robust UAV Tracking

author.name: Yuehai Chen

entry.summary: Addresses infrared UAV tracking where motion cues are often unreliable due to jitter, clutter, and target disappearance, using counterfactual reasoning to learn when temporal motion evidence should be trusted. Aims to prevent background structures from dominating tracker responses.

entry.title: ConFusion: Continuous Fusion Space Learning for Fine-Grained Controllable Infrared and Visible Image Fusion

author.name: Guo Yurong, He Yufei, Li Yonghao, Chang Dongliang, Zhang Ke, Ma Zhanyu

entry.summary: ConFusion learns a continuous control space for infrared-visible image fusion using Gaussian-conditioned spatial modulation, enabling fine-grained instance-level control rather than choosing among predefined discrete fusion settings. Uses a dual-branch design to disentangle modality-shared and modality-specific features.

entry.title: Multimodal Semantic-Probabilistic Objectness for Open World Object Detection

author.name: Weijun Tian, Rui Liu

entry.summary: MSPO adds task-aware language priors over known categories to probabilistic objectness in open-world object detection, arguing visual objectness alone cannot distinguish hard known instances, unseen-category objects, and background clutter. Keeps the base detector architecture and incremental learning protocol intact.

entry.title: A Fixed-Effects Causal Forest for Staggered Adoption, with an Application to Medicaid Expansion

author.name: Harry Aytug

entry.summary: Estimates covariate-conditional treatment effects in staggered difference-in-differences designs using a causal forest with fixed effects residualized inside each tree node, applied to US Medicaid expansion. The estimand is not new, but the estimator is a simpler alternative to doubly-robust R-learner approaches.

entry.title: Shannonian Criticism: Information Architecture and Sylvia Plath's 'Daddy'

author.name: Stevie Miller

entry.summary: Applies token-level surprisal and entropy from a small language model as literary-analysis instruments, regressing information-structural features against a canonicity proxy across 295 poems by 31 poets and closely reading Plath's Daddy. Finds the poem is more predictable than most of the corpus overall yet contains unusually extreme local deviations.

entry.title: CC-AOS: Cost- and Horizon-Conditioned Amortized Backward Induction for Finite-Horizon Optimal Stopping

author.name: Tianwei Yu

entry.summary: CC-AOS amortizes backward induction for finite-horizon optimal stopping so that a single learned continuation-value model covers a continuum of observation costs and multiple horizons instead of retraining per operating point. Useful for early time-series classification systems that must adapt decision thresholds at deployment time.

entry.title: LithoFormer: A Robust Framework for Stratigraphic Inference via Transformers

author.name: Shwetha Salimath, Francesca Bugiotti, Sylvain Wlodarczyk, Sohaib Ouzineb

entry.summary: LithoFormer performs stratigraphic inference by ingesting whole multivariate well logs in one pass with a sequence-to-sequence patch transformer using rotary position embeddings, instead of sliding-window classification. Processing the full log preserves geological context and reduces misaligned formation boundaries, which matters for carbon storage and geothermal siting.

entry.title: Recycling computational processes of dynamic programming for combinatorial optimization problems: a reservoir computing approach

author.name: Sora Todaka, Akihiro Yamamoto, Nozomi Akashi

entry.summary: The authors use reservoir computing to reuse intermediate dynamic-programming tables from one combinatorial optimization instance as features for solving related instances, effectively learning cross-task computation sharing rather than designing it by hand. It is an unusual take on amortizing algorithmic computation across problems.

entry.title: DRP-FLR: Data-Driven Assessment of Demand Response Potential for Flexible Load Regulation in Smart Grids

author.name: Yunhao Yao, Siyu Jing, Yang Yang, Qiang Xu, Changqi Weng, Xiang-Yang Li

entry.summary: DRP-FLR forecasts short-term load with exogenous context and then assesses how much flexible demand can actually be regulated for grid balancing across heterogeneous consumers. It targets the supply-demand imbalance intensified by AI datacenter growth and renewables.

entry.title: DSCH-Loss: A Dynamic Semantic Channel Objective for Deep Semantic Hashing

author.name: Tobias J. Bauer, Christian Riess, Daniel Loebenberger, Christian Bergler

entry.summary: Proposes DSCH-Loss, a dynamic semantic channel objective for deep hashing that replaces fixed-width predefined channels in Hamming space with adaptively learned ones. Aims at better cross-modal binary codes for approximate nearest neighbor retrieval.

entry.title: Risk Is Not the Target: A Monotonic Framework for Evaluating Wildfire Operational Risk Signals

author.name: Nicolas Caron, Christophe Guyeux, Maxime Coulmeau, Benjamin Aynes

entry.summary: Argues that standard classification metrics are the wrong yardstick for continuous wildfire risk signals, and proposes a monotonicity-based evaluation that checks whether higher predicted risk tracks higher operational load such as fire counts and deployed resources. It compares an expert index, GRU models, and a hybrid multi-agent system with LLM reasoning on a French department.

entry.title: TRW: TRACE-RealWorld---An Auditable Consistency Contract for World Models as Materialized Views

author.name: Edward Y. Chang

entry.summary: Frames a world model as a materialized view over a changing physical world where reads of ground truth are costly, delayed and unreliable, and contributes a validity abstraction for predictions, consequence-conditioned view maintenance, transaction-style compensation for invalidated commitments, and append-only provenance for exact replay. It is evaluated end-to-end on a flood-mapping SAR task.

entry.title: Semiotic logical hexagon theory for LLM logical reasoning

author.name: Yunyao Zhang, Xinglang Zhang, Zeliang Chen, Junqing Yu, Zikai Song

entry.summary: Applies semiotic logical hexagon structures to organize the implicit semantic relations in natural-language statements before formal reasoning begins, arguing that unstructured hidden meanings cause LLMs to reach wrong conclusions despite valid-looking reasoning chains. It contrasts with decomposition, symbolic translation and self-verification approaches.

entry.title: Learning Structural Convergence: A Neuro-Symbolic Benchmark for Temporal Reasoning

author.name: Michael Romei De Socio, Gian Luca Pozzato, Alessio Merlo

entry.summary: Introduces a controlled synthetic benchmark for temporal structural reasoning in event-driven systems with early-warning, pattern-detection and run-classification tasks, modeled on multi-domain military-style operations. It compares raw-event neural models, a lightweight semantic baseline, and a neuro-symbolic configuration over semantically grounded trajectories.

entry.title: Explainable Reinforcement Learning for assisting Air Traffic Controllers

author.name: Anduel Mehmeti, Gabriella Gigante, Salvatore Venticinque

entry.summary: Applies explainability techniques to reinforcement learning agents that assist air traffic controllers, motivated by the need for trust before higher automation levels can be adopted in safety-critical aviation. The work explores what explanations of RL decisions can offer in this operational setting.

entry.title: Deep Sigma Point Processes for RCS Modeling in Spaceborne SAR Imagery

author.name: Khalid El-Darymli, Christoph H. Gierull, Katerina Biron, Weimin Huang

entry.summary: Applies deep sigma point processes, a hierarchical Gaussian process approach with Bayesian inference, to predict radar cross-section for over 208,000 verified ships in satellite SAR imagery while quantifying predictive uncertainty. This replaces deterministic equations with static parameters used in traditional radar modeling.

entry.title: AI-Integrated Scientific Inquiry: A Practice-Centered Vision for Science Education

author.name: Arne Bewersdorff, Matias Rojas, Xiaoming Zhai

entry.summary: A position and vision article proposing that AI tools be taught in K-12 science education as scientific instruments embedded within authentic inquiry practices aligned to the Next Generation Science Standards, rather than as a separate AI-literacy topic. It sketches instructional design principles for AI-integrated investigation.

entry.title: FSE: Continual Learning for Named Entity Recognition by Fast-Slow Experts

author.name: Yunan Zhang, Yang Fan, Heng Li, Xiangping Wu, Qingcai Chen

entry.summary: FSE addresses continual learning for named entity recognition with a fast shared expert that filters unlikely spans at token level and a task-specific slow expert that classifies only surviving candidates, plus length-decay negative sampling. The split is intended to share knowledge across tasks while keeping per-task plasticity and reducing catastrophic forgetting.

entry.title: Optimization of time-consuming experimental conditions using pseudo-experimental data guided by adaptive polynomial regression

author.name: Hirotaka Sugawara, Yujin Taguchi, Kei Minagawa, Yusuke Hiki, Takashi Morikura, Akira Funahashi

entry.summary: The paper improves Bayesian optimization for slow, costly laboratory experiments by generating pseudo-experimental data guided by adaptive polynomial regression, addressing poor pseudo-data quality when very few real measurements exist. The aim is faster convergence under severe evaluation budgets in experimental science.

entry.title: PRIMS: Physics-guided Representation for Fluid Identification in Multimodal Sensing

author.name: Hai-Long Nguyen, Trung Thanh Nguyen, Lars Holm, Dennis Alveringh, Duc Viet Le

entry.summary: PRIMS is a physics-aware multimodal transformer for on-device fluid identification from Coriolis and pressure sensors, embedding physical knowledge in tokenization, a physical compatibility module, and attention. The goal is reliable generalization across varying flow, pressure, and temperature conditions with interpretable representations.

entry.title: Hierarchical Grading in Large Language Models

author.name: T. Shaska

entry.summary: Graded Large Language Models equip transformer representation spaces with an algebraic grading whose weighted scalar action propagates through embeddings, attention, and the training objective, extending graded neural network theory to autoregressive models. Using geometric invariant theory, the paper characterizes beneficial gradings as an open convex cone via a Kempf-Ness functional and Hilbert-Mumford style criteria while preserving expressivity and inference cost.

entry.title: Impute On-Demand: Adaptive Correlated Time Series Imputation for Changing Environments

author.name: Zhichen Lai, Huan Li, Dalin Zhang, Dong Gong, Lina Yao, Christian S. Jensen

entry.summary: AdaCTSi is an imputation model for correlated IoT sensor time series that can adapt at deployment to sensor failures, impute only selected sensors, and scale its computation to available resources via sparse, decoupled sensor-wise embeddings. It targets adaptability rather than pure accuracy on static benchmarks.

entry.title: Neonatal Hypoxic-ischaemic Encephalopathy Classification from the EEG and HRV Signals Using a Conformer based Masked Autoencoder

author.name: Shuwen Yu, William P Marnane, Geraldine B. Boylan, Gordon Lightbody

entry.summary: MAEConformer applies masked-autoencoder self-supervised pretraining with a convolution-plus-attention Conformer backbone to unlabelled neonatal EEG and heart-rate-variability signals, adding a multi-resolution spectral reconstruction loss. It is then used to classify hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy grades.

entry.title: MS-GPT: Rethinking MS/MS De Novo Structure Elucidation as Spectrum-Induced Posterior Querying of a Molecule-Language Model

author.name: Xin Zhao, Yumin Liu, Zhuo Li, Weichu Zheng, Feng Zhu, Xiaokang Yang, Yaohui Jin, Yanyan Xu

entry.summary: arXiv:2607.23607v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Molecular structure elucidation from tandem mass spectra (MS/MS) is a central inverse problem in analytical chemistry. Most existing approaches to MS/M...

entry.title: Restoration Flow Matching-Based Channel Refinement and Equalization Correction for MIMO Semantic Communications

author.name: Wenkai Liu, Nan Ma, Jianqiao Chen, Xiaodong Xu, Meixia Tao, Ping Zhang

entry.summary: Uses restoration flow matching to jointly treat MIMO channel estimation and post-equalization distortion correction as conditional generative inverse problems in a semantic communication system. Two cascaded flow-matching modules refine the channel estimate and then clean up residual latent-space errors.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Predicting Nitrous Oxide Flux

author.name: Freddy Yu, Jashanjeet Kaur Dhaliwal, Subhadeep Chakraborty

entry.summary: Builds physics-informed neural networks for predicting agricultural nitrous oxide emissions, deriving the physics residual directly from the mechanistic equations of established process-based soil models. This connects data-driven flux prediction with traceable biogeochemical constraints.

entry.title: Causal-TS: A Python Library for Causal Discovery in High-Dimensional and Nonstationary Time Series

author.name: Mohammad Fesanghary

entry.summary: Releases Causal-TS, an open-source Python library bundling several causal discovery algorithms for high-dimensional nonstationary time series with GPU-accelerated conditional independence tests, regime segmentation, and DoWhy integration. It packages the pipeline from raw series to estimated causal effects.

entry.title: AutoCluster, AutoTopicModeling, AutoTrendAnalysis: A Complete AutoML Pipeline for Predicting Emerging Trends

author.name: Ahmed Abolfadl, Marwa Mahmoud Abla, Mervat Abu-Elkheir, Maggie Mashaly

entry.summary: arXiv:2607.22641v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Predicting emerging trends is vital for businesses, researchers, and policymakers; yet traditional approaches often lack scalability and adaptability...

entry.title: Continuous surrogates versus threshold Boolean networks for modeling Arabidopsis ISR gene regulation

author.name: Gonzalo A. Ruz

entry.summary: The paper compares random forests and MLPs against a threshold Boolean network for modeling induced systemic resistance gene regulation in Arabidopsis, on both continuous and binarized expression data. It evaluates one-step and recursive multi-step prediction alongside interpretability.

entry.title: TRUAV: Distributed Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Trajectory Planning and Routing Enhancement in UAV-Aided IoT-Enabled VANETs

author.name: Muhammad Umar Farooq Qaisar, Lin Zhang, Zhen Chen, Wajdy Othman, Shehzad Ashraf Chaudhry, Chang Liu

entry.summary: TRUAV is a distributed multi-agent reinforcement learning framework using independent tabular Q-learning for joint UAV trajectory planning and routing in vehicular ad hoc networks. It avoids the global state aggregation required by centralized approaches under bandwidth and energy constraints.

entry.title: A Frozen 12B Beats Frontier Models on Verified Work: 100% Accuracy, 0 Tokens, Bit-Exact, Forever

author.name: Sietse Schelpe (Corbenic AI)

entry.summary: This paper argues for keeping a language model frozen while growing a persistent verified-solution memory, so that once a problem family is solved and independently verified, later instances are answered deterministically at zero generation tokens. Four models across vendors reportedly score perfectly on 180 fresh instances of nine problem families.

entry.title: CHiPS: Character Histograms and Positional Signals for Lightweight Authorship Attribution in Romanian Texts

author.name: Sanda-Maria Avram, George C. \c{T}urca\c{s}

entry.summary: Proposes a lightweight character-level authorship attribution method for Romanian combining character-histogram SVM classification with Fourier and Welch spectral descriptors of character position signals, plus a leakage-safe fusion variant. Designed to run without large models or heavy compute.

entry.title: Simple Language Normalization Wins: Cross-Lingual Speaker Verification for the TidyVoice 2026 Challenge

author.name: Nina Hosseini-Kivanani

entry.summary: arXiv:2607.22923v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cross-lingual mismatch remains a key source of overall degradation in modern speaker verification. The TidyVoice2026 Challenge targets this setting wit...

entry.title: Zing: Social Mind for LLMs

author.name: Zing Team, Ao Xiang, Bi Jingping, Chen Jiahui, Chen Lehan, Chen Yilin, Cheng Xueqi, Fan Yixing, Gan Kairong, Gao Haowen, Gao Jinhua, Gao Shuxuan, Gong Chang, Guo Jiafeng, Guo Ruijie, Han Zhouyu, He Guangfu, He Yichun, Jiang Shuo, Jing Shaoling, Jing Ya, Lei Chenhao, Lei Yan, Li Anqi, Li Chengao, Li Haoyu, Li Shitian, Liang Xinjian, Liu Zhaoge, Lyu Xingyu, Nie Zhuwei, Pang Liang, Quan Zeping, Shan Shiguang, Shen Huawei, Tang Xinran, Tian Feng, Wang Qian, Wang Ruiping, Wang Xiaohong, Xia Zaiyu, Xiao Yi, Xu Jiayuan, Xu Kehan, Xu Qianqian, Xu Tianyu, Xu Yongjun, Yang Haoming, Yang Jun, Yao Di, Yu Xiaoming, Zhang Futong, Zhang Jie, Zhang Shixuan, Zhang Yuxuan, Zhao Xinyu, Zhao Zhuoran, Zhong Yunfei, Zhu Shengyu

entry.summary: arXiv:2607.23740v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As large language models move from isolated task solving toward long-term service in human environments, they require social intelligence: the ability ...

entry.title: BioSentinel at EXIST 2026: Soft-Label Optimization with XLM-RoBERTa for Sexism Intent Classification in Memes

author.name: Chandru Munisamy, Karthikeya Raguveer, Alapan Kuila

entry.summary: Shared-task system for classifying sexist intent in memes using a text-centric XLM-RoBERTa base model trained with a composite loss combining KL divergence over soft annotator distributions and weighted cross-entropy on hard labels. Reports mid-range official soft and hard label scores under a learning-with-disagreement setup.

entry.title: LEX-EC: A Lexical Evidence-Channel Audit Framework for Zero-Shot LLM Personality Classification in Black-Box Settings

author.name: Brittany Harbison, Ashok K. Goel

entry.summary: Proposes a black-box audit framework that combines prevalence and agreement diagnostics with lexical ablation to check whether zero-shot LLM personality labels reflect real trait signal or just base-rate priors. Results suggest most apparent signal is weak and genre dependent, casting doubt on LLM personality inference.

entry.title: From transcription to semantic corpus analysis: unsupervised learning of sentence representations for ancient languages

author.name: Th{\'e}otime de la Selle (ISC, HiSoMA, CNRS)

entry.summary: Compares two fully unsupervised methods (TSDAE and contrastive sentence embedding) for turning token-level ancient-language models into corpus-specific sentence encoders, using only raw noisy OCR text.
